areas.title: the loader and the core modules
areas.coverage: Read whole: bin/kit, libexec/kit-call, the 13 bash modules in scope (kinds.sh does not exist), 4 jq modules, 10 verbs, tests/trust.bats. Sampled other tests' titles. Ran 12 bats files in an isolated copy (216 pass) and a reproduction per confirmed finding. findings.md not written: Write refused it.
areas.summary: Two new security findings in trust: `kit trust` can name one release while the loader runs the clone's own `kit/`, and a directory with no `.git` gets its `bash_path` loaded by `kit help` unasked. Ctrl-C does not stop a loop or `kit ci` that calls kit. Three 11-10 findings still reproduce: `kit tools run` with a dash-word, `settings:declare` on unindented lists, and `--` reaching verbs. Also: a trust record lost to a missing newline, a yaml cache key without its expression, and stale keys after a JSON merge. 216 of 216 in-scope tests pass. findings.md was not written: the Write tool refused a report file, so everything is in this result.
strengths: A worktree's trust name is confirmed from the desk's side (the admin directory must sit under the desk's own .git/worktrees/ and name the worktree back), the same in POSIX sh and in bash, with no git run before the check; tests/trust.bats tries three spoofs.
kit trust always runs on the installed release, so a clone's own kit cannot keep its trust.

The loader is POSIX sh with sed as its only process: it refuses an unknown option with exit 2, checks a version's shape before using it in a path, checks the digest before unpacking, unpacks beside the cache and renames, and counts hand-offs so two loaders cannot loop.
list:fill carries a command's status in band, so a failed read is never an empty answer; a midway failure, an exit, and a return status all behaved as documented when probed.
file:replace writes beside the path and renames, names the temporary for the process, and keeps one EXIT trap for every module.
The yaml cache is validated by the file's text, not its size and time, and is used only as a directory and files this user owns that are not links.
One guard refuses every verb's bad arguments in the same words with exit 2 and names the nearest verb for a typo; the 20 refusals probed each exited 2 with one line and a remedy.
A log never fails the call it logs.
216 of 216 tests in the twelve bats files of this scope pass in an isolated copy.

findings.title: kit trust does not show the release the loader will run
findings.claim: trust:asks returns at once with no kit.yml and otherwise reads version through yq, while the loader's pinned reads the first ^version: line with sed and falls back to .kit/manifest. So a clone can run its own kit/ after a prompt that named something else, against kit-trust:12.
findings.evidence: Clone with kit/bin/kit, no kit.yml, and .kit/manifest 'version unreleased': kit trust --yes prints 'asks kit to run nothing beyond the kit itself', then kit kinds prints 'CLONE-OWN-KIT ran: kinds'. With kit.yml '"version": 0.1.0' plus that manifest the prompt says 'run kit 0.1.0, downloaded from its release', and the clone's kit runs; a repeated version key prints three garbled lines.
findings.fix: Have trust:asks report what the loader would choose, from one reader (first version: line, then the manifest), and print each value on one line. Add the three cases to tests/trust.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced all three. No kit.yml plus .kit/manifest 'version unreleased': kit trust --yes says 'run nothing beyond the kit itself', then kit kinds runs the clone's kit/bin/kit. '"version": 0.1.0' and '{version: 0.1.0}' prompt 'run kit 0.1.0' and the clone's kit runs. Repeated key prints three garbled lines. tests/loader.bats:71 covers only the loader side.

findings.title: Outside a clone, a directory's kit.yml loads bash into every kit command, unasked
findings.claim: kit:trusted-at answers yes for any directory in no clone, and use:load-path then reads bash_path from the kit.yml in the working directory. An unpacked source archive with no .git runs its own bash in kit help, kit version, and kit trust; the loader itself ignores that kit.yml.
findings.evidence: Directory with no .git, kit.yml 'bash_path: [kit:modules/bash/, evil/]', evil/help.sh with one echo: kit help --text usage, kit version, and kit trust --check . each print 'PWNED: code from the unpacked directory ran'. After git init there, nothing of it loads; tests/trust.bats:78 checks only that no refusal prints.
findings.fix: Outside a clone, read no bash_path and run no gate from a kit.yml, or hold the directory to a trust record by its own path. Add a test that a kit.yml outside a clone loads nothing.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: no .git, kit.yml 'bash_path: [kit:modules/bash/, evil/]'; kit help --text usage, kit version, kit trust --check . and kit kinds each source evil/*.sh. After git init nothing loads. Deliberate per kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:137; only from the directory holding kit.yml, not a subdirectory. tests/trust.bats:78 checks only the missing refusal.

findings.title: kit tools run refuses a command line that holds a dash-word (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: kit-tools:38 says <command>… is taken as typed, dash-words included, but the matcher picks the wrong alternative and guard:arguments answers any --help or -h itself. Only kit tools run -- <command> works.
findings.evidence: At 0e76266c, kit syntax tools --match -- run prettier --check . gives status 1, missing --outdated; run npm outdated --json gives "unknown argument 'run'". kit tools run jq --help and -h print kit's own page for tools.
findings.fix: Let opens look past a leading optional group, as firsts does, and leave --help alone once a repeated operand has taken its first word. Add both to tests/arguments.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Real but narrower than the title. Refused: kit tools' own option names in the command (--check gives 'needs --outdated', --json gives "unknown argument 'run'"), and --help/-h print kit's page. Other dash-words pass without --: kit tools run jq --version, run ls -l, run echo -n x all match and run. 'Known since 11-10' not checked.

findings.title: Ctrl-C does not stop a script, a loop, or kit ci that calls kit
findings.claim: kit-call traps INT to log the call and then exits 130 normally, so the calling shell takes the signal as handled and its loop goes on. A verb called directly dies of the signal and its caller stops.
findings.evidence: A script running a 4-second verb three times with '|| echo failed', SIGINT to the group after 1.5 s: through bin/kit, 'member 1 failed with 130', then members 2 and 3 run to the end, status 0; calling bin/kit-sleepy directly, the script ends at once with 130. kit ci has the same shape: run kit "${verb}" || refused=….
findings.fix: After log:call, when the verb died of a signal, reset the trap and send the same signal to $$. The same forwarding would let a TERM sent to kit alone reach the verb.

findings.title: settings:declare corrupts a kit.yml whose lists are not indented two spaces (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: The awk in settings:declaration-kept takes only lines starting with two spaces as a block's items. A list at the key's column, or indented one space, is valid YAML, and its items are kept as stray lines after the new block.
findings.evidence: settings:declare 0.1.0 "" kit style/bash on 'packages:' / '- kit' / '- style/bash' / 'excludes:' / '- workflow' leaves the new block followed by the three old '- …' lines; yq then says 'did not find expected key'. The same with ' - kit'.
findings.fix: Treat any following line that is indented or starts with '- ' as the block's continuation. Add both shapes to the test 'the declaration is rewritten where it stands'.

findings.title: kit trust says it trusts a clone that the trust file then does not hold
findings.claim: trust:with prints the file with cat and then the new record, so a hand-edited trust file whose last line has no newline gets the record joined to that line. kit trust prints its success line without checking, and both clones are untrusted afterwards.
findings.evidence: Trust file holds t1's path with no newline (kit trust --check in t1 exits 0); kit trust --yes in t2 prints '✅ kit trusts …/t2'. The file is then one line '…/t1…/t2', and kit trust --check exits 1 in both t1 and t2.
findings.fix: End the old text with a newline in trust:with when it has none. In kit-trust, check kit:trusted "${record}" after trust:record and fail when it does not hold.

findings.title: A kept yaml result is replayed for another expression, so releases can read each other's cache entries
findings.claim: A cache entry is named for the read's name and the file's path only; the expression, the yq options, and the release are not in it. Every release on a machine shares ~/.cache/kit/yaml, so the first release that changes yaml_facts_expression or the fields or kinds expression replays the other's facts for up to seven days, silently.
findings.evidence: yaml:yq x.yml fields ".a" prints 1; yaml:yq x.yml fields ".b" on the same unchanged file then also prints 1, not 2.
findings.fix: Put a digest of the expression and options, or the release's version and a format number, into the entry's name or header and treat a mismatch as a miss. Do it before 0.1.0 fixes the format.

findings.title: A -- the guard accepts reaches the verb as a word (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: tests/arguments.bats:128 claims '-- never reaches a verb as a path' and checks kit context alone. Ten verbs loop over "$@" themselves after the guard sorted the words, and only four of them drop --.
findings.evidence: kit kinds -- README.md prints a row for a path named '--' and switches layout; kit help --text -- version and kit usage -- version print "unknown verb '--'". kit completion -- zsh prints nothing and exits 0.
findings.fix: Read syntax_operands in these verbs, as 18 verbs already do, or have the guard hand each verb its words without the --.

findings.title: merge::apply keeps a key an earlier release wrote and the new release dropped
findings.claim: apply walks the keys of $new only: it drops base's array entries that new lacks, but a scalar or object key that base wrote and new dropped stays, and merge::holds cannot see it, so kit check passes. No release has dropped a key yet, so nothing is wrong today.
findings.evidence: cur {a:1, deny:[x,mine], old:{k:1}, mine:true}, base {a:1, deny:[x], old:{k:1}}, new {deny:[y]} gives {a:1, deny:[mine,y], old:{k:1}, mine:true}: a and old stay. place.sh:176 calls apply alone on an update.
findings.fix: On an update, first remove the keys base has and new lacks where the value is still as base wrote it, then apply. Add a tests/jq case.

findings.title: Nine options take their value as the next word, thirty-one after =
findings.claim: Across 153 usage lines, 31 distinct options are --name=<value> and 9 are --name <value> (--choices, --duplicate-of, --file, --fix, --message, --pr, --title, --to, --toolchain) in 8 verbs. The second kind accepts both forms; the first refuses the next-word form.
findings.evidence: kit welcome --fix <check> [--folder=<path>] has both on one line: kit syntax welcome --match -- --fix x --folder y answers '--folder needs a value', while --fix=x --folder=y is accepted.
findings.fix: Write the nine as --name=<value>, which the matcher already accepts, and drop the next-word form from the grammar once no usage line has it.

findings.title: secrets:foreign turns a secret made of hex digits into bytes
findings.claim: secrets:foreign un-hexes any keychain value that is an even number of hex digits, so a token that is itself hex is destroyed. Nothing in kit/ calls the secrets module at this commit, and its header's 'see: modules/bash/forge.sh' names a file that does not use it.
findings.evidence: With a stand-in security that answers a 40-hex-digit value, secrets:foreign printed 20 bytes (od shows 001 # E g 211 …), not the 40 characters.
findings.fix: Un-hex only when the decoded bytes hold a newline or another byte the keychain would have hexed. Say in the header that the module has no caller yet, or leave it out of 0.1.0.

findings.title: kit help, kit usage, and kit root never leave POSIX mode
findings.claim: Only kit:enter runs set +o posix, and 48 of 52 verbs call it; help, usage, root (and tui) do not. Under POSIXLY_CORRECT the guard's declare -F on a module:function name fails, and the closed-choices check is skipped.
findings.evidence: POSIXLY_CORRECT=1 kit help --text version prints "syntax.sh: line 438: declare: `help:choices': not a valid identifier" on stderr before the page; every kit <verb> --help execs kit-help and prints the same.
findings.fix: Run set +o posix in 1st.sh when a verb sources it, or at the top of guard:arguments.

findings.title: kit trust --revoke cannot take back the trust of a clone or folder that is gone
findings.claim: The record is worked out from the path on the disk, so a deleted clone is 'in no clone' and a deleted folder 'not a folder', both exit 2, and the record stays until the file is edited by hand. A new clone made later at that path is trusted without a question.
findings.evidence: kit trust --yes in t3, rm -rf t3, kit trust --revoke …/t3 prints '…/t3 is in no clone', and kit trust --list still prints it.
findings.fix: With --revoke, take a path that is not on the disk as the record itself when the trust file holds that line.

findings.title: file:replace turns a linked file into a regular one
findings.claim: mv -f over <path> replaces a symbolic link with the new file, so a file linked from a dotfiles repository stops being the link and the linked file is never updated.
findings.evidence: With ~/.config/kit/trusted linked to another file, kit trust --yes left trusted as a regular file (-rw-r--r--) and the link's target still held its one old line.
findings.fix: When <path> is a link, resolve it and write through to its target, with the temporary made beside the target.

findings.title: log_days 0 keeps logging until the day ends, and starts yq on every call
findings.claim: log:write reads log_days only when today's log does not exist, so a 0 set during the day is ignored until tomorrow. Once it is honored, every call finds no file and runs yq again, against the header's 'starts no process but on a day's first line'.
findings.evidence: With a log written today, adding log_days: 0 and running kit root twice took the log to 79, then 80 lines. With no log file and log_days: 0, three calls of kit root started yq six times, against three with the setting absent.
findings.fix: Keep the day's decision in an empty marker file under .kit/logs, or read log_days from kit.yml's text with a builtin before asking yq. Honor 0 when today's file is there.

findings.title: An empty first word runs kit tui
findings.claim: The loader takes "" as the verb, and verb=${1:-tui} in kit-call turns it into tui with the next word as its argument. A script that runs kit "${verb}" with the variable unset opens the TUI.
findings.evidence: kit "" version printed 'kit tui needs an interactive terminal'.
findings.fix: In kit-call, take tui only when there are no words ($# == 0), and refuse an empty verb with guard:unknown-verb.

findings.title: Key and option tables written twice
findings.claim: kit.yml's top-level keys are listed in settings:validate and in kit.schema.json, package.yml's keys in resolve:validate and its schema, and the loader's four options in completion:kit-options and bin/kit's header. Each pair is kept in step by hand.
findings.evidence: jq '.properties | keys' on kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/kit.schema.json gives 20 keys, the same 20 as the case arms at settings.sh:55-57 today.
findings.fix: Read the key lists from the schemas at validate time, and generate the kit options' candidates from the loader's header, as each verb's are read from its own.

areas.title: the workflow verbs
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 27 scoped files, 4,175 lines. Sampled: 1st.sh, file.sh, forge.sh, the providers' pr-* calls, the loader, three workflows. Ran 136 bats tests in 10 suites (0 failures) and 20 reproductions, in out/B2/copy/tests/b2*.bats and out/B2/e1.sh, e2.sh.
areas.summary: 28 findings in the workflow verbs: 1 critical, 2 high, 8 medium, 17 low; 14 are new, 14 were known on 11-10 and are still open. Critical: bin/release pack publishes an empty digest, so no release can be fetched. High: kit work 7 adopts and pushes a start commit onto release/7-0; kit commit silently undoes two commits a stale index never saw. No path loses a stash, a branch, or a pull request body except a two-process race on the stash drop. Twelve workflow findings of 11-10 are fixed. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the Write as a report file, so the full text is here.
strengths: The sweep in kit work is safe by construction: the stash is known by its hash, refs/stash is compared before and after the push, the top entry's subject is checked, and file:at-exit puts the work back on any stop; tests/work.bats 11-15 pin it.

kit rebase forces only over the tip it read (--force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>, an empty sha for a branch the remote lacks), takes the remote's commits first, and resets to the commit it started on; a failed push run again ends correct (ran).
git:push names the refspec, so push.default and an upstream of another name never decide where a branch goes.

kit tidy keeps a worktree when the forge cannot be read, when git refuses the removal, and when a commit is on no remote and not under the change's head; a head this clone lacks keeps the branch and names the fetch.

kit commit judges the tree it commits: an index of its own for named paths, commit:moved and commit:same-tree just before git runs, --cleanup=whitespace, NUL-separated paths, and :(literal) pathspecs throughout.
issue:link-in-body returns 1 and writes nothing when the pull request body cannot be read, and a test holds it.
kit release deletes its tag when the push fails, pushes that tag alone, and refuses a failed read of the remote's tags rather than taking it for none.
The tracker seam is small and even: one contract, a provider per prefix, and the web provider refuses each call it cannot make with the page to do it on.
list:read keeps a command's status where a process substitution would lose it, and no module sets a trap of its own.
Twelve of the 27 workflow findings of 11-10 are fixed in this tree (its 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 17), each with a test; all 136 tests of the ten suites in scope pass.

findings.title: bin/release pack publishes a .sha256 with no digest, so no release can be fetched
findings.claim: pack calls release:digest, which exists nowhere (the function is file:digest, kit/modules/bash/file.sh:175); the call is inside a printf argument, so errexit misses it and pack reports success. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran bin/release pack release/9.9.9-rc.1 with the fake go: 'line 116: release:digest: command not found', then '✅ packed', status 0, and the file holds '  kit-9.9.9-rc.1.tar.gz' while the tarball's digest is 1ab8f8dc…. The loader (kit/bin/kit:256-263) and release:fetch (release.sh:125-132) refuse a tarball whose digest differs from the published one; the test greps the file name only.
findings.fix: Call file:digest and fail unless it prints 64 hex characters. Assert the digest in tests/release.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Ran bin/release pack release/9.9.9-rc.1 with the fake go: 'line 116: release:digest: command not found', then '✅ packed', status 0; the .sha256 holds two spaces and the file name. kit/bin/kit:256-263 and release.sh:125-132 compare a real digest with an empty one and refuse. Only a path in KIT_VERSION or KIT_BASE escapes.

findings.title: kit work N adopts, commits to, and pushes any branch whose last path part starts with N-
findings.claim: git ls-remote --heads origin "${key}-*" matches the tail of a ref from any slash, so release/7-0 or dependabot/7-zip is taken for issue 7's branch when no 7-… branch exists. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran kit work 7 with origin holding release/7-0 and a fake gh: 'Creating worktree …/worktrees/release/7-0', 'Adding the start commit', gh call 'pr create --draft --base main --head release/7-0', and origin's release/7-0 then ends in '#7 start: Fix the thing'.
findings.fix: Ask for refs/heads/${key}-* (ran: it lists 7-real and neither nested branch) and keep only names that start with ${key}-.
findings.verdict_note: Ran kit work 7 in a bats world whose origin holds main and release/7-0, fake gh with no open head for 7: worktree worktrees/release/7-0, 'pr create --draft --base main --head release/7-0', origin's release/7-0 ends in '#7 start: Fix the thing'. No caller guards it; forge/github.sh:114 filters by prefix, issue.sh:365 does not.

findings.title: kit commit undoes two commits the index never saw, against what its page promises
findings.claim: commit:behind compares the staged blob only with the blob before the last commit that changed the path, so an index two commits behind on a path passes. kit-commit's page says it 'never undoes a commit the index did not see'. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran: another session commits a twice from an index of its own (MM a), then kit commit --message '#7 B: add b.txt' with no paths: '✅ committed e7549e0', status 0, stat 'a | 2 +-; b.txt | 1 +', and git show HEAD:a prints the oldest content.
findings.fix: Refuse when the staged blob equals the path's blob at any earlier commit that git log -- <path> lists and the disk differs, or bring the shared index up to HEAD for paths it never staged.
findings.verdict_note: Extended tests/commit.bats's peer script: two peer commits to notes.txt, private index left at the first content (MM notes.txt). kit commit --message '#7 mine: a file' exits 0 and HEAD:notes.txt is the oldest content. The existing test (commit.bats:428) covers one commit only. It needs a session committing from an index of its own.

findings.title: kit commit cannot commit a file taken out of tracking, and the remedy it prints for a placed file is refused
findings.claim: A deletion staged by git rm --cached, the file kept on disk, is read by commit:behind as an index left behind when the file's last commit added it; naming the path answers 'nothing to commit'. commit:guard tells the person to run git rm --cached on a placed path HEAD tracks, then refuses that staged deletion too.
findings.evidence: Ran: commit local.env, git rm --cached local.env, kit commit: '❌ local.env is staged as it was before ca1f4df …; committing it would undo that commit'. Ran with .kit/1st.md (refused by commit:behind) and with .kit/logs/x.log changed by two commits (behind=0, guard=1 with the same 'run: git rm --cached').
findings.fix: In commit:behind, pass a staged deletion when the disk holds HEAD's blob. In commit:guard, judge only paths staged as added or changed (--diff-filter=ACMR).

findings.title: the pre-commit checks read the disk, and the commit takes the index
findings.claim: Without paths, commit:checks lints ${PWD}/<path> while git commits the staged blob, which may differ. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran: stage bad.sh with 'echo $1', fix the disk copy without staging (AM bad.sh), kit commit: '✅ every governed path passes its rule's linter', '✅ committed 0b82595', and git show HEAD:bad.sh ends in 'echo $1'.
findings.fix: Refuse a staged path whose disk copy differs from the index, or lint a git checkout-index of the tree to be committed.

findings.title: bin/release retire deletes a pre-release that branches still reach, once the repository has many branches
findings.claim: Under pipefail, 'git branch --remotes --contains … | grep --quiet' fails when git dies of SIGPIPE, and the if then deletes the release and its tag; a gh release list that fails inside < <(…) is never seen and prints 'retired 0', status 0. The SIGPIPE half is known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran out/B2/e2.sh: with 602 remote branches containing the commit (32 KB), 123 of 200 runs took it as unreachable; with 62 branches, 0 of 200. The gh half is by reading.
findings.fix: Capture each command's output first, fail on a failed read, and test the captured text, guarding the empty case.

findings.title: an Azure DevOps tracker with its own closed_state is never read as closed
findings.claim: tracker/ado:close sets the record's closed_state or removed_state, while tracker/ado:state knows only the literals Closed, Done, Removed. kit settle is then not safe to run again, kit tidy never sees the issue closed, and kit linked counts it open.
findings.evidence: Ran with closed_state: Resolved and a fake az: close sent '--state Resolved' and state then printed OPEN. kit settle 3 on a work item already Resolved sent '--discussion Closed by pull request #3 …' and '--state Resolved' again.
findings.fix: tracker/ado:state reads the record's closed_state and removed_state beside the three defaults.

findings.title: a rebase that conflicts leaves no way forward, and every other failure is called a conflict
findings.claim: On any failure of git rebase, git:rebase aborts and prints '<branch> conflicts with <target>' with no remedy, while the delivered deny list refuses git rebase to an agent, so a real conflict with the default branch has no supported resolution. The mislabelled failure and the guessed 'main' are known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran with the default branch trunk and no origin/HEAD: 'fatal: invalid upstream 'origin/main'' then '❌ 1-x conflicts with origin/main; the rebase was aborted'. kit/packages/agents/claude/files/repo/.claude/settings.json:6 denies 'git rebase *'.
findings.fix: Tell a conflict (unmerged paths) from another failure, name the paths, and name the supported way to resolve one. Read the default branch from the remote when <primary>/HEAD is unset rather than guessing main.

findings.title: bin/release publish packs the working tree and lets gh make the tag
findings.claim: pack copies kit/ as the disk has it and takes the version from the tag's name without reading the tag; publish runs gh release create with no --verify-tag, which creates a missing tag at the default branch's head. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: By reading; a desk may publish a pre-release (bin/release:124). The gh half is gh's documented behaviour, not run here.
findings.fix: Refuse unless the tag's commit is HEAD and the tree is clean, or pack from git archive of the tag. Pass --verify-tag.

findings.title: the primary issue gets no Closes line, so a change is unlinked wherever the forge links no branch
findings.claim: issue:start writes Closes only for a primary in another tracker; on GitLab, and for a branch found on origin by name, nothing links the change to the forge's own issue, so kit linked fails in CI and the issue stays open on merge. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: forge/gitlab:link-branch (gitlab.sh:193) creates a branch by name, forge/gitlab:pr-create passes --description "", and docs/integrations/glab.md:119 gives 'Closes #n in the description' as the link. One merge request opened by glab with an empty description from a branch 7-x, then closes_issues, would settle it.
findings.fix: Always add the Closes line for the primary; issue:link-in-body adds it once.

findings.title: kit work names a branch the default policy refuses when the title has no ASCII letter or digit
findings.claim: The slug keeps [a-z0-9] only, so a title in another script gives the branch '<key>-', which the default policy.branch refuses; every kit commit in the worktree kit work made is then refused. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran the same expressions on '修复登录问题': branch=[ab4521-], and ^[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (kit.schema.json:411) does not match it.
findings.fix: Fall back to the key and a fixed word for an empty slug, in one function shared with the GitLab provider.

findings.title: kit rebase reads a relative path from the repository root, not from where it was typed
findings.claim: kit:enter changes to the root and the raw operand goes to git -C, unlike kit commit, which uses context:relative. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran from desk/sub: kit rebase ../worktrees/7-fix-the-thing printed '❌ ../worktrees/7-fix-the-thing has no branch checked out, so there is nothing to rebase', status 1.
findings.fix: Resolve the operand with context:relative before git:rebase.

findings.title: what a reference looks like is written three times, and the three disagree
findings.claim: The schema allows a prefix of ^[A-Za-z]*#?$, tracker:parse takes any declared prefix, and commit.sh holds the literal ^([A-Z]+)?#[0-9]+ and a space twice. A subject with a declared reference kit's literal does not know gets the reference twice, and commit:attach never fires for it.
findings.evidence: Ran with prefixes PROJ and lin# declared: 'PROJ4521 fix the thing' became 'PROJ4521 PROJ4521 fix the thing', 'lin#12 fix…' became 'lin#12 lin#12 fix…', and '#7: fix the thing' became '#7 #7: fix the thing'.
findings.fix: One tracker function that reads a subject's leading reference from the declared prefixes, used by both callers.

findings.title: kit gather exits 0 when an issue could not be put under the parent
findings.claim: issue:gather sets failed=1 and never returns it; the page promises 1 when an issue could not be put under the parent. issue:assign and issue:close return theirs.
findings.evidence: Ran with forge:issue-add-sub failing: two '⚠️ … could not be put under #5' lines, '#5', 'gather status=0'.
findings.fix: return "${failed}" after the printf of the parent.

findings.title: three definitions of a version's shape; a pre-release kit release accepts cannot be fetched
findings.claim: releases:valid allows a hyphen inside the suffix (tests/release.bats asserts release/1.2.3-rc-2 verifies), while release:fetch and the loader's is_version allow letters, digits, and dots only.
findings.evidence: Ran: releases:valid 1.2.3-rc-2 succeeds; release:fetch 1.2.3-rc-2 prints '❌ '1.2.3-rc-2' is not a kit version'; the loader's is_version refuses it and accepts 1.2.3-rc.2.
findings.fix: One pattern for all three, and the same test cases against each.

findings.title: these verbs die with git's status and git's words when a remote cannot be reached
findings.claim: Each fetch in kit rebase, kit tidy, and kit work is a bare command under errexit, so the verb exits 128 with no kit line, where its page promises 0, 1, or 2.
findings.evidence: Ran kit rebase ../wt with an origin that cannot be read: git's five lines only, status 128.
findings.fix: Check each fetch, say what could not be reached, and return 1.

findings.title: kit settle, kit ready, kit linked, and kit work --pr read a change's number four ways
findings.claim: kit ready and kit linked refuse '#7' with status 2; kit settle and kit work --pr strip a leading # or ! and check nothing else, so a word that is no number reaches the forge and exits 1. kit linked tests the raw $1, the others syntax_operands.
findings.evidence: By reading the four entry points.
findings.fix: One function that strips the forge's sigil and refuses the rest with status 2, used by all four.

findings.title: settling a closed change takes the author off an issue their other open change still closes
findings.claim: issue:settle looks at the closed change alone, so closing a superseded change comments 'this is backlog again' and unassigns the author while a newer open change closes the same issue. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: By reading; CI's Settle job and kit tidy both run it.
findings.fix: Skip an issue that an open change still closes; forge:open-prs lists them.

findings.title: kit work starts a closed issue without a word
findings.claim: Only the title is read, so a closed issue gets a branch, an assignment, and a draft change that kit linked then refuses. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: By reading: no state call between the title read and issue:branch.
findings.fix: Read the state with the title, and refuse or warn.

findings.title: a staged type change is invisible to kit commit
findings.claim: --diff-filter=ACMRD leaves out T, so a file replaced by a symbolic link is 'nothing staged' alone, and beside another path is committed with no guard and no check. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Ran: replace notes.txt with a link and stage it (T  notes.txt); kit commit answers '❌ nothing is staged', status 1.
findings.fix: Add T to both filters.

findings.title: kit gate looks for the justfile's ci recipe outside the toolchain that runs it
findings.claim: detect-gate runs a bare just --summary while the gate runs through toolchain:run, so where just is only in the project toolchain or its container, kit gate fails with 'the root justfile could not be read'. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: By reading; not run.
findings.fix: Run the probe through toolchain:run, or fall through to the next gate when just is missing.

findings.title: the Azure DevOps tracker drops a new issue's body, and takes a failed read for an unassignment
findings.claim: tracker/ado:create ignores the body the seam's contract passes, so kit gather under a # record claimed for ado loses its task lines and still says Gathered; tracker/ado:unassign returns 0 when it cannot read the assignee. assign, close, and comment never check for az and hide its errors.
findings.evidence: By reading against the contract at kit/modules/bash/tracker.sh:38-49.
findings.fix: Pass --description, return 1 on a failed read, and guard:require tool:az in each call.

findings.title: the swept stash is dropped by its slot, read a moment earlier
findings.claim: Both drops read stash list for the hash's slot, then run git stash drop stash@{n}; a stash another session pushes between the two moves the slots, and the drop removes that session's entry. The stash is shared by every worktree, as the file's header says.
findings.evidence: By reading; the window is two processes wide and was not raced.
findings.fix: Check that stash@{n} still names the hash immediately before the drop, or keep the swept work out of the shared list.

findings.title: kit submit says 'origin refused the push' for any remote and any failure
findings.claim: commit:push-refused names origin whatever remote the branch pushes to, and calls an unreachable remote a refusal. That kit work and kit submit use origin is documented at docs/features.md:122; the message is not.
findings.evidence: Ran in a clone whose only remote is github, with primary: github: '❌ origin refused the push of 7-fix-the-thing', then git's ''origin' does not appear to be a git repository'.
findings.fix: Name the remote git:pushes-to printed, and say it could not be reached when git's words are not a refusal.

findings.title: kit linked's last line names closed and foreign issues as linked
findings.claim: closes is built from every line the forge gave, whatever its state or repository, each written #<n>, so an issue of another repository or a closed one appears in '✅ … is linked to'.
findings.evidence: By reading: the two loops above count and warn, and the list is built again from refs unfiltered.
findings.fix: Collect the references that counted in the two loops, and print those.

findings.title: kit commit --all stages every tracked change before any check, and a refusal leaves it staged
findings.claim: git add --update runs before commit:behind, the guard, the linters, and the policy, so a refused commit leaves the shared index holding every tracked change, which may be another session's work.
findings.evidence: By reading the order of commit:commit, lines 441-471.
findings.fix: Build the --all tree in an index of its own, as the named-path mode does, and stage only once the checks pass.

findings.title: commit.sh's header still says kit submit commits
findings.claim: The header says 'kit submit commits when there is something to commit, then pushes', while commit:submit (lines 519-521) and kit-submit's page say it commits nothing.
findings.evidence: By reading both.
findings.fix: Rewrite the header's paragraph to match commit:submit.

findings.title: five readers of git worktree list, and two copies of the slug
findings.claim: git:linked-worktrees and git:worktrees are the same loop with a different filter, and issue:worktree, issues:checkouts, and git:tidy each parse the same porcelain again; the title-to-slug expression is at issue.sh:380 and forge/gitlab.sh:196.
findings.evidence: By reading the five places and the two slug lines.
findings.fix: One git:checkouts that prints path, detached, and branch for every checkout, filtered by its callers, and one slug function; B2-11 is then fixed once.

areas.title: delivery: packages, regions, templates, generation
areas.coverage: Read whole: the 15 modules, template.jq, the 11 verbs, bin/refresh, all 19 package.yml and the packages layout; file.sh and parts of release, settings, resolve, 1st, serve. Ran install, hydrate, update, uninstall, packages, generate, template, new, context, lint, facts in isolated throwaway repositories, and 118 bats tests (105 pass; 12 failures environmental, 1 real). bin/refresh not run.
areas.summary: 21 findings: 2 high, 10 medium, 9 low; 20 reproduced. One root sits under the worst three: .kit/manifest should say what kit placed, but every hydrating verb rewrites it from what the release delivers. After that, kit update cannot apply a changed answer (B3-1), a repository's own file under .kit/ is replaced on the second command (B3-2), and an overriding package never lands (B3-3). kit serve keeps stale delivery caches and reports files placed that are not (B3-4, B3-5). One test in the tree fails at this commit (B3-12). Nine findings are known since 11-10 and still open. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from a subagent, so the full report is this result.
strengths: file:replace and file:copy write beside the path and rename over it, name the temporary for the process, and sweep from one EXIT trap; a failed producer leaves the file as it was.

region:has judges the markers in one awk pass with a third status for a shape a write would damage, and place:refusals runs it over every region before update, remove or uninstall touches anything; the 11-10 region findings 1, 2, 10 and 11 are fixed by it.
package:remove now has uninstall's edit guard (place:edited), and a failed render:all returns from add, remove and uninstall (11-10 findings 12 and 13 fixed).
list:read carries a command's status out of a process substitution and is used for nearly every list, so a failed read is rarely taken for an empty one.
generate:expand checks a unit's whole shape before running any command, refuses conflict markers, writes only when the whole expansion succeeds, and names file and line in each refusal.
manifest:paths refuses a record that climbs out of its root; sources:fetch checks the digest before anything is unpacked and refuses a record without one.

materialize:hydrated now looks under .kit/packages/ for anything newer than .kit/.gitignore (11-10 finding 8 fixed for separate processes); context:matcher compiles to its own file, renames it into place, and prunes by age.
facts:document checks each pipeline stage by hand, and a change that could not be read is an error object, never null.
Headers and comments state the guarantee at the place a reader needs it; most findings here were found by holding the code to its own header.

bin/refresh reads and writes the index only through git checkout-index and git read-tree, which follow GIT_INDEX_FILE, so it holds under git commit -a and in a linked worktree's hook (checked what git exports there).

findings.title: Any verb that hydrates re-records the manifest, and kit update then cannot apply a changed answer
findings.claim: materialize:hydrate ends with manifest:write repo, which records the running release's digest for every delivered path, including those outside .kit/ that hydrate never places. kit update then takes the stale copy for a repository edit and merges it against a base equal to the new render, a no-op that exits 0.
findings.evidence: kit install github/ci, add answers.ci_runner: macos-latest to kit.yml: kit update straight away prints 'unchanged since unreleased, replaced' and the file changes. With one 'kit context README.md' in between (the Claude hook is such a verb), kit update prints 'edited since unreleased, three-way merged', the file keeps ubuntu-latest on every rerun, and kit check says 'run: kit update'.
findings.fix: Hydrate rewrites only the records of the paths it materializes and keeps the recorded digest of every other path; better, a record is written when a path is placed and never derived from the release. This also closes B3-2, B3-3 and 11-10 Delivery 9.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a sandbox. Update straight after the answer edit: 'unchanged since unreleased, replaced', macos-latest. With one 'kit context README.md' between, the manifest digest for kit-ci.yml changes, update says 'three-way merged', exits 0, the file keeps ubuntu-latest on rerun, and kit check says 'run: kit update'. The Claude hook runs 'kit context --claude'.

findings.title: A repository's own file at a delivered path under .kit/ is left alone for one command, then replaced
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 3), still open. materialize:all names and skips an unrecorded path that holds a different file, then the manifest is written with a record for that path, so the next verb's full run replaces it.
findings.evidence: With .kit/manifest and .kit/.gitignore absent (a fresh clone) and 'MY OWN RULE' in .kit/rules/bash.md, kit hydrate warns 'a different file is there already', prints ✅ and exits 0. The next 'kit context README.md' prints '.kit/rules/bash.md was changed in place, or came from another release; replaced' and the file is the kit's.
findings.fix: materialize:all hands back the paths it refused and manifest:text leaves them out, in hydrate and in kit update (line 235). kit hydrate exits 1 while a path is refused.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. With manifest and .kit/.gitignore removed and 'MY OWN RULE' in .kit/rules/bash.md, kit hydrate warns, exits 0, and writes a manifest record for the path. The next 'kit context README.md' prints 'changed in place ... replaced' and the file is the kit's, with no copy kept. A read-only own file survives until the next full run.

findings.title: kit packages add does not place a path the new package overrides, and kit update cannot repair it
findings.claim: place:beyond lists only paths the new set delivers and the old set does not, so a path whose winning layer changes is neither placed by add nor restored by remove, while the manifest records the new winner. docs/packages.md:131 says the later package in dependency order wins. The remove half is known since 11-10 (Delivery 21), still open; the add half is new.
findings.evidence: With github/ci installed, a repository package that depends on it and delivers its own .github/workflows/kit-ci.yml: 'kit packages add local' prints ✅ and names no path, and the workflow is still github/ci's. kit check says 'differs from the pinned release; run: kit update', and kit update prints 'three-way merged' and changes nothing.
findings.fix: Add and remove compare the winning source of every path in both sets (place_source under the two keys) and re-place each path whose source changed, behind the place:edited guard.

findings.title: A second hydrate in one process reuses the first one's list of delivered paths, as under kit serve
findings.claim: place_delivered, render_rendered and render_rendered_all live as long as the process; kit serve calls materialize:hydrate in its own shell whenever kit.yml changes (serve.sh:240), and only materialize_real is emptied. The stale pass then touches .kit/.gitignore, so materialize:hydrated passes for every later process too.
findings.evidence: A script that sources the modules, runs materialize:hydrate --full, adds kinds/two.yml to an active repository package, touches kit.yml and hydrates again: materialize:hydrated says work to do, yet nothing is placed. Afterwards 'kit context a.two --json' in a fresh process gives kinds ["any"] and .kit/kinds/two.yml does not exist.
findings.fix: One function that empties the three caches and removes the rendered directories, called where materialize:all empties materialize_real.

findings.title: Under kit serve, kit hydrate and kit new say a file is in place and place nothing
findings.claim: Every tool call the MCP server runs has kit_serve_hydrated=1, under which materialize:hydrate returns 0 at once, --full included; kit hydrate still prints its ✅ and new:offer still says the thing is in place. The server places again only when kit.yml changes, so a file an agent adds to a repository package through the server stays unplaced.
findings.evidence: 'kit_serve_hydrated=1 kit new kind three --path=*.three' prints '✅ kit unreleased hydrated .kit/' and 'the three kind is in place; run: kit kinds three'. .kit/kinds/ has no three.yml.
findings.fix: Let an explicit kit hydrate through under the server, or have the server watch .kit/packages/ as materialize:hydrated does. Until then both messages say the server places it when kit.yml next changes.

findings.title: A kind a file gets from its first line is read from the working tree, not from the tree the facts describe
findings.claim: facts:tree-in hands the tree's paths to context:classify, which tests the file on disk and reads its first line there. The header says the tree holds what is staged and not what is on disk, and that text is read from the blob.
findings.evidence: Stage bin/tool with a bash shebang: kit facts --moment=commit gives kinds [any, bash, text]. Overwrite or delete the working copy without staging and the same blob (size 28) has kinds [any], so a policy rule over bash files does not see the staged script.
findings.fix: For regular files no glob has decided, read the blob's first line with one git cat-file --batch and feed it to the classifier in place of the disk read.

findings.title: kit context exits 0 with no rules when a rule's frontmatter cannot be read
findings.claim: context:load fills context_file_kinds from a pipeline whose status it never checks, and every caller runs it under ||, so a rule or style yq cannot parse governs nothing.
findings.evidence: With a rule whose frontmatter is 'kind: [one', kit context a.one prints yq's ❌ line and exits 0 with no rule; --json gives rules []; kit context --claude gives no hook answer and exits 0. kit lint a.one exits 1 on the same file.
findings.fix: Read each file's kinds with list:read and return 1 on a failed read, as the loop above does for a kinds file; add the case to the verb's exit line.

findings.title: kit new kind writes a pattern in YAML double quotes, so a regex with a backslash breaks every classifying verb
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 15), still open. --path and --content values are written inside double quotes, where a backslash is a YAML escape.
findings.evidence: kit new kind zsh --content='^#!.*/env\s+zsh' then kit packages add local: kit context README.md prints '.kit/kinds/zsh.yml: … found unknown escape character' and 'the kinds in it cannot be read', exit 1.
findings.fix: Write single-quoted scalars with each single quote doubled, and drop the double-quote refusal at new.sh:193.

findings.title: A path glob with a [ that never closes hangs every verb that classifies
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 18), still open. expr gives 0 for an unclosed bracket, so i += -1 is followed by i += 1 and context:glob-ere never ends.
findings.evidence: kit new kind draft --path='docs/[draft*.md' is accepted; after kit packages add local, kit context README.md ran until a 20-second timeout killed it. The Claude hook, kit lint and kit facts compile the same way.
findings.fix: Take an unclosed [ as a literal \[, and have kit new kind compile its globs before it writes the file.

findings.title: A source tarball laid out as the header says is cached empty, and its packages are never found
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 16), still open. --strip-components 1 removes packages/ from a tarball with packages/ at its top, sources:roots then skips the source silently, and the cache directory stops any refetch.
findings.evidence: A tarball of packages/guides/… pinned by digest (file:// URL): kit packages add guides prints 'Fetching the source team…' then ''guides' is not one of the choices'. The cache holds <digest>/guides/.
findings.fix: After unpacking, refuse and do not cache a source with neither packages/ nor kit/packages/; strip a component only when the tarball has one top-level directory.

findings.title: Home delivery is shared by every repository with no count of who uses it
findings.claim: Latent in 0.1.0, since no shipped package delivers to home; 11-10 named it and did not run it. kit uninstall in one repository removes home files another still declares, and manifest:write home keeps lines by a grep -F substring match that doubles them.
findings.evidence: Two repositories install a package delivering .config/tool/rc and rc.d to home: uninstall in the first removes both, and the second's kit check prints 'home: nothing is installed … not checked'. After kit install in a third repository the home manifest holds the rc.d line twice, and the next kit update prints 'rc.d: edited since unreleased, three-way merged' for an unedited file.
findings.fix: Match the whole record line (awk $0 == digest "  " path) when keeping lines. Record which repositories deliver each home path, or leave home alone on uninstall unless asked, and have check judge home from this repository's packages.

findings.title: A test in the tree fails at this commit: the forge-provider template lacks six calls the seam's header lists
findings.claim: forge.sh lists bot-app, bot-installation, bot-installations, bot-token, bot-repositories and bot-revoke under the calls every provider implements; the delivered forge-provider template does not hold them, and gitlab.sh and ado.sh do not define them. The test that holds header and template together is red.
findings.evidence: In a copy of the snapshot, test 66 of the run ('each seam's header lists the calls its providers' template holds…') fails. Recomputing both lists on the snapshot gives 60 names in the header and 54 in the template, the six bot-* calls being the difference.
findings.fix: Either mark the six as calls a provider may implement, as the header does for other optional calls and as the bot-accounts feature at forge.sh:234 suggests, or add them to the template and to the GitLab and Azure DevOps providers. Then run tests/template.bats.

findings.title: kit template fix exits 1 without a word on a file that has no ASCII hole
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 17), still open. Under pipefail, grep's status 1 fails the count assignment and errexit ends the verb.
findings.evidence: kit template fix t1 t2, where t1 has no hole, prints nothing, exits 1 and leaves t2's <<name>> unrewritten. In the other order t2 is rewritten and the verb exits 1 with no line for t1.
findings.fix: { grep … || true; } | wc -l.

findings.title: A rendered template loses its mode
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 22), still open. render:fill writes with printf >, so an executable template arrives without its x bit, though docs/packages.md says a template's result is placed exactly like a files/ file.
findings.evidence: A package with files/repo/bin/plain and templates/repo/bin/hello, both 755: after kit packages add, bin/plain is -rwxr-xr-x and bin/hello is -rw-r--r--. No shipped template is executable.
findings.fix: [[ ! -x "${file}" ]] || chmod +x "${out}/${rel}" after the write.

findings.title: kit new file takes a relative path from the repository root; its sibling verbs take it from where it was typed
findings.claim: kit-new resolves only an absolute path through context:relative, after kit:enter changed to the root. kit context, kit generate, kit lint and kit template fix resolve a relative path against kit_invoked_in. The header of kit-new does state its rule.
findings.evidence: In sub/, 'kit new file b.note --body=x' prints '✅ made b.note' and the file is at the root, with sub/ left empty. 'kit context b.note' typed in the same place answers for sub/b.note.
findings.fix: Pass every path through context:relative, as the others do, and say so in the header.

findings.title: kit uninstall leaves a one-byte kit.yml when the file held only the declaration
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 24), still open. grep --invert-match over an empty here-string sees one empty line and takes it for something else in the file.
findings.evidence: A kit.yml of version, packages and '- kit' alone, with no modeline: kit uninstall prints 'kit.yml: version and packages dropped' and ls shows a 1-byte file.
findings.fix: Test [[ -z "$(grep --invert-match '^# yaml-language-server:' <<<"${kept}" | awk NF)" ]].

findings.title: Taking a region out moves blank lines in a file that opens with one
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 27), still open. In region:strip, held is set by a leading blank line and is still set after the first text line is printed, so the blank line comes out after it.
findings.evidence: A .gitignore of two blank lines, mine-before, mine-2, a blank line, mine-3: after kit install and kit uninstall, diff shows the leading blank lines gone and a new one between mine-before and mine-2. A file that does not open with a blank line came back byte for byte.
findings.fix: Clear held on the first printed line when nothing was printed before it.

findings.title: kit new template lists the new variant first, so it becomes the default for kit new file
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Delivery 29, third bullet), still open. The awk inserts the variant right under templates:, and kit new file defaults to the first variant the rule lists that the path allows.
findings.evidence: kit new template note first, then kit new template note second: the style lists second above first, and kit new file a.note answers 'the second template of the note rule needs --body=<…>'.
findings.fix: Append the variant after the last item of the templates: block.

findings.title: kit generate has three inputs it does not guard
findings.claim: An output that opens its own region recurses without end, because the opened-twice check runs only on the finished expansion. --iterations is not validated, and a file whose last line has no newline is reported stale.
findings.evidence: A region whose command cats a file holding the same directive ran until a 30-second timeout. --iterations=abc dies with 'generate.sh: line 425: abc: unbound variable', and --iterations=-1 prints '✅ … expanded in 0 pass(es)', exit 0.
findings.fix: Carry the open names down generate:unit and fail on one already open; refuse an --iterations that is not a positive integer with status 2. Keep the file's last-line ending when writing the expansion.

findings.title: A template line that only mentions kit:generate is read as a directive
findings.claim: template.jq opens a region at any line where kit:generate\b matches and closes it at any kit:end\b. generate.sh takes a directive only where nothing alphanumeric stands before the marker.
findings.evidence: A template whose second line is '# The table below is filled by a kit:generate directive elsewhere.': kit new file fails with 'the region opened at line 2 never closes'. kit generate --check on a file with that line says there is no directive.
findings.fix: template.jq and region:host-insert test the line with generate.sh's marker pattern, kept in one place.

findings.title: The same tables and the same removal walk are written out in several places
findings.claim: From the code, not run. The extension-to-comment table is listed twice (region:markers, region:known); what marks a directive is defined four ways; the judge-walk-guard-remove sequence is written in uninstall:run, package:remove and the retire loop; and kit update keeps its algorithm, with recorded-digest and lacks-base, in the verb file where no test can call a step.
findings.evidence: region.sh:42-48 and 57-67 repeat the same extensions by hand. kit-update:104-135 defines functions inside the verb, while install, packages and uninstall have modules.
findings.fix: One table of extension to opener and closer, one marker pattern, a place:take-out shared by the three removals, and an update.sh module.

areas.title: the forge seam and the GitHub provider
areas.coverage: Read whole: forge.sh, forge/github.sh, forge.jq. Sampled the four test files and callers. Ran 112 suite tests in a copy (all pass), 14 reproductions with the fake gh, and real gh 2.103.3 against a loopback proxy. One slip: a dummy-token gh call reached api.github.com (401), carrying no project data.
areas.summary: 22 findings: 2 high, 12 medium, 8 low; 17 confirmed, 5 plausible; 5 known since 11-10 and still open (B4-1 to B4-5). The GitHub provider lets gh choose the repository and host, so the primary is not honoured, for reads or writes. Same-named checks hide a failure. The snapshot survives a change made during a read, and a reused process number stalls every read 120 seconds. Rate limits are misnamed on the repo-view and marks paths. Of the contract's calls, runs does not hold and nine hold partly. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write of a report file, so this result is the only copy; the reproductions are in out/B4/work/tests/b4*.bats.
strengths: The contract at the top of forge.sh is precise enough to test against, and failed reads print nothing on stdout: attestations, environments, teams, runs, and open-prs gather first and print last.
forge:fold and forge:json make an answer that is not the JSON asked for a failed read with a line, and the `| arrays` / `| objects` checks keep "no repository" apart from "cap reached".

Whole-or-fail is real for the long lists: gh --paginate --slurp, cursor loops for open changes, threads, checks, and closed issues, forge:whole at 10000, and rest-of-pr refusing checks of a head that moved.
The snapshot is replaced by rename and read under a floor, the lock is one `ln -s`, and a failed read keeps nothing; four processes make one read.
Marks by ETag with If-None-Match cost nothing while nothing changed, and a kind that fails is null while the others are still read.
The App calls keep the JWT and token off argv (curl reads the header on stdin), check IDs before any request, and tell network, limit, refusal, and 5xx apart.
Unsupported calls answer 3 from the declaration before the provider runs, and stand-ins are applied after the snapshot, so one snapshot serves any kit.yml.
forge:primary checks a setting before it reaches git as an argument, and forge:none never takes a wrong setting for none.
The team-slug retry degrades one field instead of the whole read.

findings.title: The GitHub provider never tells gh which remote is the primary, so gh's own choice is read and written to
findings.claim: The seam says changes, builds, releases, and issues are read from the primary (kit.yml's, else origin), and GitLab and Azure DevOps read the primary's URL; the GitHub provider sets no GH_REPO and uses gh repo view and {owner}/{repo}, so gh picks upstream, then github, then origin, or gh repo set-default. Writes (issue create, issue develop, issue close, pr create) go to that repository too, while the snapshot is keyed by origin's URL.
findings.evidence: gh 2.103.3 behind a logging loopback proxy, remotes origin=me/fork and upstream=them/project: `gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/milestones'` sent GET /repos/them/project/milestones, and gh repo view and gh pr list sent owner them, repo project. With origin and a remote named github it asked third/mirror.
findings.fix: Read owner and name from the primary's URL as the sibling providers do, and run every gh through one wrapper that exports GH_REPO=<host>/<owner>/<name>. Add a conformance test with two GitHub remotes. Known since 11-10 (Filed issues #68/#50), still open.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced through kit's own seam with gh 2.103.3 behind a loopback proxy: origin=me/fork, upstream=them/project, forge:primary says origin, yet forge:call repo and releases asked them/project; gh issue create targeted them/project. With origin plus `shared`, gh asks origin, so `primary: shared` is ignored. No GH_REPO or -R anywhere; forge:call (forge.sh:550) sets only color variables.

findings.title: A failed check is hidden by a check of the same name that started later
findings.claim: checks keeps one run per name, the latest by start, and GitHub names a check run by its job alone, so two workflows with a job of one name, or one workflow on push and pull_request, leave only the later run counted.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4c.bats R10: contexts `build` FAILURE at 10:00:00 and `build` SUCCESS at 10:00:02 give checks {"state":"SUCCESS","passed":1,"total":1,"failing":""}.
findings.fix: Ask checkSuite { workflowRun { event workflow { name } } } and group by workflow, event, and name, so only a later attempt of the same job supersedes. Known since 11-10 (Flow 1), still open.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with the kit's jq: two `build` CheckRuns, FAILURE at 10:00:00 and SUCCESS at 10:00:02, give state SUCCESS, total 1, and forge::state "ready". The query (github.sh:546) reads only name, status, conclusion, and times, so nothing tells workflows or events apart. That GitHub gives both runs one name was not checked against a real forge.

findings.title: gh api goes to gh's default host, not the primary's
findings.claim: gh repo view and gh pr list follow the checkout's remote, but gh api user, graphql, and rate_limit go to github.com unless GH_HOST is set or gh has one login; github.sh sets no GH_HOST and passes no --hostname. On a desk logged in to github.com and an Enterprise host, every GraphQL read, forge:me, and the rate limit read ask github.com.
findings.evidence: In a repository whose remotes were all on github.localhost, with a github.com token set and no GH_HOST, `gh api graphql --field owner=123 ...` was answered by api.github.com with Bad credentials (HTTP 401). grep for GH_HOST or hostname in github.sh prints nothing.
findings.fix: Export GH_HOST=<primary's host> in the one gh wrapper of B4-1. Known since 11-10 (Flow 10, plausible), still open, now observed.

findings.title: runs keeps what is left of the 50 newest runs of any kind, not the 20 newest that no pull request owns
findings.claim: The seam promises the 20 newest runs not owned by a pull request; the provider reads gh run list --limit 50 and filters afterwards, with no {"limited"}. A repository with steady pull request traffic draws a short or empty builds table and says nothing.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4.bats R9: 50 runs whose event is pull_request give exit 0 and `[]`; the call logged is `run list --limit 50 --json ...`.
findings.fix: Ask by event and branch (gh run list --event push --branch <default>, --event schedule, --event workflow_dispatch, and tags), 20 each, and merge. Known since 11-10 (Flow 12), still open.

findings.title: A change made while another process reads leaves the pre-change snapshot behind for up to a minute
findings.claim: forge:forget removes *.json, but a reader that began before the change then writes its answer, stamped with the second it began, and every later reader within the minute takes it. kittui reads in the background while a person acts, so the window is ordinary.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4b.bats R2: open-prs with a gh that answers after 3 seconds; at 1.5 seconds the title becomes CHANGED and pr-set-title runs (exit 0). Afterwards the next open-prs makes no read (reads stay 1) and prints the title "Fix the thing".
findings.fix: Have forge:forget write the second it ran into the snapshot directory, and have forge:snapshot-read refuse (or forge:snapshot-take not keep) a snapshot that began at or before it. Known since 11-10 (Flow 24, low, plausible), still open, now reproduced.

findings.title: With GraphQL's rate limit spent, most reads say the checkout does not resolve to a GitHub repository
findings.claim: Fourteen call sites begin with forge/github:repo or :repo-url, which run gh repo view, itself a GraphQL request, discard what gh said, and always print one line; so a spent limit, a network failure, and a bad token all read as a wrong checkout, against the provider's header. Each also spends a point and a round trip on a name the remote's URL gives.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4d.bats R12, repo view and api graphql both answering "API rate limit already exceeded": open-prs, merged-prs, deployments, bots, pr-closing-issues, artifacts, and rulesets each print "run: gh repo view (this checkout does not resolve to a GitHub repository)". The conformance test at line 1715 passes only because its fake lets repo view succeed while GraphQL is refused.
findings.fix: Read owner and name from the primary's URL once a process, with no request (as B4-1). Make the rate-limit test's fake refuse repo view too.

findings.title: A mark read under a spent rate limit names gh auth status and marks every scanner refused for ten minutes
findings.claim: forge/github:mark reads only the status line, so a 403 or 429 that is a rate limit is told "gh auth status", and for a scanner it becomes the verdict refused, kept 600 seconds. The alerts mark therefore changes when the limit is met and again ten minutes after it lifts, reloading the alerts stage twice for nothing.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4.bats R1, gh api --include answering HTTP/2.0 403 with "API rate limit exceeded": out={"issues":null,"alerts":"refused refused refused"}, err "gh auth status (the issues mark could not be read)", and three marks-*.verdict files holding "<now> refused".
findings.fix: In forge/github:mark, give a 403 or 429 body to forge/github:limited first, fail the mark when it is a limit, and keep no verdict for it.

findings.title: A repository or owner named in digits, or true, false, or null, fails every GraphQL read
findings.claim: Ten call sites pass --field owner=... --field name=..., and gh's --field converts integers, true, false, and null to JSON types, which GitHub refuses for String!. open-prs, bots, deployments, iterations, merged-prs, pr-closing-issues, rulesets, bypasses, and the rest-of reads all fail with "gh auth status" for a repository such as someone/2048.
findings.evidence: gh 2.103.3 behind the proxy: `gh api graphql --field owner=123 --field name=2048 ...` posted "variables":{"name":2048,"owner":123}; gh api --help documents the conversion. b4.bats R3 shows kit sending `--field owner=123 --field name=2048`.
findings.fix: Use --raw-field for owner and name at lines 106, 188, 305, 458, 557, 648, 1081, 1089, 1143, and 1187, as forge/github:teams already does for org. Keep --field for the numbers.

findings.title: A repository with Issues turned off fails open-issues with gh auth status, and the snapshot cannot pass a 3 on
findings.claim: The contract lets a call answer 3 when the repository has the feature off and says the seam passes it on; gh refuses gh issue list there in its own words and forge/github:ask turns that into gh auth status. forge:snapshot-take has `answer=$(forge:call "$1") || return 1`, so open-prs and open-issues could never answer 3 anyway.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4.bats R7, gh answering "the 'empowerite/example' repository has disabled issues" (a string the gh binary holds): exit 1, "run: gh auth status (the issues could not be read)". Not seen against a real repository; gh issue list in one with Issues off settles it.
findings.fix: Answer 3 when gh says "has disabled issues", and carry the provider's status through forge:snapshot-take and forge:snapshot.

findings.title: A lock whose process number another process of the same user now has is waited on for two minutes at every read
findings.claim: A lock is stale only when kill -0 fails, so after a kill -9, crash, or power loss during a read, once the number is reused by the same user every reader waits forge_snapshot_wait (120 seconds), reads on its own, keeps no snapshot, and leaves the lock. Nothing is said, and it never clears until that process exits.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4c.bats R8, the lock naming the test's own live shell and the wait cut to 2 seconds: first call exit 0 after 3s, lock still there, snapshot kept 0; second call the same, reads 2.
findings.fix: When the wait runs out, take the lock over and keep the snapshot; or treat a lock older than a bound as stale, or name the process's start time in the link beside its number.

findings.title: One pull request with more than 20 reviewers fails the open changes of the whole repository
findings.claim: Threads, checks, and closed issues past a page are read on, but review requests or reviews past 20 on any one pull request fail the whole open-prs read, for every stage and verb that uses it, and the line does not name the pull request.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4d.bats R14, a second pull request with latestReviews.totalCount 21: exit 1, "kit reads at most 20 review requests and 20 reviews of a change (the pull requests could not be read)".
findings.fix: Read the rest by cursor as forge/github:rest-of-pr does, or at the least draw that change with its first 20 and name its number.

findings.title: A pull request from a fork whose branch has the same name is taken for this branch's
findings.claim: on-branch asks gh pr list --head <branch>, which filters on the head's name alone, so pr-for-branch, pr-last-, pr-state-, pr-head-for-branch, pr-here, and branch-for-issue can answer with a fork's pull request. On main, with an open pull request from a fork's main, kit linked, ready, settle, and the rules' facts default to that change.
findings.evidence: gh's help: --head "<owner>:<branch>" syntax not supported; the proxy log shows the query is pullRequests(states, headRefName: $headBranch, ...) with no owner. Not asked of GitHub; gh pr list --head main --json number,isCrossRepository in such a repository settles it.
findings.fix: Ask for isCrossRepository as well and keep only pull requests that are not, in on-branch and branch-for-issue.

findings.title: An issue's iteration is cut without a word, and any refusal of the projects but one fails every open issue
findings.claim: issue-iterations reads 5 projects and 20 field values an issue with no totalCount, so a value past them is silently none, against whole-or-fail. Only INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES becomes "no iterations"; a fine-grained token or a runner's GITHUB_TOKEN is refused with FORBIDDEN instead, and open-issues then fails over an optional column.
findings.evidence: By reading: the query at 884 has no totalCount, and line 897 tests only insufficient_scopes and 'required scopes' before failing with "gh auth status (the issues' iterations could not be read)". The refusal's wording is from memory; a run with a fine-grained token without Projects permission settles it.
findings.fix: Ask totalCount and fail or mark the cut; treat any refusal of projectItems as no iterations, with one warning.

findings.title: A pull request title that holds "rate limit" turns an unrelated failure into a rate limit
findings.claim: forge/github:ask gives forge/github:limited gh's stdout as well as stderr, and limited matches *'rate limit'* anywhere, while a GraphQL answer with an error prints its data on stdout.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4d.bats R13, an answer with a FORBIDDEN error and a pull request titled "Back off at the rate limit": "wait for GitHub's rate limit to reset; run: gh api rate_limit (the pull requests could not be read)".
findings.fix: Match stderr, and in stdout only .errors[].type == "RATE_LIMITED" or the top-level .message.

findings.title: gh is run from 33 places through four wrappers and bare, each with its own idea of a failure
findings.claim: ask (32 uses), refused (3), alert-pages (4), mark, and 25 bare gh lines each decide alone what a failure says, which is why B4-6 and B4-7 never reach limited and why B4-1 and B4-3 need a change in 33 places. The GraphQL cursor loop is written five times with different guards: three check forge:whole, two do not.
findings.evidence: Counted with grep in github.sh; the scope test is repeated by hand at lines 305-316 and 893-905, and the loops are open-prs, pr-closing-issues, rest-of-closes, rest-of-pr, and issue-iterations.
findings.fix: One forge/github:gh that sets the repository and host and classifies a failure (limit, scope, off, refused, other), and one helper that pages a GraphQL connection.

findings.title: The calls that change the forge disagree on what a failure prints
findings.claim: Nine changing calls end `>/dev/null 2>&1` and fail silently, a rate limit included; link-branch, pr-set-body, and pr-create let gh's stderr through; issue-create says a kit line. pr-create prints ${url##*/} unchecked where issue-create checks for digits.
findings.fix: One helper for a change that keeps gh's stderr, runs it through limited, and says one line; check pr-create's number as issue-create does.

findings.title: A host in capitals names no forge, and ssh.github.com gives the App calls a base that does not exist
findings.claim: forge:url-host keeps the host's case and forge:of compares with lower-case patterns. ssh.github.com, GitHub's SSH-over-443 host, is github by *.github.com, and forge/github:api-base then prints an Enterprise base for it.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4.bats R6: git@GitHub.com:empowerite/example.git gives "origin's host 'GitHub.com' names no forge the kit knows"; with ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/... api-base prints https://ssh.github.com/api/v3.
findings.fix: Lower the host in forge:url-host; in api-base treat github.com and any host under it as api.github.com.

findings.title: A marks stand-in of every: 12.5 passes the check and then breaks the arithmetic
findings.claim: The stand-in check accepts any number of 10 or more, and forge:marks puts it in bash arithmetic, which takes whole numbers only.
findings.evidence: Reproduction b4.bats R4: "forge.sh: line 721: 1794486101 / 12.5 : arithmetic syntax error", exit 1, no kit line.
findings.fix: Require a whole number in the check: ($v.every | floor) == $v.every.

findings.title: Lists inside a change are cut without a word: 20 labels, 10 assignees
findings.claim: labels(first: 20) on a pull request and on each issue it closes, and assignees(first: 10), ask no totalCount and no next page, where every sibling list reads on or fails. A drafts stand-in by label (forge.sh:840) would miss a 21st label.
findings.evidence: By reading the query; no fixture was run.
findings.fix: Ask totalCount and fail, or read on by cursor, as the contract's whole-or-fail rule says.

findings.title: The bypasses of a protection GitHub shows only to an admin are neither listed nor counted as hidden
findings.claim: For a caller who is no admin, controls sets the protection to {rules: null, full: null}; rulesets prints it with rules null, but github_bypasses selects . != null on full and prints nothing, so the branch reads as having no bypass. The contract gives "hidden" for what the forge hides.
findings.evidence: By reading github.sh:1113-1115, github.sh:129-130, and forge.jq:1145; no fixture was run.
findings.fix: Print one waiver for the protection with actor and reason null and hidden marked unknown, or say in the contract that a hidden protection has no row.

findings.title: forge:unlock reads the link and removes it in two steps, so a take-over can remove a lock just taken
findings.claim: Two waiters that both see a dead holder: the first removes the link and makes its own, and the second, between its readlink and its rm -f, removes the first's, so two processes read at once. The cost is one extra read, never a torn snapshot, as the snapshot is replaced by rename.
findings.evidence: By reading; not reproduced.
findings.fix: Take over by renaming the link to a name of one's own and checking what was moved, or accept it and say so in the comment.

findings.title: A name part of "." is accepted for an App's repository (fixed one commit later)
findings.claim: forge/github:app-ok accepts ./x as owner/name, and curl folds /./ out of the path, so bot-installation asks /repos/x/installation. The next commit on the branch, e4ab3b99, says it refuses a . or - leading part.
findings.fix: None beyond e4ab3b99; recorded so nobody files it again.

areas.title: the GitLab and Azure DevOps providers and the trackers
areas.coverage: Read whole: forge/gitlab.sh, forge/ado.sh, forge/github.sh, forge.sh, tracker.sh, tracker/*, forge.jq, docs/trackers.md, kit-linked. Sampled: issue.sh, the three test files, forge-conformance's GitLab world, docs/integrations az and glab. Ran: the three bats files (41/41 pass), 16 own reproductions, four jq runs. No live az, glab, or gh.
areas.summary: Two high findings, both plausible: Azure DevOps open-issues is silently cut at az's 1000 work items, and only GitHub closes a primary issue on merge (GitLab gets no closing line, so kit linked fails; Azure DevOps needs a transition nobody passes). Ten medium: closed_state ignored by reads, GitLab unresolved counts notes, ADO builds span the project's repositories, assign replaces on ADO, web tracker fails kit settle, tracker/ado drift, PAT sign-in, iterations team, per-change read cost, allow_failure. Nine low. 13 confirmed by 16 reproductions against the fakes; 5 known since 11-10. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused a report file, so this result is the whole report; reproductions are in out/B5/b5-repro.bats and out/B5/repro.out.
strengths: One failure shape: every read goes through ask and fold, so a tool that fails or answers non-JSON is one line and exit 1, and "none" is only an answer the forge gave; forge/gitlab:on-branch checks for a list first, and tests/forge-ado.bats:642 pins "never answers nothing".

The 11-10 review's worst GitLab findings are fixed: every per-merge-request read has `|| return 1`, a fork's pipeline is read under its own project with a fallback to one check, every list is paged and capped by forge:whole, and epoch reads an offset.
A provider declares its contract version and what its forge lacks, and the seam answers 3 without running it; a stand-in is validated against what the forge can carry before any call.
forge/ado.sh names organization, project, and repository on every az call with --detect false; {"limited": N} means the same in every capped list of all three providers.
Each answer kit reads has a schema and provenance note under docs/integrations/, which made the 1000-item cut findable from the repository alone.

The tracker seam is small and its exit codes mean something (2 for a reference no tracker answers, 1 for trackers that cannot be read), and the web provider refuses by naming the page where a person can do the thing.

All 60 seam calls are defined by GitHub; GitLab and Azure DevOps each define 54 and leave the 6 bot-account calls to the seam's version gate, with explicit return-3 stubs (2 on GitLab, 11 on ADO) matching their lacks declarations.

findings.title: Azure DevOps lists at most 1000 open work items, the oldest, and says nothing
