findings.claim: forge/ado:open-issues reads `az boards query … ORDER BY CreatedDate ASC` once and checks only forge:whole (10000), so a project past 1000 open work items gives the 1000 oldest with exit 0, breaking the seam's "A list is whole or the call fails". The WIQL also takes every work item type, test cases and plans among them.
findings.evidence: docs/integrations/az/boards-query.schema.json says the extension "reads the first 1000 work items it finds"; --only-show-errors hides any warning. Not run against a live az: settle it with a project past 1000 items.
findings.fix: Fail when the answer holds 1000 items, or read ids through `az devops invoke --area wit --resource wiql` and the items in batches. Add a work item type filter from a setting.
findings.verdict_note: Probe (out/B5/verify-1/tree/tests/probe-b5.bats): a fake az answering exactly 1000 items gives exit 0, 1000 documents, no stderr; kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh:301 checks only 10000. The repository's own schema (docs/integrations/az/boards-query.schema.json:4,22) states the 1000 cap. The WIQL has no type filter. The cap itself was not run against a live az.

findings.title: Only GitHub closes the primary issue on merge: GitLab gets no closing line, Azure DevOps no transition
findings.claim: issue:start writes `Closes <ref>` only for a non-forge issue and issue:settle's MERGED arm closes only other trackers' issues, leaving link and close to the forge. On GitLab a `<iid>-slug` branch plus an API-created merge request with an empty description yields no closing reference, so closes_issues is empty, kit linked fails on every kit work change, and the issue stays open; on Azure DevOps the linked work item only moves with --transition-work-items, which kit never passes.
findings.evidence: `tracker:is-forge "${primary}" || in_body+=("${primary}")`; glab mr create is called with `--description ""`; docs/integrations/az.md:68 says work items "move on completion with --transition-work-items". No test runs kit work, linked, or settle on a GitLab or ADO forge; settle it by creating branch 7-x and its MR through glab api and reading closes_issues.
findings.fix: Let a provider declare whether its forge closes a linked issue itself; where it does not, write `Closes #n` in the body (GitLab) and have issue:settle close the forge's own still-open issues after a merge (ADO). Correct docs/trackers.md:50.
findings.verdict_note: Kit's side holds: gitlab.sh:451 sends an empty description, issue.sh:603 adds no Closes for a forge primary, and docs/integrations/glab.md:119 says linking needs one. GitLab's empty closes_issues needs a live forge. Azure DevOps is overstated: ado.sh:367 links the item, so kit linked passes, and kit completes no pull request, so the transition is the completer's choice.

findings.title: Azure DevOps reads a work item as closed only in Closed, Done, or Removed, whatever closed_state says
findings.claim: The close calls honour closed_state and removed_state, but issue-state, the open-issues WIQL, and tracker/ado:state hard-code three names. A work item kit closed to a configured state reads OPEN, so kit settle comments and closes it again at every run, kit linked counts it, and kit tidy keeps its worktree.
findings.evidence: Repro R4: with `closed_state: Resolved`, issue-close asks az for `--state Resolved`, then `forge:issue-state 7` and `tracker:of AB#7 state` of a Resolved item both print OPEN. tests/forge-ado.bats:179 sets `Done`, one of the three, so it cannot see this.
findings.fix: Keep one list of closing states, the three defaults plus the two settings, and pass it to ado_closed, the WIQL, and tracker/ado:state. Say so in docs/trackers.md:83.

findings.title: GitLab counts unresolved notes, where GitHub and Azure DevOps count threads
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow finding 8), still open: `unresolved` counts every resolvable, unresolved note of every discussion, not discussions.
findings.evidence: Repro R1: one discussion with three notes gives `unresolved=3`. tests/forge-conformance.bats:190 has one note a discussion, so it passes.
findings.fix: Count discussions with `any(.notes[]?; .resolvable and (.resolved | not))`, and add a three-note thread to the fixture.

findings.title: Azure DevOps builds and artifacts are the whole project's, other repositories' among them
findings.claim: forge/ado:runs and forge/ado:artifacts read `az pipelines runs list --project` and never look at a run's repository, so a project with several repositories shows a neighbour's builds as this repository's. GitHub and GitLab answer for the one repository.
findings.evidence: Repro R10: runs of repositories billing and example, asked from example, print `[[41,"billing-ci","failed"],[40,"example-ci","passed"]]`. ado_deployments already compares `$run.repository.name`, so the field is known.
findings.fix: Keep only runs whose repository.name is the repository's, in ado_builds and before the artifacts loop, reading more than 50 to fill 20.

findings.title: Assigning on Azure DevOps replaces the assignee, while kit says it adds one
findings.claim: A work item has one assignee and `--assigned-to` overwrites it, so kit work and kit assign --to take a work item from a colleague while saying they share it. On GitHub and GitLab the same call adds.
findings.evidence: Repro R15: issue:assign "#7" on an item assigned to bob prints "#7 is already assigned to bob; adding you as well. Coordinate before continuing." and then runs `boards work-item update --id 7 --assigned-to ada`.
findings.fix: Let a tracker say it holds one assignee, and have issue:assign say it takes the item from bob there, or refuse without a flag.

findings.title: A web tracker's issue in a change's body fails kit settle, and kit linked names a remedy that cannot work
findings.claim: tracker/web:state always refuses, and both callers take the refusal for a read that failed. A merged change whose body says `Closes LIN#12`, the line kit work writes for a secondary issue, makes kit settle exit 1 in the delivered CI at every such merge.
findings.evidence: Repro R16: `kit settle 3` exits 1 with "LIN#12 could not be closed: its state could not be read"; `kit linked 3` exits 1 with "run: … kit linked again once the tracker answers", which a web tracker never will.
findings.fix: Give the tracker seam the forge seam's unsupported answer (return 3) for a call a provider cannot make. issue:settle then skips the issue naming its page, and kit linked says the tracker cannot be read.

findings.title: tracker/ado.sh answers four calls worse than forge/ado.sh answers the same ones
findings.claim: create drops its body (kit gather loses the task lines when `#` is an ado record), prints `null` with exit 0 for an answer with no id, unassign exits 0 when the read of the assignees failed, and assign, comment, and close exit 127 silently with no az on PATH. The last is known since 11-10 (Flow finding 26), still open.
findings.evidence: Repro R6: `tracker:at '#' create Parent <body>` runs `boards work-item create --title Parent --type Task --project Claims --org …` with no --description; an id-less answer gives `status=0 output=null`; unassign after a failed show gives status=0. Repro R12: assign and comment give status=127 and no output.
findings.fix: Pass `--description "${2:-}"`, check `.id | numbers`, `|| return 1` on the read, and guard:require tool:az in every call. Better, share one implementation with forge/ado.sh (B5-17).

findings.title: A personal access token signs az devops in, but not forge/ado:me, so require fails on a runner
findings.claim: forge/ado:me and forge/ado:require read `az account show`, the Azure account, which a login by AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT alone does not have, so every verb that starts with forge:require stops with "run: az login" on an Azure Pipelines job although each az repos and az boards call would work. Every other az failure names az login too.
findings.evidence: docs/integrations/az.md:4 names both sign-ins: "`az login`, or a personal access token in `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT`"; the provider reads SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_PULLREQUESTID, so it means to run there. Settle it with `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT=… az account show` where az login never ran.
findings.fix: When the token is set, read the caller from the Azure DevOps profile or connection data through az devops invoke, and name `az devops login` in the remedy.

findings.title: Azure DevOps iterations need a team that kit passes only when a setting names it
findings.claim:
forge/ado:iterations runs `az boards iteration team list --project

` with no --team unless forge_settings.ado.team is set, and the extension declares --team required for that command. Without the setting az fails on usage and kit says "run: az login (the iterations could not be read)".
findings.evidence: The code's comment says az "takes" the default team when it is not named; the fake at tests/forge-ado.bats:112 answers the call without --team, so the test passes. Settle it with `az boards iteration team list --help`.
findings.fix: With no team set, read the project's default team (`az devops project show` gives defaultTeam) and pass it.

findings.title: The open changes cost five glab processes or three az processes each, one after another
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 for GitLab (Flow finding 17), still open, and now true of Azure DevOps: GitLab makes 2 + 5N glab calls and ADO pages + 3N az calls, each preceded by two runs of forge/ado:place, where GitHub asks once per 100. A snapshot is good for 60 seconds from when its read began, so a longer read is stale when kept and every stage reads again.
findings.evidence: 30 open changes are 152 glab processes or 91 az processes by the loops at the lines named; forge_snapshot_seconds=60 at kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:278. Timings were not measured here.
findings.fix: Read GitLab's merge requests with pipelines, discussions, and approvals through GraphQL, one request a page. For ADO read threads and policies in parallel, or only for the changes a stage draws.

findings.title: A GitLab job allowed to fail fails the gate, and a review that asks for changes blocks nothing
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow finding 9), still open: gitlab_runs ignores allow_failure, approval is only `not_approved`, and a GitLab reviewer is never `changes`. GitHub's CHANGES_REQUESTED is blocked:approval.
findings.evidence: jq run: a failed job with `allow_failure: true` beside a passed one gives `{"state":"FAILURE","failing":"lint"}`; gitlab_pr with `detailed_merge_status: "requested_changes"` gives `state: "ready"` and the reviewer `requested`.
findings.fix: Count a job that is failed and allow_failure as passed, add requested_changes to approval, and read each reviewer's state from merge_requests/<n>/reviewers.

findings.title: GitLab takes a branch name, a remote URL, and an issue title into a URL or a branch as they come
findings.claim: The branch is put in the query unencoded and the project path is wrong for several spellings of the remote (both known since 11-10, Flow findings 21 and 22, still open); repo-url uses the ssh host as the web host; a title with no ASCII letter or digit makes link-branch create the branch `7-`. GitHub and ADO pass the branch as an argument.
findings.evidence: Repro R2: glab is asked `merge_requests?state=opened&source_branch=feat/c++&state=merged#x`. Repro R3: `gitlab.com:empowerite/example.git` gives repo `gitlab.com:empowerite/example`, a trailing slash `empowerite/example/`; R11: `--raw-field branch=7-`.
findings.fix: @uri the branch, parse the remote's URL once as forge/ado:place does and refuse what it cannot read, and fall back to `<iid>-issue` for an empty slug.

findings.title: forge/ado:place misreads three forms of the remote's URL
findings.claim: forge/ado:decode turns each %XX into a code point of its own, so a non-ASCII project name is mangled in every --project; a URL with no project segment reads the organization as the project; a trailing slash is refused.
findings.evidence: Repro R5: `…/acme/Caf%C3%A9/_git/example` gives repo `CafÃ©/example`; `https://dev.azure.com/acme/_git/example` is accepted with organization https://dev.azure.com and project acme; a trailing slash gives "names no Azure DevOps repository".
findings.fix: Decode bytes (jq 1.8's @urid), take the repository's name as the project when the path has none, and strip a trailing slash.

findings.title: The closing-keyword pattern is written three times, with no word boundary, and one bad number fails the read
findings.claim: "prefix AB#12" and "prefix #7" match as `fix …`, so kit linked can pass on a change that links nothing under the closing-issues stand-in; a prefix with `&` is mangled by sed; the stand-in fails whole on a number the forge does not have. On an ADO forge `Closes AB#7` is read by neither the stand-in nor tracker:body-refs.
findings.evidence: Repro R7: body-refs of "This adds a prefix AB#12 to the parser.\nCloses R&D#5" prints `AB#12 RD#5`. Repro R8: "adds a prefix #7" gives `7 OPEN team/example`; `Closes #7` with `Fixes #99999` gives status 1 after printing the first line.
findings.fix: One function gives the pattern, with a non-alphanumeric or line start before the keyword; print the prefix with printf; skip an issue the forge says it lacks.

findings.title: The marks stand-in accepts every: 60.5 and then fails in bash arithmetic
findings.claim: Validation takes any number of 10 or more; the use divides in `$(( ))`, which takes integers only.
findings.evidence: Repro R9: `marks: {every: 60.5}` gives exit 1 and "forge.sh: line 721: 1794486168 / 60.5 : arithmetic syntax error: invalid arithmetic operator".
findings.fix: Require a whole number in the check, or divide in jq.

findings.title: The Azure DevOps work item calls exist twice, and three more things are copied where one would do
findings.claim: tracker/ado.sh and forge/ado.sh's issue calls are the same ten calls on the same az commands written apart, and B5-3, B5-6, and B5-8 are their drift. Also copied: the GraphQL cursor loop three times in gitlab.sh (lines 307, 707, 740), the `40[34]` stderr test four times (97, 180, 574, 766), the title slug (gitlab.sh:196, issue.sh:380), and tracker/forge.sh chooses GitLab's issue URLs by `if provider == gitlab` beside an issue-url hook only ADO uses.
findings.evidence: grep shows the closing states in forge.jq:448, forge/ado.sh:298, and tracker/ado.sh:83; milestones pages with `--field`, members and vulnerabilities with `--raw-field`.
findings.fix: One set of work item functions taking organization, project, and settings, used by both seams; one cursor-loop helper; give all three providers the issue-url and issue-new-url hooks.

findings.title: GitLab's writes let glab find the project, while its reads name the primary's
findings.claim: Reads go through forge/gitlab:api with `projects/<primary's path>`, but nine writes run `glab issue …` and `glab mr …` with no --repo, so where primary in kit.yml is not the remote glab picks kit reads issue 7 of one project and changes issue 7 of another. ADO's header states the rule ("never lets az detect them from git"); GitHub has the same gap (11-10, filed issues #68 and #50).
findings.evidence: issue-assign is `glab issue update "$1" --assignee "+$2"`, pr-create `glab mr create …`, with no project named. Settle it in a checkout with two GitLab remotes and `primary: upstream`.
findings.fix: Pass `--repo "$(forge/gitlab:project)"` to every glab issue and glab mr call.

findings.title: Smaller differences in what GitLab answers: no merge commit, a 404 read as off, group milestones, the milestones mark
findings.claim: A fast-forward merge has no merge_commit_sha, so pr-state gives an empty hash and kit settle writes "merged as : <url>"; iterations answers 3 for any 404, which is also a project the login cannot see. Plausible only: milestones reads the project's own while issues carry group milestones, and the milestones mark asks a `sort` GitLab's milestones API does not document.
findings.evidence: Repro R13: pr-state prints `MERGED\t` with nothing after the tab. Repro R14: a "404 Project Not Found" on iterations gives status 3 and no line; the last two need GitLab's API reference to settle.
findings.fix: Fall back to `.sha` for the merge commit; check the project is readable before taking a 404 for a missing feature; ask milestones with includeAncestors; compute the milestones mark from the list itself.

findings.title: Azure DevOps reads a pull request or a work item by a number that is the organization's, not the repository's
findings.claim: `az repos pr show --id` and `az boards work-item show --id` take no project, so kit settle or kit close of a number acts on that pull request or work item in any project the login reaches, where GitHub and GitLab say the repository has none. pr-closing-issues names every linked work item this repository's, whatever project it is in, and kit linked counts it.
findings.evidence: The calls carry only --org; pr-closing-issues prints `\(.id) … \($repo)` for each linked item without reading System.TeamProject. Azure DevOps ids being organization-wide was not checked live.
findings.fix: Compare a pull request's repository and project, and a work item's System.TeamProject, with the primary's, and refuse or name the other project.

findings.title: What the three in-scope test files cannot see
findings.claim: All 41 tests pass and none fails for B5-1 to B5-10: the closed-state test uses `Done`, the iterations fake answers with no --team, create is never given a body, the discussions fixture has one note a thread. No test runs kit work, kit linked, or kit settle on a GitLab or Azure DevOps forge.
findings.evidence: `bats tests/forge-ado.bats tests/forge-stand-ins.bats tests/tracker.bats` gives 41 ok; the 16 reproductions in out/B5/b5-repro.bats show the defects against the same fakes.
findings.fix: Add the reproductions' cases as tests, and one kit work, linked, and settle run on each forge against the fakes.

areas.title: flow, the apps, and workspaces
areas.coverage: Read whole: every bash, jq, and bin file of the scope, plus 1st.sh and the loader's option loop. Tests sampled, not read whole. Ran the eleven bats files (206 of 213 pass; 7 need projects/tui, not copied), shellcheck (clean), and fourteen reproductions. Not read: kittui Go, forge providers, issues.sh, changes.sh.
areas.summary: 15 findings: 1 high, 6 medium, 8 low; 13 reproduced. The high one: --jq after kit --workspace= drops the workspace and prints another answer with exit 0, for every verb here. Medium: a first fetch drawn as branches pruned; three marks that do not move when their stage does; above desks --json leaving out a failed desk; a cross-repository close hiding a local issue; duplicate keys on incoming's tracking rows; three member names for one Azure DevOps repository. B6-2, B6-5, B6-12 are known since 11-10, still open. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write of a report file, so the full text is in this result alone.
strengths: list:read carries a command's exit through a process substitution, and the scope uses it for every list git or yq gives, so a failed read is not an empty list.

A stage read in part is printed and then fails with the member or stage named: across:merge, across:cut, apps:across, flow:picture, kit-workspace. Above desks now exits 1 too (11-10 Flow 14 is fixed).
The workspace file's lock: ln -s to take it, a rename aside before a stale one is removed, a wait by the clock, removal only by the process it names. Twelve edits at once all land.
Values reach yq through strenv, never in the expression's text, and a remote's name from kit.yml is checked before git sees it.
workspaces:check runs before every read over a workspace and names what is wrong (11-10 Serve 8, 10, 11, 12, 19, 20, 27 are fixed).
Paths with spaces, a detached desk, a detached worktree, a worktree whose directory is gone, and a repository with no commit all draw correctly.
The glyphs are one table, glyphs.json, from which the bash declarations and both legends are generated.
The app verbs are one runner, apps:main, and a module of declarations each: a new stage is one function and one array entry.
The suite is broad, 213 tests over the scope, and isolates HOME, the cache, and git's configuration; shellcheck is clean.

findings.title: --jq after kit --workspace= drops the workspace, and prints another answer with exit 0
findings.claim: guard:jq runs the verb again as `kit <verb> … --json | jq .` with no --workspace=, and the loader sets KIT_WORKSPACE from the option alone, so the second call has no workspace. Every verb of the scope takes --jq, and no test runs it with --workspace=.
findings.evidence: In a member of group team: `kit --workspace=team workspace remotes --json | jq -c '[.rows[]|.member]'` gives ["github.com/o/a","github.com/o/b"], the same with --jq gives [null] (this repository alone, exit 0). Outside a repository the --jq form exits 2 with 'kit workspace reads a repository', and `flow desk --jq` prints the bare desk object, not {rows, errors}.
findings.fix: Have guard:jq hand the workspace on, `${KIT_WORKSPACE:+--workspace=${KIT_WORKSPACE}}` before the verb, and pin --jq to --json's document in across.bats. The --jq branches in across:flow, across:start, apps:shown, kit-workspace, and kit-workspaces are unreachable and can then go.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced on a fresh copy (out/B6/verify-1/repro.sh). In member a of group team: --json lists both members; --jq gives [null], this repository alone, exit 0. Outside a repository --jq exits 2. flow desk --jq prints the bare desk object; workspaces --current --jq answers "repository", not the group. guard:jq (1st.sh:655) re-execs bin/kit without --workspace=; no test covers it.

findings.title: The first fetch of a remote is drawn as its branches pruned
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow 7), still open. flow:fetch-diff's awk `NR == FNR` is true for every line of the second file when the 'before' snapshot is empty, so each new ref is printed as gone; that is any remote never fetched in a repository with no tag.
findings.evidence: After git init and git remote add origin: `kit flow incoming` prints '🛬 fetched 2 branches pruned', and --json gives branches {"new":[],"updated":[],"gone":["main","feature"]} with two rows of change gone. git branch -r lists both as fetched.
findings.fix: Tell the files apart by `FILENAME == ARGV[1]`, or pass the snapshots as awk variables. Add a first-fetch test to incoming.bats.

findings.title: Three marks do not move when what their stage draws does
findings.claim: kit flow's desk and worktrees marks hash git status, which names a changed path but not its content, while the stage draws +added -removed; kit workspace's worktrees mark leaves out the default branch its base column counts against. By reading, kit flow's issues mark is the forge's alone though its rows draw here, local, worktree, and the claiming branch.
findings.evidence: Appending to an already dirty file: marks stay {"desk":"3122744016","worktrees":"818440553"} while desk added goes 1 to 3. A fetch that moves origin/main changes workspace worktrees base from [0,0] to [0,1] and leaves the mark 26274dde… unchanged.
findings.fix: Add `git diff --numstat <fork or HEAD>` to what marks:status sums, and the base ref's commit to workspace's worktrees mark. Join the worktrees mark and marks:refs into the issues mark.

findings.title: Above desks, --json leaves out a desk whose kit flow printed nothing
findings.claim: flow:above's fallback to {path, status: null} never runs for an empty output file, since jq given an empty file prints nothing and exits 0. The array kit-flow's header says holds one {path, status} per desk is then short, and does not say which desk failed.
findings.evidence: Two desks, b with `flow: [nope]` in kit.yml: `kit flow --json --no-fetch | jq -c 'map(.path)'` prints ["a"], exit 1. `jq -c --arg path b '{path: $path, status: .}' empty.json` prints nothing and exits 0.
findings.fix: Test `[[ -s "${scratch}/${index}.out" ]]` before the first jq, else print the null row.

findings.title: A change that closes another repository's issue hides the local issue of the same number
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow 5), still open. backlog::unclaimed matches closes on the number alone, issues::rows then gives the other repository's issue the local one's milestone, and changes::concerning has the same match.
findings.evidence: jq run with open issue 5 'local five' (milestone M1) and a change closing o/other#5 gives only [{"number":5,"title":"OTHER repo five","status":"underway","repository":"other","milestone":"M1"}]. 'local five' is in neither backlog nor underway.
findings.fix: Match on source, organization, repository, and number in all three; the documents already carry them.

findings.title: Two local branches on one upstream give incoming two rows with one key
findings.claim: A tracking row's key is remote, kind, and the upstream's branch, but there is one row per local branch, and `git switch -c x origin/main` sets origin/main as upstream by default. By reading, workspace::branches keys two local branches on one gone upstream alike.
findings.evidence: With main and 7-fix both tracking origin/main and one commit behind: {"key":"origin tracking main","local":["7-fix"],"behind":1} and {"key":"origin tracking main","local":["main"],"behind":1}.
findings.fix: Key a tracking row, and a gone row, by its local branch.

findings.title: One Azure DevOps repository has three member names, and its organization holds _git or v3
findings.claim: workspaces:url-member keeps the URL's whole path, which is one name for GitHub and GitLab over https and ssh but three for Azure DevOps' three URL forms. A group listing the https name shows an ssh clone as not cloned, and forge::place cuts every app row's organization from that path.
findings.evidence: The same repository by each URL: dev.azure.com/org/proj/_git/repo (organization 'org/proj/_git'), ssh.dev.azure.com/v3/org/proj/repo ('v3/org/proj'), org.visualstudio.com/proj/_git/repo ('proj/_git'). docs/workspaces.md does not mention Azure DevOps.
findings.fix: For a host forge:of calls ado, spell the member dev.azure.com/<organization>/<project>/<repository> from any form, as forge/ado.sh:559 already parses them, and have place give organization and project.

findings.title: --add of a member the group excludes says it was added, and writes it twice
findings.claim: --add compares the members given with workspaces:fixed, which leaves the excluded out, so an excluded member is appended to repos again and stays excluded. Only a hand-edited file has exclude, as no form writes it.
findings.evidence: With repos and exclude both [github.com/o/a]: `kit workspaces --add=team github.com/o/a` prints '→ 📚 team: added github.com/o/a', exit 0; --show gives members [], and repos now holds the entry twice.
findings.fix: Compare with the group's repos entries, and for a member under exclude either take it out of exclude or refuse, naming the key.

findings.title: --use with a folder says the repository is kept when it could not be, and exits 0
findings.claim: workspaces:recall says its failure through workspaces:unwritable, then goes on to print the desk and return 0, though its header says it returns 1. The caller's `|| exit 1` never runs.
findings.evidence: With cache/kit/workspaces/recent a directory: the ❌ 'could not be written there' line is followed by '→ 📘 …/d is among the recent repositories', exit 0.
findings.fix: Return 1 after workspaces:unwritable, and write recent through file:replace.

findings.title: kit workspaces takes -- for a repository
findings.claim: The first loop, workspaces:misplaced, and guard:arguments all honour --, but the second loop files it under args. The same loop also splits any later word that starts -- and holds =.
findings.evidence: `kit workspaces --add team -- github.com/o/c` prints "❌ '--' names no repository; write host/owner/repo, a git URL, or a checkout's directory", exit 2.
findings.fix: On --, append the rest to args and stop, as the first loop does.

findings.title: An uncommitted path with a space, and a rename, are drawn as git quotes them
findings.claim: flow::checkout cuts `git status --porcelain` at column 3, but git quotes a path that holds a space and writes a rename as `old -> new`. The quotes, or both names, land in changes[].path of the JSON.
findings.evidence: A worktree with an untracked 'new file.txt' draws `?? "new file.txt"` under kit flow worktrees.
findings.fix: Read `git status --porcelain -z`, which quotes nothing and gives a rename's two paths apart.

findings.title: The checks cell's test pins a count where the forge gives a name
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow 25), still open. The test feeds `failing: 2` and expects '❌ 2 failing 3 / 5 31s', but forge::checks sets failing to the first failed check's name.
findings.evidence: kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:83: `([$latest[] | select(.verdict == "failed") | .name] | first // "") as $failing`; the test's title is 'a failed checks cell names the failing count'.
findings.fix: Feed the test a name, and word flow:check-cell's header as what it draws.

findings.title: The seven stages, and which of them print an object, are spelled out in a dozen places
findings.claim: settings_stages is the list, yet the names are written again in flow:stage-purpose, flow:stage, flow:asks-forge, flow:picture (three cases), flow:render, across:flow, and marks:stages, and 'desk, worktrees, incoming print an object' in across:stage and across:picture. A stage added to one and not another fails without a word.
findings.fix: One table, stage to {purpose, forge or local, array or object, render, draw, mark}, read by all of them; glyphs.json already holds a row per stage and could carry it.

findings.title: Four pieces of logic are copied, and five --jq branches are dead
findings.claim: The kittui hand-off is written five times with hand-kept lists of the forms that stay in text, which differ; 'the last line a read said, less its ❌' five times; a list-to-JSON helper three times. workspaces.sh calls five forge: functions but does not `use forge`, which arrives only through git.sh.
findings.evidence: Hand-off: kit-flow:304, 319, 392, apps.sh:52, kit-workspace:178. Last line: across.sh:96, apps/platform.sh:134, apps/audit.sh:60, 107, 186; workspaces.sh:16 against :824.
findings.fix: One tui:hand-off, one out:last-line, one list helper, `use forge` in workspaces.sh, and the unreachable --jq branches removed with B6-1's fix.

findings.title: Three headers say what the code does not
findings.claim: people.sh says the forge's marks call reads every kind at once for every app, where marks.sh:15 and apps:forge-mark read only the kinds a stage asks for. kit-workspace's header says --json and --jq print the stages as text, and kit-audit:29 is 143 columns wide.
findings.evidence: kit-workspace:28-29: 'Without one, or with --text, --json, or --jq, it prints the stages as text.' apps.sh:327: 'Each kind is read once a process, and only those a stage asks for'.
findings.fix: Correct the three lines.

areas.title: policy, serve, tools, toolchains, dependencies
areas.coverage: Read whole: policy.sh, serve.sh, toolchain.sh, dependencies.sh, all providers, serve.jq, toolchain.jq, kit-policy, kit-serve, kit-tools, kit-toolchains, both Rego files, the serve, policy and toolchains docs. Sampled the callers. Ran 174 bats tests (all pass), shellcheck (clean), and hand reproductions offline. Not run: real mise, nix, brew, docker, uv, Linux.
areas.summary: 26 findings: 5 high, 11 medium, 10 low; 20 reproduced. Worst: kit policy runs opa, jq and yq from PATH directories the branch fills, so the base-policy guarantee can be bypassed; kit commit reads tracked Rego from the disk and drops data files and subdirectories. Five documented guarantees were contradicted by a reproduction (B7-1, 2, 6, 7, 10). Nine 11-10 findings are still open. Of the 17 serve tools, 14 match the documents; packages, tools and work do not, and syntax offers a mode it cannot serve. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused a report file, and I did not work around it, so the answers table exists only in this summary.
strengths: serve's path guard (serve:inside, serve:resolves-inside) held against every case tried: a link out, a link in followed by .., an absolute path inside the root, a path with spaces, /etc/hosts, a sibling repository.

The 11-10 serve findings that could kill or fool the server are fixed: a NUL anywhere is refused, a non-object params is refused, results and requests travel by file and stdin, an operand off its enum or equal to a word that acts is refused, and flow incoming is given --no-fetch.
Stdout carried only protocol lines in every run, and each message left one log line with its outcome.

policy:from-base, policy:base-held and policy:runner-base do what the header says on GitHub and GitLab: a branch that blanks a pattern, edits the base's Rego or redefines a kind is judged by the base, and a runner whose event names no base fails.
Every engine failure fails closed: a missing opa, Rego with no deny, a failing jq or sort (PIPESTATUS checked in policy:deny and policy:warn).
The kit toolchain refuses to lock on a runner, unpacks apart and moves into place only once bin holds the command, and keeps path and active to tools.lock alone.
kit tools install now finds the dependency providers again after the toolchain installs, and brew filling in no longer swallows a failed read (11-10 Command line 2 and 8, fixed).
shellcheck -x is clean over the scope, and all 174 tests of the seven bats files pass.
No :choices function among the thirteen modules that have one asks the forge, so the syntax tool's read-only hint holds on that point.

findings.title: The engine and tools that judge a branch come from directories the branch fills
findings.claim: kit policy judges a branch by its base's settings and Rego, but runs opa, jq and yq from a PATH it first prepends with the branch's toolchain directories, node_modules/.bin and .venv/bin. The delivered workflow runs kit tools install from the branch's files before kit ci, so 'A branch cannot loosen the rule that judges it' and 'The two judgements come before any command of the branch's own runs' do not hold.
findings.evidence: Base rule refuses everything and kit policy on the branch prints '❌ own.rego refuses every commit'; after package.json, package-lock.json and an executable node_modules/.bin/opa printing an empty result exist, it prints '✅ the opa policy allows the branch, 2 commit(s), the tree'. The runner path (npm ci, tools.lock pinning opa, jq, yq, gh) is read from kit-ci.yml, not run.
findings.fix: For the two judgements, do not put node_modules/.bin or .venv/bin first, and resolve the engine as the base pins it (tools.lock at the base against the installed .kit-sha256), or refuse when the files that pin the judging tools differ from the base's. Say in both documents what the guarantee does not cover.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced from committed files only: branch commits package.json, package-lock.json and a file: package whose bin is opa. Fresh clone: kit policy refuses; after kit tools install (npm ci) it prints 'the opa policy allows the branch'. No guard between kit-policy:64 and opa.sh:30. The GitHub runner itself was not run.

findings.title: kit commit judges by the disk's .kit/policy/, without its data files and subdirectories
findings.claim: policy:from copies only top-level .kit/policy/*.rego, reads from the index only a link into the repository, and copies every other file from the disk. So a file git tracks directly under .kit/policy/ is judged as the disk has it, and a data file or subdirectory is left out, though tests/policy.bats:577 uses that layout for kit policy.
findings.evidence: A staged tracked own.rego that refuses everything stops kit commit; emptied on the disk without staging (' M .kit/policy/own.rego'), kit commit prints '✅ committed 4979e1c'. A tracked rule reading data.max_files from .kit/policy/limits.json refuses under 'opa eval --data .kit/policy' and kit commit commits.
findings.fix: Build the commit's Rego with the reader the base uses (policy:base-held, given the index as its tree), then add what the release delivers.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a worktree. Tracked own.rego refusing everything stops kit commit; emptied on disk, unstaged, the commit lands. A staged rule reading data.max_files from staged limits.json refuses under opa eval --data .kit/policy, yet kit commit commits. tests/commit.bats:544,557 cover only kit.yml.

findings.title: kit tools run <command> still takes the command's flags for its own
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line 1), still open: a command that holds one of kit tools' own flags is refused or loses the flag, and only 'run -- <command>' works. The header says '<command>… as typed, dash-words included' and, two lines above, 'kit takes it even after run's command'.
findings.evidence: 'kit tools run echo --check .' prints '❌ kit tools needs --outdated', exit 2; '… echo --json' prints "❌ unknown argument 'run'"; '… echo -h' prints kit's page. 'kit tools run echo --toolchain ambient x' prints 'x'.
findings.fix: Once the literal run is seen, give every later word to the command. Drop the sentence that contradicts it.
findings.verdict_note: All outputs reproduced: --check gives 'needs --outdated' exit 2; --json, --jq, --outdated give "unknown argument 'run'"; -h and --help print kit's page. 'run -- echo --check .' works; --foo and -l pass through. --toolchain after the command is deliberate (tests/tools.bats:108). All but -h fail loudly.

findings.title: A uv.lock of ordinary size makes kit tools fail
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line 3), still open: the whole lock, as JSON, is passed to jq as one --argjson argument.
findings.evidence: A generated lock of 400 packages with 12 wheels each (1,460,404 bytes) gives 'uv.sh: line 36: …/jq: Argument list too long', then '❌ uv: the pinned tools could not be read', on macOS (ARG_MAX 1,048,576). Linux's 128 KiB cap on one argument was not run.
findings.fix: Feed the lock to jq with --slurpfile or on stdin.
findings.verdict_note: Mechanism real (uv.sh:36, one --argjson argument). On this Mac a 417 KB lock (100 packages, 12 wheels each) lists fine; a 1.04 MB lock fails with 'Argument list too long'. So 'ordinary size' does not hold on macOS; it rests on Linux's 128 KiB per-argument cap, which was not run.

findings.title: Every package in uv.lock is expected in .venv, a marker's exclusions included
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line 4), still open: the filter is unchanged, so a package the lock holds for another platform, as colorama for win32, lists as missing and dependencies:installed uv never succeeds.
findings.evidence: Read from the code: 'select(.source.virtual == null and .source.editable == null)' is the only filter. Not rerun with a real uv; kit tools in a project that depends on click settles it.
findings.fix: Judge with 'uv sync --frozen --check', or compare only what uv resolves for this platform.
findings.verdict_note: Run with real uv 0.13.7 offline on hand-made wheels: clicky requires coloramy only on win32. After uv lock and uv sync --frozen, kit tools prints '❌ coloramy · 0.4.6' and dependencies:installed uv fails. Effect: a lasting ❌ row and a welcome check (welcome.sh:319) that never holds; kit tools exits 0.

findings.title: kit serve exits, unanswered, when a watched file changes while kit.yml cannot be placed
findings.claim: serve:reload execs kit-serve when a file under the release's bin/ or modules/ changed, and the new process hydrates under errexit before reading anything. A kit.yml that does not parse at that moment ends the server with the request unanswered, though docs/serve.md says every call is refused with -32603 until a placing succeeds.
findings.evidence: With kit.yml set to 'packages: [unclosed' a tools/call gets -32603 as documented; after 'touch kit/modules/bash/serve.sh' the next tools/call gets no answer in 15 s and the process is gone. $TMPDIR/kit.*/pending.* is left holding the line.
findings.fix: In a resumed process (kit_serve_pending set), make a failed first hydrate set serve_unplaced and go on serving, as serve:reload does.

findings.title: Rego held only in a subdirectory of .kit/policy/ is never judged
findings.claim: policy:engine picks opa only when a .rego file is at the top level of the policy directory, while the base reader and the documents count every file under it, 'in a subdirectory too'. With Rego in a subdirectory alone the patterns engine runs and the rule is skipped without a word.
findings.evidence: The default branch tracks only .kit/policy/sub/deny.rego, which refuses everything; kit policy on main and on a branch both print '✅ the patterns policy allows …'. kit policy --rules names patterns.
findings.fix: Look for a .rego file at any depth, as with find … -name '*.rego' -print -quit.

findings.title: On an Azure Pipelines pull request build kit policy judges no branch, commit, or title
findings.claim: policy:branch and policy:runner-base read GitHub's and GitLab's runner variables and none of Azure DevOps', though the ADO forge provider reads SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_PULLREQUESTID for the same run. A pipeline's detached HEAD therefore has no branch: nothing past the default is judged, and the tree is judged by the checkout's own policy.
findings.evidence: A branch whose commit 'no issue reference at all' and whose base rule both refuse at a desk reports neither after 'git checkout --detach' with TF_BUILD and the SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_* variables set. Only the branch's own tree rule is reported.
findings.fix: Read SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCEBRANCH and the target's tip as the GitLab path does. On any runner, refuse a detached HEAD that names no change rather than pass it.

findings.title: Ambient kit tools runs with the repository root first on PATH
findings.claim: PATH="$(toolchain:path | paste …):${PATH}" starts with an empty element when no dependency provider is usable, the ordinary ambient case, and an empty element is the working directory. An executable at the repository's root named as a command kit runs is run, by kit tools and by the MCP tools tool.
findings.evidence: In a fresh kit install repository, an executable ./shellcheck makes kit tools print '✅ shellcheck · ./shellcheck'. With an executable ./yq and a cold YAML cache, that ./yq ran 8 times.
findings.fix: Join the directories first, then PATH="${dirs:+${dirs}:}${PATH}", as toolchain:run does.

findings.title: A cached download is installed without its bytes being hashed
findings.claim: toolchain/kit:fetch returns as soon as a file named by the wanted digest is in the cache, and the download reaches the cache by mv from TMPDIR, a copy across filesystems. A short or altered cache file is installed and stamped with the lock's digest, against 'A download whose bytes have another digest … is refused'.
findings.evidence: After overwriting ~/.cache/kit/downloads/<sha256> and removing the installed tool, kit tools install prints '→ hello: 1.0 installed' and kit tools run hello prints TAMPERED. .kit-sha256 holds the lock's digest while the file's is another.
findings.fix: Hash the cached file before using it. Write it to a temporary in the cache directory, then rename.

findings.title: kit tools update moves a pin down, and a failed install leaves kit.yml moved without its lock
findings.claim: toolchain/kit:outdated calls any pin that differs from the source's latest 'behind', and update writes that latest into kit.yml before it locks. A pin newer than latest, as a release candidate or Node's current line against the LTS, is moved down, and a failed download leaves kit.yml changed with tools.lock as it was.
findings.evidence: With a fake gh answering v1.5.0 and a failing curl, kit tools --outdated lists 'thing 2.0.0-rc1 … 1.5.0' and 'other 3.1.0 … 1.5.0' as behind. kit tools update rewrites both versions to 1.5.0, fails at the download, and exits non-zero.
findings.fix: Compare with a version sort and report only a newer latest. Lock into a copy and replace kit.yml and tools.lock together once every tool locked.

findings.title: kit toolchains use brew is refused where brew is the only project toolchain
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line 6), still open under the verb's new name: with a Brewfile and nothing else, choosing brew is refused, and after 'use ambient' no command leads back. With two others usable the names are not joined.
findings.evidence: '❌ brew fills in for the tools brew does not pin; choose brew', exit 1. With mise and docker usable: 'mise docker does not pin; choose mise docker'.
findings.fix: Refuse only when usable does not hold brew. Join the names with a loop.

findings.title: kit toolchains use <name> reports success while an active toolchain overrides it
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line 7), still open: the choice is recorded and reported as in use while an active toolchain goes on winning.
findings.evidence: With MISE_SHELL set, mise.toml and toolchain.Dockerfile, 'kit toolchains use docker' prints '✅ kit uses docker for the project'. The next kit toolchains pins mise.
findings.fix: Say that the active one wins until its shell is left, or refuse.

findings.title: The packages tool refuses a package that came into reach after the server built its schema
findings.claim: serve_specs and serve_opts, the closed choices among them, are built once per process, and a changed kit.yml sends only notifications/resources/list_changed. A package made or added while the server runs is off the enum for as long as the server lives.
findings.evidence: After one packages call, .kit/packages/mine/package.yml is created and 'kit packages mine --json' in a shell lists it; even after 'kit packages add mine' the tool answers "package's value mine is not one of: agents/claude, …".
findings.fix: Drop serve_specs, serve_opts and serve_tool_list whenever the server places .kit/ again or .kit/packages/ changed, and send notifications/tools/list_changed then.

findings.title: work's annotations and the page understate what the tool does
findings.claim: work carries idempotentHint true and destructiveHint false, and docs/serve.md says the hint is true for all but gather; but the title argument creates an issue on every call, and kit work sweeps the desk's uncommitted work into the new worktree by a stash. A client that retries an idempotent call makes a second issue.
findings.evidence: The tool list the server printed shows work with idempotentHint true and a title property; kit-work's header says --title 'creates an issue with that title' and 'Uncommitted work on the desk is swept into the new worktree'. Not run against a forge.
findings.fix: Set idempotentHint false for work. Name the sweep, the start commit and the push where the page lists what work writes.

findings.title: A tool's verb has no deadline, and a cancellation is dropped
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Serve 6), still open: the call is a synchronous subshell and every notification returns at once, notifications/cancelled among them. One stalled gh call or linter blocks every later message, ping included.
findings.evidence: Read from the code; not run. A verb made to sleep settles it.
findings.fix: Run the verb under a deadline and answer isError when it passes; honor cancellation.

findings.title: The two engines still disagree on the same facts
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Workflow 20), still open: patterns counts bytes under a C locale where opa counts characters, and matches a missing pattern as the literal null.
findings.evidence: A title of 100 two-byte characters passes opa and patterns under UTF-8, and is refused by patterns under LC_ALL=C or LANG=C. A facts document without policy.branch gives "branch '7-x' does not match policy.branch: null" from patterns and [] from the Rego.
findings.fix: Read each pattern with // "", and match under a fixed UTF-8 locale.

findings.title: An invalid pattern in policy: is reported as a subject that does not match
findings.claim: An invalid regular expression fails closed but is never named as the fault: bash's own diagnostic leaks, then the subject is said not to match, once per commit for a commit rule.
findings.evidence: policy.branch '^(unclosed' prints 'patterns.sh: line 13: [[: invalid regular expression … parentheses not balanced', then "❌ branch '7-x' does not match policy.branch: ^(unclosed".
findings.fix: Try each pattern once in policy:rules (status 2 from =~) and refuse it by name.

findings.title: kit tools update takes the blank lines out of kit.yml
findings.claim: The version is written with yq --inplace, which drops the file's blank lines, where settings.sh rewrites packages: as text to keep them.
findings.evidence: The same yq expression over this repository's kit.yml with one version changed gives a diff of '11d10', '38d36' and the one intended line.
findings.fix: Replace the one version: line as text, or go through the settings writer.

findings.title: A tool whose URL kit cannot ask fails --outdated and update for good
findings.claim: Any URL outside GitHub releases, nodejs.org, go.dev and ftp.gnu.org makes kit tools --outdated, --check and update exit 1 on every run, with no key to say a tool is not asked. With gh on PATH but logged out, the GitHub branch fails rather than falling back to curl (that part plausible, not run).
findings.evidence: With a file:// URL: '❌ hello: kit cannot tell the latest version from …', then '❌ kit: could not tell whether every tool is behind', exit 1.
findings.fix: Add a per-tool 'latest: none', reported as a warning. Fall back to the public API when gh api fails.

findings.title: The syntax tool offers match and word, and refuses every word that is a flag
findings.claim: The operand rule that refuses a value starting with - also covers syntax's word, so the mode that judges a command line can judge none that holds a flag. The packages tool's package description likewise offers a glob the enum refuses.
findings.evidence: {"verb":["tools"],"match":true,"word":["--toolchain","--outdated"]} is refused with "word's value --toolchain starts with -". {"package":["style/*"]} is refused as 'not one of'.
findings.fix: Emit -- before an operand that runs to the end of the line and let its values start with -. Cut the glob from the description the tool shows.

findings.title: Smaller protocol edges that are still open
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Serve 16 and 24): a batch array is refused though the server offers 2025-03-26, which requires receiving batches; serve:resume withholds both list_changed notifications from a pending line that holds the text "initialize"; a deleted file is never a change.
findings.evidence: '[{…ping…}]' is answered '-32600 Invalid Request: a message is one JSON object' (run). The other two are read from serve.sh:299 and the find -type f -newer at serve.sh:220.
findings.fix: Answer a batch member by member or stop offering 2025-03-26. Test the parsed method, not the text.

findings.title: The headers' lists of toolchain names leave out kit
findings.claim: <name> is listed without kit in both headers, though kit is a project toolchain and the one this repository's CI names. house.rego's banner says kit/ holds only bin/, modules/ and packages/, and its rule allows libexec/ too.
findings.evidence: kit toolchains lists 'kit project'; 'kit tools --toolchain kit' and 'kit toolchains use kit' both ran. house.rego:36 has kit_dirs := {"bin", "libexec", "modules", "packages"}.
findings.fix: Print the names from toolchain:providers. Correct the banner.

findings.title: --toolchain <name> is one of the options that still takes its value as a separate word
findings.claim: kit policy, flow, facts, new and workspaces write --opt=<value>; kit tools --toolchain writes a space, with assign --to, close --duplicate-of, commit --message, gather --title, work --title and --pr, and syntax --choices. The space form is what lets an MCP value such as --outdated reach the verb as a word of its own.
findings.evidence: Usage lines read across kit/bin; '--toolchain=kit' and '--toolchain kit' both ran. The tools tool with {"toolchain":"--outdated"} ran 'kit tools --toolchain --outdated', which the guard read as a value.
findings.fix: Use one form in every usage line.

findings.title: Three system providers are one file three times, and three places build the same PATH
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/toolchain/apt.sh:1, kit/modules/bash/toolchain/dnf.sh:1, kit/modules/bash/toolchain/pacman.sh:1, kit/modules/bash/toolchain.sh:421, kit/modules/bash/dependencies.sh:109, kit/bin/kit-tools:152
findings.claim: apt.sh, dnf.sh and pacman.sh differ only in the command's name, the install words and the tool-to-package table. toolchain:path, dependencies:onto-path and kit-tools' locked-dirs each join the toolchain's directories and the providers' with small differences, and B7-9 is a fourth, wrong copy; serve.sh:81-138 keeps the tool tables by hand (known since 11-10, Serve 25).
findings.evidence: diff apt.sh dnf.sh and diff apt.sh pacman.sh show only names and the case table. Only toolchain:path adds brew filling in; only onto-path takes a provider whose tool is absent.
findings.fix: One system provider reading a table of command, install words and packages. One function that prints the directories, with flags for what to include.

findings.title: tests/dependencies.bats uses run --separate-stderr without the minimum version
findings.claim: dependencies.bats, toolchains.bats and house-policy.bats lack the bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0 their siblings have. No test covers B7-2, B7-7, B7-9, B7-10, B7-11 or B7-14.
findings.evidence: The run of the seven files passes 174 of 174 and ends with 'BW02: Using flags on run requires at least BATS_VERSION=1.5.0 … tests/dependencies.bats, line 234'.
findings.fix: Add the line, and a test per finding as it is fixed.

areas.title: terminals, welcome, tutorials, and the hand-off to kittui
areas.coverage: Read whole: terminal.sh, welcome.sh, tutorials.sh, tui.sh, ten readers, terminal.jq, terminals.json, kit-welcome, kit-tutorials, kit-tui, bin/tutorials, tutorials.yml, nine tutorial pages. Sampled: the five bats files, bin/kit, 1st.sh, kittui main.go and kit.go. Ran 129 tests (all pass) and reproduced each confirmed finding with fakes. Not read: welcome pages, projects/tutorials.
areas.summary: 19 findings: 1 high (plausible), 11 medium, 7 low. The high: nothing in the tree deploys the online tutorials' site that v0.1.0 links to. Confirmed by reproduction: kit tui drops --workspace; welcome has no Azure DevOps forge checks; a checkout path with a space freezes kittui's build digest; Windows Terminal's defaultProfile is never honoured; a failed reader leaves {config}/{profile} in a probe's fix; the TOML readers give false findings; --keep writes dead keeps. Four findings are known since 11-10 and still open (B8-5, B8-10, B8-12, B8-16). All 129 tests in scope pass in a copy. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from a subagent, and I did not work around it; everything is in this result.
strengths: One table, terminals.json, holds every terminal, finding, and probe; the ten readers share one contract (one JSON object, defaults filled, within a second), and kit never writes a terminal's settings.
terminal:bad turns a finding that reads a key its reader did not give into 'a bug in kit' in the heading, not a false finding, and a test compiles every bad.
terminal:timed stops a reader with its whole process tree, keeps its TMPDIR inside its own scratch, and holds no pipe open; the tests time it.
terminal:color matches colorprofile 0.4.3's envColorProfile line for line (compared with the library's source, the 'st' substring included).
The terminal is asked once, in the main shell, the answers travel in KIT_TERMINAL_PROBES, and a late answer is drained so it never lands in the shell.

welcome runs no fix but the one --fix names, marks a shell-only fix runs: false, judges folders in parallel and prints them in order, and with no yq still prints every check and names yq's site (run and seen).
list:read keeps a command's status where '< <(...)' would lose it; keeps are written through file:replace and leave the rest of the person's settings file as it was.
bin/tutorials refuses a page by file and reason, kit generate --check keeps the catalogue current, and a machine with no opener still gets the link.
The JSONC reader handles strings, both comment kinds, and trailing commas, with a test for half a megabyte.
All 129 tests in scope pass in a copy: terminal 60, tui 10, tutorials 16, tutorials-catalogue 9, welcome 34 (the last needs a TMPDIR other sessions do not clean).

findings.title: The online tutorials' site has no deploy in this tree, so a release's first tutorial may open a missing page
findings.claim: kit tutorials kit-tutorials, the first tutorial listed (order 1, for the newcomer), opens https://empowerite.github.io/kit/tutorials/<line>/kit-tutorials/?kit=<version>, line 0.1 for v0.1.0, and nothing in the tree publishes that site.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'tutorials|pages|Pages|deploy' .github/workflows/*.yml (kit-ci, release, retire-pre-releases) matches nothing and bin/ci only builds the site as a check, while projects/tutorials/README.md:10-11 says the lines are on this repository's GitHub Pages. No network here, so whether /kit/tutorials/0.1/ and /main/ are served is unseen; a curl -I of both settles it.
findings.fix: Add the site's deploy to release.yml (one build per line, TUTORIALS_BASE set) before v0.1.0, or ship the one online tutorial in the kit as the other nine are.
findings.verdict_note: Tree half holds: reproduced, a 0.1.0 kit builds https://empowerite.github.io/kit/tutorials/0.1/kit-tutorials/?kit=0.1.0; no workflow or bin script publishes; the publish plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-tutorials-2-published.md) has 33 steps, none ticked. Whether it 404s is unseen (no network). Narrower: one online tutorial of ten; nine ship in the kit, and the URL prints.

findings.title: kit --workspace=<w> with no verb, and kit --workspace=<w> tui ..., open kittui over the wrong workspace
findings.claim: kit-tui hands kittui its words alone, so the workspace is lost: kittui names the workspace on each read (kit.go:34 over) and bin/kit:399 empties KIT_WORKSPACE on every call without --workspace=. Every sibling passes it (kit-welcome:173, kit-flow:311,327, kit-workspace:185, apps.sh:57).
findings.evidence: With a fake kittui on a pty: 'kit --workspace=none welcome' runs 'kittui welcome --workspace=none', but 'kit --workspace=none' runs 'kittui', 'kit --workspace=none tui welcome' runs 'kittui welcome', and '... tui flow' runs 'kittui flow'. main.go:57 reads --workspace only for an app verb or welcome, never for no verb.
findings.fix: Have kit-tui add --workspace="${KIT_WORKSPACE}" after the verb, kittui read it for the empty verb too, and the guard's hand-off re-exec with --workspace=. Add the three cases to tests/tui.bats.

findings.title: A repository on Azure DevOps gets no forge check in kit welcome
findings.claim: welcome:forges keeps github and gitlab and drops every other forge ('(*) continue'), though forge:of answers ado and forge/ado.sh needs az, its azure-devops extension, and az login. The tool is chosen by '[[ forge == github ]] || tool=glab', a two-way table.
findings.evidence: In a repository with origin https://dev.azure.com/acme/shop/_git/web, kit welcome --checks --json gives tool-bash, tool-git, tool-jq, tool-yq, toolchain-system, repo-git, kit-installed, toolchain-project, all true. The same with a github.com remote adds forge-cli-github.com and forge-login-github.com.
findings.fix: Let each forge provider say its tool, login check, login command, and site as data that welcome:forge-cli and welcome:forge-login read. Add the ado rows: az on PATH, the extension, az account show.

findings.title: A kit checkout under a path with a space runs a stale kittui for good, after 498 lines of cat errors
findings.claim: tui:cached pipes find | sort | xargs cat, and xargs splits each path at the space, so no source is read: the digest covers 'go version' alone, the status is 0, and the cached binary never changes.
findings.evidence: In a copy at '.../sp ace/', tui:cached printed 498 lines such as 'cat: .../sp: No such file or directory' and kittui-c6f1c8d54aedc3af; after a line was added to cmd/kittui/main.go it printed the same name. Every verb that opens kittui prints those lines.
findings.fix: Use find -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z | xargs -0 cat, and fail the build when the digest's pipeline fails. Add the case to tests/tui.bats.

findings.title: The build's digest leaves out the seven JSON files kittui embeds, and nothing prunes the cache (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line, 12), still open. The digest reads *.go, go.mod, and go.sum, but kittui embeds terms.json, customize.json, clones.json, workspaces.json, fields.json, tutorials.json, and verbs.json with //go:embed.
findings.evidence: Appending a line to internal/palette/verbs.json left tui:cached at kittui-2d2ced2d40ac7f24, so an edit to a catalogue alone runs the old kittui. Each change to a Go file, a test file included, leaves one more binary under ~/.cache/kit/.
findings.fix: Digest every file the build reads, as go list's EmbedFiles names them, or everything under projects/tui but testdata and _test.go. Remove the other kittui-* builds once a new one is in place.

findings.title: A probe's fix prints {config} or {profile} as written when the terminal's reader failed
findings.claim: A probe's fix is filled from the reader's object, and an unreadable terminal gives none, so the braces stay. The WezTerm case is ordinary on macOS: its reader runs wezterm from PATH only, where Ghostty's uses GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR, and WezTerm sets WEZTERM_EXECUTABLE_DIR.
findings.evidence: With TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm, no wezterm on PATH, and the kitty keyboard probe failed (WezTerm's default), terminal:checks gives the fix 'add config.enable_kitty_keyboard = true to {config}'. Windows Terminal with LOCALAPPDATA out of reach gives '... in the profile {profile} in settings.json'.
findings.fix: Run wezterm from WEZTERM_EXECUTABLE_DIR first, and give each row with a placeholder a wording for a missing key, or let a failed reader still print the keys it knows. Extend the test at tests/terminal.bats:62 to check every {key} of a line, held line, and fix against its reader's keys.

findings.title: Windows Terminal's reader never finds defaultProfile, and judges the first profile of the list
findings.claim: Inside first($list[] | select(...)) the dot is the profile, so .defaultProfile is null and compares as an empty string: the fallback matches only a profile with no guid, then falls to $list[0]. A keep is then written for the wrong profile.
findings.evidence: With the fixture's defaultProfile set to its second profile, Ubuntu (kittyKeyboardMode false), and no WT_PROFILE_ID, terminal:settings wt gives "profile":"Windows PowerShell","kitty_keyboard":null and the check says that profile leaves the kitty keyboard protocol on. The fixture's default is its first profile, so tests/terminal.bats:551 cannot tell.
findings.fix: Bind the global first, '.defaultProfile as $default', and compare to $default. Make the fixture's default its second profile.

findings.title: The TOML readers match lines, so an equal spelling of a setting is read as unset and fails a finding
findings.claim: Warp's reader finds left_alt only on a line 'extra_meta_keys = { ... }' under [terminal.input], and Alacritty's finds option_as_alt only under a [window] header or as a dotted key. An equal spelling then fails the option finding and tells the person to set what is set.
findings.evidence: '[terminal.input.extra_meta_keys]' then 'left_alt = true' reads as {"left_meta": false,...}, and 'window = { option_as_alt = "Both" }' reads as "option":"None"; yq -p toml -o json reads both right. Which spelling Warp itself writes is unseen (closed source).
findings.fix: Read both files through yq -p toml, as tabby.sh reads YAML. Say in Alacritty's header that import is not followed, or follow it.

findings.title: kit welcome --keep= takes a finding of another terminal, or a check that holds, and writes a keep for it
findings.claim: welcome:keep checks the id against every terminal in terminals.json, not the one kit runs in, and terminal:kept-id adds the profile of the terminal kit runs in. So a keep typed in tmux or over ssh for an iTerm2 finding never matches, and a keep of a check that holds silences it the day it fails.
findings.evidence: Over ssh, 'kit welcome --keep=terminal-iterm-option' exits 0, prints nothing, and writes '- terminal-iterm-option', which never matches terminal-iterm-option@<profile>. 'kit welcome --keep=terminal-probe-color' on a probe that holds prints its ✅ line and writes the keep.
findings.fix: Refuse with 2 an id that is not among the checks terminal:checks gives now, and one that holds and is not kept. Say so when kit did not ask the terminal.

findings.title: With a kittui that does not build, kit welcome, kit tutorials, and kit help end with 1 on a terminal (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line, 13), still open. tui:binary --probe says yes whenever a checkout has go, and the build that follows is fatal, though each header says the text form prints without a kittui.
findings.evidence: With a go whose build fails, 'kit tutorials' on a pty printed '→ building kittui...', 'compile error', '❌ kittui could not be built from ...', status 1.
findings.fix: On a failed build, warn and fall through to the text form.

findings.title: Nine places repeat the hand-off to kittui by hand, and a test keeps them alike by grep
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-tui:50, kit/bin/kit-welcome:169, kit/bin/kit-tutorials:62, kit/bin/kit-help:76, kit/bin/kit-flow:308, kit/bin/kit-workspace:182, kit/modules/bash/apps.sh:55, tests/terminal.bats:692
findings.claim: Each site writes the same steps: probe for a kittui, build it, terminal:export-probes, export KIT, then exec with its own spelling of the workspace word. They have drifted: kit-tui passes no workspace (B8-2), kit-welcome asks the terminal at its top, and all stop on a failed build (B8-10).
findings.evidence: tests/terminal.bats:692 greps each file for '=$(tui:binary)' beside 'terminal:export-probes', which holds the copies in place and misses the guard's hand-off at 1st.sh:739.
findings.fix: One tui:exec <word>... in tui.sh that owns the terminal test, the probe, the build and its fallback, the probes, KIT, and the workspace word, and returns where there is no kittui so the caller prints text.

findings.title: At a terminal, kit welcome --checks | cat writes colour escapes into the pipe (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line, 9), still open. out:sgr decides by stderr, and welcome:show writes it to stdout.
findings.evidence: On a pty, 'kit welcome --checks | cat -v' shows '^[[90mcd .../emptyrepo && kit install^[[0m'.
findings.fix: Have stdout's writers test -t 1.

findings.title: A terminal that answers without a cursor report is said to draw 📚 in two cells and ↑ in one
findings.claim: measured_badly takes a null width for a good one, and the check then prints the held line, which states a measurement that was never made.
findings.evidence: terminal:parse $'\e[?62;22c' gives "emoji_width":null,"ambiguous_width":null, and the checks say '... draws 📚 in two cells' and '... draws ↑ in one cell'.
findings.fix: For a null width, hold with a line that says the terminal did not say where its cursor was.

findings.title: A settings file yq cannot read takes the terminal's checks away, with yq's and jq's own errors
findings.claim: terminal:kept prints nothing when yq fails, terminal:checks then hands jq an empty --argjson and returns 2, and welcome:plan-terminal takes that for a terminal with no checks. A kept: that is one string is matched by substring, as index on a string is.
findings.evidence: With 'terminal: [unclosed' in ~/.kit/settings.yml: yq's 'bad file' error, 'jq: invalid JSON text passed to --argjson', status 2. 'kept: terminal-probe-emoji-width-and-more' kept terminal-probe-emoji-width.
findings.fix: On a failed read, give the heading with 'kit could not read <file>', and take kept only where it is an array of strings.

findings.title: --fix takes its check after a blank or =, and --keep=, --unkeep=, --folder= after = alone
findings.claim: One verb parses its valued options two ways, and one refusal names the wrong pair (the fault of 11-10, Command line 19, at another line of syntax.jq).
findings.evidence: 'kit welcome --fix tool-jq' and '--fix=tool-jq' both run, while 'kit welcome --keep terminal-probe-color' prints '--keep needs a value'. 'kit welcome --keep=terminal-probe-color --folder=.' prints '--folder cannot be combined with --folder'.
findings.fix: Write --fix=<check> in the usage, in welcome:left's line, and in kittui's WelcomeFix. Name the option the unused one clashes with.

findings.title: A tool that does not answer --version is 'not installed' (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Command line, 11), still open. welcome:version fails where '<tool> --version' exits non-zero, so a rule with 'lint: go vet' gives 'go is not installed' with kit tools install as its fix, for good.
findings.evidence: 'go --version' exits 2 here, and welcome.sh:333 is 'out=$("$1" --version 2>/dev/null) || return 1'.
findings.fix: Let command -v say whether the tool is there; --version only adds the version.

findings.title: welcome:fix-one splits a fix at blanks, so a quoted word or a path with a space would run wrong
findings.claim: 'read -r -a command <<<"${fix}"' takes no quotes. Every fix written today is plain words, so nothing breaks yet; a kit check finding whose run: names a path with a space, which out:folder single-quotes, would.
findings.evidence: Read from the code; the remedies of brew, apt, dnf, and pacman, kit hydrate, and gh auth login are all plain words. A kit check finding with such a command settles it.
findings.fix: Keep a fix as an array from where it is made, or refuse to run one that holds a quote.

findings.title: Offline, the forge login check says 'not logged in' and offers a login
findings.claim: 'gh auth status --hostname <host>' asks the host, and any failure is read as no login, with gh auth login as the fix.
findings.evidence: Read from the code; a run with the network off settles it.
findings.fix: Tell a stored token (gh auth token --hostname) from a host that did not answer, and say which.

findings.title: Tests that would have caught the above are missing, and welcome's jq 'not installed' branch cannot be reached
findings.claim: The Windows Terminal fixture's default profile is its first (B8-7); no test runs kit --workspace=<w> with no verb (B8-2), builds from a path with a space or after a JSON edit (B8-4, B8-5), keeps another terminal's finding (B8-9), fills a placeholder through a failed reader (B8-6), or gives welcome an Azure DevOps remote (B8-3).
findings.evidence: With no jq, kit welcome prints 'install jq with this machine's package manager (jq is not on PATH)', exit 2, from the guard, so welcome:jq's 'not installed' line never prints (11-10, Command line 10: the line no longer names mise; the branch is still dead).
findings.fix: Add the six tests with their fixes. Let welcome run before the guard's jq requirement, or drop the dead branch.

areas.title: README and the core documents against the code
areas.coverage: Read whole: the 11 scoped documents, the loader, kit-call, 1st.sh, log, completion, context, generate, trust, bin/*, the workflows, every package.yml, rule, style, and kinds file, 16 verbs. Sampled: other verbs' headers, serve, settings, forge, yaml. Ran kit in an isolated copy, four bats files, lychee, direnv. Not run: terminal, forge, network.
areas.summary: Eleven documents checked against the code: about 548 claims, 494 held (README 84 of 96, architecture 62 of 74, features 95 of 108, modules 62 of 68; logs and completion all). One real bug surfaced: after `kit packages remove kit`, context, kinds, lint, and policy fail, though the README says they work. Setup lacks `kit trust`; the documents still say `gh pr ready` where `kit ready` exists; three links point at git-ignored `.kit/` files; the layout and seam descriptions are stale. Eight findings were known on 11-10, in whole or part, and are still open. Of 96 relative links, 93 resolve in the commit. findings.md was not written: the Write tool refuses report files, so everything is here.
strengths: logs.md (22 of 22), completion.md (14 of 14), context.md (52 of 54), and generate.md (45 of 48) hold almost line for line, and every behavior I ran matched the page: log line fields, log_days, completion candidates, the refusals of kit generate.
install.md (36 of 38) matches the loader exactly: the four-step choice of release, the path form of --version=, the cache, the digest check, and trust.

The README is honest about limits: the deny list matches literal patterns, only CI holds every agent, kit ships no ruleset, --no-verify skips the hook; the "What verifies what" table keeps its "no check" rows.
A verb's header is its only help, kit syntax --check holds every header to it in the gate (it passes), and every usage line a scoped document quotes matches kit usage.
The serve groups, wrong in four places on 11-10, now agree in the README, kit-serve, and serve.sh.

Lists that could drift and have not: the 31 forge features and contract 6 in architecture.md against forge_features; the app table in features.md against apps.go; the 20 schema keys against settings:validate; the packages table against the 19 package.yml files; both deny lists.
The gate checks links with fragments, kit check passes on the snapshot (the installed copies match their sources), and all 17 jq modules have tests.

findings.title: With the kit package removed, context, kinds, lint, and policy fail; two documents say they work
findings.claim: The README says `kit packages remove kit` is supported and that without the package `kit context` names no rule, `kit kinds` lists no kind, `kit lint` covers no file, and `kit policy` still runs. After `kit install` and `kit packages remove kit`, all four exit 1, because `context:load` takes a declared version with no kinds for a `.kit/` not yet placed.
findings.evidence: In a scratch repository: `kit context foo.sh`, `kit kinds`, `kit lint foo.sh`, and the `kit policy` section of `kit ci` each print `no kind is defined under .kit/kinds; run: cd … && kit hydrate`; `kit hydrate` succeeds with `packages:` empty and they still fail. `tests/packages.bats:134` tests the removal and `excludes:` only.
findings.fix: In `context:load`, raise the hydrate error only when an active package delivers a kinds file, and add a test that asks for a rule after the removal. Or refuse the removal and correct README.md:98,155 and features.md:292.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced after `kit install` and `kit packages remove kit`: `kit context foo.sh`, `kit kinds`, and `kit lint` over a named or staged file exit 1, before and after `kit hydrate`. Narrower: `kit policy` fails on the default branch and where the base has no kit.yml, and passes on a branch whose base holds kit.yml (kit/modules/bash/policy.sh:464).

findings.title: The README's Homebrew install line has no counterpart in the repository (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: `brew install empowerite/tap/kit` is the first install path of README and install.md, and nothing in `bin/release`, the release workflow, or `kit/` writes or bumps a formula. On 11-10 the tap answered "This repository is empty"; I had no network to ask it again.
findings.evidence: A search for `formula`, `homebrew-tap`, and `empowerite/tap` over `bin`, `.github`, and `kit/bin` finds nothing; only README.md:78 and install.md:22 name the tap. `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents` would settle it.
findings.fix: Publish the formula from `bin/release publish`, or lead with the `gh release download` path until a formula exists.
findings.verdict_note: Confirmed: only README.md:78 and docs/install.md:22 name the tap; no formula code exists here. That is by decision: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-release-readiness.md:29 and :341 put the formula and its bump in the tap, after the 0.1.0 tag, both unchecked. Whether the tap is still empty needs `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents`.

findings.title: README and architecture mark a pull request ready with gh and glab, not kit ready
findings.claim: `kit ready` exists and the delivered `.kit/workflow.md:23` tells agents to use it on any forge, yet README step 5 and architecture step 3 say `gh pr ready` and `glab mr update --ready`, which leave a draft stand-in in place and have no line for Azure DevOps. The README's list of workflow verbs omits `kit ready`, and features.md's six workflow steps have no ready step.
findings.evidence: `kit-ready` header: "the last step of the workflow: the forge's own draft ends, or the stand-in … is taken off". In the 11 scoped documents `kit ready` appears once, at architecture.md:197.
findings.fix: Name `kit ready` in README.md:245 and :155, architecture.md:138, and as a step in features.md's workflow list.

findings.title: The README's Setup has no kit trust, so direnv allow fails twice and leaves the tools off PATH
findings.claim: Setup runs `direnv allow` before any trust, and the `.envrc` calls `kit tools path` and `kit hydrate --quick` with no terminal to ask on, so both refuse. direnv then exports `kit/bin` alone and does not run the `.envrc` again until `tools.lock` changes, so `lefthook install` three lines later is not on PATH (that last step is reasoned, not run).
findings.evidence: In a fresh copy with an empty trust file, `direnv allow . && direnv export json` prints two `kit runs nothing in … until you trust it` lines and a PATH with 0 of the 13 tool directories; with the copy trusted first, the same export carries all 13.
findings.fix: Put `kit/bin/kit trust` before `direnv allow` in README.md's Setup block, as the release workflows do with `kit trust --yes`.

findings.title: Three links in the scoped documents point at files git never holds
findings.claim: `.kit/workflow.md` in the README and `../.kit/rules/bash.md` and `../.kit/styles/bash.md` in modules.md are placed by kit and ignored by git, so the links are dead on the forge's rendering and in a clone before `kit hydrate`. The gate does not see it, because `bin/ci:62` runs lychee over a hydrated checkout.
findings.evidence: `lychee --offline --include-fragments README.md docs/modules.md` gives 0 errors in my hydrated copy and 3 "File not found" errors in the snapshot. The other 93 relative links and every fragment resolve in the commit.
findings.fix: Link the sources under `kit/packages/…/files/repo/.kit/`, or write the three paths as code spans.

findings.title: The checks section still counts kit lint's work among the four checks (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: features.md says "The four checks are fixed. What each one runs is found at run time" and then lists the linters, the `pinned` check, and the templates, which belong to `kit lint`, not to `kit ci`. The row "The gate ran with the pinned tools … in CI" stands against the delivered default `ci_toolchain: ambient`, and "What no check covers" names one gap where the architecture table has four.
