findings.evidence: `kit-ci:33` runs `for verb in linked policy gate check`; `kit/packages/github/ci/package.yml` has `ci_toolchain: ambient`. The text is unchanged from Documents findings 2, 8, and 9 of the 11-10 review.
findings.fix: Say in both tables where `kit lint` runs (kit commit, the lefthook hook, or a gate that calls it), qualify the pinned-tools row, and list all four uncovered claims in features.md.

findings.title: "kit flow <stage> prints one stage" does not hold on a terminal, and --text is refused with a stage (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Three documents say `kit flow <stage>` prints one stage and that `--text` prints; a stage line takes no `--text`, and on a terminal a bare stage opens kittui, as features.md:252 itself says.
findings.evidence: `kit flow desk --text` prints `--text cannot be combined with desk` and exits 2; the usage line is `kit flow desk [--json | --jq] [--cached]`.
findings.fix: Give the stage lines `--text`, as `kit workspace <stage>` has, or have the three documents say "prints off a terminal, or with --json".

findings.title: Three documents describe a release layout the tree no longer has
findings.claim: architecture.md:21 says "A checkout has no `libexec/`" though `kit/libexec/kit-call` is there and runs every call; README.md:253 and AGENTS.md:15 say `libexec/kittui`, built from `tui/` (known since 11-10) where it is `kittui-<os>-<arch>` from `projects/tui/`. `modules/` is called one directory per language though it also holds `tutorials/` and `tutorials.yml`, and "`bin/` holds only commands a person runs" stands against seven plumbing verbs (known since 11-10).
findings.evidence: `ls kit/libexec` gives `kit-call`; `ls kit/modules` gives `bash jq tutorials tutorials.yml`; `bin/release:49-51` builds `./cmd/kittui` in `projects/tui` into `kittui-${goos}-${goarch}`. AGENTS.md:14 and install.md:8 already describe `libexec/` correctly.
findings.fix: Keep one description of the layout in architecture.md, correct it, and have README, AGENTS.md, and modules.md agree with it, with rows for `libexec/`, `projects/`, and `tests/`.

findings.title: The seam table leaves out providers the code has
findings.claim: The toolchain row omits `toolchain/kit.sh`, kit's own toolchain, which this repository and its CI use, and architecture.md:224 and features.md:283 repeat the list without it; the tracker row omits `tracker/web.sh`. "Five files each define a seam" also passes over `terminal.sh` with ten readers under `terminal/`, laid out as modules.md:124 says a seam is.
findings.evidence: `ls kit/modules/bash/toolchain` has `kit.sh` (450 lines) beside the eight listed; `ls kit/modules/bash/tracker` has `web.sh`; `ls kit/modules/bash/terminal` has ten files.
findings.fix: Add the two providers and "kit's own" to the three lists, and add a terminal row or say why it is no seam.

findings.title: How a repository pins a release, and what kit update moves to, is told two ways
findings.claim: install.md, README.md:182, and the code say a repository pins with `version:` in kit.yml and `kit update` moves to the release that runs it, named as `kit --version=0.2.0 update`. features.md still says a repository pins kit "with mise, with Homebrew, or by hand" and that `kit update` "moves a repository to the release it pins", and the notes `bin/release publish` attaches say "Pin it in mise.toml … then kit install".
findings.evidence: `kit-update:7-10`: "moves … from the release kit.yml declares … to the release that runs it … A plain kit update runs the declared release". install.md:27 puts the mise pin in the person's own `~/.config/mise/config.toml`.
findings.fix: Rewrite features.md:323-326 and architecture.md:56 to match kit-update's header, and the release notes in bin/release:133-135 to match install.md.

findings.title: install.md's requirements know two forges and ten verbs
findings.claim: The page names `gh` or `glab` as the forge's tool and `az` only for an Azure DevOps tracker, though `forge/ado.sh` is a forge provider over `az`. Its list of verbs that need the tool omits `kit ready`, `kit issues`, `kit changes`, `kit delivery`, `kit people`, and `kit audit`.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:173 and features.md:262 both list Azure DevOps through `az` as a forge; `kit-ready` loads `forge`, and the five app verbs read the forge through `apps.sh`.
findings.fix: Add `az` for the Azure DevOps forge and the six verbs.

findings.title: The jq module table lists 11 of 17 modules (known since 11-10, still open and wider)
findings.claim: The table omits `apps.jq`, `glyphs.jq`, `serve.jq`, `terminal.jq`, `version.jq`, and `workspace.jq`.
findings.evidence: `ls kit/modules/jq/*.jq` gives 17 files, each with a `tests/jq/<module>.test`; the table has 11 rows. It was 10 of 14 on 11-10.
findings.fix: Add the six rows, or generate the table from each module's banner as a kit:generate region.

findings.title: The stages are listed in an order, and a number, the code does not have
findings.claim: features.md says work moves left to right through seven stages and puts incoming second (known since 11-10 in its earlier form); it also says Flow in kittui is every stage of the `flow` setting while its own table gives five. README and features.md list five stages for `kit workspace` and leave out `repos`.
findings.evidence: `kit flow --stages` prints issues, desk, worktrees, changes, builds, incoming, releases; `apps.go:82` says "kit flow's desk and worktrees are not" drawn; `kit workspace --stages` prints repos first of six.
findings.fix: Reorder the bullets, say Flow draws the stages but desk and worktrees, and add `repos` to the two lists.

findings.title: Small statements that went stale
findings.where: docs/context.md:75, docs/features.md:61, docs/generate.md:29, docs/modules.md:285, docs/testing.md:42, docs/features.md:275
findings.claim: context.md says the bash rule lists five templates (it lists six) and its sample frontmatter matches no shipped file; features.md says the template language has one construct though the block `<prefix>§name` exists; generate.md's sample region and "the sentence" are not the region's text (both samples known since 11-10). modules.md says one yq process per read, testing.md says loading yaml runs yq three times (plausible only: read, not counted), and features.md:275 writes the workspace file as `kit/workspaces.yml`.
findings.evidence: `rules/bash.md` frontmatter has five provider variants and `verb`; `template.jq:9` and `templates.md:63` define the block; `yaml.sh:6` says one yq run answers every read of a file and `yaml:detect` trusts `kit_yq`; `workspaces:file` is under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.
findings.fix: Correct each line; show one real file for the two samples.

findings.title: The README's maintenance lists are short (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: The `bin/` row omits `bin/tutorials`; the installed-copy table omits `.kit/welcome/` and the kit package's six templates and gives all of `.kit/templates/bash/` to the house package; testing.md lists the gate without the tutorials site's checks or kittui's every-statement coverage rule. New: "The release workflow runs two commands" where `release.yml` now has a trust step and a tools step first.
findings.evidence: `ls bin` gives ci, refresh, release, tutorials; `kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/` holds `welcome/` and `templates/bash/{verb,*-provider}`; `bin/ci:63-85` runs ajv and `npm run check` for the site and fails on any uncovered statement.
findings.fix: Complete the three lists and say what the workflow's other steps are.

findings.title: A rule in AGENTS.md that eight modules break, and a see: line to a page that does not exist
findings.claim: AGENTS.md says a path in a file under `kit/` is written from `kit/`, as `modules/bash/forge.sh`, yet eight modules' `see:` lines name `kit/bin/kit-flow` and the like. The loader's header ends with `docs/releases.md`, which does not exist.
findings.evidence: `see:` lines at flow.sh:62, commit.sh:34, serve.sh:71, builds.sh:15, issues.sh:32, changes.sh:12, marks.sh:22, and releases.sh:10 start with `kit/bin/`. `docs/releases.md` is the only `docs/` path named under `kit/`, `bin/`, or `.github/` that is missing.
findings.fix: Drop the `kit/` prefix in the eight lines and point the loader at `docs/install.md`.

findings.title: Features in code that no scoped document mentions
findings.claim: `kit root` is in no document at all, and `kit facts` and `kit template` are in none of the 11 scoped ones; the other 49 verbs are named. completion.md does not say the kit options before the verb complete, and no scoped page names the Settle job that runs `kit settle` when a pull request closes, or the settings `facts`, `linked_exempt`, `policy`, `require_signing`, and `trackers`.
findings.evidence: A count of `kit <verb>` over the scoped documents gives 0 for root, facts, and template; `kit completion candidates kit -` prints `--version=`, `--workspace=`, `--help`, `--version`. The five settings are in docs/policy.md, docs/trackers.md, and docs/packages.md.
findings.fix: Add a line for the plumbing verbs in modules.md, the kit options in completion.md, and Settle beside the CI job in features.md.

areas.title: the feature documents against the code
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 32 documents in scope, apps.sh, apps/*.sh, apps.jq, every package.yml, delivered agent files, CI template. Sampled: forge providers' caps, toolchain providers, serve.sh, terminals.json, TUI main.go, apps.go, fields.json. Not read: forge.jq, most of flow.sh, welcome.sh, most Go. Ran app verbs, workspaces, serve, policy, tutorials, install/uninstall, lychee.
areas.summary: The feature documents are largely accurate: of about 459 checkable claims, about 428 held, and all 115 relative links resolve. serve.md, terminals.md, policy.md and tutorials.md held completely. The gaps cluster where code moved after the page: the trust gate (in none of these pages), the verbs that take --workspace=, two kit.yml keys, the sh kind, the verb template, kit ready, and the TUI README's inventory. One code bug surfaced: stage marks skip linked files, so .kit/policy never moves them. No documented feature lacks code. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the Write of a report file, so the full findings are here only.
strengths: Every relative link and fragment in scope resolves: lychee offline, 115 checked, 0 errors.
docs/serve.md is exact: the 17 tools, their annotations, the resources and media types, both protocol eras, and six refusals all came back as written.
docs/terminals.md and terminals.json agree one to one: 31 findings across ten terminals, four probes, and all 15 anchors the checks link to.
docs/apps.md's caps and scopes match the providers' code, and every stage's field list matches apps.jq and fields.json.
docs/workspaces.md's commands, messages, and exit codes held as run, and it states what is not built (match, project, Browse), which the code refuses by name.
docs/trackers.md's eleven calls equal the seam's header; docs/policy.md's defaults, facts fields, and the 65536-byte cap equal the code.
docs/tutorials.md was corrected since 11-10 and matches kit tutorials in every form run.
Package dependencies, bundle members, notices, expectations, regions, and host templates in docs/packages.md held in a fresh install.

findings.title: The trust gate is in none of the feature documents, and three of them describe flows it refuses
findings.claim: The loader runs nothing in an untrusted clone, and only docs/install.md says so. serve.md's harness-started server, agents/claude's hook, and github/ci.md's line for another CI system ("calls kit tools install and kit ci") all fail there, and the delivered workflow's own trust step is not listed on its page.
findings.evidence: In an untrusted clone, a server/discover request piped to kit serve, kit context --claude, and kit ci each print "kit runs nothing in ... until you trust it" and exit 1 with nothing on stdout. kit-ci.yml:107-108 runs kit trust --yes "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}" before anything else.
findings.fix: Name the trust step in github/ci.md, in the job's list and in the other-CI line. Say in serve.md and agents/claude.md that the server and the hook run only in a trusted clone.

findings.title: workspaces.md names three verbs that take --workspace=; eleven do, and the rest ignore it silently
findings.claim: The page says only kit flow, kit workspace, and kit workspaces --current follow the workspace rule and every other verb takes no --workspace=. The seven app verbs and kit welcome take it too, and a verb that does not is not refused.
findings.evidence: kit --workspace=acme platform settings --json printed 40 rows from two members, and audit policy one row at scope organization. kit --workspace=acme lint printed "nothing to lint" and exited 0, having read only the folder's repository.
findings.fix: List the verbs that span a workspace in one place. Have the loader or kit:enter refuse --workspace= for a verb that does not read KIT_WORKSPACE.

findings.title: A stage's mark skips every linked file, so .kit/policy/ never moves the marks apps.md says hash it
findings.claim: apps:hash lists a directory with find -type f, which leaves out symbolic links, and kit delivers a file under .kit/ as a link when its source is in the worktree, the way policy.md tells a repository to ship its own Rego. The policy and services marks therefore ignore such files.
findings.evidence: find .kit/policy -type f | wc -l is 0, and kit audit --marks gives policy as main=582975ca..., the same hash kit platform --marks gives settings, which is kit.yml alone. Appending a line to house.rego, then removing it, changed neither the policy mark nor the services mark.
findings.fix: Use find -L, or match -type f and -type l. Add a test whose policy file is a link.

findings.title: packages.md's Settings section is two keys behind the schema, and "the kit writes three keys" is false
findings.claim: The settings table lists 18 of the schema's 20 keys: forge_settings and tools are missing, though apps.md, trackers.md, and using-kit.md lean on them. The section says the kit writes only version, packages, and excludes, but kit tools update rewrites a tool's version under tools:.
findings.evidence: jq '.properties|keys_unsorted' on kit.schema.json prints 20 keys. toolchain/kit.sh:152 runs yq --inplace '.tools[strenv(kit_tool)].version = strenv(kit_version)' kit.yml.
findings.fix: Add the two rows. Say the kit toolchain rewrites a tool's version under tools:.

findings.title: The TUI README's inventory is stale: screens, the tutorials screen, the layout, and the test commands
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open in part. It says six screens (shell.go names twelve and the workspaces' screen), says tutorials are tabbed by audience and share internal/tabs (they are cards under a control line and do not import it), omits seven of 22 packages from Layout, and files manage.go and popover.go under internal/flow.
findings.evidence: kit tutorials screens, its example, is refused with "'screens' is not one of the choices", exit 2; the id is screen. internal/tutorials/testdata holds 7 golden files the -update command does not name, and bin/ci:79 fails on any uncovered statement, which "runs the same three" leaves out.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening list, the two tutorials lines, the example, and Layout. Add ./internal/tutorials to the golden command and name the coverage gate.

findings.title: docs/packages/workflow.md says the workflow file names gh pr ready because no kit verb exists; one does
findings.claim: The page says the delivered file names gh pr ready and glab mr update --ready "where there is no kit verb for the step". The delivered workflow.md says kit ready, on any forge, and kit/bin/kit-ready exists.
findings.evidence: kit/packages/workflow/files/repo/.kit/workflow.md:23 and :47 say kit ready. A grep for 'gh pr' or 'glab mr' over that file finds nothing.
findings.fix: Replace the paragraph with one line on kit ready.

findings.title: workspaces.md says a workspace's flow has "kit's eight" stages; it has seven
findings.claim: "Over a workspace, the stages are kit's eight" is wrong by one.
findings.evidence: kit --workspace=acme flow --stages prints issues desk worktrees changes builds incoming releases. kit/bin/kit-flow:115 and docs/packages.md:290 both say seven.
findings.fix: Write seven.

findings.title: The counts the sh kind moved: seven rules and "seven files" are eight
findings.claim: kit.md lists seven rules and leaves out sh, which ships as rules/sh.md. cursor.md and copilot.md each say the package places only its seven files; each places eight rule files and an MCP file.
findings.evidence: kit packages add agents/copilot placed eight files under .github/instructions (ls | wc -l is 8) and .vscode/mcp.json. kit/packages/agents/cursor holds eight .mdc files, kit-sh.mdc among them.
findings.fix: Name sh in kit.md. Say "one file per rule, and the MCP entry" in place of a number.

findings.title: The kit package delivers a sixth template, verb, that no document names
findings.claim: templates.md and kit.md say the kit package delivers five templates, the seam providers. The bash rule lists a sixth, verb, for kit/bin/kit-*, which every consumer receives and cannot use, since templates.md says a verb is made in the kit's own source alone; packages.md's kit row names no template at all (known since 11-10, still open).
findings.evidence: rules/bash.md frontmatter has variant: verb, path: "kit/bin/kit-*", executable: true. A fresh kit install printed .kit/templates/bash/verb.
findings.fix: Move the verb template to the house package, which already carries one, or document it in the three pages.

findings.title: Small stale statements in apps.md and trackers.md
findings.claim: apps.md says a control's source is ruleset or protection, but that field is kind; it lists six of the issues tab's seven presets, leaving out Compact; and it gives tools' fields without path. trackers.md calls the code forge GitHub or GitLab and Azure DevOps a separate system, though it is the third forge provider.
findings.evidence: apps.jq:115 is del(.url, .source) + {kind: .source ...}, and fields.json's issues presets end with Compact. kit platform tools --json with no toolchain prints rows of {name, path, from}.
findings.fix: Correct the four lines.

findings.title: using-devcontainer.md says it is offered last, after docker; the kit toolchain comes after it
findings.claim: The order toolchains are offered in ends devcontainer, then kit, and toolchains.md never states the order. Its kit tools table gives what install and update run for four providers and leaves out nix and kit, and its opening list of tool managers leaves kit out.
findings.evidence: toolchain.sh:170 ranks mise 1, nix 2, brew 3, docker 4, every other 5, in the providers' name order. kit toolchains --json lists devcontainer before kit.
findings.fix: State the order once in toolchains.md and correct the devcontainer page. Add nix and kit to the table.

findings.title: A workspace's repos rows do not have the fields workspaces.md says every row has
findings.claim: The page says every row carries organization and repository as the remote names them, and gains its member. The repos stage's rows hold the host and path under repository and have no member, so one field name holds two things across the tabs of one app.
findings.evidence: kit --workspace=acme workspace repos --json prints "repository":"github.com/acme/one" and no member key. A branches row of the same workspace has "repository":"one" and "member":"github.com/acme/one".
findings.fix: Give repos rows member and the bare name, or say in the page that repos is the exception.

findings.title: The settings schema names a default for one key of twenty, so Platform's settings tab shows null
findings.claim: apps.md says an unset setting shows the schema's default, null where it names none. Only log_days has one, so the tab shows null for settings whose defaults packages.md states in prose.
findings.evidence: kit platform settings --json gives ["primary",null,"default"], while packages.md says primary's default is origin. flow and policy_engine read null the same way.
findings.fix: Put the defaults the prose states into the schema.

findings.title: A merged JSON file the kit created is left as {} after removal, which the documents do not say
findings.claim: packages.md says uninstall takes out what the packages delivered and that a region's file is removed if left empty. A merged JSON file the kit itself created is left behind as an empty object.
findings.evidence: After kit install, kit packages add agents/copilot hooks/lefthook agents/claude, their removal, and kit uninstall in a fresh repository, .mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, and .vscode/mcp.json remained, each {}. An empty .github/instructions/ remained too.
findings.fix: Remove a merged file that is {} and that kit created, or say in packages.md that it stays.

findings.title: Two statements known since 11-10 are still open
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. packages.md says the gate validates every package.yml, but the house package's is not covered, and generic.md calls the AGENTS.md region "the sentence" when it is a heading and two sentences.
findings.evidence: bin/ci:27-28 globs kit/packages/*/package.yml and kit/packages/*/*/package.yml only. kit/packages/agents/generic/regions/repo/AGENTS.md has a ## heading and two sentences.
findings.fix: Add .kit/packages/*/package.yml to bin/ci's globs. Reword generic.md.

areas.title: kittui flow package, the screen and its actions
areas.coverage: Read whole: the ten scoped files, plus rows, marks, kept, fix, heading, packages, apps, source/*, shell/layers, table/view, screens. Sampled their tests. Ran the package's tests once and 14 test files of mine in out/G1/work/projects/tui/internal/flow (g1*_test.go). Not read: legend, glyph, fields, team, grid, tabs.
areas.summary: Two crashes and five stale-state bugs, all reproduced. A failed reload keeps the old rows behind the refusal: keys act on rows nobody sees (`a` ran `kit assign #7`), and at 53 columns or fewer kittui panics. A picture with no stage panics on tab. A watched stage never reloads after one failure. A crumb's Restore and a late workspace leave tables wrong. Clicks are sound: 1,243 of 1,243 landed on the drawn row. Six 11-10 findings are still open and two criticals are fixed. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write of a report file, and I did not work around it; the full text is in this result. Timings were taken at load average 57.
strengths: A click lands on the row drawn: 1,243 of 1,243 clicks on lines naming an issue, at 6 sizes, with rows open, scrolled, paged, maximized, and under a preset line.
No line is wider than the screen at 40 columns or more and no screen is taller than its height, in 22 states; overflow starts at 20 columns, in the menus alone.
source.Load numbers its reads, so a superseded answer and a late kept copy are dropped, and a test proves it.
shell.Layers gives keys, clicks, the keys bar and drawing one order; an action's dialog takes every key and click.
An unknown stage survives every key and a full click sweep without a panic.
Actions run kit's verbs in the member's checkout, list what they will change before asking, and refuse (nowhere) rather than act in the wrong repository.
Both 11-10 criticals in this area are fixed: each record decodes into a fresh value (decoding[T]), and an open column card no longer panics when the header goes.
Spot deep-copies each table (cloneTable), and the presets file is read again, merged, and renamed into place, never clobbered when unreadable.

findings.title: A failed reload over frozen headings that take more lines than the refusal crashes kittui
findings.claim: take keeps the old rows when a reload fails, so table.FrozenLines still counts their frozen headings while allLines gives only the refusal's lines. `allLines(...)[FrozenLines:]` then slices past the end inside Update and the program dies.
findings.evidence: g1g_test.go: issues searched for `jig`, grouped by status, milestone, assignees, at any width from 20 to 53 columns; restart then an error answer gives `panic: slice bounds out of range [2:1] (frozen lines 2)` at table/view.go:97 under flow.go:1056. A longer chain of single-valued groups wraps at 80 columns too.
findings.fix: Give no rows for a stage that is loading or refused (G1-2). Have ScrollLines, Laid, and Model.lines clamp the skip to len(lines).
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a copy (verify-1/projects/tui/internal/flow/v1_test.go, v1b_test.go): `jig` + status, milestone, assignees panics `[2:1]` at 53 columns (not 54) at table/view.go:97 via flow.go:1056; an 11-group chain panics at 80. rows.go:309 ignores refusal, despite rows.go:278's comment. No recover anywhere. Default views (one frozen line from 32 columns) do not crash.

findings.title: After a failed reload the old rows stay live behind the refusal, and keys act on them
findings.claim: rows.go:278 promises no rows while a stage loads or after a refusal, but build never checks either and take leaves s.rows as they were. takeKept does the same when it decodes a kept copy and then abandons it.
findings.evidence: g1c/g1d_test.go: #7 selected, reload answered with an error: the group heading and `7 selected` stand over the refusal, Close as Not Planned and Open Selected are enabled, and pressing `a` ran `kit assign #7`. g1e_test.go: a kept copy with a failed member leaves a heading over `loading`.
findings.fix: build returns an empty shown for a loading or refused stage, or take clears the rows as restart does. takeKept decodes into a scratch stage and copies only what it keeps.

findings.title: With no stage in the picture, tab, shift-tab, alt-right and alt-left crash kittui
findings.claim: table.Scrolled runs before the inRows guard, and Expand with subtree goes straight to Grow or Peel; each indexes m.stages[m.stage]. `flow: [desk]` is a setting kit accepts (settings.sh:313) and kittui draws neither desk nor worktrees.
findings.evidence: g1n_test.go: FAKE_FLOW_STAGES="desk worktrees", OpenApp gives 0 stages, Update(tab) panics `index out of range [0] with length 0` (flow.go:624 via flow.go:858). The shipped no-stage test (edges_test.go:21) does not send these four keys.
findings.fix: Guard both cases with len(m.stages) > 0, as `[` and `]` are. Add the four keys to TestAPictureWithNoStageTakesEveryKeyQuietly.

findings.title: A watched stage whose reload fails is never read again, and the keys bar still says watching
findings.claim: tookMarks passes over a stage while its refusal is set, and only restart clears a refusal. One failed reload ends Watch for that stage until someone presses Refresh.
findings.evidence: g1c_test.go: issues watched, mark moved with FAKE_FLOW_REFUSE=issues, then the refusal lifted and the mark moved three more times: no `flow issues` call ran, the refusal stayed, and the keys bar ended `🔭 watching`.
findings.fix: Let a refused stage take marks too, so the next read of the marks runs again. Clear refusal in take when a read lands without an error.

findings.title: Going back along a crumb puts back each stage's table as it was when the link was followed
findings.claim: Restore replaces every stage's whole table.Table with Spot's copy, but a hidden picture goes on taking answers. A load that landed meanwhile loses its Blank columns and its auto-grouping, and nothing runs autoGroup again.
findings.evidence: g1e_test.go: issues loaded, Spot(), changes lands, Restore(spot): changes goes from `groups [] blank [member source organization repository]` to `grouping true, groups [source organization repository], blank []` and draws `▾ none · none · none 3`.
findings.fix: Restore only what the person set (cursor by key, scroll, outline, selection, view name, search). Keep Blank, Grouping, Grouped and the grouped View of a stage that loaded since, or run blank and autoGroup again.

findings.title: The workspace told after rows were built does not rebuild them
findings.claim: WorkspaceMsg sets m.ws and returns, but short, here, deskOf, memberValue and failures read m.ws and their output is cached in m.built. Rows keep the long member names, and `here` for `desk`, until something else rebuilds.
findings.evidence: g1d_test.go: over a group, changes answered before the workspace: the screen shows `▾ github.com/o/a 1` and `❌ github.com/o/b: …`, is unchanged after WorkspaceMsg, and shows `▾ a 1` and `❌ b: …` only after m.rebuild().
findings.fix: Call m.rebuild(), clamp and fit in the WorkspaceMsg case, as meMsg and SettingsMsg do.

findings.title: A reload keeps the cursor's index, not its row (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: take only clamps the cursor. Watched stages reload by themselves, so space, `a`, or New… then act on another issue than the one the person was on.
findings.evidence: g1j_test.go: cursor on `#8 #4`, the stage reloads with one new issue that sorts first, and the cursor is on `#1 #2`.
findings.fix: Keep the key of the row under the cursor before decode and find it after, as crumb.go's Restore does.

findings.title: The tab menu costs a pass over every row per line per draw (known since 11-10, fixed in part)
findings.claim: enabled(k) rebuilds tabItems up to three times and walks the rows for each line; refs and refsByMember use slices.Contains, so they are quadratic in the selection. The 11-10 quadratic fold cost is gone; a linear cost with a large constant is left.
findings.evidence: g1i_test.go, least of three at load average 57: menu draw 39 ms at 300 issues, 152 ms at 1,000, 659 ms at 3,000, 1.88 s at 10,000, 3.35 s with 10,000 selected; ↓ in the rows 191 ms at 10,000. The tree's 8 ms wheel test measured 17-20 ms at the same time.
findings.fix: Compute the menu's facts once per draw (selected rows, members, pages, fold state) and hand them to enabled. Use a set in refs and refsByMember.

findings.title: Add to Pull Request… can never be enabled in the Issues app (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: mine() reads this screen's changes stage, and the Issues app has issues, issues/milestones and issues/iterations only.
findings.evidence: g1j_test.go: Issues app, one issue selected, me `ada`: enabled false. Flow app, same state: enabled true.
findings.fix: Read the caller's open pull requests from kit, or leave the line out where the app has no changes stage.

findings.title: Nothing typed in an action's dialog, the search, or a preset's name can be pasted (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: No code handles tea.PasteMsg, so a title pasted into "Title of the parent issue" types nothing.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn PasteMsg projects/tui --include=*.go` finds no handler outside tests, and flow's update has no case for it.
findings.fix: Route tea.PasteMsg to whatever types, through shell.Type, on every screen.

findings.title: The tab menu is one table written as five switches on the lines' labels
findings.claim: tabItems, enabled, pick, acting, act and oneMember each match a line by its English label. pick ends in a fall-through that clears the selection for any label it does not know, and act returns nil, so a renamed label fails silently.
findings.evidence: menu.go:175-177: `// Clear Selection, the one item left that acts` then `clear(s.Picked)` for every unmatched name; act.go:140 lists four labels as strings.
findings.fix: One slice of items, each with glyph, label, key, what it needs, an enabled func and a run func. Packages' actions fit the same shape.

findings.title: Watch is offered, and says watching, while the marks cannot be read
findings.claim: watchable is true while the marks hold no value for the stage, which is also the state after the first read failed and the poll turned itself off. Watch then waits on nothing until Refresh All.
findings.evidence: g1m_test.go: the fake kit refuses --marks; m.marks.Off() is true, Watch is enabled, and choosing it draws `🔭 watching`.
findings.fix: watchable is false while m.marks.Off(), or the keys bar says the marks cannot be read.

findings.title: A failed `kit flow --me` is dropped and never asked again (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: meMsg with an error does nothing and asked stays true, so @me matches nothing and Add to Pull Request… stays dim for the session, with no notice.
findings.evidence: g1e_test.go: FAKE_FLOW_REFUSE=me, open the tab's menu: `asked true, me "", note ""`; lifting the refusal, reopening the menu and Refresh All leave me empty.
findings.fix: On an error, say it in the notice and clear asked.

findings.title: An action's answer clears a selection made while kit ran, and actions can overlap (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: acted clears the stage's whole selection, whatever it holds by then. Nothing marks an action as running, and Act has no limit but the screen's context.
findings.evidence: g1h_test.go: Assign to Me started, six more rows selected before kit answered, and 0 are selected after the answer.
findings.fix: actedMsg carries the keys it acted on and clears those alone. Allow one action at a time.

findings.title: kit's answer about the trackers replaces a dialog opened meanwhile
findings.claim: newIssue sets m.ask whatever is open, and on whichever tab is selected when the answer comes.
findings.evidence: g1h_test.go: `bo` typed into "Assign to which login?", then trackersMsg arrives: the dialog is "New issue in which tracker?" and the typed text is gone.
findings.fix: Drop or queue the answer while m.layers().Opened(m).

findings.title: The wheel scrolls the rows under an open dialog or menu
findings.claim: Keys and clicks go to the topmost layer first, but the MouseWheelMsg case never asks m.layers().
findings.evidence: g1h_test.go: with the Close as Not Planned dialog open, two turns of the wheel move the rows' offset from 1 to 7.
findings.fix: Do not scroll while a layer is open, or give shell.Layer a wheel handler.

findings.title: A jump to a row that is not there waits forever on a stale stage
findings.claim: land clears landing only when the row is found or the stage is neither loading nor stale. A stage whose mark moved and is not watched stays stale, so the jump lands at some later reload.
findings.evidence: g1h_test.go: changes stale, jump("changes/#999"), back to issues: landing is still `changes/#999`.
findings.fix: Clear landing when the stage is stale by its mark rather than by a kept copy, or when the person moves the cursor.

findings.title: Three tests miss what breaks, and one asserts wall-clock time
findings.claim: No test fails a reload of a stage that shows rows, the no-stage test leaves out four keys, and no crumb test lands a load between Spot and Restore. The 10,000-issue wheel test compares milliseconds against a fixed budget.
findings.evidence: TestATurnOfTheWheelOverTenThousandIssuesIsWellUnderAFramesTime failed 4 of 4 runs here (17.3 to 19.7 ms against 8 ms) at load average 57. Plausible that this is load alone; a run on a quiet machine would settle whether #272 slowed the wheel.
findings.fix: Add the three cases. Count work (rows built, lines drawn) instead of milliseconds, as TestAStagesLinesAreDrawnOnceForWhatItShows does.

findings.title: A refusal longer than the screen is cut where its remedy is
findings.claim: bottom clips the notice to one line, so the tail of a long refusal is lost, including the one nowhere writes itself.
findings.evidence: g1m_test.go at 80 columns: the 110-cell notice shows `❌ kit has not said where github.com/empowerite/infrastructure is checked out;…`; "pick the workspace again from -" is gone.
findings.fix: Wrap a refusal over the pane's last lines, or lead the sentence with the remedy.

findings.title: Who has the keyboard is three booleans and an int, set by hand in ten places
findings.claim: inRows, onPreset, inPanel and stop are assigned together across flow.go, views.go, heading.go, column.go, fix.go and host.go, and nothing stops inRows standing over a refusal (G1-2). take and takeKept, pages and links, refs and refsByMember each repeat the same lines.
findings.evidence: The same four-way assignment stands at views.go:394, 427, 441 and heading.go:39; fix.go:69 sets two of the four.
findings.fix: One focus value with a setter that checks the stage can take it, and one helper for the shared tail of take and takeKept.

findings.title: An issue's reference is rebuilt as #<number>; kit's ref is ignored
findings.claim: kit prints ref on every issue and changes key their rows by it, but issueRows names an issue "#"+number and the actions hand that to kit. Once a tracker with another prefix lists issues, Close as Not Planned would close the forge's issue of the same number.
findings.evidence: forge.jq:286 prints `ref: "#\(.number)"`; testdata/trackers.json already has the prefix `AB#`. Today kit lists only the forge's own issues, so the two agree; what settles it is whether v0.1.0 lists other trackers' issues.
findings.fix: Carry ref in the issue struct and use it for the row's key and for the action's words.

areas.title: kittui flow package, rows, fields, and glyphs
areas.coverage: Read whole: the 20 scoped Go files, fields.json, legend.jq, six test files; sampled flow.go, act.go, view.go, internal/table, kit's jq modules. Ran in-scope tests (pass) and eight scratch reproductions under out/G2/work. findings.md is NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from subagents, so everything is in this result.
areas.summary: Two high bugs: an issue row is keyed by number alone, so an action on another repository's issue (which kit lists when a pull request closes it) runs on this repository's issue of that number; and every issue and pull request link is guessed from `origin`, wrong on Azure DevOps, GitLab subgroups, and forks (known since 11-10, still open). A refused or loading tab still lets Select All and the actions run on rows it does not draw. 20 of 32 tabs have no legend, tab glyph, or color, since those are Go tables by stage name. The catalog repeats four fields in all 32 stages (35% of it), and Go still builds 49 fields by hand. Fixtures do not match what kit prints.
strengths: The catalog is checked as it is read: unknown keys refused, check() on every schema, and a test that every type and renderer it names is registered and every preset names only its stage's fields.

decode refuses precisely and names the command (wrong shape, a record without its key, two records of one key, a member or links of the wrong type); memberAndLinks checking that a link list is all strings is what makes the bare l.(string) in linkValue safe.
A record is decoded once (parsed), and a test counts the decodes.
unbuilt lets a builder leave a field to the catalog's path; it is the right seam for removing the builders, so keep it.
The glyphs region of glyph.go is generated from kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json and a test fails when it is stale; the state and build glyphs are held to the catalog by TestTheCatalogsGlyphsAreTheLegends.
The legend lists only what the screen shows, in reading order, and scopes each glyph to the lines it means it on.
stageOf takes the longest stage name a link starts with, with a test that holds changes/reviews/3 bob apart from changes.
The Packages actions list what they take out and ask first; over a group an action refuses to run where kit has not said the member's checkout (nowhere) rather than run in the wrong repository.
A calendar day is drawn in UTC and an instant in local time, tested east and west of UTC.
The team's presets are written beside the file and renamed into place, and a name whose slug is taken is refused.

findings.title: An issue row is keyed by its number alone, so an action on another repository's issue runs on this one's
findings.claim: issueRows makes a row's reference and key from i.Number only and drops source, organization, and repository, which kit prints because a pull request can close another repository's issue (kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:179); every issues action then hands kit the bare #N in this checkout. The same key gives a wrong title link and refuses the whole tab when one pull request closes two issues of one number.
findings.evidence: With the package's own fixture row #7 of empowerite/jig selected in empowerite/kit's picture, Close as Not Planned asks `["#7 Fix the thing"]` (jig's title) and runs `kit close --not-planned #7`; its title link is https://github.com/empowerite/kit/issues/7. Two underway rows of number 12 under pull request 5 give the refusal `kit flow issues --json printed two records of the key 12 5`.
findings.fix: Key a row by organization, repository, and number, in issueRows and in the catalog's key, and pass kit a reference that names the repository or leave the actions dim on a row this checkout does not hold. kit/modules/jq/backlog.jq:12 has the same number-only match (11-10 finding 5, still open); the kittui part is new.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: fixture row #7 of jig has key `#7`, link https://github.com/empowerite/kit/issues/7, asks `#7 Fix the thing`, runs `close --not-planned #7`. kit's own issues.jq, given a pull request closing kit#12 and jig#12, prints both rows; the screen refuses `two records of the key 12 5`. Real reach is underway rows only; backlog rows are always this repository's.

findings.title: Every issue and pull request link is guessed from origin: wrong on Azure DevOps, GitLab subgroups, plain-named GitLab hosts, and forks
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (finding 8, medium), still open; the Azure DevOps case is new and is why I rate it high. kit prints no url for an issue or a change, so Origin.issue and Origin.pull build one from `git remote get-url origin`: its last two path segments, GitLab's shape only where the host's name contains "gitlab", GitHub's otherwise.
findings.evidence: parseRemote gives https://dev.azure.com/_git/policy/pull/7 for https://dev.azure.com/acme/Claims/_git/policy, https://gitlab.com/sub/kit/-/merge_requests/7 for git@gitlab.com:group/sub/kit.git (origin_test.go:14 asserts it), and /pull/7 for a GitLab at git.example.com. With `primary: upstream` in kit.yml and origin a fork, ReadOrigin gives me/kit and issue 7 opens https://github.com/me/kit/issues/7.
findings.fix: Have kit print each row's page, as builds, releases, and the app verbs' links do, and have issueRows and changeRows use it. Keep origin.go only for the title's fallback.
findings.verdict_note: All cases reproduce: parseRemote gives dev.azure.com/_git/policy/pull/7, gitlab.com/sub/kit, and /pull/7 on git.example.com; origin.go:17 reads origin whatever `primary` says; kit prints no url (forge.jq:285, underway.jq:19). But only links opened or copied are wrong, no kit verb uses them: medium, not high. The 11-10 history is unchecked.

findings.title: A tab that is refused, or loading, still holds its last rows for Select All and the actions
findings.claim: rows says it gives "nothing while it loads or after a refusal", but shown and build draw from s.parsed whatever the stage's state, and a refusal leaves s.parsed as it was. The tab's menu therefore selects and acts on rows the pane does not draw.
findings.evidence: Issues loaded, then refused with `gh cannot read the forge`: the pane shows one ❌ line, Select All is enabled and selects 7, and Assign to Me runs `kit assign #7 #1 #8 #46 #31 #45`. While it loads, a row selected before stays selected and Close as Not Planned is enabled over the word `loading`.
findings.fix: Have rows give none for a stage that loads or is refused, as its comment says, or have enabled refuse the selection's lines and the actions then, and clear Picked on a refusal. The heading over the groups that stays above a refusal is asserted by fix_test.go:127, so leave that.

findings.title: 20 of the 32 tabs have no legend, no tab glyph, and no color, because those are Go tables keyed by stage name
findings.claim: legends, marks, stageGlyphs, and stageColors are generated from kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json, which names 14 stages (two no longer drawn), while the catalog names 32. Two of Issues' tabs, three of Changes', three of Delivery's, and every tab of People, Trust, and Platform draw a bare name in no color, and ? explains none of their rows' glyphs.
findings.evidence: At 200x50, changes/checks draws ✅ ❌ 🏃 and its legend lacks all three, delivery/deployments lacks ✅ ❌ 🔘, changes/reviews lacks 💬, each with color "" and glyph "". The test passes because it looks for a field's glyph in the union of all stages' legends.
findings.fix: Read a tab's legend from its own catalog fields, which already hold each field's and each enum value's glyph, and put the tab's glyph and group in its catalog entry. 11-10 finding 17 named this for planned tabs; they are real tabs now.

findings.title: The fixtures are not what kit prints, so no test draws a tab as a person sees it
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (finding 17, last point), still open, with new evidence. The hand-written fixtures have drifted from kit's output and nothing holds them to it.
findings.evidence: A jq comparison of fixture keys with field paths shows 27 of 32 fixtures carry no source, organization, or repository, which kit adds to every row and every view groups by. audit-controls.json has ruleset/protection under `source` and no `kind`, where kit/modules/jq/apps.jq:115 prints it under `kind`, so the tested Controls tab groups by source into protection and ruleset.
findings.fix: Generate the fixtures from kit over the tests' fake forge, or add a bats test that holds each fixture's keys to what the verb prints, as tests/syntax.bats does for the syntax fixtures.

findings.title: A row: link reaches only a stage of the row's own verb, and every app's home tab is another verb's
findings.claim: rowLink names its target as stageNamed(verb, name), but the home tab of Changes, Issues, and Delivery is kit flow's stage, so no row of kit changes, kit issues, or kit delivery can lead to it. That is why a review or a check has `links: {}` and its change is not a button.
findings.evidence: rowLink("changes", "row:changes/#3", "") gives kittui:changes/changes/#3, which stageOf takes for the changes tab and a row keyed `changes/#3`, so the cursor lands on no row. rowLink("delivery", "row:builds/9", "") gives kittui:delivery/builds/9, a stage of no app.
findings.fix: Let a link name its verb, as row:flow/changes/<key>, or resolve the stage among the app's tabs by label before falling back to the verb's.

findings.title: The catalog repeats itself, and the Go still knows stages, fields, and values by name
findings.claim: member, source, organization, and repository are written out in all 32 stages, and four stages are still built in Go field by field, with a fifth struct (release) kept only to type-check JSON. Each built row has two identities, the catalog's key that decode checks for duplicates and the key the builder makes.
findings.evidence: Counts: 32 stages, 361 fields, 127 of them (35%) those four fields, member 31 times word for word; Go builds 49 field ids by hand (issues 20, changes 10, builds 10, repos 9; rows.go:476-637, repos.go:88) and names stages at apps.go:25-38 (8 apps, 32 names), rows.go:325-331, 426, 503, 524, 549, view.go:210, legend.go:156, packages.go:19, act.go:38. Enum values are repeated in Go at rows.go:221, glyph.go:270, fields.go:168, quota.go:21, and the eight state glyphs are written three times across fields.json and glyphs.json, tied only by a test.
findings.fix: Add a list of common fields to the catalog, keep the states once in glyphs.json for both readers, and turn the builders' real needs (a link to another tab, the checks' counts) into renderers or link rules the catalog names. Make catalogRows leave out of `more` the keys a field's path reads, not those equal to a field's id.

findings.title: The legend leaves out glyphs its own tab draws, and titles itself by the stage's internal name
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (finding 20), still open. The pull request states hang under changes only (`if name == "changes"`), the repos legend has no ❗, and the box is titled `workspace/repos legend` where the tab says `repos`.
findings.evidence: At 200x60 the issues tab draws 🔥 🔨 🏁 💬 in its state column and its legend lacks all four; the test excuses it by name. worktreeNames draws `🌿 wt ❗` for a detached worktree and legends["workspace/repos"] has no Detached entry.
findings.fix: With G2-4, read a tab's legend from its fields, and title the box by label(name).

findings.title: A click on the legend where it stands over a refusal's line is the refusal's, not the legend's
findings.claim: update asks remedyClick before legendClick, and remedyClick takes any left click on the refusal's lines. Once the line is selected its run button is live under the legend; I reproduced the lost arrow click, not a run through the legend.
findings.evidence: On changes refused with `run: kit help flow`, the legend moved to the top right: a click on its ↙ arrow at x=115, y=6 leaves it in corner 1 and selects the refusal's line. On a tab not refused the same click moves it to corner 2.
findings.fix: Make the legend a layer, as the menus are, or ask legendClick before remedyClick.

findings.title: Azure DevOps has no glyph, and the forges are named in three Go places beside the catalog
findings.claim: source is github, gitlab, or ado (kit/bin/kit-flow:74), but the catalog's source and forge enums, forgeGlyphs, and the legend's "forge requests left" each list only the first two. A row from Azure DevOps draws the word `ado` beside 🐙 and 🦊, and its rate limit draws as `ado N/M`, which the legend does not explain.
findings.evidence: 23 source or forge fields in fields.json list `github` and `gitlab` with glyphs and no `other`; quota.go:21 is `{"github": GitHub, "gitlab": GitLab}`; legend.go:144 loops over `[]string{GitHub, GitLab}`.
findings.fix: Give the third provider a glyph in kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json and read the forges' glyphs from one place.

findings.title: A change is #3 on the changes tab and 3 on reviews, checks, and merged
findings.claim: The changes tab draws kit's ref (#2, or !2 on GitLab), while the three tabs beside it read .change or .number, a bare number, and Automatic drops the glyph every row shares.
findings.evidence: A dump of the Changes app from the fixtures shows `🔀 #2` on changes and `3`, `3`, `7` in the change column of reviews and checks, `2`, `1` on merged.
findings.fix: Have kit/modules/jq/apps.jq print the change's ref on those rows and point the three fields at it.

findings.title: A date that is not seconds draws as 1970-01-01, or 1969-12-31 west of UTC, with no error
findings.claim: table.Mapped discards ParseInt's error, so the date and day renderers draw the epoch for any value that is not a number. I found no provider that prints one of the nine date fields as text today; a conformance test of each provider's value for at, merged, expires, last, until, due, start, and end would settle it.
findings.evidence: `dates(table.Field{}, table.One("2026-10-02T00:00:00Z"))` gives `["1969-12-31"]` on this machine.
findings.fix: Draw the raw text when it does not parse as a number.

areas.title: kittui table package
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 28 non-test files of internal/table, grid/panel.go, grid/ranges.go; sampled tests, flow's preset code, catalogs. Ran tests (plain, -race, coverage 100%), vet, gofmt, a random walk, a preset round trip, reproductions in out/G3/work/tui/internal/table/zz_*_test.go. findings.md not written: the Write tool refused a report file.
areas.summary: Two high bugs. The fields dialog panics (index out of range) on a table with no rows that groups by nothing, or when its list shrinks under it. Two kittui on one presets file drop each other's presets and favorites of the same table. Eight medium: starring leaves the cursor behind; writers share one temp name without a lock; the 8 ms wall-clock test fails under load; a `[` in a workspace path hides team presets; same-named groups share a spot; level folds follow depth; cursor moves redraw every row; flow and Sheet duplicate preset keeping. Preset round trip and edge handling are sound: 0 of 3,000 panels differ, 0 panics in 1,500 guarded random walks.
strengths: A preset restores its panel exactly: 3,000 random panels round-tripped through PresetOf and Preset.Panel with the same groups, sort keys, column order, filters, renderings, and flat lists, and PresetOf is a normal form. Positions, depths, and priorities are 1-based on both sides, with no off-by-one found.

KeepPresets, KeepFavorites, and KeepLast never write over a file they could not read, say why in the notice, and keep other tables' presets, favorites, and last panels. A missing file is no presets, and a failed read is never taken for an empty answer by those writers.
Slug keeps a preset's name out of the file path, so no name reaches the file system unescaped.

With G3-1 guarded, 1,500 random walks of 300 steps (keys, clicks, wheel, panes 1 to 30 lines by 10 to 130 cells, empty tables, searches that match nothing, a draw and keys bar after each step) found no panic. Fit, Page, Laid, RowAt, BoxAt, the popover, and the outline hold at the edges.
Records, ReadFrom, and KeyFrom tell nothing printed, null, and a document of another shape apart, each with its own error, so a failed read is not an empty table.
Preset.Panel never sets a field to do what the catalog says it cannot: hide a column without a label, group, sort, or filter one that cannot, or pin a rendering not its own.
100% statement coverage, go vet and gofmt clean, and the suite passes under -race. The < and > folds are linear now, where the 11-10 review measured them quadratic.

findings.title: The fields dialog panics on a table without rows that groups by nothing, and when its list shrinks under it
findings.claim: Columns.Keys and Columns.Act index c.Listed(h)[c.At] with no bound, and Listed() offers only columns a row holds a value in plus the groups. So f or a click on Fields over an empty ungrouped table, or a reload to fewer filled columns while the dialog is open, panics on the next keys bar.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on a Sheet: 'listed with no records: []' then 'Keys() panicked: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0'; after SetRecords(nil) with At=3, 'index out of range [3] with length 1'; 4 of 400 random walks hit columns.go:331. Tables that open ungrouped: workspaces/groups, welcome/customize, tutorials, flow's workspace/remotes; flow opens the same dialog over the same Listed() (flow/views.go:251, by reading).
findings.fix: Clamp At in one place as Columns.Card already does at columns.go:48, giving a dialog with esc alone when nothing is listed. List a table's fields when it has no rows.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. Ungrouped sheet, no records: Listed() is [], f or a click on Fields opens the dialog, then Keys() and space panic 'index out of range [0] with length 0' (columns.go:331, :220). Also on the real workspaces screen with no group: up, f panics. SetRecords(nil) at At=3 panics [3] with length 1. Flow not run.

findings.title: Two kittui on one presets file lose each other's presets and favorites of the same table
findings.claim: KeepPresets re-reads the file but sets this table's list to the one the caller built from what it read at start, so a preset another kittui saved for the same table since is dropped; favorites likewise. The comment's promise that what another screen saved since stays holds for other tables only.
findings.evidence: Two sheets of 'things' on one file, a.saveAs("from a") then b.saveAs("from b"): 'file holds ["from b"]'; a stars Compact, b stars Default: 'favorites: ["Default"]'. Flow passes its in-memory list the same way (flow/views.go:269-277), and the existing two-writers test covers two different tables only.
findings.fix: Give the store the change, not the result: KeepPresets takes a function applied to the table's list as the file holds it. Or re-read the table's list before SaveAs, Rename, Delete, and Star.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: two sheets of one table on one file leave ["from b"], favorites ["Default"]. But it needs two kittui processes saving presets of the same table at once, and store.go:117-119 promises only every other table's are kept; sheet.go:913-914's 'another screen's' is the loose wording. Real silent loss, not high.

findings.title: Starring a view moves the view and leaves the cursor, so the next press acts on another line
findings.claim: A starred view moves to the favorites, first in the presets dialog and the presets' menu, and neither moves its At with it, though shift with up or down does. Space twice in the dialog stars two views, and * in the menu leaves the keyboard on a heading.
findings.evidence: Dialog: cursor on Compact, space, cursor now on Default, second space gives starred=[Compact Default]. Menu: at=6 was Compact, after * at=6 is the heading 'built in'; TestAStarredViewIsAFavoriteTheFileKeeps sets presets.At by hand after the star, which hides it.
findings.fix: After a star, put At on the line of the view starred.

findings.title: The store's writers share one temporary name and take no lock
findings.claim: Every writer writes presets.json.new and renames it, with nothing locking read, change, and write. Two writers at once truncate each other's temp file, fail a rename with ENOENT, let a reader see a short file, and let a stale read win.
findings.evidence: Four writers, 500 KeepLast each: '1099 of 2000 writes failed (first: rename .../presets.json.new .../presets.json: no such file or directory)'. Flow calls KeepLast on every panel change and drops the error (flow/flow.go:655).
findings.fix: Use os.CreateTemp beside the file for the name. Hold an advisory lock or a lock file around read, change, and write.

findings.title: The wheel's cost test asserts 8 ms of wall time and fails whenever the machine is busy
findings.claim: TestATurnOfTheWheelOverTenThousandRowsIsWellUnderAFramesTime fails any run slower than 8 ms by the clock, and the gate runs it with coverage and every package side by side (bin/ci:76). Its comment that a turn does not cost every row is not true either.
findings.evidence: On this shared machine (load average 60 to 85) it failed 14 of 14 runs without -race, at 15 ms to 44 ms, and passed with -race, where the budget is 80 ms. Whether it fails on the project's runner was not checked.
findings.fix: Assert that a turn does not draw the rows again, as the test above it does, or count work such as calls of Drawing.Draw or allocations, in place of the clock.

findings.title: A workspace path with [ in it hides every team preset, and sharing a view there makes it vanish
findings.claim: ReadTeam builds a glob pattern from the folder's own path and drops Glob's error, so a path holding a glob class reads as no presets without a word, while WriteTeam writes there. In flow, Share with team then removes the view from the person's and finds it in neither list.
findings.evidence: Folder 'plain': wrote 1, read 1; folder 'my [old] repo': wrote 1, read 0, err=<nil>. Flow's share path is flow/team.go:66-78, by reading.
findings.fix: Read the table's folder with os.ReadDir and test the suffix. Report a folder that does not read.

findings.title: Two groups whose names read alike in the heading share one spot
findings.claim: NamesIn finds each group's name by searching the drawn heading from its start, so two groups of one name both land on the first: the second takes no click or stop, and a click on its fold folds the rows' level. Known since 11-10 in part (Components 5 fixed the search by id), still open for this case.
findings.evidence: packages/packages ships the pair: includes is a list whose one value is named member, beside a groupable field labelled member. Grouped by both, the control line reads '▾ member ▾ member ▾ 3' and BarNames gives {member 4 10} and {includes 4 10}.
findings.fix: Have grid's group give each name's span as it draws it, or search for each name after the end of the one before.

findings.title: A level's fold is kept by its depth, so it lands on another level once the groups change
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 8), still open: ToggleLevel writes LevelKey(depth) and nothing clears or moves it when the panel's groups change.
findings.evidence: Grouped by kind then note, note's level closed, kind ungrouped: only headings remain and every row is folded away, with outline map[group1:false].
findings.fix: Key a level by its field's id and the rows' level by a name of its own, or drop the level keys in SetPanel when Groups() changes.

findings.title: A move of the cursor draws every row again, and a wheel turn still walks every row
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (its #92 row), still open for a Sheet: the line cache is keyed by the row under the cursor, so each down draws all rows. Frozen and SelectedRows copy the whole outline with grid.Every several times a frame, drawnFor sorts every open and selected key per call, and Selected is quadratic.
findings.evidence: Under load: down plus draw 3.4 ms at 300 rows, 74 ms at 3,000, 232 ms at 10,000; a wheel turn 8.7 ms at 1,000 and 30 ms at 10,000, 67 ms with all selected; Selected() 555 ms at 10,000 and 9.4 s at 40,000. The < and > keys are linear now, not quadratic as on 11-10.
findings.fix: Draw only the window's rows, or key the cache by row and redraw the two rows the cursor left and reached. Keep the frozen and selected counts with the rows built, and use a set in Selected.

findings.title: Flow and Sheet each implement the keeping of presets, so each fix is owed twice
findings.claim: Sheet's keep, keepStarred, favor, saveAs, rename, choose, and managed have near copies in flow, down to the notices' words, because flow is a Host of its own and holds no Sheet. G3-1, G3-2, G3-3, and G3-12 are each in both.
findings.evidence: Read flow/views.go:261-297 against sheet.go:916-948: the same KeepPresets and KeepFavorites calls with the same in-memory arguments and the same failure notices.
findings.fix: One presets controller in table that both hosts hold (the views, the file, the notice), or move flow's stages onto Sheet.

findings.title: The preset line can name a view the panel has left, and Save can be lit on a view it says is unchanged
findings.claim: Views.Is accepts the panel as the chosen view auto-grouped (Table.Grouped), PresetEnabled compares with the saved view alone, and saveAs leaves Grouped as the view before set it. The selector can read a view unstruck while Save is lit, and Save then writes the automatic group into the view.
findings.evidence: After Save As Mine and the sort taken off again: is="Mine" same-as-Mine=false save-enabled=true. Mine applied over rows it auto-groups: groups=[kind] is="Mine" save-enabled=true.
findings.fix: Clear Grouped in saveAs and rename, and give PresetEnabled the same test Is uses.

findings.title: A name is not unique across the table's own, the team's, and the person's views once files change
findings.claim: SaveAs and Rename refuse a taken name, but nothing checks what is read, so a catalog that gains a preset of a name the person used, or a team file pulled with that name, gives two views of one name. The person's can then be neither applied, renamed, nor deleted.
findings.evidence: With a person's Compact in the file: menu lists Compact under 'built in' and again under 'mine', the dialog lists it once, and Mine("Compact") is false. Chosen takes the first, so both menu lines apply the table's own.
findings.fix: On reading, rename the person's view that clashes, for example 'Compact (mine)', and say so once.

findings.title: In the presets dialog, d deletes at once with no way back, and leaves the cursor past the last view
findings.claim: d on a person's view writes the file without it straight away, with no confirmation and no undo. After deleting the last view listed, At is one past the end, so no line is under the keyboard until up.
findings.evidence: listed=[Default Compact Mine] at=2, press d, listed=[Default Compact] at=2, and the keys bar reads 'esc close ↑↓ move'.
findings.fix: Clamp At after a delete. Ask once before deleting, or keep the view deleted last for an undo.

findings.title: ctrl+a drops the rows selected that the search hides
findings.claim: Sheet.Selected says a row stays selected though the search hides it, and space keeps it, but SelectAll clears Picked whole before selecting what shows.
findings.evidence: leek selected, search 'pear', ctrl+a: Selected() is [pear], and leek is still gone once the search is cleared.
findings.fix: Clear and set only the keys of the rows shown.

findings.title: The catalog's check lets through what a table later indexes by, and a null stage panics
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 15), fixed in part: fields without renderings and stages without a preset are now refused. Still accepted are an unknown type, an unregistered rendering (a nil func call at render.go:90), an unknown placement, a preset naming a field the stage lacks, and two presets of one name; a null stage panics in check.
findings.evidence: ReadCatalog on a stage with all five gives err=<nil>; ReadCatalog on {"stages":[null]} panics with a nil pointer dereference. Registered and DrawsGlyph have no caller outside tests.
findings.fix: Add a Catalog.Check that a screen runs after it registers its renderers, covering types, renderings, placements, and presets. Refuse a null stage in ReadCatalog.

findings.title: WritePresets writes over a file that does not read, where its siblings refuse
findings.claim: WritePresets drops readFile's error and writes, while KeepPresets, KeepFavorites, and KeepLast refuse the same file and leave it. Its one caller today is flow's migration after the file was found missing, so nothing is lost now.
findings.evidence: Over a version 1 file holding a preset, WritePresets returns err=<nil> and the file then holds the new stages alone.
findings.fix: Refuse as the others do, a missing file apart.

findings.title: Team presets are found by file and removed by slug
findings.claim: ReadTeam takes every *.json and trusts the name inside it, while RemoveTeam and WriteTeam go by Slug(name). A file named by hand, or two files with one name after a merge, are listed and cannot be deleted or renamed from kittui.
findings.evidence: a.json and b.json both naming Shared: read 2 presets with no error; RemoveTeam fails with 'remove .../things/shared.json: no such file or directory'; 2 remain.
findings.fix: Keep each preset's file path as read and remove that. Refuse, with the file named, a second file of one name.

findings.title: Smaller things known since 11-10 and still open
findings.claim: Folding still switches on the tab menu's words (11-10 Components 30); a label wider than 16 cells, or 14 with the filter mark, is still not clipped in the fields dialog (Components 22); ItemViews, DrawsGlyph, and Registered still have no caller outside tests (Components 29).
findings.evidence: outline.go:357 reads case "Show More", "Show Less"; columns.go:138 pads the label with pane.Pad, which leaves a wider text as it is; 'hidden bypassers' in audit/waivers is 16 cells.
findings.fix: Name the folds by a type, clip the label, and remove or use the unused exports.

areas.title: kittui grid, form, pane, tabs, style, palette
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 15 source files in scope (6,538 lines). Sampled tests and one golden; verbs.json and 39 goldens unread. Ran the six suites (pass), go vet (clean), 24 throwaway tests in a copy, kit help from a scratch copy, and an exhaustive pane.Frame/Window check. Read table, flow, kit, app callers only to settle findings.
areas.summary: 27 findings in kittui's grid, form, pane, tabs, style, palette: 4 high, 9 medium, 14 low; 15 new, 12 known since 11-10 and still open. Highest: the form panics from keys alone (kit flow: --jq, then issues) and pre-chooses options nobody chose; pastes are dropped; Enter on an optional pick takes its first row with no way to clear it; group values differing by case interleave. New grid bugs: the rows' fold folds nothing when headings join; summaries and multi-line titles are measured wrong. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused a report file, and I did not work around it; everything is in this result. Reproductions: out/G4/work/tui/internal/*/zz_review*_test.go.
strengths: pane.Frame holds its contract over every n to 14, room to 12, want, first, and last: never longer than the room, always shows first, marks agree with its ends.
Widths are terminal cells throughout; pane.Clip, Tail, and Cells keep a line's width exact with two-cell glyphs cut at either edge.
grid.Panel never changes the map it was given (with), so a panel is safe to hold and compare.
The widths cache is keyed by the first row's address and count, holds the slice so the address cannot be reused, and is locked.
The form asks kit for choices and the match off the update loop, and matched drops an answer about a command line that changed since.
form.Quote is right for an empty word, a quote inside a word, and --name=value.
The form has a golden for each of the 40 verbs; the grid, tabs, and palette tests read as specifications.
tabs did not panic at widths 0 to 11, and MenuAt and StaleAt match what View draws.

findings.title: A one-of row's choice lands on another row when an earlier row changes, and the form panics
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 1, rated critical there), still open. Collect keeps a row's choice by its ordinal in the walk, choose returns it unchecked, and group indexes n.Alternatives[f.Chosen][0] with it.
findings.evidence: Live form, keys only: kit flow, down down, tab x3, space (--jq), up up, tab x6, space (issues): Update panics 'index out of range [2] with length 2' (same for six other stages). In kit packages, choosing --inactive then the second usage line leaves 'add' chosen and the command line 'kit packages add'.
findings.fix: Key a choice by the group's path in the grammar, drop the choices of rows that left, and bound chosen in choose.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with keys only through Model.Update: kit flow panics 'index out of range [2] with length 2' for issues through releases; packages gives ['add']. fields.go:293 returns the stale ordinal's choice unchecked, fields.go:265 indexes it. Reachable: the palette opens any verb's form (app.go:118, palette.go:498). Bubble Tea recovers and ends kittui.

findings.title: A paste is dropped: nothing in the form or the palette takes tea.PasteMsg
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 4), still open. Bubble Tea 2.1.1 turns bracketed paste on unless View.DisableBracketedPasteMode is set, shell.View does not set it, and neither Update has a case for tea.PasteMsg.
findings.evidence: On kit commit's --message lines, tea.PasteMsg{Content:"#1 a pasted subject"} leaves input empty and the command line empty while typing works; in the palette's search the query stays empty. grep -rn PasteMsg projects/tui finds nothing.
findings.fix: Route a paste to the control that types, as typed text, in one place both screens share.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: PasteMsg leaves the form's input and the palette's query empty; typing works. No PasteMsg in any non-test Go file under projects/tui; form/model.go:130 and palette/palette.go:382 have no case; shell/view.go:15 leaves DisableBracketedPasteMode unset, and bubbletea v2.1.1 cursed_renderer.go:140 then turns the mode on.

findings.title: Enter on an optional pick takes its first row, and nothing takes the answer back
findings.claim: The keys bar names Enter 'next' on every field, but on a Pick it sets the value to the row under the cursor, the first row when nothing was typed. Backspace only erases the filter, so no key clears a pick.
findings.evidence: kit new file, focus on optional --rule: one Enter gives values=["a"] and the command line 'file --rule=a'; backspace, backspace, space leave values=["a"].
findings.fix: Enter with nothing typed and no cursor move goes on without taking; backspace on an empty filter clears an optional pick, named on the keys bar.
findings.verdict_note: Enter taking the row is designed and tested: the list draws '⏎ takes it · type to filter' (model.go:976; edges_test.go:55), and tab skips the field. What stands: the keys bar says '⏎ next' (model.go:245), and an optional pick once taken cannot be cleared (model.go:532 only erases the filter). Reproduced values=['a'] sticking.

findings.title: Closing the rows' level folds nothing when every innermost heading stands on its parent's line
findings.claim: group draws the rows' fold from Shows(len(at)) and table.ToggleLevel writes LevelKey(len(groups)), but FoldAway hides rows by Shows(Levels(rows)), and Levels is one short when the inner headings all join the outer lines.
findings.evidence: Grouped by a then b, rows (x,p) and (y,q), outline {LevelKey(2): false}: heading reads 'a b ▸ 2', both headings show ▸, Levels is 1, and FoldAway folds 0 rows. With a third row (y,r) Levels is 2 and the rows fold.
findings.fix: Take the rows' level from the groups the panel found among the columns, not from the heading keys drawn.

findings.title: Group values that differ only by case interleave into several headings sharing a key
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 6), still open; taken from that list and re-run, not found in my own pass. Entries sort by natural, which ignores case, while headings are cut by exact value.
findings.evidence: Labels Bug, bug, Bug, bug give 'Bug 1 | 1 | bug 1 | 2 | Bug 1 | 3 | bug 1 | 4': four headings, two pairs with one key each.
findings.fix: Break ties of natural by the exact text in group's compare.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: 'Bug 1 | 1 | bug 1 | 2 | Bug 1 | 3 | bug 1 | 4'. ranked falls to natural, which lowers runes (grid.go:151), so the stable sort keeps input order; same() compares exact values (panel.go:624), and keys repeat. Needs case variants alternating in input order, as labels across a workspace's members may.

findings.title: A cell's summary does not count toward its column's width, so the closed row clips it
findings.claim: need sets n to the summary's width, then overwrites it with the first value's width for every cell that does not wrap, against its own comment.
findings.evidence: Cell{Values:{a,b}, Summary:"12 things"} needs 1, not 9; a cell with Summary '~/code/kit +1' draws '~/code/ki…' in an 80-cell pane with room to spare. flow/repos.go:125 and table/json.go:70 build such summaries.
findings.fix: n = max(n, width(first+more)) instead of the assignment.

findings.title: A title of several lines needs the sum of its lines, so other columns are cut for no reason
findings.claim: need measures a value with ansi.StringWidth, which gives a newline no width, so a wrapping cell of several lines needs them end to end and fit shrinks the other columns to capWidth.
findings.evidence: A title of 12 lines of 12 cells needs 144; in an 80-cell pane the 32-cell column beside it is drawn 'a-rather-long-b…' on every row, closed and open, with 30 cells empty.
findings.fix: For a wrapping cell take the widest line of each value.

findings.title: A chosen flag in a row adds a required toggle: a stop nobody sees, or a second block at the bottom
findings.claim: Choosing an alternative that is one flag adds a required, inert Toggle after the row. Under a vertical row it is not drawn but is still a stop; under a side-by-side row it is drawn again at the top margin after everything else.
findings.evidence: kit context, choose --claude, press down: focus 1 of 2, no ▸ on the screen, space does nothing. kit audit, choose --json: '--json' with its description appears again below 'policy', focusable and inert.
findings.fix: Add no field for the flag an alternative opens with and have Collect record it from the row's choice, or skip such a field in move and Layout.

findings.title: Hiding down to one column makes every row an aside: folds, the header, and parents stop working
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 7, rated high there), still open. grid tells a row from a heading by len(r.Cells) > 1, hide runs before FoldAway, and nothing stops Placed(id, Hidden) at two columns.
findings.evidence: Palette's shape grouped by group with description hidden, 'files' closed: its row 'context' still shows, Header gives no line, Parent gives -1; with the last column hidden each row draws blank.
findings.fix: Tell rows from asides by Row.Aside; until then refuse the hide that leaves fewer than two columns, as Blanked does.

findings.title: A click anywhere right of the last tab selects it, or drops its menu
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 9), still open. hit gives the last tab whose start is at or before the column, with no upper bound.
findings.evidence: Two tabs, canvas 18 cells on a 118-cell screen: hit(100) is 1, a click at column 100 selects tab 1, and OnSelected(100,1) is true once it is selected.
findings.fix: Return -1 where at >= l.width.

findings.title: The drawer finds a row's alternatives by a count the walk does not share
findings.claim: alternatives counts every group of several alternatives in the grammar, while Fields counted only those in chosen alternatives, so a nested row can be matched to a group of another usage line.
findings.evidence: kit tools, second usage line, run chosen: the row 'install | update | path | run' finds [--json | --jq], vertical is false, and '<command>… required' is drawn at the top margin outside its row.
findings.fix: Keep on the Field what the drawer needs (its alternatives, or whether it nests), set by the walker.

findings.title: A literal after leading optional groups opens no alternative
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 12), still open; taken from that list and re-run. opens reads an alternative's first node only.
findings.evidence: Fields(tools, Answers{Literals:{"run"}}) chooses the first usage line and the command line is empty, so kit tui tools run opens the wrong form.
findings.fix: Skip optional nodes before the first required one.

findings.title: The grammar is walked three times, each counting groups its own way
findings.claim: walker.group, emitter.group, and drawer.alternatives each re-derive which group a row is from a running count, and the counts agree only by convention.
findings.evidence: G4-1 and G4-11 are both that convention failing.
findings.fix: One walk that gives each row an identity (its group's path) and its alternatives, read by Collect, CommandLine, and Layout.

findings.title: refreshExtension runs kit on the update loop
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 13), still open. enter and New call runner.Extend, a kit process, inside Update, while tryRun and fetch ask kit off the loop.
findings.evidence: By reading: kit/kit.go:176 is r.run("syntax", verb, "--extend", …), called from model.go:808 with no command around it.
findings.fix: A command and a message, as fetch is.

findings.title: The palette panics on a page that is empty or does not end in a newline
findings.claim: text[strings.Index(text+"\n", "\n")+1:] slices one past the end when the text holds no newline. kit's pages end in a newline today, so it is latent.
findings.evidence: pageMsg{page:""} panics 'slice bounds out of range [1:0]'; "one line, no newline" panics '[21:20]'.
findings.fix: _, body, _ := strings.Cut(text, "\n").

findings.title: The palette's page wrap squashes the argument table's columns
findings.claim: page rebuilds every line from strings.Fields, so runs of spaces inside a line go, also on lines that fit, and kit's pages align arguments in columns.
