findings.evidence: '  --json      the stages…' comes out '  --json the stages…'; a real page (kit help --text commit) has '    --all             stages…' with continuation lines indented 22, which no longer line up.
findings.fix: Leave a line that fits as it is; wrap a longer one after its first run of two or more spaces, hanging at that column.

findings.title: The cursor's band stops at kit's own reset
findings.claim: Band reopens the band after \x1b[m only, but kit help ends bold with \x1b[0m (help.sh:280,315,362), and those lines are the palette's open row. pane.Restyle takes both forms.
findings.evidence: Band("\x1b[1mUsage\x1b[0m", 12) gives '…Usage\x1b[0m       \x1b[m': the padding is off the band.
findings.fix: Reopen after \x1b[0m too, or normalise it on the way in.

findings.title: The filter's none misses a row whose raw value is an empty string, which groups head as none
findings.claim: passes takes NoValue as len(raw) == 0, while key and groups take Raw [""] as no value; table/read.go:197 appends an empty JSON string as a raw value unless the field sets Empty.
findings.evidence: A row with Raw [""] under the filter none gives 0 rows.
findings.fix: NoValue passes where no raw value is non-empty.

findings.title: A filter value that reads as a range is a range on any field
findings.claim: passes tries Range on every value whatever the field's type, and the popover offers a text field's own values.
findings.evidence: A row whose value is '1-2', filtered by '1-2', gives 0 rows.
findings.fix: Read ranges only for the fields table.Ranged names.

findings.title: A wildcard field's lines change order between rebuilds, and a line without -- is dropped
findings.claim: wildcardValues ranges over a map, so the lines reorder on each rebuild and backspace takes an arbitrary last one. The dropped line is known since 11-10 (Components 27), still open.
findings.evidence: Five options gave 5 distinct orders in 200 builds; 'hole=value' vanishes on the next rebuild and '--bare' becomes '--bare='.
findings.fix: Sort the keys in wildcardValues or keep the lines as typed; refuse a line that is no --x=y with a note.

findings.title: A click on the column before a cut, right-aligned, linked cell opens that cell's link
findings.claim: For a right-aligned cell LinkAt starts the word at col.x + col.w - width(face), left of the column when the view cut it narrower than its value.
findings.evidence: At width 50 a 30-digit linked number cut to 15 cells answers for x = 18 to 32, the text of the column before it.
findings.fix: Clamp start to the column's first cell and measure the face as closedLine clips it.

findings.title: A group's heading wider than the pane loses its depth's indent
findings.claim: An open heading that does not fit goes through pane.Wrap, which drops leading spaces, and Draw then reads the indent back from the line and finds none.
findings.evidence: At width 40, grouped by a then b, the depth-1 heading 'a value that is rather long,' starts at column 2 where its sibling 'short 1' starts at column 4.
findings.fix: Cut the indent off before wrapping and put it before each line.

findings.title: A list's answer writes its note under whichever field has the keyboard, and an older answer can land last
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 14), still open. choices sets m.note whatever the focus is, and others leaves the list's own values out of asked, so two flips' reads answering out of order leave older rows as fresh.
findings.evidence: By reading only; a test with a runner that answers out of order would settle it.
findings.fix: A generation per key; write the note only when the list has the keyboard.

findings.title: natural misorders negative and fractional numbers
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 26), still open. natural compares digit runs as unsigned whole numbers.
findings.evidence: natural("-5","-3") is 1, natural("1.5","1.10") is -1, and two runs of 23 digits compare equal.
findings.fix: Compare parsed floats where a field's type is number.

findings.title: pane.Window spends a line to say one row is hidden; pane.Frame never does
findings.claim: Frame moves a start of 1 to 0 so it never hides one row it could show; Window, which the tables, welcome, and tutorials use, does not.
findings.evidence: Window(10, 5, 1) gives start 1, end 4, above, below: a line saying 1 is hidden in that row's place.
findings.fix: The same rule in Window, or one function for both.

findings.title: The tabs' package comment describes a layout the code does not have
findings.claim: The comment says tabs that fit share the line in proportion to their widths; layout (tabs.go:310) lays each at its own width and runs the line under the bar to the edge.
findings.evidence: Two tabs on a 120-cell screen take 18 cells; the rest is the rule.
findings.fix: Say what layout does.

findings.title: Small duplications that will drift
findings.claim: palette.under copies grid's unexported under, sgr is the same regexp in grid and pane, and appLabel is in form and palette. palette.go:378 also reads n and calls a pointer method that changes it in one return, an order Go leaves open.
findings.evidence: A small program shows gc calls first, so the return works today.
findings.fix: Export grid.Under, share sgr from pane, and call fetch on its own line.

areas.title: kittui shell, app, the command, screens, the kit client, sources, the opener
areas.coverage: Read whole every non-test file in scope (kit, source, opener, screens, app, shell, testkit, transcript, cmd/kittui); sampled tests, flow's callers, kit's bash. Ran go test, -race, vet, cover (100%) and reproductions under out/G5/work (review*_test.go.off). findings.md is NOT written: the Write tool refused report files; everything is in this result.
areas.summary: 25 findings: 3 high, 9 medium, 13 low; 21 reproduced. High: a form's verb is exec'd where kittui started, not in the workspace switched to (known 11-10, still open); a paste types nothing anywhere (known, still open); a kit child that prompts on the terminal is stopped in its background process group, its prompt drawn over the screen, until the limit or forever for an action (new; Setsid fixes it, tested). Medium: same-name workspace changes remake nothing, a successful kit reported failed when a grandchild holds its pipes, a poll that stops silently, kit run on the update loop, multi-line refusals, --workspace=none welcome, symlinked folders, a vanished folder misreported. Seven findings were in the 11-10 review.
strengths: partial (kit.go:316) keeps a stage's document when kit exits 1 after printing one, only for a JSON object or array; it closes 11-10's empty-refusal finding and is tested from both sides.

A call that ends takes its whole process group with it: SIGTERM, half a second, SIGKILL, and a bounded wait for the pipes, with a test that nothing is left. Keep the group kill if G5-3 moves it to a session.
Every call that can hang has a limit and a context, and the error says which ended it.
Answers go to kit as argv, never through a shell, and after --, so paths with spaces and answers starting with - are safe.
Late answers are dropped by number everywhere (a load's gen, a walk's count, the root's asked, a screen's epochs); the same pattern fixes G5-13 and G5-15.
The root gives kit flow's words to every app it makes (Taking), closing 11-10's Apps 6.
A screen that cannot open over a new workspace gives way to the welcome with kit's line before anything is closed.
source.Clock and testkit.Clock keep waits out of tests; the nine packages are at 100.0% of statements, clean under -race and go vet.
kit.Installed reads kit.yml as the loader's pinned does (quotes, a comment beside, the manifest fallback).
The keys bar is derived from the path to the keyboard, and Layers gives keys, clicks, the bar, and drawing one order; neither is written per screen.
The walk for clones runs off the update loop, bounded by depth and count, skipping .git, hidden folders, and node_modules.

findings.title: A form's verb runs where kittui started, not in the workspace the person switched to
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 3), still open: main execs with the runner it made at start (Exec chdirs to r.Dir), while the root moves its own runner to the picked workspace's checkout and opens Help with that one. The form's choices are read in B and the verb runs in A.
findings.evidence: Test over the fake kit: kit welcome started in A, PickMsg{B}, Help, OpenMsg{version}, shift+enter logs "kit [version] exec'd in .../001" where .../001 is A and B is .../002. With commit, submit, or tidy that changes the wrong repository.
findings.fix: The root exposes its runner (or the form's result carries the runner it was made with) and finish execs with that. Decide separately what a verb does while a group is shown.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced through main.run over the fake kit: kit welcome started in A, PickMsg to repository B, Help, palette.OpenMsg{version}, shift+enter; execKit got r.Dir = A. main.go:55/75 keep the start runner by value; screens.go:234-239 move only the root's copy, which screens.go:493 gives Help. kit re-reads pwd (1st.sh:52), so the verb runs in A.

findings.title: A paste types nothing anywhere in kittui
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 4), still open: Bubble Tea 2.1.1 has bracketed paste on by default, so a paste arrives as tea.PasteMsg, and no code in projects/tui handles it. shell.Type reads KeyPressMsg.Text alone and the root gives a paste to the screen under an open dialog.
findings.evidence: A real tea.Program fed a\x1b[200~/Users/me/code\x1b[201~b received key:a, pastestart, paste:/Users/me/code, pasteend, key:b. A PasteMsg sent to the root left the Open Repository dialog's Typed unchanged and the focused search empty.
findings.fix: shell.Type (or a shell.Pasted) takes a paste's content as typed text, newlines dropped. The root gives PasteMsg to the open dialog first and each screen to the control that types.
findings.verdict_note: No PasteMsg or DisableBracketedPasteMode anywhere in projects/tui, and no bubbles text input. A real tea.Program wrote ESC[?2004h and delivered key:a, pastestart, paste:/Users/me/code, pasteend, key:b. tea.PasteMsg sent to the root left opener.Typed and the focused search unchanged; screens.go:325 has no case for it.

findings.title: A kit child that asks on the terminal is stopped, its prompt drawn over the screen, until the limit
findings.claim: grouped starts kit with Setpgid, a background process group of kittui's terminal, and sets nothing that stops git, ssh, or gh from prompting; only marks:incoming guards itself (marks.sh:119), the git fetch of incoming and every Act verb do not. A read of /dev/tty there gets SIGTTIN: the stage hangs for its 2 minute deadline, an action forever (Act has no limit).
findings.evidence: Under tmux, a fake kit doing printf 'Password...' >/dev/tty; read x </dev/tty through Runner.Rows showed STAT T in ps, the prompt on the pane, and err=context deadline exceeded only at my 6 s limit. With Setsid in place of Setpgid the same call answered at once, nothing drawn, and the kit package's tests still passed.
findings.fix: Use SysProcAttr{Setsid: true} so the child has no controlling terminal and a prompt fails fast (the group kill by -pid still works). Also add GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 to the client's environment.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced under a pty (script): the fake kit, and real git ls-remote against a local 401 server, both showed STAT T with PGID != TPGID, the prompt written to the terminal, and Rows ending only at the deadline. Only marks.sh:119 guards; flow.sh:580 does not. Narrow point: gh itself does not prompt without a TTY on stdin.

findings.title: A workspace that changes its folder or members, but not its name, remakes and reloads nothing
findings.claim: answered calls the place moved only when kind or name differs, and kit names a repository by its member, so Open Repository on a worktree or second clone of the repository shown closes the dialog and moves only the root's runner. Screens made keep reading the old folder, screens made later read the new one; a group whose members changed is likewise only retitled.
findings.evidence: Test: with github.com/o/a shown at .../002, an openedMsg for the same name at .../006 set root runner.Dir to .../006 while the welcome kept its typed search and epochs stayed empty.
findings.fix: Compare the checkout too, and a group's members, and remake (or Refresh All) when either differs.

findings.title: A kit that exits 0 while a grandchild holds its pipes is reported as failed, 2 s later
findings.claim: grouped sets WaitDelay, so cmd.Run returns exec.ErrWaitDelay for a command that succeeded; outputTold and Act treat any non-ExitError as kit failing to run, and outputTold drops the stdout it has. Which helper holds the pipe in practice I did not establish.
findings.evidence: A fake kit of echo '[]'; (sleep 6) & exit 0 gave from Rows, Act, and Workspaces alike: err=.../kit: exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete after 2s, Rows with out="".
findings.fix: Where the error is exec.ErrWaitDelay and cmd.ProcessState.Success(), return stdout with no error; where the exit was non-zero, build the ExitError as usual.

findings.title: A poll whose first read fails stops for the session and tells no one
findings.claim: Known in part since 11-10 (Apps 15), still open: Take turns the poll off on a first failure and sets no wait, and Off() is read by nothing outside tests. One slow forge at start leaves no stage ever stale and Watch offered with nothing to wait on, until Refresh All.
findings.evidence: Test: a read that fails once then would answer gave took=Failed, no wait set, off=true, and Ask returned nil afterwards. grep finds no non-test caller of Off() or of source.Failed.
findings.fix: A failed first read waits and asks again as a later failure does (the wait may grow). The screen that draws watching reads Off() or the last error.

findings.title: Opening an app, Help, or the palette's search runs kit on the update loop
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 13), still open: show and answered call open, which runs kit flow --stages (flow.OpenApp) or kit syntax --list (app.OpenHelp) inside Update, and app.find runs List there too, each with a 30 s limit and no cancel. app.open does the same kind of read as a command.
findings.evidence: Measured with the copied kit: kit flow --stages 0.62-0.67 s, kit syntax --list 1.27 s. The screen takes no key for that long on every first switch, cross-app link, and workspace pick.
findings.fix: Open at once and read the stages or the verbs as a command, as app.open does.

findings.title: A refresh does not end a stage's first read
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 12), still open: NewLoad leaves stop nil and the first Read runs in the screen's context, so Again has nothing to end, against the file's header. Over a slow git fetch that is two fetches of the same remotes at once.
findings.evidence: Test: three reads started as Read, Again, Again ended with context canceled, <nil>, <nil>: only the second was ended, the first ran to its end beside the third.
findings.fix: NewLoad (or the first Read) makes a context and stop of its own, as Again does.

findings.title: Kit's stderr reaches the screen whole: several lines break the frame, a long line loses its remedy, an empty one says nothing
findings.claim: ExitError.Error() is all of stderr minus one leading ❌, where Act picks the last ❌ line; the root puts it on its last line, in the dialog, and in the workspace menu uncut and unwrapped. A silent non-zero exit gives an empty text, which the root and the opener show as nothing (flow's refusalOf covers it).
findings.evidence: Stderr of a git warning plus kit's ❌ line gave a 31-line view on a 30-line screen, the ❌ before git's line. A real kit refusal in my run was 250 cells, its 'run:' remedy at the end, past the screen's edge.
findings.fix: One client function gives kit's line (last ❌ line, else last line, else 'exited N with nothing on stderr'), used by Error() and Act. The root truncates with an ellipsis or wraps.

findings.title: kit --workspace=none welcome opens with a refusal in the workspace menu
findings.claim: kit-welcome hands kittui --workspace=none, main takes it as the group, and the root's first ask treats any word without / or : as a group to keep, running kit workspaces --use=none, which kit refuses, so the workspace is never asked. Every screen's menu then starts with that ❌ line (the drawing read from BooksMenu.lines, not driven).
findings.evidence: With the real kit in an isolated home: Model{start:"none"}.ask("none")() gave err='none' is no workspace in .../workspaces.yml, while kit --workspace=none workspaces --current --json answers {"kind":"none",...} with exit 0.
findings.fix: ask keeps no last group for none, and keeps one only for a pick, not for what kittui started with.

findings.title: Find clones under a folder that is a symbolic link finds nothing
findings.claim: findClones walks with filepath.WalkDir, which follows no link, the root included, while Folders lists with os.Stat, which does. A linked ~/code, or anything under /tmp on macOS, shows its folders and then reads as having no clones.
findings.evidence: Test: code linked to real holding repo/.git: Folders gave [repo], findClones(code) gave [], findClones(real) gave [repo]; a linked folder inside was listed ([alias repo]) and not walked.
findings.fix: Resolve the root with filepath.EvalSymlinks before the walk, keeping Under as typed for the rows' names. State in the header whether links below are followed.

findings.title: A folder that is gone reads as 'kit: no such file or directory'
findings.claim: Every call sets cmd.Dir = r.Dir and reports a failed start as '<kit>: <error>'; Go's error for a missing working directory names the program. A worktree removed by kit settle or kit tidy while kittui reads it makes every stage say kit is missing.
findings.evidence: An existing kit with Dir /nonexistent/dir with spaces gave '.../kit: fork/exec .../kit: no such file or directory', the same words a missing kit gives.
findings.fix: On this error (or before the start) os.Stat(r.Dir) and say the folder is gone, with the remedy: Open Repository or the workspace menu.

findings.title: Esc on Open Repository does not take back the ask, and ctrl+q does not quit under a dialog
findings.claim: opened drops an answer only by number, so one arriving after esc closed the dialog still switches the workspace. The root passes every key but ctrl+c to an open dialog, though shell.Quit says ctrl+q quits on every screen.
findings.evidence: Test: enter (busy, asked=1), esc (closed), then the answer: workspace became group w. Ctrl+q produced a quit with no dialog and nothing, dialog still open, under Open Repository and Settings.
findings.fix: Esc while busy increments asked. Both key cases let shell.Quit through as they let ctrl+c.

findings.title: The error path skips root.Close(), and an outside SIGINT ends 1 with a line
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 26), still open: run returns failed(err) before root.Close(), and Bubble Tea returns ErrInterrupted for a SIGINT that is no key. Kit's children, each in its own group, run on, and the exit is 1 with a ❌ line instead of 130.
findings.evidence: Read main.go:68-73 and Bubble Tea tea.go:692-797; not run.
findings.fix: Close the root before checking the error, and map tea.ErrInterrupted to 130 with nothing printed.

findings.title: Enter twice on a verb opens its form twice, the second over whatever the first holds
findings.claim: Each palette.OpenMsg starts a grammar read with nothing marking one as under way, and opened replaces m.form unconditionally. A second answer replaces a form already being filled, and a late answer for verb A wins over B.
findings.evidence: Test confirmed two presses yield two openedMsg; I did not get text into the fake's form to show it lost.
findings.fix: Number the asks as screens.asked does, and drop an answer that is not the latest or that arrives while a form is open.

findings.title: A submodule is drawn as a worktree of the repository that holds it
findings.claim: desk takes any .git file whose gitdir contains /.git/ as a linked worktree; a submodule's is gitdir: ../../.git/modules/<path>. The submodule stands under the superproject's heading and takes its member mark.
findings.evidence: Test with real git: the walk gave 'app desk work/app' and 'app/vendor/lib desk work/app'.
findings.fix: Treat only a gitdir ending in /.git/worktrees/<name> as a worktree; anything else is its own desk.

findings.title: Tab completion can cut a character in half
findings.claim: complete shortens the shared prefix a byte at a time, so folders that share only the first byte of a multi-byte character leave invalid UTF-8 typed.
findings.evidence: Test: folders é1 and è2 completed to "\xc3".
findings.fix: Shorten by rune with utf8.DecodeLastRuneInString.

findings.title: The Open Repository dialog reads the folder from disk at least twice per frame
findings.claim: list calls Folders (os.ReadDir plus os.Stat of every entry), and body (from View) and Keys each call list, as move, Wheel, and Click do. A large folder or a network mount is read whole on every draw.
findings.evidence: Read from the code; not timed.
findings.fix: Keep the names with the dialog and read again only when what is typed changes its folder or its start.

findings.title: Past its limit, a call over a workspace names the option, not the verb
findings.claim: The limit's line is built from args[0], which over and Workspace make --workspace=<name>.
findings.evidence: Test: Quota over group team and Workspace("team") each gave 'kit --workspace=team took longer than 300ms; it was stopped'.
findings.fix: Name the first word that is not an option.

findings.title: An Azure DevOps repository cloned over HTTPS is titled _git/<repository>
findings.claim: repoName keeps the member's last two segments and workspaces:url-member keeps the URL path as is, so dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo shows as _git/repo in the title, favorites, and recents. The third provider reads differently from the other two.
findings.evidence: Test: repoName gave o/a for GitHub, sub/repo for a GitLab subgroup, _git/repo for the Azure HTTPS member.
findings.fix: Drop a _git segment, in kit's member or in repoName.

findings.title: shell.Over still trusts its top line
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 2); the guard in Over itself is still absent, so a negative top panics. Whether a caller can still pass one (the column menu at HeaderTop() == -1 was the 11-10 case, outside my scope) I did not check.
findings.evidence: Over([]string{"a","b"}, []string{"x"}, -1, 0) panics with index out of range [-1].
findings.fix: Add i >= 0 to the bound in Over so no caller can crash the program by where it stands a box.

findings.title: A search longer than the screen makes the menu bar a cell too wide
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 18), still open: once SearchAt is 0 the line is two gap cells plus width-1 of search, and pane.Clip cuts the end where the caret is.
findings.evidence: Test: 50 characters typed at 40 columns gave a 41-cell line ending in an ellipsis, the caret gone.
findings.fix: Count the two gap cells and keep the tail of what is typed.

findings.title: testkit.Drive treats a batch's messages differently from a single command's
findings.claim: The doc says Drive gives every message produced and holds a tea.QuitMsg back; in the batch branch messages are queued but never added to produced, and a quit is fed to the model. A test looking for a message or the quit in produced depends on whether the screen happened to batch.
findings.evidence: Test: a single command gave produced [{}]; a batch of two gave produced [tea.BatchMsg] alone while the model saw both; a batch with tea.Quit fed tea.QuitMsg{} to the model.
findings.fix: The batch branch appends each message to produced and holds a quit back, as the single branch does.

findings.title: The client runs kit three ways, each with its own mapping of errors
findings.claim: Rows and Me (no limit, output), telling (a limit, outputTold), and Act (own buffer, own ExitError) each build the command, environment, and error; append(os.Environ(), "NO_COLOR=1") is written twelve times. They already differ, and fixes for G5-3, G5-5, and G5-12 have three places to go.
findings.evidence: A cancelled context is 'context canceled' from Rows and '<kit>: context canceled' from Act; a refusal is all of stderr in one and the last ❌ line in the other.
findings.fix: One call(ctx, opts) taking the limit, the progress writer, and whether stderr joins stdout, returning one error type; the methods become its callers.

findings.title: Two small tables written as code
findings.claim: needsTerminal pairs verbs with lines and --text remedies in four ifs, beside appVerb and open's switch, so a verb that gains a screen is added in three places. openLine says what a click does with seven fields tested one by one in Click and cloneClick.
findings.evidence: Read main.go:85-153 and open.go:472-482, 613-637, clones.go:399-443.
findings.fix: One table of verb, screen, and remedy in main; one enumerated 'does' field on openLine.

areas.title: kittui welcome, tutorials, workspaces, markdown, fix, syntax
areas.coverage: Read whole: all non-test Go and catalogs of the six packages; tests sampled, goldens not read. Ran go test, -race, -cover (100.0% each), vet; scratch reproductions through Update; shipped welcome and tutorial pages at 80 and 120 columns; kit syntax for all 52 verbs. Not run: a real terminal, bats. findings.md refused by the harness.
areas.summary: 23 findings: 3 high, 6 medium, 14 low; 22 confirmed by a run or by the code, 1 plausible. Two crashes: PgDn on a welcome step whose search shows no check (known since 11-10), and a click on blank space where the hidden table's Fields button would be, on the workspaces screen with no group and on tutorials before kit answers. No screen takes a paste (known since 11-10). Medium: a hidden check's fix can run, the workspaces dialog cuts what is typed, customize's links break from a subfolder, a group's uncloned members go unsaid, a ## in a code block breaks the terms and customize tables. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the file.
strengths: fix.Words and fix.Process never hand a command to a shell: anything past plain words is copied, not run, and the cd <folder> && that kit writes is read back by the rules shown writes it with.
welcome reads a click on a row's buttons against the line as it was drawn, copied or not, and only on the row's first line; tests cover a click on a row off the cursor and on keep inside a note.

source.Load numbers its reads, a later read cancels the one before, every screen ends its context on quit and Close, the progress channel never blocks kit's read, and -race is clean on all six packages.
The pages' order and ids match the bash exactly (order against the awk in welcome:pages, idOf against ${name#*-}), and syntax.Render and syntax.Key match syntax.jq line for line.
Terms, customize, tutorials, and workspaces are JSON catalogs on one shared table.Sheet, so presets, search, grouping, and the fields dialog come with each.
The workspaces screen never writes the file: every action is a kit workspaces call, the owner's name is checked by a pattern before it goes into --from, and a rename or delete tells the root.

markdown is small and right on what ships: all five welcome pages and all nine tutorials render cleanly at 80 and 120 columns, tabs in code blocks included, and every kittui: link names a real screen or stage.
100.0% statement coverage on all six packages, no stale syntax fixture, and a bats test that keeps the fixtures current.

findings.title: PgUp, PgDn, Home, or End crashes kit welcome on a step whose search shows no check
findings.claim: page indexes rows[min(max(at+n,0), len(rows)-1)] with no guard for an empty rows, and leaving the search sets inPane true whether or not the step has a row. Known since 11-10 (then lines 698-707), still open.
findings.evidence: Driving Update against the fake kit with 2, /, zzzz, enter, PgDn gives panic: index out of range [-1] at welcome.go:969. down has the guard at line 948; page does not.
findings.fix: Return from page when len(rows) is 0, and give the pane the keyboard from the search only when the step has rows.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced against the fake kit: step 2, /, zzzz, then enter, down, esc, or tab leaves inPane true with 0 rows (welcome.go:667); PgUp, PgDn, Home, and End each panic index out of range [-1] in page (welcome.go:969). down guards at 948, up returns early; page has no guard and no caller adds one.

findings.title: A click where the hidden table's Fields button would be crashes the workspaces and tutorials screens
findings.claim: Both screens pass a click to their sheet while they draw no table (workspaces: no group yet, reading, or refused; tutorials: reading or no tutorials), which opens the fields dialog of a sheet with no records, and Columns.Keys indexes an empty Listed. Any table.Sheet with no records, as an empty Flow tab, is plausibly hit too.
findings.evidence: With no group, a click on line 2 at columns 97-118 of 120 (57-78 of 80) gives index out of range [0] with length 0 on the next View; the same on tutorials at columns 97-105 before kit answers and with an empty catalogue. No group yet is the workspaces screen's first-run state.
findings.fix: Pass no click and no key to a sheet that is not drawn, and make Columns.Keys answer an empty list. Click Fields on an empty Flow tab to settle how far it reaches.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced by sweeping clicks. Workspaces with no group, reading, and refused: panic index out of range [0] with length 0 at line 2, columns 97-118 of 120 (57-78 of 80). Tutorials while reading and with an empty catalogue: columns 97-105. With records, no click panics. The Flow part is the reviewer's guess; not tested.

findings.title: Nothing takes a paste, so a git URL or command pasted into a workspaces dialog types nothing
findings.claim: Bubble Tea v2.1.1 delivers pasted text as tea.PasteMsg because shell.View leaves bracketed paste on, and no Go file under projects/tui handles PasteMsg. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: grep -rn PasteMsg over projects/tui finds no handler; cursed_renderer.go:140 sets bracketed paste unless DisableBracketedPasteMode. The workspaces prompts ask for a git URL, a folder, or a command, which people paste; the three searches drop a paste too.
findings.fix: Let shell.Type take a paste as typed text, and route PasteMsg in each screen to the control that types.
findings.verdict_note: No PasteMsg handler anywhere under projects/tui; shell.View (shell/view.go:15) leaves bracketed paste on, and bubbletea input.go:36 delivers PasteMsg. Sent to the model: the New Workspace prompt's typed and the search's Query stay empty, while a key press types. Not driven on a real terminal; typing still works, so "high" is arguable.

findings.title: With no row shown, the cursor stands on the first check kit printed, and c and r act on it
findings.claim: find returns index 0 when the step has no row, and fixUnder then reads m.checks[0], whatever step it belongs to. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: With the failing jq check first, 3, /zzzz, enter, r on setup, which draws no check matches the search, ran welcome --fix jq and the keys bar offered c copy r run. With the real kit the first check is tool-bash, which has no fix, so the wrong run needs another order.
findings.fix: fixUnder and keeping require slices.Contains(m.rows(m.step), m.cursor).

findings.title: A workspaces dialog cuts what is typed, what to type, and kit's refusal at its right edge
findings.claim: The dialog's lines go through shell.Dialog, which truncates each with … at the right, in a box of 64 text cells at most, so the end of a long line being typed, with its cursor, is off the box.
findings.evidence: At 80 columns, a name and four repositories read › tools github.com/empowerite/kit github.com/empowerite/edge github.com/e…; the hint ends or a…, and a refusal ends kit can find …, without its reason.
findings.fix: Draw what is typed with pane.Tail so its end stays in sight, and wrap the hint and the refusal.

findings.title: Customize's where links are joined to the folder the command was typed in, not the repository's root
findings.claim: readPages finds the pages under git's top level, but rooted joins each relative link to runner.Dir, which is where kit welcome was typed. A link with a scheme and no ://, as mailto: or kittui:, becomes a path too.
findings.evidence: With runner.Dir at <root>/src/deep, the kit.yml link of the Packages part is <root>/src/deep/kit.yml, which does not exist, while <root>/kit.yml does.
findings.fix: Carry the folder the pages were read from in pagesMsg and root the links there; leave any link with a scheme alone.

findings.title: kit welcome started over a group never names the members not cloned
findings.claim: m.workspace is set in Open alone, main opens the first welcome on the zero workspace, and the root does not remake the screen when kit answers with the group kittui started on, so a WorkspaceMsg changes the title only.
findings.evidence: Open(runner{Group: w}, kit.Workspace{}) then the WorkspaceMsg of a group with an uncloned member: the title reads - w 2 and setup has no not cloned: line; the same screen opened on that workspace has it.
findings.fix: On shell.WorkspaceMsg, keep msg.Workspace in m.workspace as well as in m.books.

findings.title: A ## or ### inside a code block is read as a section of a terms or customize page
findings.claim: hasTopics and parseIn track comments but not fences, so a heading-like line of a code block starts a section or turns the page into one of topics. The shipped pages have no such block; a house package's replacement can.
findings.evidence: A customize page with ## Hooks, a fenced shell block holding ## install the tools and ### then the hooks, and ## Policy gives hasTopics true and one row, then the hooks under install the tools; Hooks and Policy are gone.
findings.fix: Track the fence in both loops, as markdown.render does, and skip headings inside one; do the same for pageTitle.

findings.title: The three screens each repeat the chain of menus, search, and notices, and differ
findings.claim: welcome, tutorials, and workspaces each write their own order of app menu, workspace menu, recent searches, search, and table layers, in keys, clicks, and wheel. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: G6-2, G6-10, G6-12, G6-13, G6-18, and G6-19 are each one copy that differs from its siblings; workspaces also keeps no past searches and drops a catalog's read error (workspaces.go:47) where the other two panic with a message.
findings.fix: One shell type that owns the menu bar's controls and answers a key, a click, and a wheel turn, asked first by each screen.

findings.title: In tutorials, a key the focused search does not take moves the cards or focuses the control line
findings.claim: The comment says what the search does not take nobody does, but shell.NotSearch falls through to the cards' keys; welcome returns after its search in every case (welcome.go:656-675).
findings.evidence: With the search focused, shift-tab moved the cursor from card 2 to card 1, and up left controlled() and search.Focused both true with the keys bar naming the search alone.
findings.fix: Return after the switch when the search has focus.

findings.title: A click under the tutorials pane opens the card the pane clips
findings.claim: cardAt bounds a click above the pane and not below it, and shownUntil always shows one band however tall.
findings.evidence: At 120x10, with a 5-line pane and an 8-line card, a click on the blank line under the pane (y=8) and on the keys bar (y=9) opened Tutorial 1 in the browser.
findings.fix: Return -1 when y is at or past paneTop + paneHeight().

findings.title: The wheel scrolls welcome's pane under the open tab menu
findings.claim: The guard names appMenu, books, and recent and leaves tabMenu out, though the comment says a turn while a menu is open scrolls nothing.
findings.evidence: After : a wheel turn over the pane moved the offset from 0 to 3; with the app's menu open it stayed 0.
findings.fix: Add m.tabMenu.Open to the guard.

findings.title: A welcome step's search keeps the keyboard after a click on another tab
findings.claim: Each step keeps its own shell.Search with its Focused flag, and choose does not take the focus away from the step it leaves.
findings.evidence: On toolchains, /, a click on the setup tab, a click back: the search has the keyboard again and 3, which selects a step from anywhere, was typed into it.
findings.fix: choose sets Focused false on the search of the step it leaves.

findings.title: A code block inside a comment is drawn
findings.claim: The fence case stands before the comment case, so a fence inside <!-- opens a block, where the package says a comment is dropped. Front matter that ends at the file's last line, or is empty, is drawn as text.
findings.evidence: A page of before, <!--, a fenced secret code, -->, after renders the line secret code; ---\ntitle: x\n--- renders --- title: x ---.
findings.fix: Test comment before the fence, and let withoutFront take a closing --- at the end of the text.

findings.title: A web address wider than the pane is cut, so it cannot be read or copied
findings.claim: WrapWords clips a word wider than its line with …, and a link's URL, kept so the person has it, is one word.
findings.evidence: At 30 cells https://github.com/empowerite/kit/blob/main/docs/integrations/forges.md is drawn https://github.com/empowerite…; at 80 columns a URL of 76 characters loses its end.
findings.fix: Break such a word across lines, as pane.Break does, or scroll it as a block.

findings.title: welcome draws a link to a kittui screen as a link and follows none
findings.claim: welcome's wide drops the links markdown.Wide gives and click has no case for one, while the text is still drawn underlined; tutorials follows the same link (tutorials.go:646).
findings.evidence: page.go:20 reads lines, _, blocks := markdown.Wide(md, width). No shipped welcome page has a kittui: link; a house page can.
findings.fix: Follow the link as tutorials does, or draw it as plain text on welcome.

findings.title: 12 of 52 verbs have no syntax fixture, so the round-trip test does not cover them
findings.claim: assign, close, facts, gather, ready, settle, trust, tutorials, unassign, uninstall, workspace, and workspaces have no fixture, and tests/syntax.bats:283 checks only the files that exist. Known since 11-10 (10 of 44 then), still open.
findings.evidence: I printed the 12 with kit syntax and ran the Go tests over them: all pass, and none of the 40 existing fixtures is stale.
findings.fix: Make the bats test loop over kit/bin/kit-* and fail on a verb with no fixture.

findings.title: The workspaces keys bar says esc goes to the tabs, on a screen with none
findings.claim: The table's own segment is appended as it is, so the bar reads esc tabs ↑↓ move → show, and esc tabs ↑↓ move even under no group yet, where there is no row.
findings.evidence: keys().String() with no group: = menu - workspace / search n new │ esc tabs ↑↓ move. tutorials removes table.TabsHint (view.go:142-149).
findings.fix: Drop the TabsHint binding here too, and append the segment only while the table is drawn.

findings.title: What kit did is not clipped on the workspaces screen's last line
findings.claim: bottom is a space and m.note.Text, and style.Bottom does not clip; a refusal there is plain text, where tutorials clips its note and draws a refusal as one.
findings.evidence: A note of 267 cells gives a last line of 268 cells on a 120-column screen. What the terminal then shows, cut or wrapped, I did not see.
findings.fix: pane.Clip(m.note.Text, m.width-1), and style.Refusal for a note that is not Done.

findings.title: Add an Owner's Repositories… lists 1000 repositories at most, and GitHub's alone
findings.claim: The command is gh repo list <owner> --limit 1000, so a larger owner is cut at 1000 with no word, and there is no GitLab or Azure DevOps form though kit reads all three.
findings.evidence: The words are built at workspaces.go:391-392. I did not run gh; a run against an owner with more than 1000 repositories would settle it.
findings.fix: Say in the dialog that the list stops at 1000, or page it; offer glab and az forms or name GitHub in the menu's line.

findings.title: The tab-bar tutorial says welcome has no tabs
findings.claim: The page says the welcome and the tutorials have none, but welcome's steps are a tab bar with numbers, counts, and the : menu; its Refresh also has no R key, which line 36 gives every tab menu.
findings.evidence: welcome.go:15-17 names internal/tabs as the steps' bar, and menu.go:22 says Refresh has no key because r runs a check's fix.
findings.fix: Say the tutorials have none, and that welcome's Refresh has no key.

findings.title: The title's fallback reads _git/repo for an Azure DevOps remote
findings.claim: repoOf takes the last two path segments of origin's URL, which is wrong for Azure DevOps and for a GitLab subgroup; it shows only until kit says the workspace.
findings.evidence: repoOf(https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo) gives _git/repo, and https://gitlab.com/group/sub/repo.git gives sub/repo.
findings.fix: Drop a _git segment, or leave the fallback empty and wait for kit's answer.

findings.title: What a check's id means is written in three places
findings.claim: An id's step is a case in bash, its column a Go table, and a terminal's finding is told from its heading by a dash in Go and by ^terminal-[a-z]+- in jq.
findings.evidence: They agree only because every terminal key in terminals.json is [a-z]+; a key with a dash would make Go take the heading for a finding and offer keep on it.
findings.fix: Have kit's JSON say each check's column and whether it is a finding, and read it in Go.

areas.title: the gh research against the GitHub provider
areas.coverage: Read whole: gh.md, github.sh, forge.sh, forge.jq, bin/ci. The 34 schemas read by machine (titles, descriptions, property paths, examples). Sampled forge*.bats and callers. Ran jsonschema over 37 examples and 14 fixtures, 23 jq folds, gh 2.103.2 through a loopback proxy. Not run: bats, go, real forges. findings.md not written: the harness refused a report file.
areas.summary: For gh, the product uses 59 of 91 researched capability rows whole or in part (reads 44 of 60, writes 15 of 31), and all 34 schemas describe a call it makes. The research is reference only: the gate checks each schema against its own example, so five schemas and three test fixtures have drifted from the provider. Two bugs from 11-10 remain open: digit-named repositories break ten GraphQL reads, and builds reads 50 runs of any kind. Unused and most valuable: rerun and logs of a failed run, deployment approvals, what is live where, the Projects Status. Smallest design: an x-kit key per schema, examples as the tests' fixtures, and the provider's declaration as one data file.
strengths: Each schema's title is the command as kit runs it, and its description names the provider function, the jq fold, and the upstream type it was typed from; every function named exists but one. Keep this: it is most of a machine-readable link already.
All 37 schema examples validate, and all 23 example and fold pairs I ran produce the seam's documents, so the examples are good enough to become the tests' fixtures.

The research records what was checked live (refusal texts, scopes, 404 for a non-admin), and the provider matches those texts in forge/github:off, forge/github:refused, and forge/github:alerts-refused.
The provider never draws a partial list as whole: it compares totalCount, says {"limited": N}, or fails, and a refusal names the scope to add or who can grant it instead of a bare gh auth status.
Cost is designed and written down: the points of each GraphQL read, ETag marks that cost nothing on a 304, and a ten-minute verdict for a scanner that is off.

The GitHub provider implements contract 6 and lacks only swimlanes, so every tab of Flow, Changes, Issues, Delivery, People, and Trust has a native read behind it; apps.jq passes the seam's documents through unchanged.
The seam's versioned contract, forge/<name>:lacks, and forge:capabilities are the right base for a declaration read as data; the proposed design extends them and undoes nothing.
The GitHub App's JWT and token reach curl on standard input, never in argv, and every path part is checked before a request is made.
tests/forge-conformance.bats states plainly what a fake cannot prove about a real forge.

findings.title: Nothing ties the gh schemas to the code or to the tests, and all three have drifted
findings.claim: The gate validates each schema only against the example embedded in the same file, so the 34 schemas are reference with a self-check: no test loads one, no code is generated from one. gh.md:311-313 says each is 'a JSON Schema of the fields kit reads', which does not hold.
findings.evidence: Fields the provider reads that the schema lacks: issue-list `milestone` (github.sh:485), open-prs `latestOpinionatedReviews` (github.sh:539), releases `assets[].digest` (github.sh:42), branch-protection five fields (forge.jq:1087-1091), rulesets actor `slug`/`login` (forge.jq:1117); issue-iterations (github.sh:881) has no schema. out/I1/check.py (Python jsonschema): 37 of 37 examples valid, but 3 of 14 conformance fixtures invalid against the schema of the command they fake (closing.json and open-prs.json lack required `pageInfo`, issues.json lacks `labels`).
findings.fix: Run every schema example through its forge:: fold in the gate (all 23 pairs I folded by hand already pass), and make the tests' fixtures come from, or validate against, the schemas. Then add the missing fields and the issue-iterations schema.

findings.title: A repository or owner named in digits breaks ten GraphQL reads (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Owner and name go to `gh api graphql` with `--field`, which types 2048, true, false, and null, so GitHub gets an Int for a `String!` variable and open changes, merged, bots, deployments, iterations, rulesets, and closing issues all fail with 'run: gh auth status'. The research table (gh.md:317-327) codifies the flag.
findings.evidence: Reproduced the client side with the pinned gh 2.103.2 through a loopback proxy (out/I1/proxy.py): `--field name=example` sent "name":"example", `--field name=2048` sent "name":2048. This is item 15 of the 11-10 review; teams (github.sh:856) and issue-iterations (github.sh:893) already avoid it.
findings.fix: Use `--raw-field owner=… --raw-field name=…` in the ten places and in the research table and schema titles. Add one test with a repository named 2048 whose fake refuses a non-string.

findings.title: The builds stage reads the 50 newest runs of any kind, though the research lists the filters (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: The seam promises the 20 newest runs no pull request owns, but the provider asks for 50 runs of every event and filters afterwards, with no `limited` mark. A repository busy with pull requests draws few builds or none.
findings.evidence: Fifty `pull_request` runs made from run-list.schema.json's example and folded through forge::github_builds give `[]`. gh.md:215 already documents `--branch`, `--event push`, `--event schedule`, and `--event workflow_dispatch`.
findings.fix: Ask per event with the documented filters, or say `limited` when the 50 held fewer than 20 unowned runs.

findings.title: A third of the researched gh capability is unused, and the most useful part is cheap to add
findings.claim: 32 of 91 capability rows in gh.md have no call in the product: Flow and Changes name a failed check and step but cannot rerun it or show its log, Delivery draws `waiting` but not who must approve nor what is live in each environment, and kit writes sub-issues it never reads. Every forge-backed tab (Flow, Changes, Issues, Delivery, People, Trust) is otherwise read from GitHub natively.
findings.evidence: Used whole or in part by section: pull requests read 24/24 and write 5/5, issues read 8/12 and write 10/11, Projects read 2/6 and write 0/3, Actions read 5/6 and write 0/4, releases and deployments read 5/12 and write 0/8. grep over kit/, bin/, .github/, and kittui finds none of `run rerun`, `run cancel`, `log-failed`, `pending_deployments`, `latestCompletedDeployment`, `subIssues`, `stateReason`, `generate-notes`, `statuses/`, `--milestone`.
findings.fix: Backlog in this order: 1 rerun, cancel, and failed log of a run; 2 pending approvals, read and approve; 3 what is live where (one GraphQL request); 4 the Projects Status field (one more fragment in the query at github.sh:884); 5 sub-issue read; 6 set an issue's milestone or iteration; 7 a forge release from kit release; 8 the gate as a commit status. None blocks v0.1.0.

findings.title: The research is not structured to drive code: its links to the product are prose
findings.claim: A schema names its provider function and jq fold only inside its `description` text, the GraphQL selections live in bash strings no schema is checked against, the capability tables are markdown cells with no key joining a row to a seam call or feature, and the status column is per service. The seam's feature table is three bash arrays (forge.sh:287-309) repeated in its header prose.
findings.evidence: The 'Schemas of its output' table is hand-kept: 33 of 34 rows equal the schema titles and one is abbreviated. One named fold, forge::github_dismissals, does not exist (three alert schemas).
findings.fix: Three steps, each useful alone: (1) an `x-kit` key per schema, {provider, call, feature, fold, args}, and a generated gate loop that folds each example; (2) one copy of each answer, the tests' fixtures drawn from or validated against the schemas, with additionalProperties false on GraphQL answers; (3) forge_features, forge_feature_of, and each provider's contract and lacks in one JSON file that forge.sh reads and `kit generate` uses to fill the seam header, the schema table, and a 'kit uses' column in gh.md. A live, opt-in run of each read against a real repository is a fourth, larger step.

findings.title: gh.md and the schema descriptions are stale against the provider in eight places
findings.claim: The open issues' command lacks `milestone` (gh.md:104, :344, and the issue-list schema title); gh.md:46 omits `latestOpinionatedReviews`, Bot, and Mannequin; Projects has status `none` (gh.md:16) though kit reads its iterations, and gh.md:150 says it answers a status field nothing reads; gh.md:346 gives a `gh pr list` command kit runs in neither form.
findings.evidence: gh.md:45 and github.sh:505 say 18 points a page while tests/forge-conformance.bats:1628 says 19. Three alert schemas say `forge/github:bypasses` reads the dismissed alerts and `forge::github_dismissals` folds them; grep finds no such function, and gh.md:54 says a dismissal is not read again.
findings.fix: Correct the lines, and generate the schema table from the schema files.

findings.title: Six kinds of call the product makes are not in the research
findings.claim: Undocumented: `gh pr edit --add-label/--remove-label`, the releases mark, the open issues' project items by GraphQL, the six GitHub App REST calls made with curl, the event payload's pull request number, and `gh release delete`; `releases/latest` as kit runs it has no schema. The six App calls also have no caller outside the seam and its tests at this commit.
findings.evidence: Of 29 kinds of call the product makes, 20 are documented whole, 4 in part, 5 not. grep finds none of `add-label`, `installation`, or `access_tokens` in gh.md or its schemas; the bots verb is still a plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-12-bots-1-kit-bots.md).
findings.fix: Add the rows, a schema for each answer kit reads, and a GitHub Apps section. Say in the release notes that bot-accounts has no verb yet, or land the verb first.

findings.title: The zero time the research says gh prints for a missing time fails the runs read
findings.claim: run-list and run-view schemas record that gh renders a missing time as 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z, and the folds do not guard it: one such run fails the whole builds stage with 'run: gh auth status', and one such job drops every job of its run silently.
findings.evidence: The schema's example with `startedAt` set to the zero time, folded through forge::github_builds and forge::github_jobs, ends in `jq: error: invalid gmtime representation`. Whether GitHub still sends a run with no start is not confirmed; a live read of an old Enterprise Server would settle it.
findings.fix: Treat a time before 1970 as null where the folds call `epoch`, and put the zero time in the schemas' examples so the fold is tested.

findings.title: The latest release is guessed, though the research lists two exact reads
findings.claim: github_releases marks the release created last as latest, while GitHub marks the one set as latest, by default by version and date, so a back-ported release is drawn as latest.
findings.evidence: Folding 2.0.0 created 1 October and 1.9.5 created 5 October gives `{"tag":"v1.9.5","latest":true}`. gh.md:265 lists `gh release list --json tagName,isLatest` and `releases/latest`; one live repository with a back-port would settle it.
findings.fix: Spend one `releases/latest` request, or say in gh.md:253 and the seam header that it is an approximation.

findings.title: A Dependabot finding is drawn without its package, a field the schema already holds
findings.claim: The schema declares `dependency.package.name`, but the fold keeps the advisory's id and the manifest's path alone, so a Trust findings row names no package.
findings.evidence: The schema's example folds to `{"number":1,"rule":"GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm","severity":"high","state":"dismissed","path":"package-lock.json",…}`. Other declared and dropped fields: an environment's `wait_timer`, an artifact's `workflow_run.head_branch` and `head_sha`.
findings.fix: Make the rule `<package> (<ghsa id>)`, or give the alerts' document a field for what is affected.

findings.title: A fork's pull request with the same branch name answers for the branch
findings.claim: `gh pr list --head` filters by the branch's name alone and on-branch takes the first, so pr-for-branch, pr-state-for-branch, and pr-head-for-branch may answer with a fork's change.
findings.evidence: gh 2.103.2's help: `--head string  Filter by head branch ("<owner>:<branch>" syntax not supported)`. Not reproduced; a test with two fixtures on one head name would settle it.
findings.fix: Add `isCrossRepository` to `--json` and take the first that is false, as the open changes' query already reads it.

areas.title: the glab research against the GitLab provider
areas.coverage: Read whole: glab.md, all 26 schemas, gitlab.sh, forge.sh, forge.jq, 1st.md, bin/ci, fake-tool, tracker/forge.sh. Sampled: forge-conformance.bats (GitLab worlds), other forge tests' names. Ran: a validator over 31 examples and 29 fixtures, jq folds over every enumerated status, 81 bats tests (all pass). Not verified: a real GitLab; glab is not installed.
areas.summary: findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused a report file from a subagent, so this result is the only copy and the tables are compressed into I2-11 to I2-13. Reads are well incorporated: 55 of 79 researched capabilities are served (all 28 merge-request rows, 18 of 24 issue rows), and each of the provider's 26 JSON reads has a schema. CI/CD is half used: no build jobs, logs, live-environment or approval reads, and none of 12 writes. The schemas are reference only: the gate checks each against its own examples, and 10 of 29 test fixtures fail them. One status and requested_changes are misdrawn. The capability tables are prose and cannot drive code.
strengths: Every JSON answer the GitLab provider reads has a schema and no schema is an orphan: 26 files for 26 distinct read commands, all listed in glab.md:240-267 with the command as kit runs it; all 31 examples validate.
The gate does check those examples (bin/ci:54-61), and a schema with no example fails it.

The research records GitLab constraints the code then honors, each with a test: order_by=merged_at is 17.2's and an older GitLab is asked again by update (gitlab.sh:283-302); a tier without iterations, protected environments, push rules, or the vulnerability report answers 403 or 404 and is off (exit 3), not a failure; a fork's pipeline lives in the fork's project; GraphQL is read where REST says nothing of a bot; the vulnerability report is read where REST findings are being deprecated.
All 23 capabilities of the merge request Read table and all 5 of its Write table are served by the provider.

Every read goes through forge/gitlab:ask and forge:fold: a failed or non-JSON answer is one line with a remedy, a list is whole or the call fails, and a feature the forge lacks is answered by the seam from `lacks` without running glab.

tests/forge-conformance.bats drives GitLab and GitHub through one world with a fake tool that logs every call; 71 of 71 pass in a private copy, as do 10 of 10 in forge-capabilities.bats. That call log is exactly what a schema check needs.
gitlab.sh's comments state each call's cost in requests (gitlab.sh:346-362), and they match the code.

findings.title: The schemas are checked against their own examples only; the fixtures the provider is tested on fail them
findings.claim: The only consumer of docs/integrations/glab/*.schema.json is the gate loop at bin/ci:54-61, which validates each schema's embedded examples against that same schema; no test, fake, or generator reads them, though 1st.md:117 says a schema is what a provider's fixtures can be checked against. The examples and the conformance fixtures are two hand-kept copies of one world, and they already disagree.
findings.evidence: Validating the conformance world's 29 GitLab fixtures against the schema of the command each answers (validator at out/I2/work/validate.js) fails 10: mrs-open, mrs-list, mr-by-branch, mr-states, gl-merged (no state, sha, updated_at), mr.json (no state, merge_commit_sha, squash_commit_sha, head_pipeline times and user), jobs.json (no created_at), issues.json (no updated_at; one item no labels), gl-project.json (no namespace), and the marks test's milestones fixture. All 31 schema examples pass, and grep for docs/integrations over every .sh, .bats, .go, .ts, .jq, .yml, .json finds no reader but bin/ci.
findings.fix: Add one bats test that, after the world has run, validates every JSON file a `route glab` serves against the schema whose command template matches the route, and fails on a JSON-answering call with no schema (ajv-cli is already a gate dependency). Fill the ten fixtures out and narrow each schema's `required` to what every caller of that command reads, splitting api-merge-requests.schema.json, which serves five call shapes.

findings.title: A GitLab build never carries its jobs, where a GitHub build does, though the research documents the read
findings.claim: forge/gitlab:runs reads pipelines?per_page=50 and gives every run jobs: [] ("A pipeline's jobs would cost a call each", gitlab.sh:586), while forge/github:runs pays that same call for the 5 newest runs. So kittui draws a failed build's jobs and failed step on GitHub (projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:617-643) and nothing under a failed build on GitLab.
findings.evidence: glab.md:149 documents `projects/:id/pipelines/${pipeline_id}/jobs` for a run's jobs and glab.md:141-142 says the failed step is the failed job and its `failure_reason`; grep finds `failure_reason` read nowhere in kit/. forge.jq:382 sets `jobs: []` in build($now) and nothing on the GitLab path fills it.
findings.fix: For the 5 newest runs kept, read `pipelines/${id}/jobs?per_page=100` as open-prs already does, and fold {name, state, took, step} with step the failure_reason of a failed job. Add failure_reason to api-pipeline-jobs.schema.json.

findings.title: A job or pipeline that is waiting_for_callback is drawn failed or cancelled
findings.claim: The research's schemas enumerate 13 job and pipeline statuses (api-pipeline-jobs.schema.json:14-28, api-pipelines.schema.json:33-47), but gitlab_runs and gitlab_build_state each name a subset and send the rest to failed or cancelled. A merge request whose job waits on a callback is therefore failing:gate in kit flow changes while nothing has failed.
findings.evidence: Running each enumerated value through the folds: gitlab_runs gives waiting_for_callback -> "failed", gitlab_build_state gives waiting_for_callback -> "cancelled", and gitlab_pr with one such job gives {"state":"failing:gate","checks":{"state":"FAILURE","failing":"deploy"}}. That GitLab emits the status is the research's claim from docs.gitlab.com, not verified live.
findings.fix: Add waiting_for_callback to the pending list at forge.jq:249 and the running list at forge.jq:418. Add a jq test that feeds every `enum` value of the two schemas to the folds, so a status the schema has and the fold lacks fails the gate.

findings.title: requested_changes is drawn ready, and a GitLab reviewer is only ever requested or approved
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open (that review's forge item 9, then forge.jq:199): approval is true only for detailed_merge_status == "not_approved", so a merge request with changes requested is ready, where GitHub's CHANGES_REQUESTED is blocked:approval (forge.jq:165). The seam promises reviewer states requested, approved, changes, commented (forge.sh:216-217) and GitLab can produce two of the four, as the provider reads only the merge request's reviewers and its approvals.
findings.evidence: A jq run of gitlab_pr with detailed_merge_status requested_changes and green checks gives ["ready",[{"login":"bob","state":"requested","at":null}]]. The schema lists 24 merge statuses (api-merge-request.schema.json:46-71), requested_changes among them, and glab.md names no read of a reviewer's own state.
findings.fix: Use IN("not_approved", "requested_changes") at forge.jq:272. Research, then read, each reviewer's state (plausibly GitLab's merge_requests/${n}/reviewers, not verified here) so changes and commented can be drawn.

findings.title: The research cannot drive code: capability tables are prose, and the provider's declaration is code
findings.claim: Three hand-kept things say what the GitLab provider does and nothing joins them: glab.md's 79 capability rows, keyed by a prose name ("Checks rollup") that is not the seam call (open-prs) and mixing what glab can do with what kit runs in one cell; the provider's contract and lacks functions; and forge.sh's feature table, repeated as two arrays at forge.sh:288-305. The 26 schemas are machine-readable, but their link to code is a sentence in `description`.
findings.evidence: The drift this allows is I2-6 to I2-8: two calls in no page, five fields kit reads in no schema, seven schemas naming a jq def that does not exist. glab.md:43 reads "`glab ci status --branch ...`; kit reads `glab api --paginate ...`", which no program can split into what kit runs.
findings.fix: Add one declaration per provider read as data, e.g. kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.json: {provider, tool, contract, lacks, reads: [{call, run: <glob of the glab arguments>, fold, schema}], writes: [{call, run}]}, which forge/gitlab:contract and :lacks print from. Then one bats test over it and the fake's glab.calls log: every logged call matches an entry, every served JSON validates against the entry's schema, every named fold and call exists, every entry was exercised, and glab.md's schema table plus a new seam-call column agree with it.

findings.title: kit's label calls are in no research page, and other calls are documented as another command or outside the tables
findings.claim: forge/gitlab:pr-label-add and pr-label-remove run `glab mr update --label` and `--unlabel` (contract 3's labels feature, which the drafts stand-in needs), and neither glab.md nor forges.md's coverage matrix has a row for them. glab.md:61-62 gives Set the title and Set the body as `glab mr update --title/--description`, while kit runs `glab api merge_requests/${n} --method PUT --raw-field title=/description=`.
findings.evidence: grep for --label, unlabel, add-label over docs/integrations/*.md finds only tkn.md. Three reads appear only in the schema table or a schema's description, not in a Read table: merge requests on a branch (gitlab.sh:458, 691; glab.md:40 gives `glab mr list --source-branch`), the project's labels (gitlab.sh:370), and a fork's project by id (gitlab.sh:411).
findings.fix: Add a "Label a change" row to glab.md and forges.md, state the PUT and why kit prefers it, and give each Read row the command kit runs first.

findings.title: The schemas are not "only the fields kit reads": 5 fields kit reads are untyped and about 20 typed ones are unread
findings.claim: 1st.md:113 and glab.md:236-238 say each schema holds only the fields kit reads, but gitlab_issues reads .milestone.title and .iteration.{title,start_date,due_date} (forge.jq:335-336) and gitlab_vulnerabilities reads dismissedBy.username, dismissalReason, stateComment (forge.jq:1161-1162, asked for at gitlab.sh:750), none of them typed. With additionalProperties true, an answer with "milestone": 5 validates.
findings.evidence: jq over the schemas gives the issue item's keys as assignees, created_at, iid, labels, references, title, updated_at and the vulnerability node's as detectedAt, id, location, primaryIdentifier, severity, state, title, webUrl. The other way, api-milestones.schema.json requires id, title, state, web_url where the mark reads iid and updated_at alone (forge.jq:241), and environments' slug, tier, external_url, jobs' artifacts[], and protected environments' user_id, group_id, access_level, required_approvals are typed and unread.
findings.fix: Add the five fields, and either drop the unread ones or change the sentence. The fixture check of I2-1 then keeps it true.

findings.title: Statements in glab.md and in seven schemas that the code or the page itself contradicts
findings.claim: glab.md:6-7 says kit reads through `glab api` for every call but the draft and pages each list itself, yet the provider runs glab issue create/update/close/note and glab mr update (gitlab.sh:118, 132, 134, 139, 144, 168, 479, 483, 491), reads five lists over GraphQL, and leaves REST paging to --paginate (gitlab.sh:804-808). glab.md:30 and :33 give `glab api user --jq .username` while glab.md:85 says `glab api` has no --jq, and glab.md:35 says the marks ask pipelines and releases "the same" as order_by=updated_at&per_page=1 and that a mark is the newest updated_at.
findings.evidence: Kit reads pipelines?per_page=10 and releases?per_page=1 (gitlab.sh:236-237) and the releases mark is tag_name and released_at (forge.jq:240). Seven schema descriptions (deployments, environments, issues, merge-requests, milestones, pipelines, releases, line 4 of each) name forge::gitlab_marks where the def is gitlab_mark (forge.jq:237); a script confirmed every other forge:: and forge/gitlab: name in the schemas resolves.
findings.fix: Correct the four statements; `glab api --help` settles which --jq line is wrong. A ten-line bats check that each function a schema names exists would have caught the stale def name.

findings.title: Editing a GitLab release's notes or assets does not move the releases mark
findings.claim: The releases mark is [tag_name, released_at] of the newest release alone, so the releases stage, which draws notes and assets, is not stale after an edit to them, nor after any change to an older release, until a person refreshes. GitHub's mark is an ETag of the list, which moves.
findings.evidence: gitlab_mark("releases") over two answers that differ in description and assets.count gives the same text both times: [["release/0.1.0","2026-10-27T07:30:14.000Z"]]. GitLab's release entity has no updated_at, which the research's schema (api-releases.schema.json) reflects.
findings.fix: Put what the stage draws in the mark: description | length, assets.count, and upcoming_release, over a few releases, not one.

findings.title: The milestones mark depends on sort=updated_desc, which the REST milestones list may not take
findings.claim: `milestones?sort=updated_desc&per_page=1` is read as the newest milestone by update, but as I recall GitLab's REST project milestones list filters by state, title, search, iids, updated_before, and updated_after and takes no sort, ignoring an unknown parameter. If so, the mark holds the first milestone in GitLab's default order, and an edit to any other milestone moves it only when an issue is also updated.
findings.evidence: The research states the parameter as fact at glab.md:103 and in the schema's title and cites no source for it; nothing offline can confirm it. What settles it: that route's parameters in the OpenAPI document glab.md:70 links, or one call against a project with two milestones.
findings.fix: If it is not taken, ask with updated_after=<the last mark's time>&per_page=1, or take the mark from the GraphQL list the tab already reads.

findings.title: Lens answer, table 1: 55 of 79 researched capabilities are served, 1 in part, 23 unused, and no published schema is consumed
findings.claim: By section of glab.md (served/rows): merge requests read 23/23 and write 5/5; issues read 9/13 (unused: linked items L100, closed_by L101, epics and work items L102, work item status L105) and write 9/11 (unused: set milestone L120, set iteration L121); CI read 3/5 plus a run's jobs in part (L149; a job's log L151 unused) and write 0/4; releases and deployments read 6/10 (unused: deployments in an environment L198, a deployment's approvals L201, what is live where L202, merge requests a deployment shipped L203) and write 0/8. Of the 55, 41 run the command the page gives as kit's and 14 serve it another way (owner and URL from the remote, `glab mr view` and `glab issue view` rows through `glab api`, title and body through PUT).
findings.evidence: Each row was matched to its line in gitlab.sh, e.g. L34 rate limits at 530-536, L46 merged at 283-302, L47 members at 707-733, L50 alerts at 740-781, L52 controls at 564-583, L99 open issues at 338-344, L152 artifacts at 29-35, L197 protected environments at 94-103. The published descriptions the page links (REST OpenAPI 3.0 and 2.0, the GraphQL schema dump and introspection results, the CI JSON Schema, the agent configuration schema) are fetched, vendored, or read by nothing; the 26 local schemas cite the OpenAPI document as the hand-typed source of their types.
findings.fix: Unused, by value to a user: (1) a build's jobs and failure_reason, I2-2; (2) a job's log, the answer to why a change is failing:gate; (3) what is live where and a deployment waiting on approval (environments/${id} last_deployment, deployments/${id} approvals, pending_approval_count); (4) the merge requests a deployment shipped; (5) rerun, cancel, start a run, approve a deployment; (6) glab ci lint or the CI JSON Schema in kit lint; (7) report a commit status or record a deployment; (8) linked items, milestone and iteration writes, epics and work items; (9) glab release create and changelog, unused by design as kit release only pushes a tag. Not researched though another forge has the feature: an equivalent of bot-accounts (GitLab answers 3), of bypasses, and of a reviewer's own state.

findings.title: Lens answer, table 2: of the provider's glab calls, all but two are in the research, and every JSON read has a schema
findings.claim: Only gitlab.sh runs glab (grep over kit/), and its 26 distinct JSON reads map one to one onto the 26 schema files, all listed in glab.md:240-267 with the command as kit runs it; no schema is an orphan. The gaps are the two label writes (undocumented), the two PUTs (documented as `glab mr update`), reads named only in a schema (I2-6), and two text outputs kit parses with sed that no page describes: the URL `glab issue create` and `glab mr create` print (gitlab.sh:144-145, 451-452).
findings.evidence: Reads by line: user 272, 532; jobs 31; merge request lists 50, 367, 458, 691, 287, 299; merge request 379; pipeline jobs 390, 398; discussions 401; approvals 402; closes_issues 404, 442; labels 370; projects 411, 611; issue 123; issues 341; iterations 178; seven mark lists 235-238; deployments 79; environments 92, 94; releases 541; protected branches and push rule 569, 571; pipelines 589; GraphQL 311, 618, 711, 744, 789. Writes: 113, 118, 132, 134, 139, 144, 168, 198, 451, 479, 483, 491, 495, 499.
findings.fix: Document the label writes, the PUTs, and the printed-URL parse; the declaration and call-log test of I2-5 would then keep this table true by construction.

findings.title: Lens answer: what the product shows from GitLab
findings.claim: GitLab feeds kit flow and Flow (changes with state, checks, threads, labels, reviewers, closing issues, fork owner; issues with milestone and iteration; builds without jobs; releases with notes and assets; quota; marks), kit changes (reviews, checks, merged), kit issues (milestones, iterations, backlog, underway), kit delivery (artifacts, environments with protection and approvers, deployments), kit people (people, teams, agents), and kit audit (findings, waivers, controls). It also serves the workflow verbs: kit work, ready, linked, settle, gather, assign, close, new issue, and kit policy's facts.
findings.evidence: Callers of each seam call were grepped under kit/bin and kit/modules/bash (apps/issues.sh, apps/changes.sh, apps/delivery.sh, apps/people.sh, apps/audit.sh, issue.sh, tracker/forge.sh, facts.sh, kit-ready, kit-linked). The provider declares contract 5 and lacks attestations, bypasses, swimlanes (gitlab.sh:635-639), so Trust's evidence tab is empty and bot-accounts answers 3 (tests/forge-capabilities.bats:148).
findings.fix: No change asked; the unused capability that would add most to these screens is ranked in I2-11.

areas.title: the az research against the Azure DevOps provider and tracker
areas.coverage: Read whole: az.md, the 19 schemas, docs/trackers.md, forge/ado.sh, tracker/ado.sh, tracker.sh, forge.jq, both bats files. Sampled forge.sh, issue.sh, bin/ci, kit.schema.json. Ran both bats files in a copy (30 pass), my reproductions (out/I3/run/tests/i3*.bats), and a schema check of fixtures (out/I3/validate.mjs). No az, no network: live behaviour unchecked.
areas.summary: Azure DevOps research is about half incorporated. Of 71 capability rows in az.md, 34 are used whole, 7 in part, 26 unused, 4 unavailable on the forge; of 25 az calls the product makes, 22 are documented, 1 has drifted, 2 are missing. The 19 schemas are reference only: bin/ci validates each against its own examples, and 7 test fixtures do not fit them. The provider has never met a live organization. Most serious: work items probably stay open after a merge, a refused close says nothing useful, a configured closing state reads OPEN, token sign-in is unsupported. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused a report file, so everything is in this result.
strengths: Every az call names the organization, project, and repository with `--detect false`, and every answer is shaped by jq, so a fake az drives the whole provider.
The jq folds check types (`strings // error`, `numbers // error`, `arrays // error`), so an answer in another shape is a failed read, never a row of nulls.
A feature the forge lacks is declared in forge/ado:lacks and answered 3; nothing is faked.
Every capped list says so with {"limited": N} (20 runs, 100 artifacts, 50 deployments, 20 teams, 100 members), a 101st environment fails the read as partial, and the tests cover each cap.
`epoch` reads az's Python isoformat times with offsets and fractions, and the tests feed it both.
The research is honest about what it did not verify, in the page and inside the schema descriptions.
The schema table at the end of az.md is exact: one schema for each of the 19 commands whose JSON kit reads, each naming the bash function and jq fold that read it, and bin/ci validates every example.
The tests cover the remote URL forms: https, both ssh forms, visualstudio.com, and an Azure DevOps Server collection.

findings.title: The Azure DevOps provider ships proven against its own fake alone (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: No call of the provider has run against a live organization, and five `az devops invoke` routes carry the Delivery app, the unresolved count, and labels. I3-2, I3-4, and I3-6 are places where I expect the live answer to differ.
findings.evidence: az.md:70: "The `az devops invoke` area and resource names here were not tried against a live organization"; the same at :163 and :211, and in the check-configurations schema's description. tests/forge-ado.bats:8-9: "What only a live organization can prove, that az answers as the fixtures do, is not proven here."
findings.fix: Before v0.1.0, run one recorded smoke against a throwaway organization, each seam call once, and keep the raw answers as the schemas' examples. Otherwise say in the release notes and docs/integrations/1st.md that `ado` is experimental.
findings.verdict_note: The tree admits it: az.md:70, :163, :211-212, the check-configurations schema, tests/forge-ado.bats:8-9; ado.sh has five `devops invoke` call sites (129, 158, 322, 636, 679). But the docs disclaim only those names and the checks' settings; "no call ever ran live" and "known since 11-10" are not provable from the snapshot. A disclosed gap.

findings.title: On Azure DevOps a merged pull request can leave its work items open, and kit never closes them
findings.claim: pr-create links only the branch's leading number with `--work-items` and never passes `--transition-work-items`; a secondary issue gets only `Closes #8` in the description, which the research says Azure DevOps ignores. `kit settle` skips both because tracker:body-refs leaves out forge-owned references (tracker.sh:231).
findings.evidence: az.md:68-69: "Azure DevOps closes no work item from a pull request's body by itself; work items link with `--work-items` and move on completion with `--transition-work-items`"; ado.sh:360-361 claims "the pull request closes it as the forge's own tracker closes an issue". The kit side is read from code; what Azure DevOps does on completion needs a live organization.
findings.fix: Link every issue with `az repos pr work-item add` (az.md:118, never called). Have `kit settle` close the still-open work items pr-closing-issues names on a forge that declares it does not close them itself.
findings.verdict_note: Kit's side reproduced with the fake az: `kit settle 3` on a completed pull request, item 7 linked and Active, body `Closes #8`, exits 0 silently with no `work-item update`; `#` and `AB#` are both forge records; no `--transition-work-items` anywhere. Whether Azure DevOps leaves them open depends on how completion is done; needs a live organization.

findings.title: A close Azure Boards refuses says only "could not be closed", and the default states are not those of the default process
findings.claim: issue-close discards az's output and prints nothing of its own, so a refused state change names neither az's reason nor the setting that fixes it. The defaults Closed and Removed are not states of the Basic process a new organization gets (To Do, Doing, Done), per Microsoft's documentation, not checked live.
