findings.evidence: Reproduced with the fake az refusing the state: `call issue-close 7 completed` gives `status=1 output=[]`, and `kit close --not-planned 7` prints only `❌ #7 could not be closed`.
findings.fix: On a failed state change print the remedy: set forge_settings.ado.closed_state (or removed_state) in kit.yml to a state of the work item's type, followed by az's own stderr line.

findings.title: `kit issues iterations` leaves out `--team`, which az very likely requires
findings.claim: With no forge_settings.ado.team the provider runs `az boards iteration team list --project …`, and the schema says az then takes the project's default team. As I recall the extension (`get_team_iterations(team, timeframe=None, …)`) and its reference, `--team` is required, so the tab would read `run: az login (the iterations could not be read)`.
findings.evidence: The test proves only that the fake answers the call without `--team` (tests/forge-ado.bats:110). `az boards iteration team list --help` settles it; no az is installed here.
findings.fix: If it is required, read the default team first (`az devops project show --project … --query defaultTeam.name`) and pass it.

findings.title: A work item closed to a configured state reads OPEN ever after
findings.claim: closed_state and removed_state are settings, but what counts as closed is the literal list Closed, Done, Removed in three places. The Issues app lists such an item for ever, `kit tidy` never removes its worktree, and `kit settle` comments and closes again on every run.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (out/I3/run/tests/i3.bats): with `closed_state: Resolved`, issue-close sends `--state Resolved`, the item then reads `state after close: OPEN`, and the query still asks `NOT IN ('Closed', 'Done', 'Removed')`. The `ado` tracker with `closed_state: Completed` reads `state: OPEN` the same way.
findings.fix: One definition of the closing states, the three literals plus the two settings, read by ado_closed, the tracker's state, and the WIQL.

findings.title: The provider needs `az login`, though the research names a personal access token as the other way in
findings.claim: `require` and `me` both run `az account show`, which reads the Azure subscription login and fails where only AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT is set, as in an Azure Pipelines job. Every verb that calls forge:require (settle, ready, gather, work) then stops at "run: az login" although the az repos and az boards calls would work.
findings.evidence: az.md:4: az "authenticates with `az login`, or a personal access token in `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT`". Not reproducible offline; `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT=… az account show` on a machine with no login settles it.
findings.fix: When `az account show` fails and a token is set, read the caller from the organization's connection data (`az devops invoke --area Location --resource ConnectionData`, authenticatedUser).

findings.title: The `ado` tracker's `create` drops the body, so `kit gather` loses its task lines
findings.claim: The seam's contract is `create <title> [<body>]` and issue:gather passes the gathered issues as task lines in the body (issue.sh:216), but tracker/ado:create never reads `$2`. Where a record claims `#` for Azure Boards on a GitHub or GitLab forge, the parent is created empty and gather still says "Gathered".
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `tracker:at 'AB#' create "Title" "- [ ] AB#1"` runs `boards work-item create --title Title --type Task --project Claims --org … --output json`, no `--description`, and prints 4600. The forge provider does pass `--description` (ado.sh:209).
findings.fix: Pass `--description "${2:-}"` in tracker/ado:create, and assert it in tests/tracker.bats.

findings.title: The 19 schemas are reference only; nothing ties them to the code, and 7 of the tests' fixtures do not fit them
findings.claim: The only consumer is bin/ci:54-61, which validates each schema's own examples against itself; no test loads a schema, no fixture comes from one, and nothing compares a schema's title with the command the provider runs. The research is close to a declaration but is prose, so it cannot drive code yet.
findings.evidence: With out/I3/validate.mjs, pr.json, prs.json, prs-all.json, merged.json, policies.json, delivery-runs.json, and items.json fail their schema's `required` (e.g. `lastMergeCommit`, `forkSource`, `configuration.settings`, `triggerInfo`, `System.Id`); 12 fit. The provider selects `[System.IterationPath]` (ado.sh:297) while the boards-query schema's title, properties, and example, and az.md:100 and :233, leave it out.
findings.fix: Add `x-kit: {argv, calls, folds}` to each schema, build the fake's routes and answers in tests/forge-ado.bats from argv and the first example, and add two tests: every line of az.calls matches exactly one schema's argv, and each fold gives the same document on its example with undeclared properties removed. A provider file (forge/ado.json: contract, lacks, calls to schemas) can follow, with the docs' kit-status columns generated from it.

findings.title: Azure Boards is implemented twice, and the two copies have drifted
findings.claim: tracker/ado.sh and the issue-* calls of forge/ado.sh run the same eight `az boards` commands and differ where they should not. The closing states are spelled out in both.
findings.evidence: The tracker drops the body (I3-7), passes no `--detect false --only-show-errors`, prints `null` for a missing title where the forge fails the read (`strings // error`), and encodes a project as `${project// /%20}` where the forge uses `@uri`. Its writes require no az and say nothing on failure (11-10 item 26, still open).
findings.fix: One boards.sh, each function taking the organization and the project, called by both providers.

findings.title: `forge_settings.ado.team` is read and documented, and the delivered schema refuses it
findings.claim: The provider reads `team`, and az.md:102 and docs/apps.md:89 name it, but the `ado` block of kit.schema.json has `additionalProperties: false` and no `team`. An editor that follows `$schema` flags it, and `ajv validate -s .kit/kit.schema.json -d kit.yml`, this repository's own gate step, would fail on it.
findings.evidence: `jq '.properties.forge_settings.properties.ado | {additionalProperties, keys: (.properties | keys)}'` gives `{"additionalProperties":false,"keys":["closed_state","removed_state","stand_ins","type"]}`. `kit check` passes a kit.yml that sets it (out/I3/run/tests/i3c.bats), so the setting itself works.
findings.fix: Add `team` to the schema's ado block and to the `forge` row of docs/trackers.md:76.

findings.title: A project or repository with a non-ASCII name is decoded wrong, and every call then fails
findings.claim: forge/ado:decode turns each `%XX` into one code point, so the bytes of a UTF-8 character become separate characters. The mangled name goes to every `--project` and into every page URL.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: origin `https://dev.azure.com/acme/Caf%C3%A9/_git/example` gives `repo: CafÃ©/example` and `repo-url: https://dev.azure.com/acme/Caf%C3%83%C2%A9/_git/example`.
findings.fix: Use jq's own decoder, which the pinned jq 1.8.2 has: `$s | @urid` prints `Café`.

findings.title: The Flow read costs three `az` processes for each open pull request, one after another
findings.claim: open-prs runs `repos pr policy list`, `devops invoke … pullRequestThreads`, and `repos pr work-item list` for every pull request in a loop, and each ask also runs forge/ado:place twice. az takes about a second to start, so 20 open pull requests are 61 runs and about a minute, longer than the 60 seconds a snapshot is used from when its read began (forge.sh:278, :975).
findings.evidence: Read from the code; not measured, as no az is installed here. A snapshot stamped at the start of a read longer than forge_snapshot_seconds is stale when it lands, so the next load reads again.
findings.fix: Read the place once per call, and run the three reads of each pull request in the background, a few at a time.

findings.title: About a third of the researched capability is unused; ranked by value to a user
findings.where: docs/integrations/az.md:68, docs/integrations/az.md:147, docs/integrations/az.md:196, docs/integrations/az.md:101, docs/integrations/az.md:104, docs/integrations/az.md:48
findings.claim: Of 71 capability rows in az.md the product uses 34 whole and 7 in part, leaves 26 unused, and 4 are things the forge cannot give; nearly every Repos and Boards read is used, and nothing of Pipelines writes, classic releases, or approvals. Unused, by value: (1) work-item transition and `pr work-item add`, (2) token sign-in, (3) the build timeline for failed jobs and steps, (4) pending approvals, so a deployment can read waiting, (5) work item relations, (6) `System.BoardColumn` as a native swimlane, (7) `pullRequestStatuses`, (8) classic releases, (9) linked branches.
findings.evidence: Counted row by row against forge/ado.sh and tracker/ado.sh: Repos read 12 used, 3 part, 3 not, 4 none; Repos write 4 of 5; Boards read 7 used, 1 part, 3 not; Boards write 6 used, 3 part, 1 not; runs 2 of 9; environments and releases 3 of 14. forge/ado.sh:498 says of the timeline: "A run's jobs would cost a call each, so every run carries none."
findings.fix: Take (1) and (2) before the release, as I3-2 and I3-6 say. Read the timeline for failed runs only, and pending approvals in forge/ado:deployments, after it.

findings.title: Every failure says "run: az login", whatever az said
findings.claim: forge/ado:ask discards az's stderr and names one remedy for a missing work item, a missing permission, a wrong project, and a missing extension alike; the tracker never checks for the extension, which the forge does at ado.sh:473. The same pattern was reported for GitLab on 11-10 (item 26), and the tracker's silent writes named there are still open.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: with the fake az failing as for a work item that does not exist (TF401232), `call issue-title 999` prints `❌ run: cd … && az login (the title of #999 could not be read)`.
findings.fix: Keep az's last stderr line and print it after the remedy; name `az login` only when az's message is about signing in.

findings.title: az.md is behind the provider in five places
findings.claim: az.md says the provider implements contract 3 and lacks four features, where it prints 5 (ado.sh:86) and lacks twelve (ado.sh:89); its open-issues query has no `System.IterationPath`; :117 says kit writes a task line where the forge provider runs `relation add` (ado.sh:168); the pipeline schema is linked at both `/main/` and `/master/`. Of 25 distinct az calls the product makes, 22 are documented as run, 1 has drifted, and 2 are missing: `devops invoke … pullRequestLabels` (ado.sh:679) and `extension show` (ado.sh:473).
findings.evidence: az.md:23: "It implements contract 3 and declares that Azure DevOps lacks rate limits it shows, cheap marks, releases, and branches linked to a work item"; ado.sh:86: `forge/ado:contract() { printf '5\n'; }`. `grep -n -i label docs/integrations/az.md` finds nothing.
findings.fix: Correct the five, add the two calls, and state the page's introduction and its "no OpenAPI document" paragraph once, not once per service.

findings.title: Two older remote URL forms are refused or misread
findings.claim: A remote with no project segment before `_git`, the short form of a project's default repository as I recall it, is refused on visualstudio.com and misread on dev.azure.com. Whether Azure DevOps still serves these forms was not checked.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `https://acme.visualstudio.com/_git/example` gives "origin's URL names no Azure DevOps repository"; `https://dev.azure.com/acme/_git/example` is taken as organization `https://dev.azure.com` and project `acme`.
findings.fix: When no project segment precedes `_git`, take the project to be the repository's name.

findings.title: A failed Azure Pipelines run names no job and no failed step
findings.claim: forge/ado:runs gives every run `jobs: []`, by choice, to save a call a run. The research has the route, the build timeline with records of type Stage, Job, and Task, each with a result, and GitHub's runs carry jobs and the failed step.
findings.evidence: ado.sh:498-500: "A run's jobs would cost a call each, so every run carries none." forge.jq:382 sets `jobs: []` in `build`.
findings.fix: Read the timeline of failed runs only, which are few, through `az devops invoke --area build --resource timeline`.

findings.title: docs/trackers.md describes the code forge as GitHub or GitLab only
findings.claim: Lines 4 and 21 name GitHub and GitLab as the code forge and Azure DevOps as a separate system, while lines 40-41 say Azure DevOps can be the forge. The `forge` row at :76 lists type, closed_state, and removed_state and leaves out team.
findings.evidence: docs/trackers.md:4: "It can be the code forge (the service that hosts the repository, GitHub or GitLab) or a separate system such as Azure DevOps." docs/trackers.md:21: "the code forge's own issues, GitHub's or GitLab's".
findings.fix: Name the three forges in lines 4 and 21, and add `team` to the row at :76.

areas.title: git, the category pages, and AWS
areas.coverage: Read whole: the seven integration pages in scope, docs/trackers.md, architecture.md, git.sh, forge.sh, tracker.sh, both bats files, github.sh to line 1290. Sampled gitlab.sh, ado.sh, forge.jq, all 305 git call lines, bin/ci. Not read: 33 tool pages, 78 schemas. Ran both bats files (21 pass) and seven reproductions under out/I4/work/tests/i4-repro*.bats.
areas.summary: For this slice the research is only partly in the product. git.md is an accurate catalogue of what kit runs (46 of 46 sampled forms). The category matrices hold 739 cells; kit has code for 3 providers, and of the 57 forge cells 56 agree with the declarations. AWS (258 lines) has no code. The 79 schema files are reference only: bin/ci checks each against its own examples. Worst defects: the builds stage drops default-branch runs (reads 50 newest of any kind), kit rebase rebases the desk on git older than 2.31, kit tidy dies on one unreachable remote. The pages lag the contract (3 against 6). findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused a report file, so everything is here.
strengths: The forge contract is explicit and enforced: forge:call answers 3 for a lacked feature without running the provider, an unknown feature or a version above the kit's is refused, and tests/forge-capabilities.bats proves each with a provider written in the test (21 of 21 pass in a copy).

The declarations match the code: every lacked feature is a return 3 stub, kit flow --capabilities printed exactly the three declarations, and 56 of the 57 forge-matrix cells for kit's providers agree on whether the forge answers.
Stand-ins are validated before use with the setting named in the refusal, and the JSON Schema of kit.yml mirrors the bash check.

git.md is accurate as a catalogue of what kit runs (46 of 46 sampled command forms are in the code) and states its own hazards; git:default-branch, git:push (explicit refspec, lease on the tip read), and git:unpushed are careful.
The research is honest about its limits: 'not verified' is written where it applies, and aws.md is labelled a plan.
bin/ci already runs ajv over every schema's examples, so the tool a conformance check needs is in the gate.
for-each-ref rather than git branch is used for upstream:track, so [gone] and ahead/behind are not localized.

findings.title: The builds stage reads the 50 newest runs of any kind, so default-branch runs drop out
findings.claim: forge:runs promises the 20 newest runs no change owns, but every provider asks for the 50 newest runs of every kind and filters in jq, so a repository whose pull requests run CI gets a short or empty list with exit 0 and no limited marker. Plausible in addition: az pipelines runs list --project is project-wide and ado_builds never compares the repository, so other repositories' builds appear.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (i4-repro3.bats): gh run list --limit 50 answering 50 pull_request runs gave forge:runs '[]', status 0, one call with no --event. gh.md:215 documents --event push/schedule/workflow_dispatch and --branch, az.md:146 --reason individualCI, and ci.md:131 marks the server filter cli for all three.
findings.fix: Ask the server per kind (push on the default branch, tags, schedule, manual) and merge, or page until 20 are found; print {"limited": N} when the window ran out. Filter Azure runs by repository id.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a copy (verify-1/w/tests/v1.bats, v1-ado.bats): 50 pull_request runs give [] with status 0; 47 plus 3 pushes give 3, no marker. No provider passes a server filter; forge.sh:113 and ci.md:12 promise the 20 newest. ADO keeps another repository's run; forge.jq:845 compares repository.name for deployments only. Real az not run.

findings.title: On git older than 2.31 kit rebase rebases and force-pushes the desk it promises to refuse
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (finding 28, low, plausible), still open; the consequence is new. An older git prints --path-format=absolute back, git:main-root gives nothing, and the root-checkout refusal at git.sh:458 never fires, against architecture.md:249.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with a git shim that prints the option back (i4-repro.bats R1): kit rebase on the desk printed 'dirname: illegal option -- -' then 'desk-topic is rebased onto origin/main and pushed', status 0, and origin had the branch. git.md:18-19 itself records that kit checks no version; 12 other call sites use the option.
findings.fix: Make guard:require tool:git and kit welcome refuse git below 2.31, and state the minimum in git.md and install.md.

findings.title: kit tidy stops with git's exit 128 when any one remote cannot be fetched
findings.claim: The fetch in git:tidy is unchecked under errexit, so one unreachable remote ends the sweep before any worktree is judged, with git's words, no kit error line, and an exit code the header does not promise.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (i4-repro2.bats R5): good origin plus a second remote at /nonexistent/fork.git gave 'fatal: ... does not appear to be a git repository', status 128, nothing swept. flow:incoming (flow.sh:580) already handles a failed fetch per remote and goes on.
findings.fix: On a failed fetch warn, skip branches whose upstream is on that remote, and go on; or fail with one line and exit 1.

findings.title: The category pages describe contract 3; the seam is at contract 6
findings.where: docs/integrations/1st.md:33, docs/integrations/forges.md:32, docs/integrations/forges.md:40, docs/integrations/trackers.md:11, docs/integrations/ci.md:12, docs/integrations/aws.md:186, docs/architecture.md:138, docs/architecture.md:174
findings.claim: The pages that say what kit uses are stale in at least eleven places: contract version 3 (code: 6), mark-ready has 'no seam call', reviews/checks/merged/milestones/iterations tabs 'planned' or 'no data source yet', GitHub Projects status none, CodeDeploy 'waits for a seam of its own'. ci.md:12 says each run comes with its jobs and failed step; GitHub gives jobs to 5 runs, GitLab and Azure to none.
findings.evidence: forge.sh:287 forge_contract=6; forge:pr-ready and kit ready exist; kit changes reviews|checks|merged and kit issues milestones|iterations exist; forge/github:iterations reads projectsV2; forge:environments and forge:deployments exist since 4. architecture.md:138 says run gh pr ready while line 197 and workflow.md:23 say kit ready; line 174 lists 2 of 3 tracker providers (web missing).
findings.fix: Correct the rows now, then generate kit's status rows and columns from the provider declaration so they cannot drift.

findings.title: Azure DevOps 'lacks' linked branches, which the research says its tool can make
findings.claim: The one cell of the three providers' forge columns that contradicts a declaration: the matrix says cli and az.md gives the two commands (link not verified), while the provider declares linked-branches lacking and returns 3. lacks is defined as what the forge does not have, so kit flow --capabilities says none both for 'cannot' and for 'not written' (also swimlanes against az.md:104 System.BoardColumn, and classic releases against cd.md:70).
findings.evidence: kit flow --capabilities on an Azure remote printed linked-branches, marks, releases, swimlanes all 'none'. forge.sh:194 'the features its forge does not have'.
findings.fix: Verify and implement the recipe, or mark the cell not verified; give the declaration a third state (unwritten) so the picture tells the two apart.

findings.title: The closing-issues stand-in fails silently on a forge without issues, the case the AWS plan is for
findings.claim: With closing-issues: body, forge:pr-closing-issues asks forge:issue-state, which answers 3 on a forge lacking issues, and line 822 turns that into return 1 with nothing said. aws.md:222 says the stand-in asks the tracker; the code never goes through the tracker seam.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (i4-repro.bats R2): provider lacking issues and closing-issues, body 'Closes #7': status 1, stdout empty, stderr empty. tests/forge-stand-ins.bats:109 covers only a forge that has issues.
findings.fix: Ask tracker:of "#N" state, which reaches whoever claims #, and add the test.

findings.title: Thirteen of the contract's 31 features are in no category matrix, and no matrix names a seam call
findings.claim: The four Coverage tables (19+18+8+11 rows) are keyed by free text, have no column for what kit's provider does, and omit labels, reviewers, merged, collaborators, teams, bots, attestations, the three scanners, rulesets, bypasses, and bot-accounts. People, Trust, and Platform, three of nine apps, have no category page.
findings.evidence: grep counts for reviewer, collaborator, attestation, scanning, dependabot, ruleset, bypass are 0 in all five pages. In 18 of the 57 forge cells kit's provider takes another route than the cell names (12 are GitLab's, which goes through glab api).
findings.fix: Key every row by feature or call, add a people-and-controls category, and generate kit's columns from the declaration.

findings.title: Nothing checks a test fixture or a provider against the 79 schema files
findings.claim: The schemas are reference only: bin/ci validates each schema's own embedded examples against itself, no bats file runs ajv or names a schema, and nothing is generated from them. The link from schema to provider function is a sentence in description.
findings.evidence: grep for ajv and for integrations schemas over tests/ has no hit. 1st.md:117-119 says a schema 'is what a provider's test fixtures can be checked against' and 'a fake is only as true as the documents it returns'.
findings.fix: Validate every fixture the conformance suite routes against the schema for its command, and run each provider call against a fake answering the schema's example (see I4-16).

findings.title: kit flow --capabilities is documented as kittui's, and kittui never asks for it
findings.claim: No Go source under projects/tui contains 'capabilities'; the tabs follow kit <app> --stages, which reads forge:has in bash. The declaration's JSON has no consumer but tests and a person.
findings.evidence: grep -ri capabilit projects/tui hits only two test-data files of kit flow's own syntax. apps.sh:271 is where stages consult forge:has.
findings.fix: Say who reads it, or have kittui read it once in place of the per-verb probes.

findings.title: A fractional marks interval passes validation and breaks the marks
findings.claim: marks: {every: 60.5} is a number >= 10 to both the schema and forge:stand-ins, and forge.sh:721 divides by it in bash arithmetic.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (R3): 'forge.sh: line 721: 1794487401 / 60.5 : arithmetic syntax error', status 1.
findings.fix: Require an integer in the schema and in the jq check.

findings.title: A branch that shares its name with a tag is read as heads/<name>
findings.claim: %(refname:short) and symbolic-ref --short give the shortest unambiguous name, so kit tidy looks for refs/heads/heads/v1 and keeps the branch for ever, and kit rebase and submit push a ref that does not exist. git:default-branch (git.sh:36-39) already guards against this; git.md:277 describes the field as 'the name without refs/heads/'.
findings.evidence: Reproduced (i4-repro2.bats R4) with branch and tag v1: git:gone-branches printed 'heads/v1' and git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD printed 'heads/v1'.
findings.fix: Use %(refname:lstrip=2), and strip refs/heads/ from symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD.

findings.title: The fetches of kit flow can ask for a password; only the mark is told not to
findings.claim: git.md:121 records GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and ssh BatchMode for marks:incoming alone. The incoming stage's and the picture's fetches run under kittui with the terminal attached (kit.go:424 sets only a process group), so git or ssh can prompt over the screen and wait until the call's limit.
findings.evidence: Code reading only; not reproduced, as it needs a remote that asks. A fetch with an expired credential under kittui would settle it.
findings.fix: One git:fetch helper that carries the mark's environment.

findings.title: git.md's two safety claims have exceptions, and five call forms are not in it
findings.claim: git.md says a remote reaches git after --end-of-options and a path as :(literal); policy.sh:304 passes the primary bare and policy.sh:366 and materialize.sh:381 pass plain pathspecs (safe today, since the names are checked or kit's own). 'failed to sign' is a translated git message, so under a localized git the signing refusal degrades to the generic failure.
findings.evidence: Not in git.md: log formats at flow.sh:398 and 426, for-each-ref --count=1 at flow.sh:459, rev-list --left-right --count against an upstream at flow.sh:457, rev-parse "${base}:${object}" at apps/audit.sh:243.
findings.fix: Add the two flags, list the five forms, and run that git commit with LC_ALL=C.

findings.title: The AWS plan is written against contract 3 and omits what it relies on
findings.claim: The lacks table has nine features, all of contract 1; it omits labels although line 220 says a label stand-in 'is refused here', which the seam does only for a provider declaring it lacks labels. It says nothing of the 19 features added since, several of which the page's own Read tables could answer (deployments from CodeDeploy, artifacts from CodeBuild).
findings.evidence: forge.sh:627 refuses a label stand-in only when lacks contains labels. No aws call exists anywhere in kit/ or projects/tui.
findings.fix: Restate the plan as the 31-row declaration.

findings.title: Lens answer: what was researched and is unused, by value to a user
findings.claim: Ranked: (1) a failed job's log, rerun, cancel, cli on all three kit forges; (2) server-filtered runs; (3) Jira and Linear as real trackers and any tracker's issues in the Issues stage; (4) external CI's pull request variables, without which kit linked finds no change on a detached checkout; (5) what is live where and approvals; (6) native board status or lane; (7) Azure's linked branch, releases, mark, and GitLab/Azure jobs; (8) Forgejo, Gitea, Bitbucket, then AWS. Of kit's three CI columns 3 of 8 rows are used, of CD 3 of 11; 553 of 739 matrix cells are for providers with no code, and none of the 23 other tools is referenced in kit's bash.
findings.evidence: ci.md and cd.md mark these rows planned; github pr-here (github.sh:681) reads only GITHUB_EVENT_PATH then the branch, while architecture.md:219 says any pipeline can run kit ci. The Issues stage reads forge:open-issues alone (known since 11-10 as #77, still open).
findings.fix: Take 1, 2, and 4 before v0.1.0 or state the limits in the pages; the rest is roadmap.

findings.title: Lens answer: the research cannot drive code yet; the smallest design that makes it
findings.claim: The contract is already data in bash (forge_features, forge_feature_of, forge_call_since, :contract, :lacks) but the research is prose-keyed tables and schemas linked by a sentence. Two steps close it: a declaration read as data, and conformance generated from the schemas.
findings.evidence: Schema descriptions name provider functions in prose ('which kit reads in modules/bash/forge/github.sh (forge/github:pr-title, ...)'); kit already has kit:generate regions and ajv in the gate.
findings.fix: Move the arrays to kit/modules/forge.json and give each provider forge/<name>.json {contract, lacks, unwritten, calls: {call: {route, command, schema}}}; put "x-kit": {provider, calls} in each schema. Generate one bats loop (ajv over every routed fixture, each call run against the schema's example, fail on a command no declaration names) and the kit columns of the four Coverage tables as generated regions.

areas.title: the thirty other tools: trackers, CI, CD, and other forges
areas.coverage: Read whole: the 30 pages, 1st.md, four category pages, tracker.sh and its providers, forge.sh, kit-ci. Grepped 54 names over kit/, projects/tui, tests, specs, plans. Ran five reproductions on a copy. Tool commands not verified (no network). findings.md NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from a subagent; out/I5/caps.tsv holds the 425 rows.
areas.summary: Answer for this slice: none of it is incorporated. The thirty pages hold 425 capability rows and 83 schema links for 34 services; the product runs none of the tools, every status says none, and no plan names one. Two product claims outrun that: the welcome page names Jira and Linear, yet only a page-opening web provider exists and kit linked can never pass on its issues; and kit ci fails on other CI systems because the change-number variables ci.md lists are unread. A tracker reference cannot be ENG-123. Pages are regular for forges, free-form for trackers and CD. Build order: CI variables and check URLs, Jira, Linear, Bitbucket Cloud, Gitea, Argo CD, CircleCI and Buildkite.
strengths: The status column is honest: all 34 services say none, and 1st.md:30-31 states the one true path, that another system reaches kit only through the code forge.
The pages say what was not checked: 19 'not verified' or 'not run' marks on eight pages and a Gaps paragraph on 21 sections; a sidecar should keep these as verified: false.
The seven other-forge sections are fully regular: the same 15 reads and 5 writes in the same words; that is the model for trackers, CI, and CD.

The forge seam is the right base for declarations: a contract version, lacks, exit 3, stand-ins, and kit flow --capabilities (forge.sh:190-259); forge/ado:lacks is already a provider speaking in data.
tests/forge-conformance.bats drives each provider through one world seen through each forge's API; a new provider joins by adding its world, and that is the test shape to generate.
kit new provider <seam> <name> scaffolds from the calls the seam's providers share (new.sh:527-573), so the template follows the code.
The web provider is a clean lowest rung: two URL patterns and refusals that name the page to act on.
kit fails closed where it cannot know: an unknown host is never taken for no forge (forge.sh:516-527), and kit linked refuses when no change is found.
kit platform already draws capability, service, provider, inferred or set, and ready: the table a ci or cd binding would add rows to.
The entities spec's services, bindings, and command provider (entities-design.md:103-108,150-170) is the right plan for this slice; what it lacks is an order and the reference grammar.

findings.title: The welcome page says kit works with Jira and Linear; a change linked to either can never pass kit linked
findings.claim: The delivered welcome page lists trackers "such as Jira and Linear", but the only way either is in the product is the web provider, which builds two URLs and refuses the other nine calls. So kit work LIN#12 stops at the title read, and a change that says Closes LIN#12 fails kit linked with the remedy "run: kit linked again once the tracker answers", which can never come true.
findings.evidence: With the record docs/trackers.md:83-89 gives, tracker:of "LIN#12" title and state and tracker:at "LIN#" me each returned 1 ("kit cannot read its title in the LIN# tracker, which it reaches through its pages alone"). jira.md:35-59 and linear.md:26-50 hold a command for every one of the eleven tracker calls, and none is used.
findings.fix: Before the release either reword the line ("and opens the pages of others such as Jira and Linear") or build the two providers. Either way let kit work take a web tracker's title from --title, and have kit linked say a web tracker's issue cannot count instead of promising the tracker will answer.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: with only `Closes LIN#12`, `kit linked 3` exits 1 with "kit linked again once the tracker answers". "Never" is too strong: with open forge issue #7 also linked, it exits 0. docs/trackers.md:78-81 states the limit; only the welcome line overstates. My `kit work` repro attempted a git fetch to github.com, failed, removed; issue.sh:611 read from code.

findings.title: kit ci cannot find the change on Jenkins, CircleCI, Buildkite, Drone, Woodpecker, or Bitbucket Pipelines
findings.claim: The welcome page says kit ci runs "in any CI system", but kit ci takes no argument and forge:pr-here reads only GitHub's event file, GitLab's and Azure's variables, or the checked-out branch. ci.md:37-40 names the variable each other system sets (BUILDKITE_PULL_REQUEST, CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST, CHANGE_ID, BITBUCKET_PR_ID, CI_COMMIT_PULL_REQUEST, DRONE_PULL_REQUEST and two more) and none is read anywhere in kit/.
findings.evidence: On a GitHub remote with a detached HEAD and all eight variables set to 3, forge:pr-here returned 0 and printed nothing. kit linked then exits 1 with "name the change: kit linked <number>", which a person running kit ci cannot do.
findings.fix: Read the change's number from a table of variable and how to read it, in the seam, before the branch is asked about; the research already holds the table. Keep the fail-closed refusal for a runner that sets none.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced on a detached HEAD: `forge:pr-here` prints nothing, `kit linked` exits 1, and kit/ reads none of the eight variables. Narrower: with the branch checked out, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:690-691 asks `gh pr list --head` and printed 3. docs/integrations/ci.md:35-40 states the gap itself; Bitbucket is not a forge kit supports.

findings.title: Nothing of the thirty pages is in the product, and no plan names any of their tools
findings.claim: The thirty pages describe 34 services with 425 capability rows (245 reads, 180 writes) and 83 schema links; the product runs none of the tools and calls none of their APIs. Specs name only Jira and Linear (a mapping column, a label source, and a non-goal), and the decisions plan defers the mechanism: "the contract ships, and no provider: command".
findings.evidence: A whole-word grep for 54 tool and service names over kit/, projects/tui, and bin finds only comments and examples: tracker/web.sh:5,11-12, kit.schema.json:12, quota_test.go:42. Indirectly, external CI checks reach kit changes checks through GitHub's statusCheckRollup, and Argo CD's GitHub deployments reach kit delivery deployments.
findings.fix: Say in 1st.md that the thirty pages are a catalogue, and record a build order: (0) CI variables, check URLs, reference grammar; (1) Jira; (2) Linear; (3) Bitbucket Cloud over bkt with Pipelines; (4) Gitea and Forgejo over tea; (5) Argo CD reads; (6) CircleCI and Buildkite; (7) Jenkins; then Flux, Kargo, YouTrack, Shortcut. Leave Gerrit, SourceHut, Radicle, and the REST-only trackers to the web provider or a command provider.

findings.title: A tracker reference cannot be written the way Jira, Linear, YouTrack, Plane, Shortcut, or Taiga write it
findings.claim: jira.md:14 and linear.md:13 say the record's prefix is ENG-, and kit refuses that record: a prefix must match ^[A-Za-z]*#?$. A repository must write ENG#123, so the branch is eng123-<slug>, the body says Closes ENG#123, and none of these is the form those trackers link a change by (ENG-123, sc-123, TG-123, per the research; that part is plausible, not verified).
findings.evidence: settings:validate on prefix "ENG-" printed "a tracker needs a prefix, letters and an optional #, and a provider (prefix 'ENG-')" and returned 1, while tracker:parse ENG-123 accepted it and tracker:key printed eng123. kit check, kit update, kit tools, and kit toolchains run settings:validate.
findings.fix: Let a tracker record carry its grammar as data: pattern, key (what the branch starts with), and closes (the line kit writes in the body), with today's forms as defaults. Widen the prefix rule to what tracker:parse already accepts.

findings.title: The tracker seam has no declaration of what a provider lacks and no list call, so a provider cannot be data
findings.claim: Unlike the forge seam, the tracker seam has no contract version, no lacks, and no exit 3, so web answers nine calls with exit 1, the code for a failed read; kit platform therefore draws a web tracker as never ready. The seam also has no open-issues, parent, iterations, milestones, or labels, and a record is closed (additionalProperties: false) while provider is open, so a repository's own jira provider has nowhere valid for its site.
findings.evidence: tracker:at "LIN#" me returned 1, and platform.sh:78-79 sets ready from that call. Issues and the issues stage read forge:open-issues alone, so an ado tracker on a GitHub forge is as invisible there as Jira would be.
findings.fix: Give the tracker seam a version, lacks, and exit 3, add open-issues in forge:open-issues' shape plus parent, iterations, milestones, label and unlabel, and open one key of a record for the provider's own fields. Add ci.sh (change-here, runs, marks; later log, rerun, cancel) picked by a ci setting, and cd.sh (environments, deployments, live as {environment, revision, synced, health, url}) as a list.

findings.title: What a forge is called, where its pages are, and how it writes a change are hard-coded outside the providers
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:406-415, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:470-472, kit/modules/bash/tracker/forge.sh:33, kit/modules/bash/issues.sh:117, kit/modules/jq/workspace.jq:27-28, kit/modules/bash/workspaces.sh:490-491, kit/modules/bash/welcome.sh:740, projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:556, projects/tui/internal/flow/quota.go:21
findings.claim: docs/packages.md:293-294 tells a repository it can add forge: bitbucket with its own module, yet fourteen places in nine files outside the providers still decide by provider name. Known since 11-10 in part (guessed link shapes in rows.go), still open.
findings.evidence: issues.sh:117 and rows.go:556 write "!" for IN("gitlab", "ado") and "#" otherwise although the seam has forge:noun; workspace.jq:27-28 knows pages for github and gitlab only; welcome.sh:740 picks gh for github and glab for everything else. quota.go:21 has glyphs for two forges.
findings.fix: Move these into one declaration a provider gives as data beside contract and lacks: hosts, runner variable, login file, tool, noun, pages (issue, new issue, branch, commit, change), glyph. kit flow --capabilities can carry it to kittui.

findings.title: The thirty pages are alike enough to read by eye, and not alike enough for a program
findings.where: docs/integrations/1st.md:95-99, docs/integrations/kubectl.md:12, docs/integrations/jira.md:33, docs/integrations/tea.md:128, docs/integrations/fly.md:37, docs/integrations/jenkins.md:41
findings.claim: The skeleton holds (each service has one Read, one Write, one schemas heading), but the status is spelled three ways, 15 pages open with the tool and 15 with boilerplate, two tables have a column per tool, and capability names are free text outside the forge pages. A cell holds one code span in 262 of 425 rows, several in 125, and none in 38, with nothing to say which span is the command.
findings.evidence: Scripted counts: the seven forge sections share one fixed list of 20 capabilities, while ten trackers use 31 read and 19 write labels for eleven calls and CD uses 25 read labels. There are 103 placeholder names, nine of them for the instance's URL and three for the issue.
findings.fix: Keep the prose and put the rows in a sidecar per tool, docs/integrations/<tool>.yml: {service, category, status, rows: [{call: <seam call name>, kind, via: cli|api|page|none, run: [argv], read: <jq>, verified}]}. Generate the page tables and the category coverage matrices from it, and let a provider declaration be the same rows plus tool, reference grammar, fields, lacks, and pages, run by one generic provider.

findings.title: The research index describes a seam three versions old
findings.where: docs/integrations/1st.md:33, docs/integrations/1st.md:17, docs/integrations/trackers.md:11-12, docs/integrations/trackers.md:33-34, docs/integrations/forges.md:40-43, docs/integrations/ci.md:49, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:287
findings.claim: 1st.md:33 says a provider declares what it lacks "in the forge seam's contract version 3" while forge_contract is 6, and the category pages mark as planned the iterations, milestones, reviews, checks, and merged tabs that kit issues and kit changes now serve. The seven other-forge sections were written to that old scope: their 20 rows map to 24 of the seam's 60 calls.
findings.evidence: forge.sh:287 is declare -gr forge_contract=6, and kit-issues and kit-changes list milestones, iterations, reviews, checks, merged. No other-forge section has a row for labels, merged changes, milestones, releases, environments, deployments, collaborators, teams, or branch rules.
findings.fix: Generate the Scope tables from forge_features and forge_feature_of so they cannot drift. Add the missing rows for the forges that come first in the build order, so the research can say what each would declare under lacks.

findings.title: No schema of the thirty is in the tree, and nothing checks a provider's fixtures against any schema
findings.claim: 1st.md:117-119 says a tool-output schema is what a provider's fixtures can be checked against, but the only reader of docs/integrations/*/*.schema.json is bin/ci, which validates each schema's own examples against itself. For the thirty there are no schema files at all, only 83 links to documents on the network that the offline gate does not fetch.
findings.evidence: grep -rn integrations tests/ finds nothing, and only gh/, glab/, and az/ exist beside the pages (34, 26, 19 files). The fixtures in tests/forge-conformance.bats and tests/tracker.bats are here-documents typed apart from the examples.
findings.fix: Write one JSON Schema per seam call's output from the seam header's prose, have the fake tool serve a tool-output schema's examples as its fixtures, and generate one bats test per provider and call that validates the seam's output against the call's schema. A declared provider with examples then has conformance tests with no test code.

findings.title: On a Forgejo or Gitea Actions runner kit takes the forge for GitHub
findings.claim: Forgejo and Gitea Actions set GITHUB_SERVER_URL to their own instance, so with no forge: in kit.yml forge:runner-of answers github for that host. The same repository gets the right refusal at a desk and gh errors on its runner.
findings.evidence: With origin https://forgejo.example.com/o/r.git and GITHUB_SERVER_URL=https://forgejo.example.com, forge:provider printed github; with the variable unset it refused with "names no forge the kit knows". tests/forge.bats:171 notes the variable and covers only the case where kit.yml sets forge: none.
findings.fix: Before trusting GITHUB_SERVER_URL, rule out a runner that names itself otherwise (Gitea sets GITEA_ACTIONS; confirm Forgejo's own variable). Record the variable in tea.md, which says nothing of it.

findings.title: A check from another CI system is drawn with no way to its run
findings.claim: External CI checks reach the changes stage through GitHub's statusCheckRollup, as ci.md:26-28 says, but the query asks for neither CheckRun.detailsUrl nor StatusContext.targetUrl. kit changes checks names a failed Jenkins or CircleCI check and cannot open it.
findings.evidence: The query reads "... on CheckRun { name status conclusion startedAt completedAt }" and "... on StatusContext { context state createdAt }". A run's document is {name, verdict, at, took}.
findings.fix: Add the two fields to the query and a url to the run's document, linked from the checks tab. It is the cheapest use of the CI research: every external system one click away with no seam.

findings.title: Small faults in the thirty pages
findings.claim: hut.md:58-59 sends the reader to trackers.md for todo.sr.ht and to ci.md for builds.sr.ht, and neither page mentions SourceHut. circleci.md:33 says "see the table above" where the page has no such table, and kubectl.md:12 gives a status of "—", which 1st.md:99 does not allow.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'sr\.ht\|SourceHut' over trackers.md, ci.md, and cd.md prints nothing. The other CI pages link ci.md#who-reports-to-the-code-forge for the same row.
findings.fix: Fix the three lines. A lint over the sidecar proposed in I5-7 would catch each.

areas.title: README and the core documents
areas.coverage: Read whole: README.md and the nine docs pages in scope (1,894 lines), plus prose.md and house.md. Sampled code to check claims: verb headers, 1st.sh, forge.sh, settings.sh, bin/ci, bin/release, kit.yml. Ran pattern greps, a sentence-length script, a duplicate finder, one yq-count reproduction. Not checked: web links, the Homebrew tap, kittui behaviour, testing.md timings.
areas.summary: No machine-flavoured prose: zero filler words, em dashes, or bold-led bullets in 19,500 words. The fault is the opposite one, over-compressed sentences. 63 of 95 sampled passages pass: README 12/16, architecture 8/15, features 12/25, modules 7/10, install 5/5, testing 6/6, logs 2/3, completion 2/2, context 5/7, generate 4/6. features.md and architecture.md's forge section hold most failures. Models: install.md, completion.md, logs.md, generate.md, testing.md. New accuracy findings include `gh pr ready` where `kit ready` exists, and three dead links. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from subagents, and I did not work around it. The 20 rewrites are findings P1-19 to P1-38.
strengths: No machine-flavoured writing in about 19,500 words: no 'ensure', 'robust', 'seamless', 'leverage', 'comprehensive', 'crucial', 'simply', or 'note that', no em dash, no bold-led bullet. Do not loosen this.

The documents say what kit does not do: README.md:50-57 (the deny list 'matches literal patterns, so `git -C <dir> commit` and `git merge` get through'; 'kit does not ship a ruleset') and the four 'no check' rows of the table at docs/architecture.md:236-249. Keep this voice.

Good models, whole pages: docs/install.md (especially 12-13 and the Trust section 110-122), docs/completion.md (42 lines, nothing to cut), docs/logs.md except 65-67, docs/testing.md (every number has a source; the incident at 18-19 justifies the rule).
Good models, passages: README.md:11-13 and 55-71; docs/architecture.md:26-34 (Bash modules); docs/generate.md:14-49 and 123-135; docs/modules.md:128-143 (Overriding a function).
Median sentence length is 9 to 17 words in every file; install.md, logs.md, completion.md, and generate.md have at most two sentences of 35 words or more between them.
Cross-references are short and uniform ('; see [x.md](x.md)', 17 times), and every relative link in scope except the three in P1-3 resolves in the tree.

Most claims checked against code hold: the four checks of `kit ci`, the three groups of `kit serve` tools, forge contract version 6, the help groups and their order, `list:read0`, `super:override`, log file names and the 14-day default, the 300-second and 35-minute limits, the eight shards, the hook matcher, the deny list, the trust file path.
Page length is right for seven of ten pages: modules.md (a reference), install.md, testing.md, logs.md, completion.md, generate.md, and context.md apart from about 15 lines.

findings.title: docs/features.md is a second manual, and half of it cannot be read in one pass
findings.claim: Line 3 promises a list 'with a pointer to the page that describes each part in full', but two sections (185 of 362 lines) are the full description: forge detection rules, release JSON fields, kittui crumbs. The welcome guide's Customize page sends newcomers here.
findings.evidence: 13 of 25 sampled passages fail a first reading, the worst rate in scope; the page has 12 of the 30 sentences of 35+ words and 32 of the 76 sentences with five or more commas, colons, and semicolons. Line 239 is one 70-word sentence: 'A link to a row of a tab the app does not have opens the app built around that tab's entity, on the tab, with the row under the cursor once it loads: from Issues, ...'.
findings.fix: Cut the page to about 150 lines of summary and links. Move 121-136 to architecture.md or trackers.md, 99-119 and 146-156 to a page on `kit flow`, and 220-258 to apps.md; rewrites are P1-26 to P1-33.

findings.title: Three documents give the last workflow step as `gh pr ready`, and kit has `kit ready`
findings.claim: README and architecture.md tell the reader to run `gh pr ready` or `glab mr update --ready`, which names nothing for Azure DevOps and leaves a stand-in label or title prefix in place. features.md's numbered workflow has no ready step, and the README's list of 'the workflow verbs' has 12 of the 20 in the workflow group.
findings.evidence: `kit/bin/kit-ready` exists ('marks a draft pull request ready for review (kit verb: workflow)'), and `kit/packages/workflow/files/repo/.kit/workflow.md:23` says '`kit ready`, on any forge, which also takes off the' stand-in. The short verb list is known since 11-10 (documents pass, finding 16), still open and now eight short: audit, changes, delivery, issues, people, ready, workspace, workspaces.
findings.fix: Write `kit ready` in all three places and add it to features.md's steps. Take the README's verb list from `kit help`.

findings.title: Three links in the tracked documents point at files git ignores
findings.claim: The links to `.kit/workflow.md`, `../.kit/rules/bash.md`, and `../.kit/styles/bash.md` are dead on the code forge's page, where a first-release reader opens the README. They resolve only in a hydrated checkout, which is why the gate's `lychee --offline` (bin/ci:62) passes.
findings.evidence: `ls -a .kit` in the snapshot of the commit prints only `packages`; README.md:265 says 'What kit places under `.kit/` is a link ... ignored by git'.
findings.fix: Link the sources: `kit/packages/workflow/files/repo/.kit/workflow.md`, `kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/rules/bash.md`, `kit/packages/style/bash/files/repo/.kit/styles/bash.md`. Run lychee once over a fresh clone before `kit hydrate` to catch the next one.

findings.title: The forge section of docs/architecture.md mixes an essay on two words with ten dense bullets
findings.claim: Lines 155-169 spend 15 lines on the origin of 'forge' and 'seam' (SourceForge 1999, Feathers 2004, tailoring), then the bullets compress contract, features, stand-ins, and swimlanes into sentences that need three readings. 'Marks', 'stand-in', and 'swimlane' are never defined; the section insists on 'code forge' at 157 and writes bare 'forge' six times.
findings.evidence: 7 of 15 sampled passages in this file fail, all but three of them here. Lines 187-191 are one 64-word sentence listing 30 feature names, a copy of `forge_features` in forge.sh that will drift.
findings.fix: Cut 155-169 to four lines, replace the feature list with a pointer to forge.sh, and give stand-ins a short section with one worked example. Rewrites are P1-19 to P1-25.

findings.title: The second half of the README is for kit's own contributors, under headings a user reads as theirs
findings.claim: 139 of 336 lines are about working on kit itself, under 'Setup', 'Getting started', 'Maintaining', and 'Release'; a new user who scans the headings lands on kit's own contribution workflow. Only line 200 says the audience changed.
findings.evidence: The table at README.md:269-283 maps 13 installed copies to sources in cells of up to 50 words, restating what the package layout and `kit check` already state (prose rule 3). README.md:283 is one cell: 'written by kit beside what it placed under `.kit/`, and ignored like it: the paths git never sees, and a digest per delivered path. ...'.
findings.fix: Move 198-336 to CONTRIBUTING.md and leave two lines and a link, so the README ends at 'Updating' near 200 lines. Also trim step 1 of 'Take the kit' (98-100 and 121-126 are detail for later pages).

findings.title: The same sentences live in two or three documents, and the copies have started to disagree
findings.where: docs/architecture.md:127-140, docs/features.md:79-95, docs/architecture.md:219-232, docs/features.md:30-39, README.md:19-24, docs/architecture.md:251-253, docs/features.md:358-360, README.md:39-46, docs/install.md:57-64
findings.claim: The `kit work` paragraph, the four checks, the 'What no check covers' paragraph, and the toolchain list each appear two or three times. The reader pays twice and the copies drift.
findings.evidence: A script (dup.py) finds 16 sentences that architecture.md and features.md share over nine or more consecutive words, 6 between README and features.md, 3 each between README and architecture.md and install.md. Drift already present: stage order (P1-11), last workflow step (P1-2), the AGENTS.md region's text (P1-13), and one 'no check' gap in features.md:356-360 against four in architecture.md:245-249 (known since 11-10, still open).
findings.fix: Give each fact one home and link to it: the README keeps the summary, architecture.md the mechanism, features.md a list of links.

findings.title: Asides packed between commas: six recurring compressed constructions
findings.claim: The ten files have 0 em dashes, 15 parentheses in prose, and 1 'for example', so every aside, example, and exception goes between commas or after a colon. Each construction saves two or three words and costs a second reading.
findings.evidence: Counts by grep over the ten files: 169 mid-sentence colons, 92 semicolons, 47 ', which', 68 ', so'; pronoun 'one'/'none' for a distant noun 43 (16 in features.md); ', as' for 'such as' or 'like' 22; ', each a ...' 9; postposed 'X first' 7; verbless tails 5; 'but' for 'except' 3; 'is no X' 6; house verbs 'names' 77, 'refuses' 40, 'holds' 32, 'says' 29, 'answers' 25. Examples: 'One `yq` cannot parse, or one read where `yq` is missing, is refused' (docs/modules.md:55); 'filled with what was given, as `kit commit` with no message does' (docs/features.md:206); 'it gives the work back to the desk, staged work staged' (docs/architecture.md:131); 'every untracked file git does not ignore, but a template' (docs/generate.md:100); '`CI_SERVER_HOST` GitLab, and `SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI` Azure DevOps' (docs/features.md:129); 'Every call answers, answers none, fails' (docs/architecture.md:185).
findings.fix: One idea per sentence in these passages; write 'such as', 'except', and the noun itself. Allow parentheses for a true aside and 'for example' before an example.

findings.title: Terms are used before they are defined, or never defined in these pages
findings.where: README.md:124, README.md:142, README.md:320, docs/architecture.md:60, docs/architecture.md:131, docs/architecture.md:190, docs/features.md:188, docs/features.md:256
findings.claim: A reader who does not know the code meets at least 14 terms with no definition in the page: 'host template', 'hydrate' (never defined in the README), 'the index', 'the primary remote', 'the declaration', 'the swept work', 'marks', 'stand-in', 'swimlane', 'preset', 'when ambient', 'in reach', 'harness', 'the worker contract', 'plans as prose'.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture.md:60 '`kit hydrate` brings every path under `.kit/` to its state from the declaration, choosing nothing' comes 19 lines before the first hint of what the declaration is. 'when ambient' (docs/features.md:188) is defined only in docs/toolchains.md:86.
findings.fix: Define each at first use in one clause, or use ordinary words: 'the uncommitted work', 'the version and packages in `kit.yml`', 'with no toolchain', 'the packages the repository can use'.

findings.title: The documents describe `libexec/` three ways, and one says a checkout has none
findings.claim: docs/architecture.md:21 says 'A checkout has no `libexec/`' and line 19 says it holds only `kittui-<os>-<arch>`; README.md:253 says the tarball adds '`libexec/kittui`, built from `tui/`'. Only docs/install.md:8-9 is right.
findings.evidence: The snapshot has `kit/libexec/kit-call`, and `kit/bin/kit:474` ends in `exec bash "${self_root}/libexec/kit-call" "$@"`, so every call depends on it; the binaries are `kittui-<os>-<arch>` built from `projects/tui/` (bin/release:39-51, README.md:327). The README line is known since 11-10, still open; the architecture.md claim is new.
findings.fix: Use install.md's sentence in all three: `libexec/` holds the loader's helper, `kit-call`, and the `kittui-<os>-<arch>` binaries, which only a release has.

findings.title: The prose rules do not name the failure these documents have
findings.claim: The five rules cover declarative sentences, mood, slogans and restating, the serial comma, and acronyms; the documents obey them almost everywhere and a third of sampled passages still fail. Rule 1 ('the thing under discussion as the subject') and rule 3 ('Do not restate'), held strictly, push toward agentless passives and pronoun chains.
findings.evidence: 32 of 95 sampled passages fail a first reading. 'A named path that is neither a file nor a directory is refused with exit 2, by the name you typed, before anything is expanded' (docs/generate.md:97-98) follows rule 1 and is harder than 'kit refuses ...'.
findings.fix: Add three rules: one idea per sentence (split at a second colon or semicolon); define a term where it first appears; prefer the ordinary word and the repeated noun ('such as', 'except', 'the stage') to a shorter construction. Say that parentheses and 'for example' are allowed.

findings.title: docs/features.md lists the flow stages out of order, and counts Flow's tabs two ways
findings.claim: Line 97 says 'Work moves left to right through seven stages' and the bullets run issues, incoming, desk, worktrees, changes, builds, releases. Line 221 says Flow shows 'every stage the `flow` setting in `kit.yml` names', and the table at 229 lists five tabs with no word on desk and worktrees.
findings.evidence: `kit/modules/bash/settings.sh:313`: `settings_stages=(issues desk worktrees changes builds incoming releases)`, the same order as the `kit-flow` header and README.md:47. The order is known since 11-10 (finding 26), still open: the count was fixed, the order was not.
findings.fix: Reorder the bullets, and say in one sentence that kittui shows desk and worktrees in Repositories.

findings.title: docs/modules.md's jq table and its layout rule are behind the tree
findings.claim: The jq table lists 11 modules and the directory has 17; three pages say `modules/` holds one directory per language, and the tree also has `kit/modules/tutorials/` and `kit/modules/tutorials.yml`.
findings.evidence: Missing from the table: apps.jq, glyphs.jq, serve.jq, terminal.jq, version.jq, workspace.jq. Known since 11-10 as 10 of 14 (finding 15), still open and wider.
findings.fix: Generate the table with a `kit:generate` region from each module's banner, and name the tutorials directory in the layout.

findings.title: Small counts and samples that do not match the files they describe
findings.where: docs/context.md:75, docs/context.md:77-87, docs/generate.md:10, docs/generate.md:29-34, docs/generate.md:153, docs/architecture.md:82-83
findings.claim: context.md says 'the bash rule lists five' templates (it lists six) and shows a frontmatter no shipped file has; generate.md calls the AGENTS.md region 'the sentence' and shows two sentences, where the region is a heading and two sentences with a `kit hydrate` fallback. architecture.md:82-83 names two things and counts 'the three keys'.
findings.evidence: `kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/rules/bash.md:7-19` lists five providers and `verb`; `kit/packages/agents/generic/regions/repo/AGENTS.md` opens with '## Follow rules defined by kit'. The sample frontmatter and the region text are known since 11-10 (findings 29 and 17), still open; 'five' and 'three keys' are new.
findings.fix: Correct each count, show one real file as the sample, and name the three keys as README.md:285 does.

findings.title: docs/testing.md's list of what the gate runs is short, and one number looks stale
findings.claim: Lines 8-9 omit the tutorials site's checks (ajv and `npm run check`, bin/ci:70-71); known since 11-10, still open. Lines 42-43 say 'Loading the yaml module runs `yq` three times', which no longer looks true.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy with a fake `yq` that logs each call, `source modules/bash/1st.sh; use yaml` started `yq` once (`--version`), with and without a `kit.yml` naming `bash_path`. I did not measure 'about 2,000 times'; the same fake `yq` under tests/template.bats would settle it.
findings.fix: Add the two checks to the list, and measure again or drop the sentence.

findings.title: Lists in the README and docs/install.md that the tree has outgrown
findings.claim: The README's directory table has no row for `projects/` or `tests/` and its `bin/` row omits `bin/tutorials` (the last known since 11-10, still open). install.md names `gh` and `glab` as the forge tools and `az` only for an Azure DevOps tracker, and its list of verbs that need the forge tool omits `kit ready`.
findings.evidence: `kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh` is a forge provider over `az`, as docs/features.md:262-263 says; `kit/bin/kit-ready` runs `use forge`. That the app verbs (issues, changes, delivery, people, audit) need the tool rests on docs/features.md:223-235, which I did not trace; in passing, outside scope, `kit/bin/kit:66` cites `docs/releases.md`, which does not exist.
findings.fix: Add the rows, name `az` as a forge tool, and replace the verb list with 'the workflow verbs and the app verbs'.

findings.title: Small breaks of the repository's own prose rules: five acronyms, two slogans
findings.where: docs/architecture.md:191, docs/architecture.md:213, docs/logs.md:34, docs/modules.md:88, docs/modules.md:286, docs/architecture.md:149, docs/testing.md:57
findings.claim: Rule 5 (expand an uncommon acronym): JWT, CD, MCP in logs.md, NUL, and CRLF are never expanded on their pages. Rule 3 (no slogans): two sentences trade meaning for a turn of phrase.
findings.evidence: 'so the next `kit work <N>` is a pick, not a search' (docs/architecture.md:149); 'Linux there beats the runner by 2 times, so the hardware is faster; macOS spends that and more' ends its paragraph (docs/testing.md:57).
findings.fix: Expand the five at first use, and say what the slogans mean, such as 'so you can see at once which issues are free'.

findings.title: One thing has two names: kit and 'the kit', person and human, code forge and forge
findings.claim: A new reader cannot tell whether 'the kit' is the release, the CLI, or the repository, or whether a 'human' differs from a 'person'. architecture.md:157 explains why kit says 'code forge' and then drops the word.
findings.evidence: 'the kit' or 'the kit's' 40 times beside bare 'kit' as a subject 21 times; 'human' 7 times against 'person' or 'people' 19; bare 'forge' 6 times in docs/architecture.md:187-203.
findings.fix: Pick 'kit', 'person', and 'code forge' (or say once that 'forge' is short for it), and replace the rest.

findings.title: Lines that are correct and give the reader nothing to use
findings.claim: Cache and process details sit in user-facing lists: when the module path is read again, when a compiled kinds program is removed, where yaml results are kept. README.md:98-100 explains how to remove the `kit` package inside the step that installs it.
findings.evidence: docs/context.md:56-58, under 'A classification that cannot be made fails': 'A compile removes the program of other kinds once a day has passed since its last use, and a program removed between a lookup and its read is compiled again.' docs/context.md:100-106 is a paragraph about `kit lint` on the `kit context` page.
findings.fix: Move the cache details to the module headers, where they already are, and the `kit lint` paragraph to its own page. context.md loses about 15 lines; no other short page needs cutting.

findings.title: Rewrite: the swimlane stand-in bullet
findings.claim: Four sentences that each need a second reading: an issue that 'says' fields, 'no forge kit reaches has a swimlane it reads the same way', and an example introduced by 'as'.
findings.evidence: 'A stand-in gives any of the three to every forge alike: the rest of the issue's first label that starts with a prefix, else a default, as `swimlanes: {label_prefix: "swimlane:", default: none}`. It answers the issue's field alone; the milestones and iterations an Issues tab lists stay the forge's own.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'Each open issue has a milestone, an iteration, and a swimlane. Any of them can be empty. kit reads the milestone and the iteration from a forge that has them. No forge has swimlanes in a form kit can read. A repository can take any of the three from a label instead. With `swimlanes: {label_prefix: "swimlane:", default: none}`, an issue labelled `swimlane:payments` is in the swimlane `payments`, and an issue with no such label is in `none`. This changes only the field shown on an issue. The milestones and iterations tabs still list what the forge has.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the four outcomes of a forge call
findings.claim: One sentence carries the whole contract in house verbs a newcomer has not learned ('answers', 'answers none').
findings.evidence: 'Every call answers, answers none, fails with one line that says what could not be read, or is unsupported, and a list is whole or the call fails; the header of `kit/modules/bash/forge.sh` holds the contract.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'Every call ends in one of four ways. It returns a result. It returns nothing, because there is nothing to return. It fails, with one line that says what could not be read. Or it reports that the forge does not support it. A call never returns part of a list. The header of `kit/modules/bash/forge.sh` gives the full contract.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the 30-name feature list
findings.claim: A 64-word sentence lists 30 features, then a 42-word sentence explains 'unsupported' with 'the verb answers as for none'.
findings.evidence: 'A provider declares the contract's version it implements, 6 today, and the features its forge lacks: issues, sub-issues, linked branches, drafts, ... swimlanes, and bot accounts (a GitHub App's JWT, installation, and narrowed token). A call of a feature the forge lacks, or one added after the provider's version, is unsupported: it exits 3 and runs nothing, and the verb answers as for none, such as no releases to list or no rate limits to draw.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'A provider declares which version of the contract it implements (6 today) and which features its forge lacks. `forge_features` in `kit/modules/bash/forge.sh` lists the features. A call that needs a missing feature, or a call added after the provider's version, exits 3 and runs nothing. The verb treats that as an empty result: `kit flow releases` lists no releases. `kit flow --capabilities` prints the declaration, which kittui reads.'

findings.title: Rewrite: choosing a stand-in
findings.claim: The definition of a stand-in is one 57-word sentence with three examples after a colon, 'marks on a timer' with no definition of a mark, and a verbless tail.
findings.evidence: '... and the seam then answers the feature itself, whether the forge has it or not: a draft as a label or a title prefix, the issues a change closes as its body names them, and marks on a timer. `kit ready` marks a draft ready for review on every forge, its stand-in taken off.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'A repository can replace a feature with a stand-in, set under `forge_settings.<forge>.stand_ins` in `kit.yml`. kit then provides the feature itself, even on a forge that has its own. There are three stand-ins. A draft can be a label or a title prefix. The issues a change closes can be read from its body. [One sentence that says what a mark is, and that a timer can supply it.] `kit ready` marks a draft ready on every forge, and removes the label or the prefix.'

findings.title: Rewrite: what `kit work` does when it stops early (the same text in two documents)
findings.claim: 'The swept work' is never defined (the text above says 'moves'), and 'staged work staged' is a verbless tail.
findings.evidence: 'When it stops before the worktree has the swept work, it gives the work back to the desk, staged work staged; when the work conflicts in the worktree, it stays in the stash, and `kit work` names the command that applies it.'
findings.fix: Rewrite, in one place only: 'If `kit work` fails before the uncommitted work reaches the new worktree, it puts the work back on the desk, and what was staged is staged again. If the work conflicts with the worktree, `kit work` leaves it in the stash and prints the command that applies it.'

findings.title: Rewrite: backlog and underway in the issues stage
findings.claim: Two sentences open with the pronoun 'One', the terms backlog and underway are defined only by relative clauses, and two 'X, not Y' slogans stand in for the meaning.
findings.evidence: 'One in the backlog, which no open pull request closes, shows the branch that claims it, so the next `kit work <N>` is a pick, not a search. One underway shows who works on it, and where. Backlog and underway are one stage, not two, so an issue is found wherever its work stands; ...'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'An issue is in the backlog when no open pull request closes it, and underway when one does. A backlog issue shows the branch someone has started for it, if there is one, so you can see which issues are free. An issue underway shows who is working on it, and in which checkout. Both are in the one stage. In kittui, a preset shows only the backlog, only the issues underway, or the issues grouped by milestone, iteration, or swimlane.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the essay on 'seam', and the integrations pointer
findings.claim: Eleven lines defend a word choice in an architecture page, and the pointer to the integrations pages stacks five comma-separated asides.
findings.evidence: 'He took it from tailoring: a seam is where two pieces of cloth join, and where a garment is let out or taken in without recutting either piece.' And: 'lists the providers of each category, code forges, trackers, CI, and CD, the ones kit has and the ones it has not, and the command line tools that reach them, git first.'
findings.fix: Rewrite 159-169: 'Five files each define a seam: a place where behavior can change without editing the code there. The term is Michael Feathers'. Each file's header lists the calls a provider must answer, and its code picks the provider at run time, from a setting or from the primary remote's host. kit says seam, not interface, because the file holds both the contract and the choice.' Rewrite 213-215: '[integrations/1st.md] lists the services in each category: code forges, trackers, continuous integration, and continuous delivery. It says which ones kit supports and which command-line tool reaches each. Each tool has a page that says what kit reads and writes through it.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the primary remote's exception
findings.claim: The exception to a five-rule list is written as a riddle: 'the last', 'a host nothing names', 'one kit cannot tell, never none'.
findings.evidence: 'The primary is the exception to the last: on a host nothing names, its code forge is one kit cannot tell, never none, so a read of its pull request fails and names the `forge` setting. ... `forge: none`, or `none` under `forges`, says a remote has no code forge the kit knows, as on Bitbucket or a plain git server; it wins over the host and a runner's server.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'Rule 5 does not apply to the primary remote. When kit cannot tell the primary's code forge, it does not assume there is none: a command that reads a pull request fails, and the error tells you to set `forge`. A primary that is a path on this machine has no code forge. Set `forge: none`, or `none` under `forges`, for a remote on a service kit does not support, such as Bitbucket or a plain git server. That setting overrides rules 2 and 3.'

findings.title: Rewrite: welcome's steps 2 and 3
findings.claim: Two list items are verbless inventories joined by semicolons and colons; 'Several usable means you choose' drops its nouns.
findings.evidence: 'Setup: each code forge's login, once for the machine; then each folder of the workspace on its own, the desk then each worktree, by repository: kit installed, with the version its `kit.yml` declares, `.kit/` in place, the hooks, its project toolchain, its linters, and `kit check`.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'Toolchains: the tools kit itself needs (bash, git, jq, and yq), then the system toolchain. When more than one is usable, you choose. Setup: first your login to each code forge, checked once for the machine. Then each folder of the workspace, grouped by repository, the desk before its worktrees. For each folder it checks that kit is installed, which version `kit.yml` declares, that `.kit/` is in place, the hooks, the project toolchain, the linters, and `kit check`.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the pointer to the applications tutorial
findings.claim: The subject is 13 words and three appositives long before the verb arrives.
findings.evidence: 'kit's screens and what each shows, Flow first, how work moves from an issue to a release, are a tutorial that ships with the kit, `kit tutorials applications`; see [tutorials.md](tutorials.md).'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'The tutorial `kit tutorials applications` describes each of kit's screens, starting with Flow; see [tutorials.md](tutorials.md).'

findings.title: Rewrite: a check that passes and still offers a fix
findings.claim: The second sentence uses a check's name as a bare noun phrase ('there kit installed holds') and interrupts itself with 'on what it infers'.
findings.evidence: 'A check that holds can still offer a fix: an offer, drawn 💡, which needs no attention and fails nothing. kit runs in a folder whose `kit.yml` declares no kit version, on what it infers, so there kit installed holds and offers `kit install`.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'A check that passes can still suggest a command, marked 💡. A suggestion is optional and fails nothing. For example, kit works in a folder whose `kit.yml` declares no version, so the check named kit installed passes there, and suggests `kit install`.'

findings.title: Rewrite: apps, their verbs, and links between apps
findings.claim: 'Entity' is used four times without an example, the app verbs are listed inline with one exception in parentheses, and the link rule is a single 70-word sentence.
findings.evidence: 'Each other app is built around one entity: its first tab is that entity's home, and its other tabs the entities around it. Each app has a verb, `kit issues`, `kit changes`, ... `kit audit` (Trust), ... and Flow has `kit flow`; on a terminal one opens its app, and `kit <verb> <tab>` opens it on that tab, maximized.' The 70-word sentence at 239 is quoted in P1-1.
findings.fix: Rewrite 222-225: 'Each other app covers one kind of thing, such as issues. Its first tab lists those, and its other tabs list what is related to them. Each app has a verb, in the table below. On a terminal, `kit <verb>` opens the app, and `kit <verb> <tab>` opens it with that tab maximized.' Add a Verb column to the table. Rewrite 239-242: 'Some values are links to a row in another app. Following one opens that app on the right tab, with the cursor on the row. In Issues, an issue's pull request opens Changes, and its checkout opens the worktrees tab of Repositories. When the workspace is a group, a member's name opens the repos tab of Repositories.'

findings.title: Rewrite: crumbs
findings.claim: Seven lines of interaction detail in two sentences of 49 and 43 words, with the key's name buried in a relative clause.
findings.evidence: 'A plain click on it, or ⌫, which the keys bar names while it shows, goes back there, the view as it was left: the tab, maximized or not, the preset, sort, filters, and groups, the row under the cursor, and the scroll. That place keeps its own crumb, so crumbs chain, each one deep.'
findings.fix: Rewrite, and move to docs/apps.md: 'Following a link to another app leaves a crumb on the new app's title line: a dim · and ↩, with the name of the app and tab you came from. Click the crumb, or press ⌫, to go back. The app you left is as you left it: the same tab, preset, sort, filters, groups, cursor row, and scroll position. If you reached that app by a link too, it still has its own crumb. The workspace menu's Manage… also leaves a crumb. Opening an app from the app menu, or switching workspace, clears the crumbs. Switching tabs does not. Crumbs last until kittui exits.'

findings.title: Rewrite: `kit packages` on a terminal
findings.claim: 'In reach' is undefined, and 'makes the only active ones the packages selected' inverts its objects.
findings.evidence: '`kit packages` alone, on a terminal, opens Packages, a row per package in reach, and `kit packages packages` opens it on its one tab. Its tab menu adds, removes, and makes the only active ones the packages selected, each by running `kit packages`; off a terminal, `kit packages` still lists them.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'On a terminal, `kit packages` opens the Packages app, with one row for each package the repository can use. The tab menu acts on the selected packages: it adds them, removes them, or makes them the only active ones. Each action runs a `kit packages` command. Without a terminal, `kit packages` prints the list.'

findings.title: Rewrite: `kit flow releases` and `kit workspace`
findings.claim: A 76-word sentence lists a release's JSON fields, and a 42-word sentence describes four stages with one verb each and no word 'stage'.
findings.evidence: 'kittui draws the rows from its catalog, so a preset shows or hides each field, and the table sorts, groups, and filters by it; a release's kind leads to its page, and an asset to its download.' And: 'Branches pair each remote's branch with the local ones that pull from it, worktrees list the desk first, commits are the ones the local branches hold and the default branch does not, and tags tell an annotated tag from a lightweight one. `kit workspace <stage>` prints one, ...'
findings.fix: Rewrite 146-150: '`--json` prints one flat object per release: version, tag, name, kind, whether it is the latest, when it was published, its page, its notes, and its assets (each file's name and download address). In kittui the table works like every other. A release's kind is a link to its page, and an asset is a link to its download.' Rewrite 154-156: 'The branches stage pairs each remote branch with the local branches that track it. The worktrees stage lists the desk first. The commits stage lists the commits on local branches that are not on the default branch.
