The tags stage says whether each tag is annotated or lightweight. `kit workspace <stage>` prints one stage, and `kit --workspace=<group> workspace` covers every repository in a group.'

findings.title: Rewrite: a `bash_path` that cannot be read
findings.claim: 'One' stands for `kit.yml` twice in one sentence, in two different senses, and the result is passive with no actor.
findings.evidence: 'A `kit.yml` that names `bash_path` is read through `yq`. One `yq` cannot parse, or one read where `yq` is missing, is refused, and `use` returns 2: the kit's own modules never stand in for a path it could not read.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'kit reads `bash_path` with `yq`. If `yq` is missing, or cannot parse `kit.yml`, `use` fails with status 2. It does not fall back to kit's own modules.'

findings.title: Rewrite: the verb header and its template
findings.claim: The opening of 'Writing a verb' is a 46-word sentence that ends a relative clause on a stranded 'to' and uses 'leaves it' and 'in it' for the template.
findings.evidence: 'Its header is the only place its help is written, and it has the shape of the verb template, `.kit/templates/bash/verb`, which the bash rule holds `kit/bin/kit-*` to: `kit lint` refuses a header that leaves it, and `kit new verb <name> --purpose=<text> --group=<group>` makes one in it.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'Its header is the only place its help is written. The header must match the verb template, `.kit/templates/bash/verb`. `kit lint` and `kit help` both reject a header that does not, and name the template line it departs from. `kit new verb <name> --purpose=<text> --group=<group>` creates a verb with this header:'

findings.title: Rewrite: exit status of a verb that prints JSON
findings.claim: The rule a script author most needs is a 47-word sentence with a colon, 'as ... do', and 'names in itself what could not'.
findings.evidence: 'A verb that prints JSON, as `kit flow` and `kit workspace` do, exits 1 when a part cannot be read: with `--json`, what was read is still printed, and names in itself what could not, a remote's `error`, a member under `errors`, or a stage of `null`.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: 'A verb that prints JSON, such as `kit flow` or `kit workspace`, exits 1 when it could not read everything. With `--json` it still prints what it read, and the document marks each missing part: an `error` on a remote, an entry under `errors` for a member, or `null` for a stage. Exit 1 with nothing on stdout means nothing could be read, and the last ❌ line on stderr says why. Exit 0 means the document is complete.'

findings.title: Rewrite: `log_days: 0`
findings.claim: The only hard passage on a good page: 'from the next new day's file on' and 'keeps it going' hide a simple rule.
findings.evidence: '`log_days: 0` writes no logs from the next new day's file on: a day whose log exists keeps it going. It leaves the logs there to remove by hand.'
findings.fix: Rewrite: '`log_days: 0` turns logging off from the next day. A log that already exists for today keeps growing until the day ends. kit does not delete the logs already written; remove them by hand.'

findings.title: Rewrite: where the context log is, and which files `kit generate` skips
findings.claim: context.md gives the same path three times before saying what a line holds; generate.md uses 'but a template' for 'except a template', which reads at first as a contrast.
findings.evidence: 'Every call appends one line per path to `kit/context.log` in git's common directory, `.git/kit/context.log` at the desk and the desk's `.git/kit/context.log` from a worktree: the epoch time and the path.' And: 'it expands every tracked file and every untracked file git does not ignore, but a template: a file under `.kit/templates/` or a package's `hosts/` is skipped, since its directive belongs to the file made from it.'
findings.fix: Rewrite context.md: 'Every call appends one line per path, the epoch time and the path, to the desk's `.git/kit/context.log`. A call from a worktree writes to the same file.' Rewrite generate.md: 'With no paths, it expands every tracked file, and every untracked file git does not ignore. It skips templates, which are the files under `.kit/templates/` and under a package's `hosts/`, because a directive in a template belongs to the file made from it.'

areas.title: the feature documents
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 30 files in scope (3,133 lines) and the prose, markdown, and house styles. Sampled code to check claims: kit-flow, kit-platform, kit-tools, serve.sh, apps.jq, books.go, the kit and agent packages' files. Ran only my own passage splitter and greps (out/P2/passages.py, counts.sh). Not checked: terminals.md and github/ci.md against code, external links.
areas.summary: No filler or agentic tics anywhere (0 hits for the usual words). The failure is the opposite one: a compressed private dialect. In a systematic sample of 59 of 768 passages, 49 pass the one-pass test (83%), but apps.md and workspaces.md pass 2 of 8 and hold 27 of the 43 sentences over 40 words and 29 of the 45 passages over 90 words. Recurring: bare "as" for "such as" (about 39), bare possessives (49), "desk" undefined (42 uses, three senses). Five docs-accuracy slips confirmed against code. Toolchain and package pages are good models. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from subagents, so the 22 rewrites are returned here as P2-18 to P2-39.
strengths: No machine-flavoured filler at all: 0 hits in 30 files for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, simply, note that, in order to; no restating summaries, no reflexive threes. Do not loosen this.

Every page opens by saying what its subject is in one or two sentences, and each page stands alone: the gate and the code forge are defined at first use on several pages (policy.md:13, packages.md:102, toolchains.md:3; policy.md:47, packages.md:276, trackers.md:3).

Good models to copy: docs/toolchains/using-mise.md, using-docker.md, using-devcontainer.md, using-no-toolchain.md, using-system-packages.md (median sentence 9 to 13 words), docs/packages/hooks/lefthook.md, docs/packages/policy/opa.md, docs/packages/agents/claude.md.

Good sections: docs/policy.md lines 1-72 and 139-291, docs/toolchains.md 'Choosing' and 'Where things are kept', docs/templates.md 'Making a file' and 'Checking a file', docs/trackers.md 'References', and each terminal's section in docs/terminals.md.

Tables are used well where they are used: toolchains.md's Detection table, every terminal's findings table, serve.md's three tool tables, the `kit tools` table on each toolchain page, claude.md's Denied/Instead table.
The toolchain pages share one shape (Set up, What kit reads, the kit tools table, On a runner), so a reader of one can find anything in another.

The agent pages end with 'Verified on 2026-10-30 against ...' and say when a source shows no version; the documents also say what kit does not do (serve.md:117-119, trackers.md:110-112, toolchains.md:148). Keep both habits.
Examples are real and small: policy.md's facts document and Rego rules, packages.md's expects and notices, trackers.md's tracker records, using-kit.md's tools block.

Checked against code and correct: serve.md's three tool lists and protocol revisions, the tutorials' page names, the welcome pages, the empowerite bundle's members, the CI answers' defaults, the tracker, toolchain, and dependency providers, and the flow setting's seven stages in packages.md.

Sample result, for the record: every 13th of 768 passages, 59 in all; 49 pass (83%), the 10 that fail hold 37% of the sampled words. By group: apps.md and workspaces.md 2 of 8, the other eight top-level pages 30 of 33, the package and toolchain pages 17 of 18.

findings.title: docs/apps.md cannot be read in one pass
findings.claim: The reference for seven verbs' JSON is written in a compressed dialect: 19 of its 50 passages are 90 words or longer (up to 197), 16 of 172 sentences pass 40 words, 47 carry five or more commas, semicolons, and colons, and it has 44 semicolons. One of the four passages my sample drew from it passed.
findings.evidence: apps.md:209-211: "GitLab's are its bot users among the members, as a project's or a group's access token makes, `acted` `null`, as GitLab does not say, and `last` the day each last acted." The content has columns (field, meaning, values; forge, read, cap, mark), and the markdown style's first rule says to use a table where content has columns.
findings.fix: For each stage, one table of fields and one table by forge (what is read, requests, cap, mark), then two or three plain sentences. Move "keys each row by" into a Key column and drop the mark bullets that repeat the Mark column (130-131, 168-172, 212-213, 276-280).

findings.title: docs/workspaces.md is six documents in one, with walls of text for kittui
findings.claim: The page covers the file, `kit workspaces`, the start rule, flow over a group, two kittui menus, `kit workspace`, `kit welcome`'s checks, and a roadmap; ten of its 47 passages are 90 words or longer and one of four sampled passages passed. The start rule is stated three times with different exceptions (56-63, 65-68, 93-95).
findings.evidence: The "Manage…" paragraph at 180-190 is 223 words listing eleven menu actions and their keys in running prose; the paragraph at 144-154 is 192 words.
findings.fix: Keep the file, members, start rule (once), and commands; move `kit workspace` (198-231) and `kit welcome` (233-251) to their own pages; turn the kittui sections into an action/key/asks-for table; cut "Still to come" to the four unbuilt items. That leaves about 150 of 264 lines.

findings.title: The prose rules do not cover the failure the documents actually have
findings.claim: The prose style's five rules (declarative, mood, no slogans, serial comma, acronyms) are obeyed, yet nothing limits what one sentence carries, requires a coined term to be defined at first use, or stops one word doing three jobs. The best guidance in the repository, tutorials.md:71-78 ("Short sentences. One idea each."), applies only to tutorials, and that page's own lines 19-36 break it.
findings.evidence: 0 hits in 30 files for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, simply, note that, in order to; against 43 sentences over 40 words and 166 with five or more commas, semicolons, and colons.
findings.fix: Add three rules to prose.md: one idea per sentence, splitting past about 30 words; define or link a coined term (desk, mark, stage, primary, placed) at first use on each page; introduce an example with "such as" and a cause with "because".

findings.title: "as" does three jobs, and the reader must work out which
findings.claim: `, as ` occurs 114 times; I classified each: about 39 mean "such as", about 12 mean "because", and about 60 are comparisons that send the reader to another command. The same scope writes "such as" 51 times, never in apps.md or workspaces.md and 12 times in serve.md.
findings.evidence: Example: apps.md:56 "as `github`, `mise`, or `patterns`", apps.md:121 "as one written to a contract before 4", workspaces.md:75 "as `.`, `~/Code/edge`". Cause: apps.md:11 "as it offers no Watch", apps.md:210 "as GitLab does not say", workspaces.md:95 "as it reads a repository"; comparison: apps.md:130 "joined, as `kit flow changes`' are".
findings.fix: Write "such as" or "for example" for every example and "because" for every cause. Keep "as X does" only where X is described on the same page.

findings.title: Coined terms are used before they are defined; "desk" has three senses
findings.claim: "desk" appears 42 times in ten files of the scope and is defined in none (the definition is in docs/architecture.md:121); it means the root checkout, a repository found under a folder, and a developer's machine as opposed to a runner. "mark" (35 uses), "form" for an output option, "primary", "placed", "the loader", and "crumb" are likewise undefined or unlinked.
findings.evidence: workspaces.md:78 "kept as its repository's desk"; workspaces.md:95 "draws each desk below, as it does above desks"; using-kit.md:73 "A desk locks". apps.md:14 "or no form off a terminal".
findings.fix: Give one defining sentence at first use on each page, or link the terms page (.kit/welcome/5-terms.md already defines desk). Write "a developer's machine" and "output option" where those are meant.

findings.title: Dropped nouns and verbs, and house verbs, make sentences that must be reconstructed
findings.claim: 49 clauses end on a bare possessive with the noun left out, verbs are dropped the same way, and ordinary words are replaced by house ones: "is no/are no" (11), "holds" (76), "judges" (41), "draws" (32), "stands" (13), "alone" for "only" (38), ", else" (20).
findings.evidence: apps.md:71 "Its first tab in kittui, issues, every open issue in the backlog or underway, is `kit flow`'s"; apps.md:88 "Azure DevOps' are its team's"; apps.md:163 "`actor` who made it; `age` seconds since". terminals.md:45 "A probe that fails where no setting of the terminal can fix it holds".
findings.fix: Restore the noun and the verb ("is one of `kit flow`'s tabs", "`age` is the seconds since it was made"). Prefer "is not", "contains", "checks", "shows", "only", "otherwise".

findings.title: Reference material is packed into one table cell or one list item
findings.claim: Five passages hold a section's worth of rules in one cell or bullet: the `change` cell is 186 words covering five cases, the base bullet is 161 words covering six places, and serve's path item is one 142-word sentence with five semicolons.
findings.evidence: policy.md:47 runs from "The open change, read through the code forge" to "so refuses a document given with `--facts` that holds one" inside a table row. policy.md's "What judges a branch" (74-137) is 64 lines and 20 bullets for one idea.
findings.fix: Give each a subsection with a small table: for `change`, value/when (object, null, {error}); for the base, where it runs/the base is (desk, GitHub pull request, merge group, GitLab merged results, GitLab otherwise). For serve's paths, state the rule in two sentences and list the edge cases.

findings.title: The pages count seven rule files and five templates; the kit package delivers eight and six
findings.where: docs/packages/kit.md:15-16, docs/packages/kit.md:26-27, docs/packages/agents/cursor.md:25, docs/packages/agents/copilot.md:24, docs/templates.md:6, docs/templates.md:40
findings.claim: kit.md lists seven rule files and omits `sh`; cursor.md and copilot.md say "its seven files" where each package places eight rule mirrors plus an mcp.json. templates.md and kit.md say the kit package delivers five templates, but the bash rule lists a sixth, `verb`, for `kit/bin/kit-*`.
findings.evidence: kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/rules/sh.md, kit/packages/agents/cursor/files/repo/.cursor/rules/kit-sh.mdc, and kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/templates/bash/verb exist; the bash rule's frontmatter has `- variant: verb`. Not in the 11-10 review.
findings.fix: Name `sh` in kit.md and drop the count from the agent pages. Add the `verb` template to templates.md and kit.md, or stop delivering it to repositories with no `kit/bin/`.

findings.title: workspaces.md says kit flow has eight stages; it has seven
findings.claim: "Over a workspace, the stages are kit's eight" contradicts the verb and two other documents.
findings.evidence: kit/bin/kit-flow:21 "seven stages" and :115 "the stages are kit's seven"; docs/packages.md:290 and kit.schema.json say "Default: all seven". The 11-10 review recorded the same slip in docs/features.md (its item 26), not here.
findings.fix: Write "seven".

findings.title: apps.md names a field of `controls` that its rows do not have
findings.claim: "`source` is `ruleset` or `protection`" names the wrong field: the row's field is `kind`, and every row's `source` is the forge.
findings.evidence: apps.md:225 lists `id, control, target, enforcement, rules, kind`; kit/modules/jq/apps.jq:115 is `del(.url, .source) + {kind: .source, ...}`.
findings.fix: Write "`kind` is `ruleset` or `protection`."

findings.title: workspaces.md calls the workspace menu the 📚 control; its glyph is `-`; other stale names
findings.claim: Lines 195 and 256 say "the 📚 workspace menu" and "the 📚 control" though line 158 and the code say `-`; the "Still to come" list holds three items that "are built"; packages.md and templates.md still say "kit tui's package view" and "`kit tui` offers" where the rest says kittui.
findings.evidence: projects/tui/internal/shell/books.go:29 `const Workspaces = "-"`, and :40 makes 📚 a group's glyph.
findings.fix: Write "the workspace menu, `-`", move the built items out of the list, and write "kittui" and "Packages in kittui".

findings.title: packages.md says the same thing three times
findings.claim: The sentence on region markers "out of order, doubled, or never closed" appears under `kit packages remove`, under `kit uninstall`, and under Regions; "A copied file the repository edited is named and left" appears twice. serve.md lists what the read-only tools do not offer at 71-87 and again at 92-110.
findings.evidence: packages.md:23-25 and 34-36 are word for word the same clause: "a region whose markers are out of order, doubled, or never closed is named, nothing is taken out, and it exits 1".
findings.fix: State the rule once in Regions and write "see Regions" in the two verb bullets. The Settings table (271-290) also repeats kit.schema.json; generate it or link.

findings.title: The documents break the repository's markdown style in small ways
findings.where: docs/serve.md:62-88, docs/toolchains.md:42-55, docs/workspaces.md:161-189, docs/terminals.md:90, docs/toolchains/using-docker.md:15, docs/apps.md:237-242
findings.claim: 32 bold spans against "Do not bold words for emphasis" (23 bold-led bullets; 3 of about 15 menu labels in workspaces.md are bold); "See:" ten times in terminals.md against `see:`; an angle-bracket placeholder in a fenced snippet; GHSA, SAST, CSI, OSC 52, WSL, and LTS never expanded. "the kit" and "kit" name one thing 72 and 122 times, split by page (packages.md 23 to 3, terminals.md 0 to 35).
findings.evidence: toolchains.md:52 "- **usable**: its tool is installed"; using-docker.md:15 `FROM debian:13@sha256:<digest>`.
findings.fix: Drop the bold on the bullets, pick one treatment for menu labels, lower-case "see:", and pick "kit".

findings.title: Two rules make the text worse where they are followed
findings.claim: The snippet rule (a supplied value is a shell variable) is applied to usage lines, which are not pasteable, so shell quoting is mixed with grammar brackets. Prose rule 1 (the subject first) is broken by the fragment openings of all twelve package pages, which nevertheless read well.
findings.evidence: templates.md:127: `kit new file "${path}" [--rule="${rule}"] [--variant="${variant}"] [--"${hole}"="${value}"]…`, while :76 on the same page writes `--purpose=<…>`. workflow.md:3 opens "Delivers `.kit/workflow.md`: …".
findings.fix: Use shell variables only in commands a reader pastes and `<name>` in a grammar. Keep the fragment openings and let the rule allow them.

findings.title: A few slogans and "X, not Y" turns remain
findings.claim: Of twelve ", not X" turns, five sentences read as slogans against prose rule 3, and each paragraph loses nothing without them.
findings.evidence: "The package is taste, not trust." "A new file is a starting point, not a finished file." "A tutorial tells you what to type; you type it."
findings.fix: Cut them, or state the fact: "The package is optional; the rules in the `kit` package apply without it."

findings.title: Two pages define the code forge as GitHub or GitLab, leaving out Azure DevOps
findings.claim: trackers.md and policy.md name only GitHub and GitLab as forges though Azure DevOps is a forge provider and trackers.md:40 says so. empowerite.md says `agents/claude` brings the deny list and the hook and omits the MCP server.
findings.evidence: trackers.md:3-4 "the code forge (the service that hosts the repository, GitHub or GitLab) or a separate system such as Azure DevOps"; kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh exists. claude.md:33 and packages.md:359 describe `.mcp.json`.
findings.fix: Name all three forges, and add "and the kit's MCP server" to the empowerite table.

findings.title: Maintainer and repository-only detail sits in user pages
findings.claim: templates.md's "Where a hole ends" and the second half of "Blocks" describe the matcher for whoever maintains it, using-nix.md ends with 17 lines about this repository's own flake, and workspaces.md ends with a roadmap. The other pages (serve, terminals, toolchains, trackers, tutorials, every package and toolchain page) are the right length.
findings.evidence: templates.md:109 "A template is matched in one pass, with no regular expression… the time is linear in the file."
findings.fix: Keep two sentences for a template author and move the rest beside the code; move the flake notes to the repository's own notes; cut the roadmap to the four unbuilt items.

findings.title: Rewrite: what a mark is
findings.claim: "A mark is a text that changes when what its stage draws does, and `null` for a stage with none, which kittui reads again only on Refresh, as it offers no Watch for a tab kit never marks."
findings.fix: "A mark is a short string that changes whenever the stage's content changes; kittui compares marks to decide when to reload a tab. A stage with no mark prints `null`, and kittui reloads that tab only on Refresh and offers no Watch for it."

findings.title: Rewrite: the stage document and its output options
findings.claim: "…prints the stage's document, `{rows, errors}`, and `limited: N` where a capped read stopped at N, the newest. `--jq` prints it formatted, and `--text`, or no form off a terminal, as a table."
findings.fix: "`--json` prints the stage as `{rows, errors}`, plus `limited: N` when kit stopped at a cap: it holds the newest N rows and the forge has more. `--jq` prints the same JSON formatted; `--text` prints a table, as does the verb with none of these options when its output is not a terminal."

findings.title: Rewrite: rows that carry their own origin
findings.claim: "A row that names its own keeps them, as an issue says the tracker and the repository that hold it, and a rule of `audit policy` the place it is in force."
findings.fix: "A row that already has these three fields keeps its own values. For example, an issue's row names the tracker and repository that hold the issue, and a row of `kit audit policy` names the place where the rule applies."

findings.title: Rewrite: tabs that belong to another command, and exit status
findings.claim: "A tab of the app that another command prints opens on a terminal as the verb's own do; with `--json`, the verb refuses with 2 and names that command. Each verb exits 0 when its stages are drawn, 1 when one could not be read, after what was, and 2 on a usage error, or outside a repository's working tree with no workspace."
findings.fix: "Some tabs belong to another command (Issues' first tab is `kit flow issues`); `kit <verb> <tab>` opens one on a terminal, and with `--json` exits 2 and names the command to run. Exit status: 0 when every stage printed; 1 when a stage could not be read (the others still print); 2 for a usage error, or outside a repository with no workspace."

findings.title: Rewrite: a provider without check-runs
findings.claim: "A forge whose provider lacks `check-runs`, as one written to a contract before 4, prints no runs on its changes: the stage has no rows, and `{feature: check-runs, off: true, lacked: true}` under `errors` says why, though `kit flow changes` counts their checks."
findings.fix: "A forge provider that does not implement the `check-runs` call, such as one written for version 3 of the forge contract, gives this stage no rows, and `errors` holds `{feature: check-runs, off: true, lacked: true}`. `kit flow changes` still shows each change's count of checks."

findings.title: Rewrite: how merged changes are read on GitHub
findings.claim: "GitHub reads the 50 pull requests updated last, as a merge updates one, and orders them by merge; … A list read by update could miss a change merged before the oldest update in it, so it keeps only those merged since, and `limited` counts them." The rewrite states a reason (GitHub cannot sort by merge time) that the original only implies; the authors should confirm it.
findings.fix: "GitHub cannot sort by merge time, so kit reads the 50 pull requests updated most recently and sorts the merged ones by merge time. That list can miss one merged earlier and not touched since, so kit drops rows merged before the oldest update in it, and `limited` is the number kept."

findings.title: Rewrite: GitLab's agents
findings.claim: "GitLab's are its bot users among the members, as a project's or a group's access token makes, `acted` `null`, as GitLab does not say, and `last` the day each last acted."
findings.fix: "On GitLab, the rows are the bot users among the project's members; GitLab creates one for each project or group access token. `acted` is `null`, because GitLab does not report what a bot did, and `last` is the day of its last activity."

findings.title: Rewrite: the policy stage's empty and null places
findings.claim: "A clone with no remote on a forge is its main checkout's directory. A place the clone has none of, the organization of a clone with no remote or the source of a remote on no forge, is `""`; `null` is only the place a merged row spans. Another checkout is read as it is, nothing placed in it…" I read "nothing placed in it" as "without delivering files into it"; confirm.
findings.fix: "For a clone with no remote on a forge, `repository` is the main checkout's directory name, and a field that does not apply is `""`: `organization` with no remote, `source` with a remote on no forge kit knows. `null` means the row was merged across that field; kit reads each other worktree as it is, without delivering files into it, and lists one it cannot read as `{branch, error}` under `errors`."

findings.title: Rewrite: how policy rows merge
findings.claim: "`policy` merges the rows of a rule that agree, its pattern, from, and engine the same. From the widest place down, a place whose rows all agree is one row, at the narrowest place that holds them all: `scope` names it, … and the fields finer than it are `null`."
findings.fix: "Rows for one rule are merged when they have the same `pattern`, `from`, and `engine`; kit merges at the widest level where every row agrees, and `scope` names that level. Fields narrower than the scope are `null`: a rule that is the same on every branch of a repository is one row with `scope: repository` and `branch: null`."

findings.title: Rewrite: kit packages' own commands (the paragraph contradicts itself)
findings.claim: The paragraph says `kit packages` "alone, with a filter, or with `--text`, … lists the packages as text" and three lines later "On a terminal, `kit packages` alone opens Packages in kittui".
findings.fix: "On a terminal, `kit packages` with no arguments opens Packages in kittui; off a terminal, or with a filter or `--text`, it prints the list as text. `--json` with no stage prints one object per package, `select`, `add`, and `remove` change the active set, and the app-verb options (`--stages`, `--marks`, `kit packages packages`) work too."

findings.title: Rewrite: who reads the workspaces file
findings.claim: "`kit workspaces`, `kit --workspace=<name> flow`, and `kit --workspace=<name> workspace` each say what is wrong and exit 1, printing nothing, as `kit flow` and `kit workspace` do outside a repository with a group used last, where they read the file for that group. Inside a repository, or with no group used, `kit flow` and `kit workspace` with no `--workspace=` read no file."
findings.fix: "A command that reads a bad file says what is wrong, prints nothing else, and exits 1. `kit workspaces` always reads the file; `kit flow` and `kit workspace` read it only when they need a group: with `--workspace=<name>`, or outside a repository when a last-used group is recorded."

findings.title: Rewrite: recent repositories
findings.claim: "`kit workspaces --use=<folder>`, with a folder written as a path, as `.`, `~/Code/edge`, or `/srv/edge`, keeps the repository whose working tree holds it first among the recent repositories… A linked worktree is no workspace of its own: its folder is kept as its repository's desk, and one kept before stands as that desk. A recent repository is no group: kit starts on it only inside it, as on any other."
findings.fix: "`kit workspaces --use=<path>`, with a path such as `.` or `~/Code/edge`, adds the repository that contains the path to the recent repositories, kept in `kit/workspaces/recent` under `XDG_CACHE_HOME`: at most ten, newest first, each once. A path inside a linked worktree is recorded as its root checkout, and a recent repository is only a shortcut in the workspace menu: it does not change which workspace kit starts on."

findings.title: Rewrite: with no group
findings.claim: "With no group used, or with `--workspace=none`, `kit flow` draws each desk below, as it does above desks, and `kit workspace` refuses with 2, as it reads a repository." The comparison "each desk below, as it does above desks" explains the thing by itself.
findings.fix: "With no last-used group, or with `--workspace=none`, `kit flow` lists each repository it finds under the current directory, up to four levels down. `kit workspace` exits 2, because it needs a repository."

findings.title: Rewrite: what a pattern matches
findings.claim: "A pattern matches the repositories `--from`'s command printed, else, for `--remove`, the group's members, else the members of the checkouts under the roots, and one that matches none is refused with 2. … a group does not follow a pattern or a command afterward, which the queries of `match` will, once they are built."
findings.fix: "A pattern is matched against one list: what the `--from` command printed, when you gave one; otherwise the group's members for `--remove`, and the checkouts under your roots for `--new` and `--add`; matching nothing is a usage error, exit 2. kit writes the matched repositories under `repos` and does not save the pattern or the command, so the group does not pick up new repositories later."

findings.title: Rewrite: the workspace menu
findings.claim: "…the recent repositories, the one shown first, or the one a worktree shown belongs to, unless a favorite names it already. The one shown is dim, wherever it stands, as is a favorite repository with no checkout. … tab completes a folder, the folders it can complete to stand under it, and a plain click on one opens it."
findings.fix: "The menu lists, in order: the groups this repository belongs to, your favorites, the other groups, and the recent repositories, the current one first unless a favorite already lists it; the current workspace is dim, as is a favorite with no checkout. The last line, Open Repository…, opens a dialog where you type a folder: Tab completes it, the completions are listed below, and a click on one opens it."

findings.title: Rewrite: serve's path rule, one 142-word sentence
findings.claim: The item runs from "a path outside the repository" through five semicolons to "the repository root's own path included" without a full stop.
findings.fix: "A path given to `context`, `kinds`, or `lint` is outside when it is absolute, climbs out through `..`, or leaves through a symbolic link. In doubt the server refuses: a `..` after a link must be inside both as the kernel resolves it and as a shell's `cd` does, a missing path is judged by its nearest existing directory, and a dangling link or a path of `PATH_MAX` or more is outside."

findings.title: Rewrite: a branch cannot loosen its rules (nine-part subject before the verb)
findings.claim: "A branch cannot loosen the rule that judges it: a pattern it blanks, a login it adds under `linked_exempt`, an engine it names, a file it stops a rule from reading, a `forge` it drops or a `forges` entry it changes, a kind it redefines, and a file it removes, adds, or edits under `.kit/policy/` change nothing."
findings.fix: "A branch cannot loosen the rules that judge it. None of these edits on the branch has any effect until it is merged: blanking a pattern, adding a login to `linked_exempt`, naming another engine, removing a file from `facts.read`, changing `forge` or `forges`, redefining a kind, and adding, editing, or removing a file under `.kit/policy/`."

findings.title: Rewrite: what kit packages lists ("which adds" has no subject)
findings.claim: "`kit packages` lists every package in reach, which are active, and which are excluded, filtered by state… On a terminal, `kit packages` alone opens Packages in kittui: a row per package in reach, what it depends on and includes, and the active packages that need it, which adds, removes, and selects the packages selected by running the verbs below."
findings.fix: "`kit packages` lists every package kit can find and says whether each is active, inactive, or excluded; filter with `--active`, `--inactive`, a name, or a glob, and `--json` prints JSON. On a terminal, `kit packages` with no arguments opens the Packages app in kittui, where you add, remove, and select packages by the verbs below; `--text` prints the plain list there."

findings.title: Rewrite: require_signing
findings.claim: "`true` makes `kit commit`, `kit work`, and `kit rebase` refuse before writing anything when git has no `user.signingkey`, makes `kit commit`, `kit work`'s start commit, and `kit rebase` sign every commit they make, refusing the commit when git cannot sign it, and makes `kit release` sign its tag."
findings.fix: "When `true`, `kit commit`, `kit work`, and `kit rebase` sign every commit they make, and `kit release` signs its tag. Each refuses, before it writes anything, when git has no `user.signingkey`, and refuses the commit when git cannot sign it."

findings.title: Rewrite: a hole never swallows a label
findings.claim: "A hole's text never holds one of the template's own whole lines that has a letter or digit, such as a section's label. Such a line inside a section would end the section there, and the rest of the file could still match with the label inside the next section, read wrong without a word. So the file does not match, at the hole's line, and `kit lint` names the file's line that holds it."
findings.fix: "A hole never matches text that contains one of the template's own labelled lines, such as `# Arguments:`. Otherwise a file with that label in the wrong place could still match with its sections silently misread, so `kit lint` reports the file and names the line."

findings.title: Rewrite: how kit judges settings and probes
findings.claim: "A finding fails only on a value kit read. A setting kit could not read is not a finding, and a finding that reads a setting its reader did not give is kit's own bug, which the terminal's heading names." and "A setting explains, and a probe measures, so they never both report one cause: a probe is left out where a setting of its need failed. A probe that fails where no setting of the terminal can fix it holds…"
findings.fix: "kit reports a finding only for a setting it read and skips one it could not read; if kit's own code asks for a setting its reader does not supply, that is a bug in kit, and the terminal's heading says so." "When a setting already explains a problem, kit skips the probe for the same need; when a probe fails and no setting can fix it, the finding stays and says what kittui does instead."

findings.title: Rewrite: tutorials.md breaks its own writing advice; two more unclear lines
findings.claim: tutorials.md:22-24: "The `--tag` values that name an audience filter the cards to the tutorials for any of them, as the text, `--json`, and `--jq` forms keep them; the filter is the table's, to change or drop." Also unclear: toolchains.md:158 "`kit welcome` holds a linter found in either" (I could not settle its meaning) and ci.md:17 "refuses, never replaces, one the runner cannot use".
findings.fix: "On a terminal, with none of `--text`, `--json`, or `--jq`, it opens kittui's tutorials screen, one card per tutorial, with the control line every kittui table has and two presets, `By audience` and `In the kit or online`. `--tag` opens the screen filtered to those audiences, and you can change or clear the filter there." For ci.md: "If the runner cannot use it, the job fails; kit does not fall back to another."

areas.title: the integrations research pages
areas.coverage: Read whole 24 of 40 pages: the six longest, four category pages, 1st.md, and 13 short ones; prose only of the other 16. Did not read the 79 output schemas or verify outside-tool claims. Ran pattern counts, cell word counts, a link and anchor check (362, 0 broken), and a function-name lookup against the code.
areas.summary: The integration pages have no machine filler (0 hits for the usual words, 0 bold). Their failure is over-compression. Of 140 passages sampled, 96 pass a one-read test (69%); 33 of the 44 failures are in git, gh, glab, and az, where implementation notes sit in table cells of up to 196 words. The 29 short pages are good models (21 of 23 pass). The category pages are stale: they call shipped features "planned", omit Azure DevOps, and state contract 3 where the code is at 6. The five multi-service pages repeat their intros and schema links. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the Write, so the 25 rewrites and per-page table are not on disk.
strengths: No machine filler anywhere: 0 hits for ensure, robust, seamless, leverage, comprehensive, crucial, or "worth noting"; 0 bold; no restating summaries. Do not add any.
Every fact is specific and usable: exact commands, fields, and limits. gh.md:31 is the model: "`gh auth status` passes with a revoked token, so kit makes a real call."

The pages say what was and was not verified (19 "not verified", 6 "not checked", 5 "not tried/run", 5 "checked live", dated checks such as "answers 404 on 2026-11-10"), and the category pages admit their ordering has no survey behind it. Keep this.
All 362 local links and anchors resolve, and the gh, glab, and az schema tables match their directories file for file (34, 26, 19).
Snippets follow the house rule: values are "${name}", with only 6 angle-bracket placeholders in 43,000 words.
One shape for every tool page (services table, Read, Write, Gaps, Schemas), explained once in 1st.md:83-99, makes any page quick to scan.

Good models to copy: gerrit.md, hut.md, rad.md (six lines tell a stranger how the system differs, and every "none" says why); flux.md, argocd.md, kubectl.md; jira.md; tea.md among the long pages (0 of 5 sampled passages fail).
ci.md:1-40 and cd.md:1-25 are the best running prose in the directory, and aws.md:153-258 (the AWS provider plan) defines its term, states costs, and lists entry conditions in short sections.

The 29 short pages are the right length (447 words each on average; 21 of 23 sampled passages pass). Only git.md is too long for what it says; gh, glab, and az have the right content in the wrong place.

findings.title: Category pages call shipped features "planned" and leave out the Azure DevOps provider
findings.where: docs/integrations/forges.md:32, docs/integrations/forges.md:40, docs/integrations/trackers.md:11, docs/integrations/trackers.md:33, docs/integrations/ci.md:14, docs/integrations/ci.md:49, docs/integrations/1st.md:17
findings.claim: The Scope tables of forges.md, trackers.md, and ci.md describe an older kit than the tool pages beside them. forges.md also has no row for nine capabilities gh.md:46-54 documents as kit's (reviewers, merged, access, teams, bots, attestations, alerts, rulesets).
findings.evidence: forges.md:40-43 says the reviews, checks, and merged tabs are planned and :32 says ready has "no seam call", but kit/bin/kit-changes:8-10 has all three stages and kit/bin/kit-ready:43 calls forge:pr-ready; trackers.md:11 says iterations and milestones have "no data source yet" while kit/bin/kit-issues:8-9 has both. ci.md:14 and :23 name only GitHub and GitLab though forge/ado.sh:501 reads Azure Pipelines runs, and 1st.md:17 names a "backlog stage" that kit-flow:299 says is no stage.
findings.fix: Update the four Scope tables from the feature table in kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:201-232 and add the nine missing rows to forges.md. Name Azure DevOps wherever ci.md names the other two providers.

findings.title: Pages state the forge contract as version 3; the code is at 6, and az.md understates what Azure lacks
findings.claim: 1st.md, az.md, and the AWS plan all cite contract version 3, and az.md lists four lacking features where the provider declares twelve.
findings.evidence: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:287 is `declare -gr forge_contract=6` and forge/ado.sh:86 prints 5. forge/ado.sh:88-91 lacks `quota marks releases linked-branches milestones bots attestations code-scanning dependabot secret-scanning bypasses swimlanes`, against az.md:23 "lacks rate limits it shows, cheap marks, releases, and branches linked to a work item".
findings.fix: Drop the number from 1st.md, give az.md the real version and point at forge/ado:lacks for the list. Re-base the AWS plan on the current feature table.

findings.title: Eighteen table cells hold 60 to 196 words each as one comma-chained sentence
findings.claim: In gh.md, glab.md, and az.md the Command column carries a capability's whole implementation story (query, limits, scopes, error messages, kit's reaction, the verb that shows it), and none of these cells can be understood in one read. The house rules "use a table where the content has columns" and "do not wrap tables" leave nowhere else to put it.
findings.evidence: A word count of every cell finds 18 of 60 words or more (gh 9, glab 5, az 4) and 7 of 100 or more; gh.md:54 is 196 words with 18 commas and 5 semicolons, and gh.md:52 is one 1,214-character line. Sample: "a login without it is asked once more without `... on Team { slug }`, its teams unnamed, among those; a dismissal is a row of the alerts, not read again; then…" (gh.md:54).
findings.fix: Keep each cell to the command and move the rest under the table as a short subsection or list per capability, in full sentences; no fact needs to go. Add a line to the markdown style: a cell holds a phrase or a command, and anything longer goes under the table.

findings.title: The five multi-service pages repeat themselves section by section
findings.where: docs/integrations/gh.md:89, docs/integrations/gh.md:207, docs/integrations/gh.md:249, docs/integrations/az.md:128, docs/integrations/aws.md:94, docs/integrations/az.md:217
findings.claim: gh, glab, az, aws, and tea read as separate research notes pasted under one title: each service section re-introduces the tool and re-lists the same schema links under new link text.
findings.evidence: 17 tool-introduction paragraphs in 5 pages, 12 of them repeats (198, 241, and 228 words in gh, glab, az); the "Microsoft publishes no OpenAPI document" sentences appear at az.md:74, 128, 169, and 219, and the CodeCommit dates at aws.md:19, 94, and 159. A script finds 11 URLs with two to four link texts (against the markdown style's Links rule 2), and az.md:167 and :217 give one schema at two URLs (main, master).
findings.fix: Keep one tool paragraph at the top of each page and let each service section say only what is special to it. Merge the Schemas lists into one per page with each URL once.

findings.title: git.md hand-indexes 110 function names in 207 places, and nothing checks them
findings.claim: The "Used by" column of git.md's Scope table (1,140 words) and its Formats tables name kit's internal functions, which a reader who does not know the code cannot use and which rot silently on a rename. The Read and Write tables (1,739 words) list every spelling of every git call the same way.
findings.evidence: I looked up all 110 distinct names in kit/modules and kit/bin: 109 exist, and `welcome:where` (git.md:32 and :33) does not; the function is `welcome:here` at kit/modules/bash/welcome.sh:683. No test or bin/ci step reads the page.
findings.fix: Cut the column to the verbs and stages, or generate the tables from the code and check them in the gate. Fix `welcome:where` now.

findings.title: A house dialect replaces ordinary words throughout the provider pages
findings.claim: The pages avoid filler entirely but lean on a compressed private idiom that needs a second read: "alone" for only, "among them" for including, causal ", as", "a request a team" for per, "draws" for shows, "tells … by" for recognizes. Prose rule 1 read strictly also yields possessive fragments such as "Premium's, refused below it".
findings.evidence: Counts by grep: ", as" 44 in 15 pages, "alone" 26 in 13, "draws" 46 in 7, "among them/those" 14 in 7, dropped-"per" forms 14 in 4, "tells" 8 in 4. Examples: "answers any other 403 `Must have push access`, which kit says names who can give it" (gh.md:48); "a team asked among none of their reviewers" (gh.md:46); "as `#7` and `AB#7` alike" (az.md:25).
findings.fix: Write the ordinary word each time, for example gh.md:48 as "Anyone else gets 403 `Must have push access`, and kit's error says who can grant it." and glab.md:52 as "The call answers `null` when no rule is set; push rules need Premium, and a lower tier refuses the call."

findings.title: Terms of art are used without a definition on the page that uses them
findings.where: docs/integrations/gh.md:36, docs/integrations/gh.md:45, docs/integrations/git.md:32, docs/integrations/1st.md:114, docs/integrations/jira.md:14, docs/integrations/gh.md:51
findings.claim: mark, desk, point, `limited`, the gate, and "the record's prefix" are never defined where a reader meets them, and several acronyms are unexpanded against prose rule 5.
findings.evidence: "mark(s)" has 63 uses in 10 pages with one passing gloss at ci.md:17; "desk" 20 uses in git.md; "a point" 6 and `limited` 6 in gh/glab; "the gate" 4 (it is bin/ci). SLSA, SAN, DER (gh.md:51), HAL (op.md:14), DID (rad.md:30), and ARN (aws.md:169) are not expanded; "stand-in" is defined well but only at aws.md:205.
findings.fix: Add a short glossary to 1st.md (seam, mark, stage, desk, stand-in, `limited`, the gate) and link the first use on each page to it. Expand the acronyms at first use.

findings.title: hut.md points to two pages that do not hold what it promises
findings.claim: hut.md sends the reader to trackers.md for todo.sr.ht's schema and to ci.md for builds.sr.ht's manifest schema, and neither page mentions SourceHut.
findings.evidence: hut.md:58-59: "todo.sr.ht's is on [trackers.md](trackers.md), and builds.sr.ht's manifest schema on [ci.md](ci.md)". `grep -i 'sourcehut\|sr.ht\|hut' trackers.md ci.md` prints nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence, or add the two rows to trackers.md and ci.md.

findings.title: Small inconsistencies between pages of the same shape
findings.claim: Pages that share one template differ in status formatting, table headings, legends, and date format, and trackers.md has a row that contradicts its own legend.
findings.evidence: trackers.md:85 is a `new-url` row of fifteen `—`, which the legend at :69 defines as "the tracker cannot" while :70 says kit builds it for every tracker. kit status is `none` in backticks in 17 rows and bare in 18 (both in tea.md:14-16); Scope headings come in three sets; the cli/api/— legend is written four ways (1st.md:92, trackers.md:69, ci.md:124, cd.md:64); dates are "March 28, 2029" and "20 August 2026".
findings.fix: Delete the `new-url` row and say in the legend that kit builds it with no call. Pick one status format, one heading set, one legend in 1st.md, and one date format.

findings.title: glab.md says kit uses `glab api` "for every call but the draft"; ten calls use other commands
findings.claim: The opening paragraph of glab.md overstates how much of the provider goes through `glab api`.
findings.evidence: glab.md:6-7: "kit reads the REST API through `glab api` for every call but the draft". kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh runs `glab issue update` (118, 168), `glab issue note` (132, 139), `glab issue close` (134), `glab issue create` (144), `glab mr create` (451), and `glab mr update` (479, 483, 491).
findings.fix: Write: "kit reads through `glab api` and pages each list itself; it writes with `glab issue` and `glab mr`."

findings.title: Single sentences that are broken, empty, misplaced, or stock
findings.where: docs/integrations/harness.md:47, docs/integrations/aws.md:110, docs/integrations/1st.md:119, docs/integrations/linear.md:52, docs/integrations/az.md:210, docs/integrations/az.md:8, docs/integrations/gh.md:208, docs/integrations/cd.md:12, docs/integrations/ci.md:10
findings.claim: A handful of sentences fail on their own: a pasted tag, a line that tells nothing, a closing slogan against prose rule 3, a mislabelled paragraph, an inverted clause, a 62-word sentence, and a 32-word stock opening repeated on 31 pages.
findings.evidence: harness.md:47 "so it is (not verified)."; aws.md:110 "Every command below is real"; 1st.md:119 "a fake is only as true as the documents it returns"; ci.md:10 "what a seam is, [architecture.md] says"; az.md:210 explains `...` after the tables that use it; gh.md:208 has `--json <fields>`. "This page says what `x` reads and writes where it meets kit's scope…" opens 31 pages though 1st.md:95-97 says it once.
findings.fix: Fix each in place: for cd.md:12-15 split into four sentences (what kit delivery lists, which forges answer, what an environment shows, what a deployment shows). Drop the stock opening from the tool pages and keep the link to 1st.md.

findings.title: git.md records that kit needs git 2.31 and checks no version
findings.claim: The page honestly documents a product gap outside the prose lens: kit calls a git option added in 2.31 and never checks git's version, so an older git would give a wrong main-checkout path.
findings.evidence: git.md:18-19: "`kit welcome` checks only that `git --version` answers. It calls `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute`, which git 2.31 added, and an older git prints the option back as a path." kit/modules/bash/git.sh:47 makes the call and welcome.sh:330-346 checks only that --version runs; not reproduced, as no old git is here (running `kit work` under git 2.30 would settle it).
findings.fix: Have `kit welcome` compare the version against 2.31 and state the minimum in the README.

areas.title: what a consumer and a newcomer read
areas.coverage: Read whole: all 46 scope files (1,786 lines): 1st.md, .kit/README.md, welcome 1-5, 8 rules, 8 styles, workflow.md, agent packages, 17 templates, AGENTS.md, projects/tui/README.md, 3 mdx. Sampled code and docs to check claims. Ran sentence statistics, pattern counts, a 52-passage sample, lychee. findings.md not written: the harness refused the Write.
areas.summary: The consumer prose under kit/packages is plain and free of machine filler (0 hits for 20 marker words in 17,379 words); 36 of 43 sampled passages pass. projects/tui/README.md fails: 5,816 words, mean sentence 28 words, 56 sentences over 35 words, one list item of 3,454 words. Overall 41 of 52 sampled passages pass (79%). The faults are compression, not padding: ", as X," for "such as", "stands" for "is", elided possessives, semicolon chains, undefined terms (harness, seam, stand-in). Docs-accuracy: the tutorials site's only page, the ".kit commits only packages/" claim, and the customize page's links are wrong. The glossary's 44 terms should be about 38: cut 11 general words, add 5 missing.
strengths: No machine-flavoured writing: 0 hits across 46 files and 17,379 words for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, simply, utilize, 'note that', 'in order to', and ten more; no hedges and no summaries that restate.

The rules and styles are the best prose in the tree: numbered, one or two sentences an item, the reason attached, mean sentence 8 to 16 words. Models: rules/sh.md, rules/jq.md, styles/bash.md, styles/gitignore.md.
1st.md:8-53 (Integrity, the desk, kit commands instead of git commands): an agent can act on every line.
Every delivered file opens by saying what it is, which package it comes from, and how to remove or replace it.
The glossary's definitions are one or two short sentences each (mean 8.7 words), each with a command; 4-customize.md gives every part the same three things: what, where, command.
workflow.md:35-50, the worker contract: ten short imperatives.
The shipped tutorials (kit/modules/tutorials/screen.md, control-line.md; sampled, outside scope): a picture first, keys as a list, mean sentence 6 to 10 words. They are the model for the TUI README.
The one-line purposes in the verb headers, and the numbered order at modules/bash/toolchain.sh:197-208, which is clearer than the welcome page that describes the same thing.
1-introduction.md says what kit is, where it works, and who it is for in 27 lines.

findings.title: projects/tui/README.md cannot be read: one list item of 3,454 words, sentences up to 126 words
findings.claim: The README is 5,816 words, and its Layout item for internal/flow/ (lines 87-253) is a 3,454-word specification of every key, click, and glyph. It also repeats the package comments (internal/flow/legend.go:1-6 against README:162-169) and docs/features.md, which styles/prose.md item 3 forbids.
findings.evidence: Mean sentence 28.0 words against 8 to 18 in every other file; 56 sentences over 35 words, 29 over 50; 3 of 7 sampled passages fail and hold 344 of 418 sampled words. Lines 102-105: "After how many rows are selected, a chip per filter, which a click opens its field's card under, on its filter, and 📇 Fields, which opens the columns dialog, as f on the line does, it names the preset the table is set as and ▼ …"
findings.fix: Cut it to about 120 lines (what kittui is, the screens, how kit finds it, one line per package, testing) and move behaviour to docs/apps.md as lists, in the form kit/modules/tutorials/control-line.md uses. Example rewrite of 102-105: "On the right, in order: how many rows are selected, a chip for each filter, 📇 Fields, and the preset's name with ▼. Click a chip to open its field's card; click 📇 Fields, or press f, to open the columns dialog."

findings.title: The tutorials site's one page describes a product that no longer exists
findings.claim: The page says "kit's tutorials are web pages, one for each feature" and that "a button opens its tutorial here, in your browser". Nine of the ten catalogued tutorials ship in the kit and open in kittui, on cards.
findings.evidence: kit/modules/tutorials.yml lists one entry with path: and nine with file: tutorials/<id>.md. kit/bin/kit-tutorials:8-10: "some ship with the kit, pages read on this machine … a card for each tutorial … a tutorial in the kit opens there, and one online in the browser".
findings.fix: Rewrite the first two sections: most tutorials ship with kit and open in kittui, the ones on this site open in the browser, and the screen shows a card for each.

findings.title: ".kit/ commits one thing, and only this: packages/" is false; team presets are committed there too
findings.claim: Both pages say packages/ is the only committed content of .kit/ and everything else is placed by kit hydrate. kittui writes a team's presets to .kit/presets/<stage>/ for the person to commit.
findings.evidence: projects/tui/internal/table/team.go:18 has const TeamDir = ".kit/presets"; projects/tui/README.md:122-128 says "checked into the workspace … which kit commit carries"; kit/modules/tutorials/control-line.md:38 says "files in the repository, under .kit/presets".
findings.fix: Name presets/ beside packages/ in .kit/README.md:12 and in the list at 1st.md:120-127.

findings.title: The customize page's links break the kit's own markdown rule, and the gate's link check reads none of kit/packages
findings.claim: rules/markdown.md:12 says a relative link resolves from its file; the page's six links ([kit.yml](kit.yml) four times, .kit/packages/, .kit/README.md) are written from the repository root because kittui joins them to the folder it reads (internal/welcome/customize.go:50-63). The gate does not notice, because every markdown file under kit/packages sits below a hidden directory and lychee skips those.
findings.evidence: On a copy: `lychee --offline --include-fragments --no-progress kit/packages` prints "0 Total … 0 Errors"; with --hidden it prints "25 Total … 7 Errors". Six errors are these links and the seventh is workflow.md:6 to 1st.md, which resolves once both are placed.
findings.fix: Write the links from the file (../../kit.yml, ../packages/, ../README.md) and have kittui resolve them from the page's directory. Pass --hidden to lychee in bin/ci, with the one cross-package link excluded.

findings.title: "toolchain" means two things on the page that introduces it
findings.claim: Line 5 and the glossary define a toolchain as a set of tools, while the title ("the toolchain that installs them"), line 28 ("the system's toolchain"), and `kit toolchains use <name>` use it for the manager, such as mise or brew.
findings.evidence: docs/toolchains.md:10-11 has the joining sentence the welcome page lacks: "Where kit's commands and this page say the project toolchain or the system toolchain, they mean the provider that fills that role."
findings.fix: Add after line 14: "kit calls the manager that fills a role that role's toolchain: the project toolchain, the system toolchain." Say the same under toolchain in the glossary.

findings.title: 1st.md spends 40% of every agent session on a package catalogue
findings.claim: Every agent reads 1st.md in every session; 938 of its 2,357 words are "What the kit delivers", and 546 of those list what each package delivers, which changes nothing an agent does next. The placement rule is stated three times.
findings.evidence: 1st.md:122-125 and 1st.md:148-149 both say "a link to its source when the source is inside the worktree, and otherwise a copy without the write bit", and .kit/README.md:21-25 says it again. `kit packages` and docs/packages.md hold the catalogue.
findings.fix: Keep lines 118-141 and "Changing what kit adds"; replace 143-196 with "`kit packages` lists every package and what it delivers."

findings.title: The prose style has no item for the faults this prose has
findings.claim: The five items stop filler and slogans, and they work; the text's faults are over-compression, which no item names. Item 1 ("the thing under discussion as the subject") also turns instructions into statements, as in rules/workflows.md:14 and "A plain click on the rule under the name turns the sort a step" (projects/tui/README.md:197).
findings.evidence: Counts in the 46 files: ", as X," for "such as" 42 (36 in the TUI README), "stands" for "is" 33, possessives with the noun left out 20 ("then the team's, team, then the stage's own"), semicolons 103, sentences over 35 words 66. Marker words such as robust, ensure, leverage, simply: 0.
findings.fix: Add four items: one idea to a sentence, split at about 30 words; define a term where it first appears and use one word for one thing; write "such as" for an example and "is" or "shows" for "stands"; repeat the noun after a possessive. Allow the imperative for anything a reader does, including in a UI description.

findings.title: Welcome pages 2 and 3 carry the newcomer's two hardest passages
findings.claim: 3-setup.md:10-12 is a 48-word list item with no verb and five semicolons, and 2-toolchains.md:19-23 is a chain of "else" items that opens "the one you are already inside, such as a shell it opened". A newcomer must read each three times.
findings.evidence: "Each folder, by repository, its desk first, then each worktree: kit installed, with the version its kit.yml declares; .kit/ in place; …; and kit check clean, run by the kit that folder pins." Line 41: "A missing one's fix is the system's package manager's command."
findings.fix: Make 3-setup.md:10-12 a lead-in ("In each folder, the desk first and then its worktrees, kit checks that:") with six items. Make 2-toolchains.md:19-23 the numbered list that modules/bash/toolchain.sh:199-203 already is, ending "If none applies, the role is ambient: kit uses the tools already on PATH."

findings.title: Terms a consumer meets before, or without, a definition
findings.claim: Seven terms are used where no definition reaches the reader: harness (7 uses, page 1 of the welcome, not in the glossary), seam and provider (8 uses), adapter (once, for an agents package), "the declaration" and "the text", "the draft's stand-in", role and folder, and "line".
findings.evidence: 1st.md:118: "The repository commits the declaration, and every worktree holds the text". workflow.md:23-24: "`kit ready`, on any forge, which also takes off the draft's stand-in where `kit.yml` chooses one"; only kit-ready's header says it is a label or a title prefix.
findings.fix: Define each in a clause at first use, or use the plain word: "agent" for harness, "the agents package" for adapter, "the label or title prefix that marks a draft" for stand-in. Add harness, role, folder, group, and preset to the glossary.

findings.title: projects/tui/README.md states five things the tree does not do
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (documentation findings 12 and 21), still open in part. `kit tutorials screens` names no tutorial (the id is screen); "six screens" omits the workspaces screen; Layout names 15 of 22 internal packages; the golden-file command omits internal/tutorials; "bin/ci runs the same three" omits the coverage check.
findings.evidence: kit/modules/tutorials.yml:40 has id: screen; internal/tutorials/golden_test.go calls testkit.Golden, so `go test ./internal/flow ./internal/form ./internal/welcome -update` leaves its golden files stale. Missing from Layout: fix, grid, markdown, opener, pane, screens, workspaces.
findings.fix: Correct the five lines, and add ./internal/tutorials to the -update command.

findings.title: The glossary defines eleven words every developer knows and omits five a newcomer meets
findings.claim: The product does not need 44 terms; it needs about 38, and not the same ones. Eleven entries are general words, 33 are kit's own or carry a kit meaning, and five words used on welcome pages 1 to 3 are missing.
findings.evidence: General: repository, remote, branch, commit, pull request, rebase, release, CI, CD, linter, package manager. Missing: harness, role, folder, group, preset; and the prose keeps several words for one layer (application, app, screen, picture, stage, tab, view; package manager, tool manager, toolchain, provider, role).
findings.fix: Cut the eleven, or keep commit, rebase, and release under the kit command's name, and add the five. The 297 lines are six lines a term and cost nothing in kittui, which draws the page as a table; the definitions themselves are good and should stay.

findings.title: The sixteen Copilot and Cursor pointer files carry one contorted sentence that is false for ten of them
findings.claim: Every body says "A file this rule governs by its content rather than its name, such as a script with no suffix, is named by `kit context <path>`." Only bash, sh, and just match by content, and the body sends the agent to the rule alone, where 1st.md:75-79 says to run kit context and read everything it prints, the style included.
findings.evidence: `grep -l '^content:' kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/kinds/*.yml` prints bash.yml, just.yml, and sh.yml only. The sentence is in the json, markdown, gitignore, jq, and workflows files of both packages.
findings.fix: Replace the body in all sixteen: "Before you change a file, run `kit context <path>` and read every file it prints. The rule for this kind is .kit/rules/<kind>.md; kit places it, so do not edit it."

findings.title: 1st.md's list of "the workflow commands" leaves out the one that ends the workflow
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (documentation finding 16), still open. The list has eleven commands and ends "Run them exactly as written here, and in no other way", and `kit ready`, which workflow.md:23 and workflow.md:47 require, is not among them.
findings.evidence: The list: kit work, commit, submit, rebase, tidy, flow, context, new file, lint, gate, hydrate. kit-ready's header puts it in the workflow group, with settle, release, assign, and close, also absent.
findings.fix: Replace both sentences with "`kit help` lists the commands."

findings.title: The bash rule delivers a paragraph and a template that apply only inside kit's own source
findings.claim: "A verb, `kit/bin/kit-<verb>` in the kit's own source, has the header kit help, kit syntax, and kit serve read…" and the verb variant (path kit/bin/kit-*) reach every consumer, and kit context prints them for every bash file. AGENTS.md:16 says everything in kit/ is written for a consumer.
findings.evidence: kit/bin/kit-new:24: "verb, or a module with --jq: in the kit's own source alone".
findings.fix: Move the paragraph and the variant to the house package. What would settle it: whether a house package can add a template variant to a rule it does not own.

findings.title: Small inaccuracies on the welcome pages and in a kind's comment
findings.claim: The glossary promises "each with a command that shows it", and seven of its commands act; it names "gh or glab" for a forge and omits az; the customize page's example new page is 7-our-team.md where the pages run 1 to 5; kinds/any.yml says "The prose style names it".
findings.evidence: Acting commands: kit work AB#4521 (83), kit commit (101), kit rebase (114, which pushes), kit trust (178), kit hydrate (243), kit toolchains use ambient (275), kit serve (297). styles/prose.md:4-5 names text, and nothing names any.
findings.fix: Give commands that read (kit help rebase, kit toolchains) or say "each with its command"; add az; write 6-our-team.md; correct the comment in any.yml.

findings.title: AGENTS.md says kittui is built from tui/
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (documentation finding 14), still open. "`libexec/kittui`, built from `tui/`" names a directory that does not exist.
findings.evidence: bin/release:49 builds from "${kit_root}/../projects/tui", and the root has no tui/.
findings.fix: Write projects/tui/.

findings.title: The delivered text breaks the delivered styles in a few places, and the linter does not hold the 120 ceiling
findings.claim: The region kit writes into every consumer's AGENTS.md is 122 columns, and 33 prose lines of the TUI README are 121 to 125, over the style's ceiling of 120; MD013 is set without strict, which by markdownlint's documentation passes a line with no space past the limit. Other breaks: a bare angle-bracket URL (4-customize.md:62), a slogan as a rule (1st.md:14), MCP never expanded (1st.md:82), six bold-led bullets and nine stub lines in the TUI README.
findings.evidence: `awk 'length($0)>120'` over the scope lists AGENTS.md:6, the region's source line 3, and README lines 11, 17, 28, 103-109, and more. markdownlint-cli2 was not on the tool path, so the linter's pass is inferred; running it on these files would settle it.
findings.fix: Set "strict": true under MD013, rewrap the region, and fix the five lines.

findings.title: workflow.md packs four subjects into step 3 and names main where the kit says never to
findings.claim: Step 3 covers where to work, the subject's form, signing in one 37-word sentence, pushing, and rebasing. Line 28 says "Nothing reaches `main` any other way" where 1st.md:28 says "the default branch" and rules/bash.md:45 says "Never hard-code it."
findings.evidence: "With `require_signing: true` in `kit.yml`, `kit commit`, `kit work`'s start commit, and `kit rebase` sign every commit they make, and refuse when git has no signing key; otherwise `kit commit` warns when commits here are not signed."
findings.fix: Split step 3 into four sub-items and write "the default branch". Signing: "If kit.yml sets require_signing: true, kit work, kit commit, and kit rebase sign every commit they make, and refuse when git has no signing key. If it does not, kit commit warns about unsigned commits."

findings.title: Three sentences on the tutorials site need a second reading
findings.claim: "This is kit's first line" uses "line" before anything says what one is; "Every 0.4.x release of kit opens the tutorials written for 0.4" is an example that does not say so, on the site for 0.1; "shows the marks plainly" does not say what the reader sees.
findings.evidence: index.mdx:26: "A page opened without it, from your browser's history say, shows the marks plainly."
findings.fix: Write "This is kit's first release line, 0.1: the releases 0.1.0, 0.1.1, and so on", "For example, every 0.4.x release…", and "A page opened without a version in its address, from a bookmark for example, shows every mark."

areas.title: comments in the bash
areas.coverage: Read whole: 12 modules (10,457 lines), kit.yml, lefthook.yml, 3 workflows, 4 bin scripts. Read the headers of all 53 kit/bin files and the other 76 modules. Ran line, width, pattern, and sentence counts over 150 files, a see: path check, and kit help --text for 52 verbs in a private copy. Not read: other module bodies, jq, tests, docs.
areas.summary: The bash comments are free of machine filler (no ensure, robust, seamless) and usually say why. Their failure is the opposite one: compression and a private dialect. Of 81 sampled passages 60 pass (74%); all 21 fails are over-packed or wrong, none padded. `kit help flow` renders 345 lines, much of it JSON shapes written as paragraphs. Verb pages are restated in module headers, and the copies have drifted: commit.sh says kit submit commits, workspaces.sh says only kit edits workspaces.yml. Seventeen findings: 1 high, 5 medium, 11 low. The harness refused the Write of findings.md (subagents may not write report files), so its full text, with tables, counts, and 24 rewrites, is in the findings_md field.
strengths: No machine-flavoured filler: over 106,214 words of comment, no ensure, robust, seamless, leverage, comprehensive, crucial, note that, or in order to (the one grep hit is the function name new:ensure-package), and no "not X, but Y". Do not add any.

Comments say why, and what the code cannot: forge/github.sh:772 (gh auth status passes with a revoked token), forge/github.sh:616, terminal.sh:166 (why one ps), 1st.sh:27, bin/ci:72, kit.yml:7, serve.sh:626.
One convention for a function comment (name, arguments, what it prints or decides, what it returns) is followed in every function of the twelve modules read whole. Keep it.
The verb header as the single source of help, usage grammar, completion, forms, and MCP schemas is a good design; the findings are about what the headers hold, not the mechanism.
Short provider headers are models: each says the one non-obvious thing (toolchain/apt.sh:10, toolchain/dnf.sh:10, terminal/apple.sh:15).

Good model files: super.sh, generate.sh, file.sh, secrets.sh, tracker.sh headers; kit-check, kit-ci, kit-gate, kit-close, kit-gather, kit-commit, kit-submit; kit-welcome:39-51 (a JSON shape as a list).
see: lines are sound: 1 dead path in 150 files.
Refusal comments say what the user will be told, and error lines name a remedy.

findings.title: The help pages of kit flow and the app verbs are JSON schemas written as paragraphs
findings.claim: A verb's header is its help page, and for the verbs a newcomer types first the page cannot be read in one pass.
findings.evidence: `kit help --text flow` prints 345 lines and 3,077 words (workspace 193 lines, audit 136); kit-flow:57-123 is 67 lines of JSON shapes in paragraphs of 17, 13, and 12 lines, and its exits (260-268) are one 150-word paragraph with five meanings of status 1. The help sends users to source files mid-sentence at kit-flow:68, kit-flow:244, and kit-serve:16.
findings.fix: Keep each page to what the verb does, its arguments, and its exits, with exits as a list. Move every --json shape to one reference, one field per line, as kit-welcome:39-51 already does.

findings.title: commit.sh's header says kit submit commits, and it does not
findings.claim: The module header and two function comments describe a kit submit that commits and takes paths; the code only pushes.
findings.evidence: commit.sh:27 "kit submit commits when there is something to commit, then pushes the branch"; commit:submit's own comment (519-520) says "It commits nothing", and kit-submit:2 is "pushes the branch, and commits nothing". Lines 38 ("the options both verbs share") and 586 ("kit submit answers the same") lag too: kit submit takes no arguments.
findings.fix: Rewrite lines 27-32 from commit:submit's comment, and drop the two stale clauses.

findings.title: workspaces.sh says only kit reads and writes workspaces.yml; the help says you may edit it by hand
findings.claim: The module header contradicts the verb's help page about who may edit the workspace file.
findings.evidence: workspaces.sh:7 "only kit reads and writes it" against kit-workspaces:19-20 "which you may edit by hand; kit keeps your comments when it edits the file". The code sides with the help: workspaces:check (407) validates a hand-written file and workspaces:edit (827) keeps comments.
findings.fix: Change the module header to match the help.

findings.title: The same text is kept in two or three places, and the copies have started to disagree
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/git.sh:262, kit/modules/bash/commit.sh:9, kit/modules/bash/welcome.sh:6, kit/modules/bash/serve.sh:21, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:15, kit/modules/bash/materialize.sh:22, kit/bin/kit-audit:19
findings.claim: Module headers restate their verb's help page, function comments restate both, and six app verbs paste one 14-line block.
findings.evidence: git.sh:262-282 repeats kit-tidy:7-24, commit.sh:9-25 repeats kit-commit:7-26, welcome.sh:6-65 repeats kit-welcome:11-63, materialize.sh:22-25 repeats 6-9; 55 distinct comment lines of 60+ characters occur 208 times in scope. P5-2, P5-3, P5-7, and P5-9 are each one copy that moved while the other stayed.
findings.fix: One home per fact: the verb page says what the verb does, the module header only what the page does not, and a function comment points with see:. Put the app verbs' shared block in one generated region or help topic.

findings.title: Sentences are packed past what a reader can hold
findings.claim: Lists, case analyses, and procedures are written as single sentences joined by commas, semicolons, as, which, and where, against prose rule 1.
findings.evidence: Of about 4,300 comment sentences the median is 23 words and the 90th percentile 53; about 300 pass 40 words and 60 pass 60 (upper bounds), with true single sentences of 143 words (github.sh:332), 118 (github.sh:1055), 110 (workspaces.sh:684), and 90 (1st.sh:40). policy.sh:51-65 is one 15-line paragraph, and "fails both" at lines 41, 60, and 69 refers to two verbs named once at line 33.
findings.fix: When a comment lists cases, fields, or steps, write a list, as generate.sh:21-27 and kit-check:10-19 do. findings_md holds 24 rewrites.

findings.title: A private dialect: "as X" for "such as X", "is no X", "alone", "a line" for "per line"
findings.claim: The comments, including the help a user sees, avoid ordinary words for constructions a reader has to translate.
findings.evidence: Over 8,112 comment lines: ", as" 699 times, about 80 meaning "such as" ("such as" itself 45, "for example" 0); "<verb> no <noun>" 258 ("none names no workspace"); "alone" for "only" 104; "where" 416; "one a line" forms 26 beside 65 "one per line". Examples: kit-audit:32 "as secret scanning disabled", kit-flow:85 "one row a thing".
findings.fix: Add four lines to prose.md (write such as, only, per, is not a) and apply them to the verb headers first.

findings.title: Six comments say the forge is GitHub or GitLab; Azure DevOps is a forge provider too
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:2, kit/modules/bash/git.sh:6, kit/bin/kit-work:25, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:7, kit/modules/bash/tracker.sh:10, kit/modules/bash/tracker/ado.sh:21
findings.claim: The forge is described as two providers in six places, one of them user help, although forge/ado.sh is a third.
findings.evidence: forge.sh:2 "the seam over the forge (GitHub, GitLab)" while forge.sh:17 maps dev.azure.com to ado. kit-work:25 says #7 names an issue on "GitHub or GitLab"; tracker.sh:16 says #4521 is the forge's own on an Azure DevOps forge.
findings.fix: Name all three, or say "the forge" and let forge.sh list them once.

findings.title: forge/github.sh names a verb that does not exist
findings.claim: The open-prs comment refers to kit status, which is not a verb.
findings.evidence: "the document kit status renders"; kit/bin has no kit-status, and the document is drawn by kit flow.
findings.fix: Write "the document kit flow draws".

findings.title: kit flow's help misstates two outputs
findings.claim: The help gives --capabilities without stand_ins, and says --json prints the stages as text.
findings.evidence: kit-flow:243-244 "{contract, forge, provider, features}, each feature native or none", but forge:capabilities (forge.sh:687-694) also prints stand_ins and a feature can be stand-in. kit-flow:33-34 and kit-workspace:28-29 say "with --text, --json, or --jq, it prints the stages as text"; kit-audit:23 words it correctly.
findings.fix: Copy forge.sh:256-258 for --capabilities and kit-audit:23 for the text and JSON sentence.

findings.title: The release workflows' headers count their steps wrong
findings.claim: The headers say two steps and one step where the jobs have six and three, and kit-ci's list leaves out the trust step.
findings.evidence: release.yml:3-4 "It has two steps, and each step is one kit command, so the same thing can be run on a laptop": the job runs checkout, trust, cache, tools, verify, publish, bin/release is not a kit command, and lines 16-17 say a desk cannot publish a release. retire-pre-releases.yml:3 "Its one step" of three.
findings.fix: Say "its two commands are bin/release verify and bin/release publish; a desk can run verify, and publish for a pre-release", and add the trust step to kit-ci's list.

findings.title: The loader's header points to a document that is not there
findings.claim: The see: line names docs/releases.md, which does not exist.
findings.evidence: `# see: libexec/kit-call, modules/bash/release.sh, docs/releases.md`; docs/ has no releases.md. It is the only dead see: path in the 150 files in scope, and lychee does not read comments.
findings.fix: Point to the page that holds the loader's rules, or drop the reference.

findings.title: Two module headers give a reason the code no longer supports
findings.claim: people.sh says the forge's marks call reads every kind for every app, and builds.sh puts builds between changes and releases.
findings.evidence: forge:marks takes the kinds to read (forge.sh:709-716), "so a caller pays only for what it draws". settings.sh:313 orders the stages changes, builds, incoming, releases.
findings.fix: Drop the first sentence at people.sh:11 (the second reason stands alone), and write "after changes" in builds.sh.

findings.title: Function comments whose signature or list lags the code
findings.claim: Four function comments omit an argument or an input the code has.
findings.evidence: 1st.sh:185-186 lists what kit_bash_path_from is made of without XDG_CONFIG_HOME (line 205 adds it); flow.sh:303 and welcome.sh:511 use <fallback> and <id> that their signatures do not show. flow.sh:213 says flow:paint colors "when stderr is a terminal", but out_color decides, which NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE also set.
findings.fix: Correct the four lines.
