findings.title: kit flow changes prints "in flight" for what the legend calls "underway"
findings.claim: One state has two names in what the user reads.
findings.evidence: flow:pr-block passes the literal 'in flight' to flow:issue-row, so each issue under a change shows "🛫 in flight". glyphs.json and the legend in kit help flow give 🛫 as "underway".
findings.fix: Print "underway".

findings.title: Lines and banners past column 120, and paragraphs left broken after an edit
findings.claim: The 120-column convention and the bash style's "banner under 120 columns" are not held, and kit lint checks neither.
findings.evidence: 25 comment lines exceed 120 characters (workspaces.sh:690 is 174, issue.sh:566 is 161, kit-audit:29 is 138); six module banners exceed 120 and four are exactly 120, mostly because of the "(sourced module)" suffix, which six other banners omit. About a dozen paragraphs have a line cut short where text was inserted (kit:60, kit-flow:114, kit-serve:14, commit.sh:173).
findings.fix: Add a width check to the bash rule's lint, and re-wrap.

findings.title: Comments that point at other comments, and comments that tell history
findings.claim: Pointer phrases add words without information, and two comments break the bash style's rule that a comment holds no history.
findings.evidence: "as the seam's header says" is in 45 function comments of the three forge providers; seven trailing comments are only "# as above" and two say "as the comment above says". kit-submit:30 "the words kit submit once took" and workspaces.sh:376 "once took it" tell history.
findings.fix: Delete the pointers, or state the reason at the line. State the present rule without the past.

findings.title: kit submit blames origin whichever remote refused the push
findings.claim: commit:push-refused prints "origin refused the push" although commit:submit may push to another remote.
findings.evidence: The message is a literal, and commit:submit pushes to the remote git:pushes-to prints, which commit.sh:28-29 says is another remote when the upstream is there. Not run: a branch whose upstream is fork/<branch> with a rejected push would settle it.
findings.fix: Pass the remote to commit:push-refused.

areas.title: the words a user sees
areas.coverage: Read whole: help.sh, all 53 rendered help pages (2,960 lines), all 765 CLI message calls, five welcome pages, nine tutorials, 32 tab summaries and empty states, 1,782 Go string literals. Sampled 22 of 85 goldens and the Go around reported strings. Ran help, 17 mistaken commands, toolchains, welcome checks in a scratch copy. Not read: docs/, Go comments, projects/tutorials.
areas.summary: findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write ("subagents return findings as text"), so the tables and rewrites it would have held are in P6-1, P6-8, and P6-11 below, which run longer than two sentences for that reason. Verdict: no filler anywhere (0 hits for the tic list across help, messages, Go strings, welcome, tutorials), but about four passages in ten are over-compressed. Sample: 94 passages, 57 pass (61%); help paragraphs 32 of 56, messages 8 of 14, kittui strings 9 of 15, welcome and tutorials 8 of 9; tab titles 26 of 32. Everyday verbs, refusals, the welcome, and the tutorials are good; the picture and workspace verbs' help is reference text in comma-stacked sentences.
strengths: No machine-flavoured writing: 0 hits for ensure, robust, seamless, leverage, comprehensive, crucial, simply, in order to, note that across 2,301 header lines, 765 messages, 1,782 Go literals, the welcome pages, and the tutorials; no 'not X, but Y', no restating summaries.
The refusals say what happened and what to run, with the real values in them (commit.sh:78, releases.sh:79, 1st.sh:686 'did you mean commit?'); of 491 errors none only says 'failed'.
The check lines of kit welcome --checks are the best copy in the tree: '✅ jq 1.8.2 reads kit's JSON; it needs 1.7 or later', each failure with its fix on the next line.

Good model help pages: kit-gate, kit-ci, kit-check, kit-install, kit-kinds, kit-submit, kit-settle, kit-close, kit-help, kit-template; for a long verb done well: kit-work, kit-commit, kit-update, kit-trust.

Good model pages: welcome/5-terms.md (45 terms, one or two plain sentences each, with a command that shows the thing), welcome/1-introduction.md, welcome/4-customize.md, tutorials/applications.md, tutorials/screen.md.
26 of the 32 tab title lines do say what the tab tells you, phrased as the question the reader has; the 32 empty states are parallel ('no open issue', 'no team has access').
kittui's menus use plain verbs in one case style, each destructive action confirms in a full sentence, and shell/settings.go:77-86 explains each setting in one line.
One source for the help page, the form, the completion, and the MCP tool is right and should stay; P6-1 asks for less text in that source, not a second source.
The manual-page habit of dropping the subject ('Draws the picture of the work.') breaks prose rule 1 on paper and reads well; do not change it.

findings.title: The help pages of the picture verbs are reference dumps; a flag of kit flow is found after 270 lines
findings.claim: kit flow --help is 345 lines and 3,077 words, and its first option (--no-fetch) is described on line 274, after the JSON of every stage field by field and a 105-line legend. Ten verbs (flow, workspace, audit, welcome, workspaces, delivery, changes, people, issues, platform) hold 11,984 of the 23,973 words of help, nearly all of it the shape of --json, and the same text becomes kittui's form labels (form/testdata/flow.golden:16-19).
findings.evidence: Rendered every page with kit help --text <verb> and counted. Per page (lines/words, verdict): flow 345/3,077 far too long, target 80; workspace 193/1,613 too long, target 60; audit 136/1,168 too long, target 45; welcome 114/1,010 too long (cut the check's JSON fields and --progress's wire format), target 60; workspaces 111/970 too long in the JSON paragraph (27-37) and the lock paragraph (39-41), target 70; delivery, changes, people, issues, platform 91-104 lines each and about 60% alike, target 40 each; packages 86, cut lines 27-31 and the legend; policy 72, paragraph 3 states the base rule three times; new 107 is right for ten subcommands; tools, syntax, serve, update, commit, work (52-58) and every other page (15-52) are right; 5-terms.md (297 lines) is long and worth it; tutorials (28-77) are right.
findings.fix: Keep in each header what the verb does, where it reads from, and its arguments; move each stage's JSON fields to docs/apps.md (or print them with a --schema flag) and the legend to a flag kittui's legend source already feeds. Keep the single source for help, form, completion, and MCP; it needs less text, not a second source.

findings.title: A help page prints its arguments under no heading, so on three pages they read as legend entries
findings.claim: help:page prints the headings Usage, Description, and Group, but help:description joins the description, the Arguments block, and Exits with blank lines and drops the word Arguments. In kit help flow, workspace, and packages the option list follows the last legend heading ("releases:") with nothing between.
findings.evidence: kit help --text flow, lines 265-274: "releases:" … "❌  failed: a check, a build, or a fetch…", a blank line, then "--no-fetch          fetches nothing; incoming says so". On every other page the argument list is an unlabelled indented block between two paragraphs.
findings.fix: Print Arguments and Exits as headings in help:page, as Usage and Description are, and put Arguments before any legend.

findings.title: Two spellings for an option's value, and the refusal for the wrong one says the value is missing
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-work:6-7, kit/bin/kit-commit:5, kit/bin/kit-assign:5, kit/bin/kit-close:5, kit/bin/kit-gather:5, kit/bin/kit-tools:5-6, kit/bin/kit-syntax:6, kit/bin/kit-welcome:7, kit/modules/jq/syntax.jq:166-168, kit/bin/kit-submit:34
findings.claim: Ten usage lines in eight verbs write --title <text> and 32 write --owner=<login>; kit welcome --fix <check> [--folder=<path>] has both on one line. The space form accepts either spelling, the equals form refuses the other with a message that is false. Known since 11-10 (CLI item 22, rated low), still open.
findings.evidence: `kit flow --owner bob --text` prints "❌ --owner needs a value; run: … kit help flow"; `kit syntax commit --match -- --message=x` and `-- --message x` both give status 0. kit-submit:34 tells the user `kit commit --message=<text>` while kit-commit:5 and commit.sh:395 write `--message <text>`.
findings.fix: Write every option --opt=<value> in the eight headers (the parser already takes it), and make the refusal say "write --owner=bob".

findings.title: The title line names a command that is not the app's verb, twice
findings.claim: appLabel is "kit " + the app's name, so the title reads "= kit repositories" for the app kit workspace opens and "kit trust" for the app kit audit opens. kit repositories is no verb, and kit trust is a different verb (it trusts a clone); the other seven apps show their real command there.
findings.evidence: workspace-repos.golden line 1: "  = kit repositories · - empowerite/kit"; apps.go maps shell.Repositories to workspaceVerb and shell.Trust to "audit". Within one screen a user also meets workspace, workspaces, Repositories, and repos.
findings.fix: Show the verb (kit workspace, kit audit) or the app's name without "kit" (Repositories, Trust).

findings.title: kit toolchains and kit tools do not name the kit toolchain, which this repository uses
findings.claim: The help lists "mise, nix, brew, docker, devcontainer, or, for the system, apt, dnf, or pacman" and the same for <name>, but kit/modules/bash/toolchain/kit.sh is a tenth provider and the chosen one in kit's own checkout. 5-terms.md has the opposite slip: "such as mise or asdf", and kit has no asdf provider.
findings.evidence: `kit toolchains` in a copy of the snapshot prints the row "kit            project  ✅            📌". grep for asdf in kit/modules and kit/bin finds nothing.
findings.fix: Add kit to the three lists in the two headers, and write "such as mise or nix" in 5-terms.md.

findings.title: kit issues does not list issues, and its refusal offers --json to someone who asked for --text
findings.claim: kit help lists "issues  lists the forge's milestones and iterations of the repository"; off a terminal kit issues prints only those two, and kit issues issues is refused. kit changes changes, kit delivery releases, and kit delivery builds behave the same way.
findings.evidence: `kit issues --text` prints "milestones:" and "iterations:"; `kit issues issues --text` prints "❌ kit issues issues opens the tab in kittui, on a terminal; issues is printed by another command; run: … kit flow issues --json".
findings.fix: Let these four print what kit flow <stage> prints. Otherwise write the purpose as "lists the milestones and the iterations; kit flow issues lists the issues" and the refusal as "kit flow issues prints the issues; run: kit flow issues".

findings.title: The grammar's generic refusal hides the verb's better one, and shows a grammar token
findings.claim: A value off a closed set is refused by the guard as "<package> 'nope' is not one of the choices": the header's notation is shown and the choices, which the guard has in hand, are not. The verbs' own messages (resolve.sh:63 "matches no package in reach; the packages are: …", kit-tutorials:81 "is not a tutorial") are never reached in the ordinary case.
findings.evidence: `kit packages add nope` prints "❌ <package> 'nope' is not one of the choices; run: … kit help packages"; `kit tutorials nope --text` prints "❌ <tutorial> 'nope' is not one of the choices; …".
findings.fix: Have the guard say "'nope' is not a package; the packages are: …" (the noun from the key, the list cut at a line's length), or let a closed choice through to the verb's own message.

findings.title: One compressed style runs through the help: "as" for three words, stacked appositives, "no X" for "not an X"; 24 passages need a rewrite
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-flow:38-39, kit/bin/kit-flow:59-62, kit/bin/kit-flow:87-91, kit/bin/kit-flow:260-268, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:18-19, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:48-53, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:77-81, kit/bin/kit-audit:60-72, kit/bin/kit-linked:17-20, kit/bin/kit-policy:20-32, kit/bin/kit-tidy:18-20, kit/bin/kit-welcome:77-79, kit/bin/kit-work:21, kit/bin/kit-tutorials:8-14, kit/bin/kit-packages:27-31, kit/bin/kit-serve:12-14, kit/bin/kit-changes:23, kit/bin/kit-ready:7-9, kit/bin/kit-tools:8-10, kit/bin/kit-commit:20-21, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:146, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:476, kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/welcome/3-setup.md:10-12
findings.claim: There is no machine-flavoured filler in this tree; the failure is the opposite one. Sentences are correct but pack a table into commas, define a term by appositive every time it comes up, drop verbs ("staged work staged", "its actor null, else null"), and use "as" for "such as", "because", and "in the way that" alike, so a paragraph takes three readings.
findings.evidence: Counts. "as": 250 in the rendered help against 0 "because", 0 "for example", 16 "such as"; about 20 bare "as <example>" in headers (kit-audit:32 "as secret scanning disabled", kit-tidy:23 "as a locked one", kit-trust:18 "as it is a judgment of the clone"). Negative existence: 11 "is/are no" and 67 "names/holds/has/gives no or none" header lines ("none names no workspace" on 7 pages; kit-flow:53 "backlog and underway are no stages"; kit-flow:267 "a forges key that is no remote name"). One boilerplate paragraph: 9 pages carry "the owner and the name of the repository kit read it in", 9 "the kit option before the verb", 8 "{member, error} under errors". "form" has three meanings in 23 uses: an output format (kit-changes:23 "with a form, is refused"), a verb's form in kittui (kit-help:8), a way to call a verb (kit-workspaces:39). Six headers open by restating usage ("kit gate takes no arguments": kit-ci:7, kit-gate:7, kit-check:7, kit-update:7, kit-root:7, kit-version:7), against prose rule 3. Rule 5 breaks: ado (kit-flow:67), SAST (kit-audit:44), PEM and ETag (forge/github.sh:1299, 941) are not expanded. Where a rule makes the text worse: rule 3 read as "never say a thing twice" yields "as kit workspaces names it" and "as kit platform's do" in place of the ten words that would say it, and avoiding "you" yields "the caller" (23 against 18 "you") and "A terminal's fixes are the person's to make" (kit-welcome:29).
findings.fix: Add two lines to the prose style ("write because and such as; keep as for comparison"; "two or more alternatives with conditions go in a list") and rewrite these. (1) kit-flow:38-39 → "outside any repository (a bare repository and a .git directory count as outside): every desk up to four levels below the current directory, each under its path; this applies when no group was used last, or with kit --workspace=none". (2) kit-flow:59-62 → "Every row has three fields that say where it came from. organization and repository are the owner and the name in the primary remote's URL; organization is null when the primary is a local path. source is the forge, or git for a row of incoming." Say it once in docs/apps.md, not on 9 pages. (3) kit-flow:87-91 → a list: "remote, one row per remote; change is fetched, unchanged, not fetched, or failed, and on failed subject is git's error line. commit, a new commit on the default branch. branch; change is new, updated, forced, or gone, and commits is how many it moved, or for a new branch how many are not on the default branch. tag; change is new or moved. tracking, a local branch behind its upstream." (4) kit-flow:260-268 → "Exits 0 when the picture is drawn. Exits 1 when the forge, a fetch, the workspace file, a member, a desk, or git's list of worktrees or remote branches cannot be read; with --json the rest is still printed. Exits 1 when a setting is wrong: flow is not a list of distinct stages or names backlog or underway; primary names no remote; a key under forges is not a remote. Exits 2 on a usage error." (5) kit-workspaces:18-19 → "A workspace is what kit looks at: one repository, or a group of repositories you name, such as the ones you release together." (6) kit-workspaces:51-53 → "makes a group the one kit starts on outside a repository. Given a <folder>, it puts that folder's repository first in the recent list instead; a worktree counts as its repository. The list keeps ten, and the workspace menu shows it." (7) kit-workspaces:48-50 → "With kit --workspace=<workspace> before the verb, it describes that workspace instead: none means no workspace, and an absolute path means the repository that holds the path." (8) kit-workspaces:77-81 → "Exits 1 when the file is malformed (the message says how), the checkouts under the roots cannot be listed, or another process holds the lock for more than 30 seconds. Exits 2 on a usage error, an unknown workspace, or a name --rename cannot use." (9) kit-audit:60-62 → "hidden counts the bypassers the forge hides or kit cannot name. They share one row per control, keyed <id> hidden, with a null actor. On every other row hidden is null." (10) kit-audit:67-72 → "kit reads kit policy --rules --json in every checkout that is on a branch. Rows that agree are merged into one row at the narrowest place that holds them all, and scope names that place. Fields narrower than scope are null." (11) kit-linked:17-20 and kit-policy:20-32 → "On any branch but the default one, kit reads linked_exempt from the base's kit.yml, so a branch cannot exempt its own author. At a desk the base is <primary>/<default>. On a CI runner it is the base in the change's event: the base commit of a pull request or a merge group, or the tip of a merge request's target branch." (12) kit-tidy:18-20 → "a branch with commits that were never pushed, and its worktree, even when its pull request is merged or closed. A commit counts as pushed when the pull request's head, as the forge recorded it, reaches it." (13) kit-welcome:77-79 → "with --checks, reports progress on stderr: '⏳ checking <check>' when a check starts, with ' in <folder>' for a folder's check, and '⏳ checked' when the machine's or a folder's checks are done." (14) kit-work:21 → "When kit work stops for any other reason before the work reaches the worktree, it puts the work back on the desk, and what was staged is staged again." (15) kit-tutorials:8-14 (117 words in three sentences) → six short sentences: what tutorials are; where they live; what a terminal opens; what --text prints; what a named tutorial does. (16) kit-packages:27-31 → "kit packages packages prints the same list as a stage, {rows, errors}. kit --workspace=<workspace> packages packages prints it for every cloned member, each row tagged with its member." (17) kit-serve:12-14 → "In a checkout of kit itself, the server is that checkout's own kit/bin/kit-serve, whichever kit you started, so a worktree that changes kit is served by its own code." (18) kit-changes:23, kit-issues:25-26 → "kit changes changes with --text, --json, or --jq is refused: kit flow changes prints that tab." (19) kit-ready:7-9 → "On a forge with draft pull requests, it ends the draft. On a forge without them, it removes the label or the title prefix that kit.yml sets to mark a draft. With neither, the pull request was never a draft, and kit ready says so." (20) kit-tools:8-10 → "It also acts on the packages each dependency provider pins, such as npm's in package-lock.json. A provider counts when its manifest and its lock are in the repository and its tool is on PATH." (21) kit-commit:20-21 → "Without paths, kit commit refuses a staged path whose staged content is the file as it was before the last commit that changed it, when the working tree holds something else. Committing it would undo that commit." (22) kit-workspaces:146 → "--workspace= goes only with kit workspaces --current; run: kit help workspaces". (23) issue.sh:476 → "nothing to sweep: git stash takes none of what is uncommitted on main". (24) welcome/3-setup.md:10-12 → "Each folder, the desk first and then each worktree. kit checks that kit is installed at the version kit.yml declares, that .kit/ is in place, that the git hooks are installed, that the project toolchain and the linters are there, and that kit check passes."

findings.title: The same refusal is worded several ways, and messages take two opposite shapes
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-ready:37, kit/bin/kit-linked:59, kit/bin/kit-settle:39, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:954, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:402, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:468, kit/modules/bash/git.sh:383
findings.claim: One situation has three sentences: "name the change: kit ready <number> (none was given, and this checkout is working on none)" (kit-ready:37, kit-linked:59) against "no pull request is named, and this checkout has none; run: kit settle <number>" (kit-settle:39). Of the messages, 68 lead with the remedy and put what happened in parentheses ("run: gh auth status (the iterations could not be read)"), which hides the fact behind a guessed instruction, and 65 say what happened and then "; run:".
findings.evidence: Counted over the 765 message calls: 20 "run: kit help <verb>" against 4 "see: kit help <verb>"; 26 start with a capital and 20 end with a period, 18 of them in issue.sh ("Created #7", "Worktree ready:", "and re-run."); "re-run" 3 times against "run … again"; 12 "is no <noun>" against 31 "is not a <noun>"; 32 "(s)" plurals (kit-lint:151, git.sh:383, kit-tools:434); 19 "see above".
findings.fix: Settle one shape, "what happened; run: <command>", lower case, no period, and bring issue.sh and the forge providers to it.

findings.title: One thing has several names on the same screen or page
findings.claim: underway and in flight (the legend says "🛫 underway", the row under a change says "🛫 in flight"); tab and stage (the legend has "tab menu" and "selected tab", then "issues stage"); workspace and group ("New Workspace…" makes a group, and the empty state beside it says "no group yet"); pull request and change; finding, problem, and difference for what kit check counts; ✅ and 🟢 for an active package on one help page.
findings.evidence: Help pages say stage 181 times and tab 31, pull request 73 times and change about 31, the caller 23 times and you 18. kit check prints "N finding(s)", kit welcome --checks printed "kit check finds 7 problems", and welcome/testdata/setup.golden says "2 differences".
findings.fix: Pick one of each (underway; tab in kittui and stage in the CLI; group for a named set; pull request; finding; you) and replace the other.

findings.title: Six of the 32 tab title lines do not yet say what the tab tells you
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/fields.json (the summary of builds, delivery/artifacts, delivery/environments, delivery/deployments, people/agents, changes)
findings.claim: 26 of 32 pass. The six that do not: builds asks a question and follows it with a fragment that parses as a sentence; artifacts has the same noun-or-verb trap and a singular "it"; environments ends on a verb with its object dropped; deployments is cute where it could be exact; changes says "pull requests" where its sibling titles say "change"; agents promises a count the tab does not show (P6-12).
findings.evidence: All 32, quoted. PASS: repos "What is cloned, where, on which branch, and how far from upstream"; issues "What is open, who has it, and where the work on it stands"; incoming "What the last fetch brought in: new commits, moved branches, tags"; releases "What shipped, when, which is latest, and what each one carries"; remotes "Where each repository pulls from and pushes to; which is primary"; branches "Every branch, local and remote: how far ahead, and how old"; worktrees "Where each branch is checked out, and what is uncommitted there"; commits "Work not yet on the default branch, and whether it is pushed"; tags "What each tag points at, who made it, and when"; packages "What each package needs, what needs it, and whether it is active"; milestones "How far along each milestone is, and when it is due"; iterations "Which iteration is current, and when each starts and ends"; reviews "Who was asked to review each open change, and what they said"; checks "Which checks pass and which fail on each open change"; merged "What landed lately, who merged it, and when; the last 50"; people "Who has access, people and bots, and with which role"; teams "Which teams have access, with which role, and who is in each"; evidence "Attestations: who signed the newest releases and artifacts"; findings "Security alerts by severity: code scanning, Dependabot, secrets"; controls "What guards the default branch, and whether each rule is enforced"; waivers "Who may bypass the controls, and which alerts were dismissed"; policy "The rules kit policy checks, what each matches, and where it is set"; services "Which service answers each capability, and whether it is ready"; toolchains "The toolchains kit can use, and which one fills each role"; tools "Each pinned tool: the version pinned, the one installed, its path"; settings "What kit.yml sets, and the default for everything it leaves out". NOT YET: changes "Open pull requests, and what stands between each and its merge"; builds "Is the default branch green? CI runs outside any pull request"; artifacts "What CI runs kept, how big, and when it expires; the newest 100"; environments "Where you deploy, who must approve, and which branches may"; deployments "What went where, who sent it, and if it worked; the last 50"; agents "Which bots act in your commits, changes, and reviews, and how often".
findings.fix: changes: "Open changes, and what stands between each and its merge". builds: "CI runs on the default branch, tags, and schedules: which passed". artifacts: "The files CI kept: how big each is, and when it expires; the newest 100". environments: "Where you deploy, who must approve, and which branches may deploy there". deployments: "What was deployed where, by whom, and whether it worked; the last 50". agents: see P6-12.

findings.title: The agents tab's title says "how often", and the tab has no count
findings.claim: "Which bots act in your commits, changes, and reviews, and how often" promises a frequency the tab does not hold. The tab is also named agents while every word on it, its empty state included ("no bot acted lately"), says bot.
findings.evidence: The stage's fields are bot, acted (pills from .acted[]: commit, change, review), and last acted; kit-people:42 gives the row as "{login, acted, last}".
findings.fix: Write "Which bots act here, in commits, changes, or reviews, and when each last did", and name the tab bots.

findings.title: Eight kittui strings are contorted or use the code's words
findings.claim: "check-runs is lacked by the provider of the forge here", "no build since the last 20 runs", "no row matches the panel", "no folder here starts so", "kit has not said where %s is checked out", and "one of required" each take a second reading. The states failing:gate, comments:open, blocked:approval, and no-check, and the Fields dialog's enum, ref, and "rendering: glyph+text", are identifiers shown as words.
findings.evidence: Read each in its Go and, where one exists, in a golden (legend-80-changes.golden shows "🔥 failing:gate"; popover.golden shows "rendering", "glyph+text", and the type column enum/ref). table/sheet.go:340 already says "no row matches the search".
findings.fix: In order: "this forge's provider does not report check-runs"; "no build among the last 20 runs"; "no row matches the search and the filters"; "no folder here starts with that"; "%s has no checkout kit knows of; pick the workspace again from %s"; "choose one (required)"; "checks failing", "threads open", "needs approval", "no checks"; "choice", "reference", "show as: emoji and text".

findings.title: A tutorial says the current screen is dim in the kit menu; it is bold
findings.claim: menu-bar.md says "The screen you are on is dim." The menu draws that line bold; dim is for a line that cannot be chosen.
findings.evidence: shell.go:439 `case item.Here: text = style.Label(text) + …`, and style/style.go:33 `label = lipgloss.NewStyle().Bold(true)`; style.Off (Faint) is used at shell.go:432 for a line that is not enabled.
findings.fix: Write "The screen you are on is bold."

findings.title: Every remedy gains "cd <folder> &&", even kit help <verb>
findings.claim: out:remedy puts "cd <folder> &&" before every command after "run:", so the most common refusals (20 messages end in run: kit help <verb>) carry up to 70 columns of path between the fact and the command. It is deliberate, so a remedy pasted elsewhere or run by kittui lands in the right folder.
findings.evidence: `kit ready x` printed "❌ 'x' is not a number; run: cd <the folder I typed it in> && kit help ready"; in the live worktree's path that is a 110-column line.
findings.fix: Keep the prefix for kittui and for a remedy that changes something; leave it out when stderr is a terminal and the folder is the one the command was typed in, or when the remedy is kit help.

findings.title: Nine purpose lines in kit help run past 80 columns
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-audit:2, kit/bin/kit-welcome:2, kit/bin/kit-tools:2, kit/bin/kit-workspace:2, kit/bin/kit-people:2, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:2, kit/bin/kit-changes:2, kit/bin/kit-update:2, kit/bin/kit-delivery:2
findings.claim: The overview wraps its first sentence at 80 by hand and help:reflow rewraps descriptions to 80, but each purpose prints whole. Nine of the 46 listed lines wrap in an 80-column terminal.
findings.evidence: Measured kit help --text: audit 100 columns, welcome 95, tools 94, workspace 91, people 89, workspaces 88, changes 87, update 86, delivery 81.
findings.fix: Hold a purpose to 64 characters, for example "lists what the forge attests, alerts on, and guards" (audit), "a guide to your first hour with kit" (welcome), "lists, installs, and updates the pinned tools" (tools).

findings.title: kit is described in three different sentences where a newcomer first meets it
findings.claim: The README and kit help describe a rule-keeper; the welcome's first page describes a command set for the development cycle, with the rules as something installing adds. A newcomer reads two products.
findings.evidence: README: kit "writes down the rules an agent must follow, puts them where each agent reads, and checks them in CI". help.sh:323: "kit keeps the rules a repository asks its agents to follow, and the checks that hold the work to them". 1-introduction.md:5: "kit is one set of commands for the whole development cycle, the same for people and for coding agents".
findings.fix: Choose one sentence and open all three with it.

areas.title: comments in the Go
areas.coverage: Read every comment in the non-test files of flow, table, grid, welcome, and shell (3,504 lines) with the declaration under each, and all TypeScript comments. Sampled 60 random non-test blocks, 45 tests, 15 other package comments, and all 1,022 test names by script. Opened code only under reported claims. Ran greps and scripts, no tests.
areas.summary: The Go comments have no machine-flavoured writing (zero tic words in 8,051 comment lines) but fail the opposite way: a compressed private dialect. 929 sentences run 40 words or more (longest 282), ", as " is on 1,411 lines while "because" is on none, and 54 of 66 large types document their members in one paragraph. Of 85 sampled passages 51 pass a one-pass reading; blocks of 40 words or more pass 4 of 22. Package comments are key-by-key manuals and hold the stale claims (grid, flow, app, main, shell, reader.tsx). The TypeScript comments are the model. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused a report file in this session, so the full content is in this result only.
strengths: No machine-flavoured writing: a grep for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, 'worth noting', simply, and 'in order to' over 8,051 comment lines finds none; no TODO/FIXME lines, two em dashes, no bold-led bullets. Do not fix the prose by adding filler.

Comments say why: tabs/tabs.go:182 explains the choice of dingbat digits over ① (ambiguous width); table/store.go:84 'written whole beside it first, so a reader never sees half of it'; grid/grid.go:667 explains the width cache and what makes it safe; shell/shell.go:149 explains why no modified esc quits.
Every declaration in flow, table, grid, welcome, and shell has a comment that starts with its name, and short comments read well: 30 of 38 sampled blocks under 40 words pass a one-pass reading.
Test names are sentences that state the behaviour (median 41 characters, 1,022 tests). Keep them; 473 tests rightly carry no comment.
The TypeScript comments in projects/tutorials/src (build.ts, version.ts, entry.ts, reader.tsx) are the best prose in scope: short, concrete, each with an example value. 19 of 20 blocks pass.

Good Go models to copy: internal/pane/pane.go:1, internal/source/source.go:1, internal/transcript/transcript.go:1, internal/kit/kit.go:1, all of internal/flow/origin.go, internal/shell/browse.go, internal/shell/keybar.go:14, internal/grid/ranges.go:1, internal/table/read.go:1, internal/table/team.go:1, internal/flow/marks.go:1.
The serial comma (prose rule 4) and the indicative for description (rule 2) are used consistently throughout.

findings.title: Doc comments are single-sentence inventories, and the members they describe carry no comment
findings.claim: The comment over a type or function lists everything it holds or does in one sentence joined by commas and semicolons, so a reader must count clauses to find which one describes which field. Following prose rule 1 literally (subject first) produced the shape "X is: a; b, which c; d, as e".
findings.evidence: Of 5,329 comment sentences, 929 have 40+ words, 227 have 60+, 18 have 100+; host.go:7 is one 282-word sentence over a 30-method interface with no per-method comment, catalog.go:16 is 184 words over 13 fields. 54 of the 66 types with five or more members have no member comment, and only 4 of 22 sampled blocks of 40+ words pass a one-pass reading against 30 of 38 shorter ones.
findings.fix: Leave one sentence over the type and move each clause to the field or method it describes, for example "Host is the screen a table's controls act on." then "SetPanel replaces the panel and rebuilds the rows." Break a function's cases into one short sentence each or a list.

findings.title: "as" stands for six different words; "because", "if", "for example", and "returns" are not used
findings.claim: One word carries "such as", "because", "see", "the same way as", "in the form of", and "that is", so the reader has to try each meaning. Ordinary connectives are avoided throughout, which prose.md does not ask for.
findings.evidence: ", as " is on 1,411 of 8,051 comment lines and "as X says/does/draws" on 800, while "because" appears 0 times, "for example"/"e.g." 0, "such as" 2, "if" 2, "returns" 8 ("gives" 1,533). flow/apps.go:172 uses three senses in one sentence: "as their catalog entries' commands name them ... as kit people's, is not, as its --marks would print null for each".
findings.fix: Write "such as", "because", "see X", "like", "if", and "returns"; for apps.go:172: "verbsOf returns the verbs of the given stages, each once. It skips a stage that kit never marks, such as kit people's, because --marks prints null for it."

findings.title: Package and file comments are key-by-key manuals, repeated across packages
findings.claim: Twenty-three files open with a comment of 8+ lines that walks through every key, click, glyph, and cell, restating what the code and tests state (prose rule 3). No test holds these to the code, so they are where every stale statement in P7-4 to P7-6 lives.
findings.evidence: tutorials.go 45 lines, tabs.go 27 (lines 1-12 describe the border one box-drawing character at a time), palette.go 23, welcome.go 22, workspaces.go 18, grid.go 16, flow.go 15, opener/open.go 15. The menu-keys sentence recurs in flow/menu.go:5, welcome/menu.go:3, and shell/dropdown.go:3; "quits with 130" in four package comments; the two-cell-glyph sentence in six.
findings.fix: Cut each to purpose, data source, and invariants (about 5-8 lines: tutorials 45 to 8, tabs 27 to 6, palette 23 to 6, welcome 22 to 8, flow 15 to 5), and state shared behaviour once in shell. Keep screens/screens.go:1, which explains lifecycle only it can, and split its long sentences.

findings.title: One thing has several names, and the working vocabulary is never defined
findings.claim: The same control goes by two or three names across comments and types, and the words that carry the text (panel, stage, picture, desk, aside, node, stop, kit's line, refusal, lets through, stands) are defined nowhere a newcomer would look.
findings.evidence: Comment-line counts: card 207 vs popover 106 (popover.go:1 opens "A field's card" over type Popover); columns dialog 62 vs fields dialog 7 vs field editor 4; menu bar 51 vs title line 38; keys bar 139 vs key hints 5; view 718 vs preset 390; "has the keyboard" 198 vs focus 78; kittui 246 vs "kit tui" 7. "panel" appears 374 times although no panel is drawn; "stands" 526.
findings.fix: Pick one name per thing and rename the type or the word to match. Add a ten-line glossary to the table and shell package comments.

findings.title: grid's package comment describes a sort click, a selection mark, and a panel that are gone
findings.claim: grid.go:10-12 says "a click on a name sorts by it. A row selected, one of several, has ✓ before its ▸. A panel beside the rows narrows them: a search ... and a field editor". None of the three is what the code does.
findings.evidence: A click on a name opens the column's card (flow/flow.go:719-721, `default: return m.openColumnMenu(column)`), and the selection mark is `const Chosen = "▣"` at grid.go:206. grid/panel.go has no drawing function; the search is on the menu bar (shell/search.go:18) and the fields are in the columns dialog (table/columns.go:1).
findings.fix: Rewrite the package comment from the code as it is, and shorten it to about six lines.

findings.title: flow's file comments contradict the code beside them in four places
findings.claim: views.go calls the preset line "the rule under the stage's header" and lists Rename… and Delete as dropdown lines; view.go:1 says the rows are drawn "beside its panel and legend"; flow.go:6 says a click "on the row under it opens or closes it". Each is stale.
findings.evidence: view.go:317 says the preset line is on "the control line" and table/presets.go:46-52 has only ItemSave, ItemSaveAs, ItemManage; legend.go:1 says the legend "floats over the screen"; flow.go:1278 says the ▸ or ▾ "and there alone" opens a row, as the switch at flow.go:1306-1310 does. views.go:3 also claims every stage has Default and Compact, while fields.json gives issues "All Issues, Backlog, Underway, ...".
findings.fix: Correct or delete each sentence; views.go:1 needs five lines, not twelve.

findings.title: Three package comments name the wrong root or leave out most of the package
findings.claim: app.go:1 says "Package app is kittui's root model", main.go:1-4 lists five screens and five verbs, and shell.go:1-3 names only the title line, the app's menu, and the menu's box.
findings.evidence: cmd/kittui/main.go:63 is `root := screens.New(r, first, m)` and app.Model is one screen it shows; `open` at main.go:85 also opens tutorials and the entity apps, twelve screens in shell/shell.go:37-49. Package shell also holds the keys bar, search, layers, crumb, notice, settings, workspace menu, and browser opener.
findings.fix: Write one accurate sentence for each package.

findings.title: reader.tsx names a script that no longer exists
findings.claim: The comment says "scripts/verify-dist.mjs fails a build whose root-relative href is outside the base", but that script is gone. It is a leftover of the fix for the 11-10 review's Infrastructure finding 16, which was about that script.
findings.evidence: projects/tutorials has no scripts/ directory and `grep -rl verify-dist` finds only reader.tsx and three docs. The check is `verify` in src/build.ts:43, called from `prerender` in vite.config.ts:23.
findings.fix: Change the sentence to "`verify` in build.ts fails a build whose root-relative href is outside the base."

findings.title: Other contorted constructions recur
findings.claim: Unusual constructions stand in for ordinary words: clipped "none for", "but" for except, postposed "apart", "one a row", inverted negation, and chained possessives.
findings.evidence: Comment-line counts: "none for/nothing for/or none" 149, "apart" 70, two possessives in a row 66 ("issues' pull requests' keys from changes'", flow.go:221), "but" for except 39, "one a row/value" 21, inverted negation 5 ("the columns the rows show not", grid/panel.go:97). schema.go:2 reads "Each holds for no table too, a nil Schema, which has no fields."
findings.fix: Write "returns nothing for", "except", "without", "one per row", "does not show", "the lines of the tab menu"; schema.go:2 becomes "Every method also works on a nil *Schema, which has no fields."

findings.title: A rename left capitalised identifiers inside ordinary words
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/table/age.go:25, projects/tui/internal/table/catalog.go:47, projects/tui/internal/table/catalog.go:100, projects/tui/internal/table/labels.go:54, projects/tui/internal/table/preset.go:11, projects/tui/internal/table/values.go:26, projects/tui/internal/table/values.go:40, projects/tui/internal/table/values.go:51
findings.claim: Eight comments in package table read as if a search-and-replace exported a name and caught the prose too.
findings.evidence: "Took gives how long a build or a job Took" (age.go:25), "Field is one Field of a stage" (catalog.go:47), "One gives a value of One raw text" (values.go:40), "in Seconds, never fewer than none" (values.go:51). The other four are "as a Preset keeps it", "draws a Pill", "a stage's Panel set", and "one a Value".
findings.fix: Lower-case the common nouns, for example "Took formats how long a build or a job took, to the second: 45s, 3m 36s, 1h 02m. It returns … while the job is running."

findings.title: Forwarding wrappers carry comments that only point at the function they call
findings.claim: One-line functions that call table.X or markdown.X each carry a comment ending "as table.X says", which restates the code under it (prose rule 3).
findings.evidence: 77 non-test comment lines match "as <pkg>.<Name> says/does/draws/gives": all 18 wrappers of flow/pane.go, plus flow/column.go, flow/heading.go, flow/fields.go:43-62, and welcome/page.go. pane.go:1 justifies them as "the names flow has always used", which is history, not a reason.
findings.fix: Delete the wrappers and call table directly, or keep one line over the group: "These forward to internal/table for the selected stage."

findings.title: Comments narrate history and hold one undated to-do
findings.claim: Twelve non-test lines describe what the code used to be, which a reader of the code as it is cannot use, and two lines state an open task as a fact with no issue number.
findings.evidence: "takes what the column menu did" (column.go:1), "as the title did before" (shell/books.go:3), "as views.json, the presets' file before presets.json, said it" (grid/panel.go:18), "the stages issues took the place of" (flow/apps.go:123). keys.go:36 and welcome/view.go:182 say home and end are "unnamed until a test shows the keys arrive in Terminal.app and iTerm".
findings.fix: Delete the history everywhere but the migration in flow/views.go:67-81. File the home/end task as an issue and cite its number in both comments.

findings.title: 99 comment lines run past 120 columns where a sentence was spliced into a wrapped paragraph
findings.claim: Paragraphs wrapped at 120 hold lines of up to 220 characters next to lines cut short, so they were edited and not re-wrapped. Three file comments also sit after the imports, attached to nothing (flow/fix.go:16, shell/keybar.go:14, shell/settings.go:16).
findings.evidence: A script counting characters finds 99 comment lines over 120 in 58 files (72 in non-test files): tabs.go:17 is 220, presets.go:80 is 203, books.go:10 is 200, menu.go:92 is 195. Short neighbours are at flow/layers.go:4, flow/menu.go:3, and flow/team.go:3.
findings.fix: Re-wrap the paragraphs and move the three detached comments above `package`. If 120 is the rule for Go comments, have kit lint check it.

findings.title: Test comments open by repeating the test's name
findings.claim: The test names are full sentences, so a comment whose first clause says the same thing adds nothing, and what follows the repeat is often one sentence of 40 to 60 words.
findings.evidence: Of 1,022 tests, 549 have a comment, and in 215 the first clause repeats at least 80% of the name's words: TestNoVerbOpensTheWelcomeGuide is followed by "No verb, as bare kit runs kittui, opens the welcome guide". 268 sentences in test comments have 40 words or more.
findings.fix: Drop the repeated clause and keep only what the name does not say, in short sentences. Leave the 473 tests with no comment as they are.

areas.title: commit subjects, specs, plans, and reviews
areas.coverage: Read whole: 400 commit subjects, 7 specs, the review summary page, 2 plans, whats-new and changelog pages, the prose, markdown, and house styles. Sampled: 15 plans (heads, some middles), about 150 lines of the findings page. Ran counts, greps, and one scratch reproduction. Did not run bin/release pack, bats, or kittui.
areas.summary: The prose has no filler at all, yet it is not plain. A house dialect (as, stands, in place of, says, names no) and stacked clauses left 16 of 53 sampled passages and 15 of 80 sampled subjects needing a second reading. 364 of 400 subjects pass 72 characters (median 131, maximum 358). Specs and plans are committed against the repository's own workflow rule, no plan says whether it is built (567 open checkboxes), and six spec statements no longer match the code. The release-readiness plan's first defect, an empty .sha256, still ships. findings.md is not written: the harness refused a report file from a subagent, so the Answers are carried here in short form.
strengths: No filler anywhere: 0 hits for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, 'note that', and ten more in 133,000 words of specs, plans, reviews, and subjects. Do not trade this for padding.

Every commit subject starts with its issue and an area and states the new behaviour as a fact; 68 of 80 sampled can be understood from the first 72 characters, and their numbers are exact ('246 bash processes, not 4,042'). Keep the first clause.

docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-11-10-code-review.md (lines 23-106, 141-174) is a model summary: one finding to a bullet, verb first, evidence in the same sentence, and a section that says where the review itself was wrong.
The findings page holds every item to one shape (place, defect, Scenario, Fix, Confirmed), so 260 items can be scanned.

The specs share one skeleton (Intent, Goals, Non-goals, Anti-goals, Decided, My calls, Left to the builder). Anti-goals and 'My calls' are worth keeping: they say what would be wrong and which decisions the writer made alone.

Good models of plain explanation: specs/2026-11-06-tutorials-design.md whole (3 of 3 passages pass); the Intent, Anti-goals, and Simplifications of the entities spec (3 of 3); the Intent and the table of GitHub's limits in the bots spec; the Intent of the terminal-checks spec.

'Decisions for the owner' in the fail-closed plan (lines 26-35): the choice, the default, and the reason in two lines each. The Goal lines of fail-closed, refusals-that-hold, and release-readiness say the outcome in one sentence.
Plans name the failing test before the code and the exact message a refusal prints, so a task can be checked against its plan.
Bold term lists in the specs' Terms sections are the most scannable parts of those files; the markdown rule against bold should not remove them.

Subjects that work as they are: '#177 kit: kit submit only pushes, and commits nothing'; '#141 kit: kit tidy keeps a branch whose commits no remote ever had'; '#142 kit: the issues a pull request closes are read page after page, past the first 100'.

findings.title: The release-readiness plan has no status, and defects it lists still ship
findings.claim: The plan that gates release/0.1.0 does not say what is built, and at least three of its items are not built at this commit.
findings.evidence: bin/release:116 still calls release:digest, which is undefined after `use git release releases` in a scratch copy (only file:digest exists), so pack writes a .sha256 line with no digest; there is no SECURITY.md, and `grep -rn changelog bin kit/bin kit/modules/bash` finds no changelog gate. Known since 11-10 (Infrastructure 1, Gaps), still open; I did not run pack itself.
findings.fix: Build Tasks 1 and 9 and the changelog gate. Then put one dated status line at the top of the plan naming each task built, dropped, or open.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: the pack test in a scratch copy prints `release:digest: command not found`, writes `  kit-9.9.9.tar.gz`, exits 0, and passes. No SECURITY.md, no changelog gate. But nothing has shipped, the plan's 50 unchecked boxes are its status (stale: `guard:missing`, 1st.sh:598, is built), and a consumer refuses the empty digest (kit/modules/bash/release.sh:125-131). Known backlog, not high.

findings.title: Commit subjects carry the commit body
findings.claim: 364 of 400 subjects (91%) pass 72 characters: minimum 37, median 131, 90th percentile 238, maximum 358; by bucket, 36 are 72 or fewer, 63 are 73-100, 165 are 101-150, 78 are 151-200, 49 are 201-300, 9 are over 300. The first clause helps (68 of 80 sampled name the change within 72 characters), and everything after it hurts: 15 of the 80 need a second reading, 70 subjects hold a second change after a semicolon, and 97 have four or more commas.
findings.evidence: Line 355: "#116 kittui: what stands under a heading that takes levels across steps in once from it, not once a level it took". A forge's commit list cuts these at about 72 characters, and git log --oneline, shortlog, and a rebase list wrap them; the plans write each subject before the work, which is why they read as lines of a spec.
findings.fix: Hold the subject to 72 characters, start it with a verb, put the rest in the body, and let policy.commit_subject cap the length. Ten rewrites: #273 "kittui: tab title lines say what the tab is for"; #266 "kit welcome: list each problem kit check finds in setup"; #268 "kit welcome: check that iTerm2 lets kittui copy to the clipboard"; #267 "kittui: dim Share with team where the clone keeps no team presets"; #249 "kittui: reopen each stage as you last left it"; #247 "kittui: kill a stage's whole process group on quit"; #243 "kittui: add Auto-hide, which hides columns with no values"; #233 "kit audit: print \"\" for a source or organization a clone lacks"; #198 "kittui: order the terms table: term, meaning, commands"; #116 "kittui: indent rows one step under a heading that merges levels".

findings.title: Specs and plans are committed against the repository's own workflow rule
findings.claim: The workflow rule this repository takes says a design, spec, or plan is never committed as a file, and docs/superpowers holds 7 specs and 17 plans (64,691 words of plans).
findings.evidence: workflow.md:32: "Write a design, a spec, or a plan as prose in the body of an issue. Never commit it as a file."; kit.yml:31 takes the workflow package. Known since 11-10 (Infrastructure 27), still open and larger: five files were added on 11-11 and 11-12.
findings.fix: Decide one way before the release: move each plan into its issue and delete the file, or change the rule to say a design is a file under docs/ and a built plan is not kept.

findings.title: No plan says whether it is built
findings.claim: All 567 checkboxes in the 17 plans are open and no plan has a status line, though the log shows most of them built.
findings.evidence: `grep -c '^ *- \[x\]'` is 0 in every plan; the review page records the build of three of its eight plans and is silent on contracts (#74), the first release's decisions (#135), release readiness (#1), tutorials 2, and the apps' tabs. Known since 11-10 ("Their checkboxes were never ticked"), then 5 plans and now 17.
findings.fix: Add one line under each plan's title: built, with its commit range; in progress, with the tasks done; or not started.

findings.title: Spec status lines and statements no longer match the tree
findings.claim: Six places in the specs, and one in docs/terminals.md, say what the code does not do.
findings.evidence: Components says kittui has four screens, "not applications" (the TUI README says nine apps; known since 11-10); terminal checks says "Status: designed" though built under #211, and with docs/terminals.md:63 says a failed check "offers later and keep" where welcome.go:9 says "offers ⧉ and keep". Workspaces says "kit welcome gains no --workspace" (kit-welcome:33 documents kit --workspace=<workspace> welcome); tutorials says kit release refuses a version with no changelog entry (nothing reads it) and writes --tag <tag> for --tag=<audience>; entities says "proposed" and that none of its domains ships, while kit-people, kit-delivery, kit-platform, and kit-audit exist.
findings.fix: Give each spec a dated status line saying what is built and which sections later work replaced. Correct docs/terminals.md:63 to "offers ⧉ and keep".

findings.title: A house dialect replaces ordinary words
findings.claim: The text has no machine filler (0 hits for comprehensive, robust, seamless, leverage, ensure, crucial, and ten more in 133,000 words) and fails the opposite way: ordinary connectives are avoided for contorted substitutes. No style rule asks for this; .kit/styles/prose.md itself writes "such as".
findings.evidence: In the 400 subjects "instead of", "such as", "for example", and "because" occur 0 times, against "in place of" 11, "as" 113 in four senses (24 subjects use it twice or more), "stand" 37, thing-as-subject "say" 72, and verb-plus-"no" 19; the specs have "stand" 24 and bare possessives 48, the plans "because" 0. Examples: "in place of that each of its rows stands here" (line 4), "so ⧉ never copies nothing unseen" (line 17), "Every form prints the key never" (bots :163).
findings.fix: Use the ordinary word: instead of, such as, because, is, shows, prints, and put the negation on the verb. Split any sentence that needs a fourth comma.

findings.title: The components spec restates the code at length and hides two live rule sets
findings.claim: It is the one spec that cannot be read in one pass (1 of 3 sampled passages pass, 20 uses of "stand"), and it is about 120 lines too long. Its Terms table and Keys rules are still normative but sit in a document marked built.
findings.evidence: Lines 240-264 list what moved between two Go packages in sentences of 100 words and more, which prose rule 3 forbids as restating the code; the package table at :19 (16,805 lines, 49 files) is stale. The Terms table's "Today" column describes names since renamed.
findings.fix: Move Terms (:159) and Keys (:199) to projects/tui/README.md or a page under docs/. Cut lines 13-53 and 240-310 to a short record of what moved where.

findings.title: A delivered module cites a spec the release does not hold
findings.claim: A see: line under kit/ points at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-terminal-checks-design.md, which a consumer does not have.
findings.evidence: bin/release:107 copies only bin, libexec, modules, and packages into the tarball, and every plan's Global Constraints say everything under kit/ is written for a consumer. The 11-10 review counted two such lines (Infrastructure 25); this one is new.
findings.fix: Point it at docs/terminals.md by its full URL, as each check's `more` does, or drop it.

findings.title: Plans carry the residue of the sessions that ran them
findings.claim: Checked-in plans hold instructions that meant something only to the agent sessions of the day.
findings.evidence: Plan 3b :31 says to "ask the TUI fork (uds:/tmp/cc-socks/77485.sock ...)", and workspaces 2 :28 and :451-457 reserve packages for "kit-e7". All 17 open with "For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL", 16 repeat the shared-worktree staging rules and export PATH, 8 repeat one Review paragraph, and the review's plans pin line numbers to 2dad3552, 400 commits back.
findings.fix: If the plans stay, cut the banner, the staging rules, and the session names. Say at the top which commit the line numbers belong to.

findings.title: What's new uses an undefined term, and both site pages are one sentence
findings.claim: "This is kit's first line." reads as a line of text to anyone who opens What's new first, and the 0.1.0 changelog entry says nothing of what the release holds.
findings.evidence: "Line" is defined only in the tutorial the sentence goes on to link; the spec (tutorials-design.md:86) asks the changelog for "what changed and which tutorials it touched". Known since 11-10 (Gaps: "What's new and Changelog are one sentence each").
findings.fix: Write "kit 0.1 is the first release line of kit. Start with Reading kit's tutorials: it explains how the tutorials are laid out, and how a page marks a passage that a later 0.1.x release added." Give the 0.1.0 entry a short list of what the release holds.

findings.title: The area label of a subject is not held to one spelling
findings.claim: A filter of the log by area misses rows, because one area has several labels and three subjects have none.
findings.evidence: kittui: 175 against tui: 11; forge: 13 against forge seam: 2; kit welcome: 12 against 46 subjects that open "kit: kit <verb>"; one plan under plan: and the rest under docs:. Lines 98, 100, and 101 have no label.
findings.fix: Pick the set of labels (kit, kittui, forge, docs, tests, ci, and a verb's name only where the commit touches that verb alone) and state it in the workflow rule.

findings.title: Small breaks of the prose and markdown styles in the specs
findings.claim: Four acronyms are never expanded (prose rule 5), three prose lines pass 120 columns, and one spec has no status line and a title in title case. Two rules make the text worse when followed: "the thing as the subject" turns a commit subject into a statement that hides the act, and the ban on bold would remove the specs' term lists, their most scannable part.
findings.evidence: SBOM (entities:115), OCI (entities:322), DECRQM (terminal-checks:158), MDX (tutorials:55), while JWT in the bots spec is expanded; long lines at workspaces-design.md:127 and :183 and planned-tabs-design.md:131. 47 bullets in the specs open with a bold run-in, and each plan opens with bold field names (268 in all).
findings.fix: Expand the four acronyms and wrap the three lines. Say in the markdown style that a bold term in a definition list is not emphasis, and in the workflow rule that a subject starts with a verb.

findings.title: Worst passage: the Dialog paragraph of the components spec
findings.claim: One 60-word sentence defines two helpers through five nested clauses.
findings.evidence: "What the four dialogs share is narrower than a dialog type: `shell.Placed`, a box as `shell.Dialog` draws it, where it stands, which draws itself and says whether a click falls off it, on its edges, or on a body line; and `shell.Step`, the line under the keyboard moving to the next line it can stand on and stopping at the ends."
findings.fix: "The four dialogs share two helpers, not a dialog type. `shell.Placed` is a box with a position: it draws itself and reports whether a click landed outside it, on its border, or on a body line; `shell.Step` moves the cursor to the next line that can take it, and stops at the first and the last."

findings.title: Worst passage: how a form reaches the menus and the search
findings.claim: The sentence must be read three times, and "making the palette for a form that stood alone" is not English a stranger can parse.
findings.evidence: "A click on the kit menu or the workspace menu drops it down, and `=` or `-` does where the field with focus types no text; the search field is the palette's, so a click on it, or `/` where no text is typed, gives the palette's search focus in the form's place, making the palette for a form that stood alone."
findings.fix: "A click on the kit menu or the workspace menu opens it, and so does `=` or `-` unless focus is in a text field. The search field belongs to the palette: a click on it, or `/` outside a text field, replaces the form with the palette and focuses its search, and kittui makes the palette first if the form was opened on its own."

findings.title: Worst passages: Views, and a call to table's
findings.claim: Two definitions end on a dangling "as" and a bare possessive.
findings.evidence: "`Views`, the rules of which view a table is set as and what the person's can be saved, renamed, and deleted as"; "Each move keeps the name `flow` gave it, a call to `table`'s."
findings.fix: "`Views`, which decides which view a table shows and which of the person's views can be saved, renamed, or deleted." "Each function that moved keeps its old name in `flow`, where it is now a one-line call into `table`."

findings.title: Worst passage: the shape of the six app verbs
findings.claim: The sentence that defines every new verb packs four statements behind colons and semicolons, and "hold for the picture" tells the reader nothing.
findings.evidence: "Each app's new tabs are the stages of one verb named for the app, shaped as `kit workspace` is: `<verb> <stage> --json` prints `{rows, errors}`, each row `{key, …, links}`, and under a group each row gains `member`; `<verb> --stages` and `<verb> --marks` hold for the picture; on a terminal `<verb> <stage>` opens kittui on that tab."
findings.fix: "Each app gets one verb, named for the app, and each new tab is a stage of it, as with `kit workspace`. `<verb> <stage> --json` prints `{rows, errors}`, each row `{key, …, links}` plus `member` over a group; `<verb> --stages` and `<verb> --marks` list the stages and their marks; on a terminal `<verb> <stage>` opens kittui on that tab."

findings.title: Worst passages: plan bookkeeping and the choice of kit audit
findings.claim: Two passages assume the reader holds another plan's task numbers in mind, and "it changes nothing" has no clear referent.
findings.evidence: "Task 9's planned line and People's hiding go, as no tab stays planned; its rules for a tab that is never stale stay, for a stage whose mark is null."; "`kit trust` already trusts a clone (#153), so Trust's verb is `kit audit`, the owner's choice; it changes nothing."
findings.fix: "Task 9's \"planned\" line and its hiding of People are dropped, because no tab is planned any longer; its rules for a tab that never goes stale now apply to a stage whose mark is null." "`kit trust` is taken: it records that you trust a clone (#153), so the Trust app's verb is `kit audit`, which the owner chose and which only reads."

findings.title: Worst passages: two inverted sentences in the bots spec
findings.claim: Word order is bent to avoid an ordinary negative and an ordinary relative clause.
findings.evidence: "Every form prints the key never."; "in CI, the person the bot's work was handed by."
findings.fix: "No form ever prints the key." "In CI, the person who handed the bot its work."

findings.title: Worst passage: what a review request to a bot is
findings.claim: "A request of a login is the forge's own" and "a request of a bot ... is the mark" make the reader work out who asks whom.
findings.evidence: "A request of a login is the forge's own. A request of a bot without `bot-review-request` is the mark `bot:<slug>` on the pull request: on an issue the mark means work it, on a change the bot does not author it means review it."
findings.fix: "A review request to a person is the forge's own review request; where the forge lacks `bot-review-request`, a request to a bot adds the label `bot:<slug>` to the pull request. The same label means \"work on this\" on an issue and \"review this\" on a change the bot did not write."

findings.title: Worst passages: the workspace dropdown and a kept finding
findings.claim: "The three lines join it with the Workspaces screen" does not say which lines or what joining means, and the kept-finding passage chains five clauses and describes buttons the code no longer has.
findings.evidence: "Until step 7, the dropdown holds the favorites and, for a repository, its groups; the three lines join it with the Workspaces screen."; "In kittui, a failed terminal check offers later and keep; it offers no now, since kit never runs its fix, which stands under it."
findings.fix: "Until step 7 is built, the dropdown lists only the favorites and, for a repository, the groups it belongs to; Browse…, New workspace…, and Manage workspaces… are added with the Workspaces screen." "In kittui, a failed terminal check shows its fix under it, with ⧉ to copy it and keep; there is no run button, because kit never changes a terminal's settings."

findings.title: Worst passage: the Homebrew decision the owner must take
findings.claim: A decision put to the owner ends in a default written in telegraphese: "not done by the tag, drop".
findings.evidence: "Homebrew: the tap bumps itself on a schedule (infrastructure issue 458, no token in kit), a `release.yml` step with a token for the tap, or drop `README.md:76-80`. Default: the first, Part B step 6; not done by the tag, drop."
findings.fix: "Homebrew. Choose one: (a) the tap updates itself on a schedule (infrastructure issue 458; kit needs no token); (b) `release.yml` updates the tap, with a token for it; (c) remove the Homebrew install from `README.md:76-80`. Default: (a), in Part B step 6, and (c) if (a) is not in place when the release is tagged."

findings.title: Worst passages: two Architecture paragraphs in the workspaces plans
findings.claim: The paragraph meant to orient the builder is the hardest in each plan: 5 of 17 Goal-and-Architecture passages fail the one-pass test, these two worst.
findings.evidence: "A pick that changes the place the screens read is a fresh start: the root closes and remakes the screens made, as they would be made there."; "Flow decodes it into the slices it already holds, desk, worktrees, and incoming becoming one entry per member, every row carrying `member`, its key made unique by it, and a member that failed drawn as its line."
findings.fix: "When a pick changes the directory the screens read, the root closes every open screen and makes each one again for the new directory." "Flow decodes it into the slices it already has: desk, worktrees, and incoming get one entry per member, every row carries `member` (also added to its key, so keys stay unique), and a member whose read failed is drawn as one line with its error."

findings.title: Worst passage on the review page: a clone whose kit.yml does not parse
findings.claim: The review page is otherwise a model, and two lines in its later sections slip into the dialect; "a take" at :204 is never defined.
findings.evidence: "a clone whose `kit.yml` does not parse is filed under origin and said where its member is drawn."; "A take over history that another session rewrote keeps the empty start commit twice."
findings.fix: "A clone whose `kit.yml` cannot be parsed is listed under its origin remote, and its member's row says so." Say what "a take" is at :204, or name the verb that does it.

areas.title: the earlier review: Workflow, Delivery, Flow
areas.coverage: Read lines 1-725 and the review page whole; the code each finding names, whole files or whole functions. Ran 34 reproductions in a copy (tests' fake gh, jq 1.7.1 and 1.8.2) and rebase.bats plus tidy.bats, 28/28. Eight findings judged by reading only, marked plausible. No Linux, no real forge, rest of bats not run.
areas.summary: Of the 86 earlier findings in Workflow, Delivery, and Flow, 31 are fixed, 50 open, 5 partly fixed, none unchecked (Workflow 11/13/3, Delivery 12/17/1, Flow 8/20/1). Of the 18 the page ranks highest, 14 are fixed; still open are Workflow 3, Delivery 4, Delivery 6, and Flow 1, plus Delivery 3 (high), and none of the five is in a plan. By earlier severity: critical 1/1 fixed, high 9/15, medium 14/30, low 7/40. The destructive verbs (rebase, tidy, the sweep, regions, cycles) now hold. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write as a subagent report file, so this result carries every finding and the counts.
strengths: Fixed at this commit and to be kept (by earlier number): Workflow 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 17; Delivery 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 25, 26, 30; Flow 2, 3, 4, 6, 11, 14, 18, 23. Partly fixed: Workflow 4, 16, 24; Delivery 29; Flow 28.

kit rebase takes origin's commits first and leases on the tip it fetched (kit/modules/bash/git.sh:487-506), and kit tidy asks the forge for the change's head before deleting (git:unpushed); tests/rebase.bats and tests/tidy.bats pass 28 of 28. Do not go back to a lease on the commit read before the fetch: the page's correction to Workflow 1 is right.

A refusal changes nothing: region:has judges the markers in one awk pass, by the link's name against the target's text, and kit uninstall, kit packages remove, and kit update judge every region before the first write (place:refusals). A lost kit:end now ends in a named refusal with the file untouched (reproduced).

Reads fail closed and whole: resolve:active prints nothing until the order is whole, list:read carries the status, context:compile compiles each content pattern alone and names the file, kind, and pattern, the GitLab open changes print nothing unless every read answered, and forge:whole refuses a list at the cap.

git:push names the refspec in one place, so push.default decides nothing in kit work, kit submit, or kit rebase; commit:git and the start commit keep the judged subject with --cleanup=whitespace, and kit commit reports the subject read back from HEAD.

kit work's sweep is safe: refs/stash is compared before and after, the stash's subject is checked, and issue:sweep-restore is registered at exit, so a failure after the sweep puts the desk's work back.

The bridge's partial (projects/tui/internal/kit/kit.go:316) keeps a JSON document kit printed with exit 1, so one dead remote no longer blanks the incoming tab while the bash side keeps its honest exit status.

kit packages remove now leaves an edited copy alone through the shared place:edited predicate (reproduced), the hydrate fast path sees a file added under .kit/packages/ (reproduced), epoch reads a time at an offset, and kit generate and kit lint refuse a named path that does not exist.

findings.title: Flow 1: a failed check is still hidden by a same-named check that started later
findings.claim: checks still keeps one run per bare check name, and the GraphQL query asks no check suite or workflow, so CI/test failing and Docs/test passing later is one passed check and the change reads ready. Known since 11-10, still open; no plan covers it.
findings.evidence: A jq run of github_runs | checks | state over a failed and a later passed run named test gives {"state":"ready","checks":{"state":"SUCCESS","passed":1,"total":1,"failing":""}}.
findings.fix: Ask checkSuite { workflowRun { workflow { name } event } }, group by suite or workflow plus name, and treat only a later attempt of the same suite as a rerun. Add a same-named-checks case to tests/forge-conformance.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in jq 1.8.2: a failed and a later passed CheckRun named test through github_runs | checks | state give ready, SUCCESS, 1 of 1. forge.jq:79 groups by .name alone; the query at github.sh:544-548 asks no suite or workflow. No test or plan covers it. Not run against a real GitHub.

findings.title: Workflow 3: kit commit still undoes a path that two unseen commits changed
findings.claim: commit:behind still compares the staged blob only with the blob before the last commit that touched the path, and #62 is not built, so a shared index two commits behind passes. Known since 11-10, still open; the page says no plan covers #62.
findings.evidence: Session A commits a twice from a private GIT_INDEX_FILE; session B stages b.txt and runs kit commit --message '#7 B: add b.txt': exit 0, '✅ committed 817d61f', stat 'a | 1 -', 'b.txt | 1 +'.
findings.fix: Walk git log -- <path> and refuse when the staged blob equals the path's blob at any commit on HEAD while the disk differs, or build #62. Add the two-commit case to tests/commit.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced (verify-1/run/w3): A adds then changes a from a private index; B stages b.txt; kit commit exits 0, 'committed c15159c', stat 'a | 1 -', 'b.txt | 1 +'. commit.sh:301 compares only with the blob before the last commit. tests/commit.bats:428 covers one commit behind only.

findings.title: Delivery 3: a foreign file under .kit/ is still left alone for one command, then overwritten
findings.claim: materialize:all refuses to replace an unrecorded different file, then materialize:hydrate calls manifest:write, which records every delivered path, so the next verb replaces the file. kit update has the same order, and its comment at line 233 says the opposite of what line 235 does.
findings.evidence: In a fresh clone with my own .kit/rules/bash.md, kit hydrate prints '⚠️ … a different file is there already; move it aside', the manifest then holds its line, and the next 'kit kinds bash' prints '⚠️ .kit/rules/bash.md was changed in place, or came from another release; replaced'.
findings.fix: Have materialize:all return the set it refused and manifest:text leave those paths out, in materialize:hydrate and kit update alike.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced (verify-1/run/d3): kit hydrate warns 'a different file is there already', .kit/manifest then records .kit/rules/bash.md, and the next kit kinds bash prints 'changed in place ... replaced' and overwrites it. kit-update:234-235 has the same order; that path was read, not run.

findings.title: Delivery 4: kit packages add still corrupts a kit.yml whose lists are not indented
findings.claim: settings:declaration-kept still takes only lines starting with two spaces as a block's continuation, so a valid kit.yml with a zero-indent list is broken by the first write. The page lists it under 'A verb destroys work'; no plan took it.
findings.evidence: With 'packages:' then '- kit', kit packages add style/json prints '✅ packages: kit style/json' and leaves '  - kit', '  - style/json', '- kit'; the next verb says 'go-yaml load error … did not find expected key'. kit uninstall leaves the stray '- kit'.
findings.fix: Treat a block as its key line plus every following line that is indented or starts with '- ', or refuse a declaration the awk cannot rewrite.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced (verify-1/run/d4, d4b): with 'packages:' then '- kit', kit packages add style/json leaves '  - kit', '  - style/json', '- kit'; the next verb fails with 'did not find expected key'. kit uninstall leaves '- kit'. settings.sh:218 takes only two-space lines.

findings.title: Delivery 6: on jq 1.7, the stated minimum, template matching still fails on non-ASCII text
findings.claim: match still mixes indices (byte offsets before jq 1.8) with code-point slices while the kit accepts jq 1.7 or later, so kit check and kit lint refuse a correct file on a desk with macOS's system jq. The page lists it under 'The release cannot ship'.
findings.evidence:
"# Guía «name»
rest
" | parts | match("# Guía foo
rest
") gives {"ok":false,"line":2} with /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1-apple and {"ok":true,"values":{"name":"foo"}} with jq 1.8.2.
findings.fix: Find the literal without indices, or raise the minimum to jq 1.8 in welcome.sh, syntax.sh, and docs/install.md.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: /usr/bin/jq 1.7.1 gives {ok:false,line:2}, 1.8.2 ok. End to end (verify-1/run/d6): kit lint refuses a correct kit/bin/kit-hello whose purpose holds 'olé' on 1.7.1, passes on 1.8.2 and with ASCII. kit check (kit-check:86) read, not run. release-readiness Task 5 plans the fix, unbuilt.

findings.title: Workflow 8: kit work 7 still adopts any branch whose last path part starts with 7-
findings.claim: git ls-remote --heads origin "7-*" still matches by trailing path component, so a release/7-x or dependabot branch is taken for the issue's branch and gets the start commit pushed to it.
findings.evidence: With origin holding release/7-x and the fake gh, kit work 7 prints 'Creating worktree …/worktrees/release/7-x', '✅ Draft pull request #4 on release/7-x', and origin's release/7-x ends in '#7 start: Fix the thing'.
findings.fix: Ask for refs/heads/${key}-* and keep only names that start with ${key}-.

findings.title: Workflow 12: the pre-commit checks still read the disk while the commit takes the index
findings.claim: commit:checks still hands ${PWD}/${path} to kit lint and kit generate --check, so a staged blob that differs from the disk is committed unchecked.
findings.evidence: I staged a bad.sh shellcheck refuses (echo $1), rewrote it on disk unstaged, and ran kit commit: '✅ every governed path passes its rule's linter', '✅ committed a0e8340', and git show HEAD:bad.sh is the refused version.
findings.fix: Refuse a staged path whose disk copy differs from the index, or check a git checkout-index of the tree being committed.

findings.title: Delivery 9: a retired file is still never removed in a fresh clone or worktree
findings.claim: place:retire still takes its candidates from .kit/manifest alone, which git ignores, so a clone or CI never removes what a release retired, and kit check passes.
findings.evidence: Two release copies, OLD.txt in 0.1.0 only: in a git clone, KIT_BASE=old kit --version=<new> update prints '✅ kit 0.2.0 is installed', OLD.txt stays, kit check passes; the original checkout prints 'OLD.txt: retired in 0.2.0, removed'.
findings.fix: Make the candidates the union of the manifest's paths and the base release's delivered paths, each judged by digest against the base's file.

findings.title: Delivery 14: a release that drops a package still leaves no verb that works
findings.claim: A package kit.yml lists and the release lacks is refused by every verb that could remove it, so only a hand edit of kit.yml gets out.
findings.evidence: With style/gone in kit.yml: kit update, kit uninstall --dry-run, and kit check each print "❌ 'style/gone' is not a package in reach"; kit packages remove style/gone prints "'style/gone' is not one of the choices".
findings.fix: kit update drops a recorded package the release lacks, says so, and lets retire take its paths; package:remove accepts a name that is recorded though not in reach.

findings.title: Delivery 15: kit new kind still writes a pattern in YAML double quotes
findings.claim: A regex backslash in --path or --content is a YAML escape inside the double quotes kit new kind writes, so the kinds file it makes cannot be read and every classifying verb fails once the package is active.
findings.evidence: kit new kind proto --content='^// proto\.v[0-9]+' writes '  - "^// proto\.v[0-9]+"'; after kit packages add local, kit kinds prints 'go-yaml load error in scanner … found unknown escape character' and 'the kinds in it cannot be read'.
findings.fix: Write the pattern single-quoted with each single quote doubled, as yaml.sh:9 says a pattern is written; drop the double-quote refusal at new.sh:195.
