findings.title: Delivery 16: a source tarball laid out as the header describes is still emptied and cached
findings.claim: --strip-components 1 still removes packages/ from a tarball whose top level is packages/, and the empty source is cached and skipped without a word. The url also still reaches curl with no -- before it (line 96), so 'url: -K<file>' is read as an option before the digest check.
findings.evidence: A file:// tarball of packages/guides/package.yml, digest pinned: kit packages add guides fetches it, prints "'guides' is not one of the choices", and the cache holds <digest>/guides.
findings.fix: After unpacking, refuse and do not cache a source with neither packages/ nor kit/packages/, or strip only a single top-level directory; put -- before the url.

findings.title: Flow 5: an issue still counts as claimed when a change closes the same number in another repository
findings.claim: unclaimed still matches on the issue number alone, so a local open issue vanishes from the issues stage when a change closes other/repo#N.
findings.evidence: A jq run of issues::rows with local #7 and #9 and a change closing other/repo#9 gives #7 in backlog and {"number":9,"title":"Nine in ANOTHER repo","status":"underway","organization":"other"}; local #9 is in neither.
findings.fix: Match on organization and repository plus number; the documents already carry both.

findings.title: Flow 7: the first fetch of a remote is still reported as its branches pruned
findings.claim: flow:fetch-diff still uses NR == FNR, which holds for every line of the after snapshot when the before snapshot is empty.
findings.evidence: In a repository with no tags, the first kit flow incoming --json after git remote add origin gives {"name":"origin","branches":{"new":[],"updated":[],"gone":["main","x"]}}.
findings.fix: Use FILENAME == ARGV[1], or pass the snapshots as awk variables, and add a first-fetch test to tests/incoming.bats.

findings.title: Flow 8 and Flow 9: GitLab still counts notes for threads, and a job allowed to fail as a failed check
findings.claim: unresolved counts unresolved notes, not discussions; a failed job with allow_failure is a failed check; and requested_changes in detailed_merge_status does not block as GitHub's CHANGES_REQUESTED does.
findings.evidence: A jq run of gitlab_pr with one discussion of three unresolved notes and one job {status: failed, allow_failure: true} gives {"state":"failing:gate","checks":{"state":"FAILURE","failing":"lint"},"unresolved":3}.
findings.fix: Count discussions with any(.notes[]; .resolvable and (.resolved | not)), count failed and .allow_failure as passed, and add requested_changes to approval.

findings.title: Flow 15: here, local, and a worktree's own change are still matched on the branch name alone
findings.claim: A fork's pull request whose branch shares a local branch's name is drawn as checked out here with the desk's path, and in a worktree changes keeps a fork's change of the same branch name.
findings.evidence: The jq run of issues::rows with a change from fork cy on branch main and worktrees {"main":"/desk"} gives {"here":true,"worktree":"/desk","fork":"cy"}.
findings.fix: Set here and local only when .fork == null, and add the same test to the select in changes:documents.

findings.title: Flow 13: a change's author is still the GraphQL login, which names a bot without [bot]
findings.claim: The open changes ask author { login } with no __typename and github_prs writes it as it comes (dependabot), while forge/github:pr-author reads REST on purpose for dependabot[bot], the spelling linked_exempt uses.
findings.evidence: The query at github.sh:530 and the fold at forge.jq:159 are unchanged; forge.jq:887 already has github_bot, which appends [bot], and it is not used here. No live read.
findings.fix: Ask __typename under author and fold it through github_bot, so --owner='dependabot[bot]' matches what the picture draws.

findings.title: Flow 12: builds still filters the 50 newest runs of any kind
findings.claim: gh run list --limit 50 and pipelines?per_page=50 are unchanged, and the fold then keeps default-branch pushes and tags, so a repository whose last 50 runs are pull request runs draws few builds or none.
findings.evidence: By reading: github.sh:797 'run list --limit 50', gitlab.sh:589 'pipelines?per_page=50', forge.jq:389 selects after the cap.
findings.fix: Ask the forge by branch and event: gh run list --branch <default> --event push, and pipelines?ref=…&source=….

findings.title: Flow 10: gh api still goes to gh's default host, not the checkout's
findings.claim: No call in github.sh passes --hostname or sets GH_HOST, so gh api user, graphql, and rate_limit ask github.com when gh is logged in to several hosts, while gh repo view follows the remote.
findings.evidence: grep for hostname, GH_HOST, GH_REPO in kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh finds nothing. A desk logged in to github.com and an enterprise host would settle it.
findings.fix: Pass --hostname "$(forge:host <primary>)" on every gh api call.

findings.title: Flow 16: closes still takes every linked issue, open or closed
findings.claim: The GraphQL query asks no state under closingIssuesReferences and gitlab_pr ignores .state, so a closed issue linked to an open change is drawn as underway.
findings.evidence: The gitlab_pr jq run with a closes_issues entry whose state is closed gave closes [9]. That the forges list a closed issue there is inferred, as on 11-10.
findings.fix: Ask the issue's state on both forges and keep open issues only.

findings.title: Flow 17: GitLab's open changes still cost five sequential reads per merge request
findings.claim: The loop now makes five paged reads per merge request (it was four) plus one per fork, one after another, against a 120 s snapshot wait and kittui's 2-minute stage deadline.
findings.evidence: By reading gitlab.sh:376-422; forge_snapshot_wait=1200 turns of 0.1 s; const deadline = 2 * time.Minute. A timed run against a project with 50 open merge requests would settle the number.
findings.fix: Read the merge requests in parallel with a bound, or in one GraphQL query.

findings.title: Workflow 19: a staged type change is still invisible to kit commit
findings.claim: --diff-filter=ACMRD (and ACMR in commit:checks) still leaves out T, so a type change alone is 'nothing staged' and beside other paths is committed unseen by the guard, the linters, and commit:behind.
findings.evidence: A file replaced by a symbolic link and staged shows 'T  notes.txt'; kit commit prints '❌ nothing is staged'.
findings.fix: Add T to both filters.

findings.title: Workflow 26: a path that starts with - is still read by grep as an option, and a stale region passes
findings.claim: generate:carries runs grep on the path with no -- before it, so a file named -dash.md is never searched for directives.
findings.evidence: A staged -dash.md with a stale region: kit commit prints 'grep: unknown --directories option', '✅ generate: no kit:generate directive to expand', '✅ committed b3b17b6'.
findings.fix: Put -- before the file in both greps.

findings.title: Workflow 15: kit rebase <path> still reads a relative path from the repository root
findings.claim: kit:enter moves to the root and the raw operand goes to git -C, so a path typed from a subdirectory names the wrong place.
findings.evidence: From desk/docs, kit rebase ../worktrees/7-fix-the-thing prints '❌ ../worktrees/7-fix-the-thing has no branch checked out'; from the root the same worktree rebases and pushes.
findings.fix: Resolve the operand with context:relative, as kit commit does.

findings.title: Workflow 18: kit work still starts a closed issue without a word
findings.claim: issue:start reads the title and the assignees and never the state, so a closed issue gets a branch and a draft change that kit linked then refuses.
findings.evidence: With issue 7 CLOSED in the fake, kit work 7 completed; the fake's call log holds 'issue view 7 --json title' and '--json assignees' only.
findings.fix: Read tracker:of <ref> state beside the title and refuse, or warn and name the rule of kit linked.

findings.title: Workflow 20: the patterns engine still disagrees with OPA on a missing key and under LC_ALL=C
findings.claim: A facts document whose policy lacks a key is matched against the literal null, and {1,120} counts bytes under LC_ALL=C; kit sets no locale.
findings.evidence: policy/patterns:deny on policy {} prints "branch '7-x' does not match policy.branch: null"; a title of 100 é passes under C.UTF-8 and is refused under LC_ALL=C.
findings.fix: Read each pattern with // "", and match under a fixed UTF-8 locale or say the limit is bytes.

findings.title: Workflow 23: kit work can still make a branch the default policy refuses
findings.claim: A title with no ASCII letter or digit gives an empty slug and the branch <key>-, which policy.branch refuses for every later kit commit; the change's title is still the issue's title unshortened.
findings.evidence: Running the slug pipeline on a Japanese title gives 'ab4521-', which ^[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ does not match. The tracker itself was not run.
findings.fix: Fall back to a fixed slug such as work for an empty one, and shorten the title to the policy's limit.

findings.title: Workflow 21: the primary forge issue still gets no Closes line when its branch was found, not made
findings.claim: The primary is left to 'the branch the forge creates', so a branch found on origin, and on GitLab a branch kit makes by name over REST, has nothing in the change's body linking it to the issue.
findings.evidence: In the R1-6 run gh pr create got --body "" and no pr edit followed; gitlab.sh's link-branch only POSTs repository/branches and glab mr create gets --description "". A real forge would settle whether a branch name alone closes the issue.
findings.fix: Always add Closes <ref> for the primary; issue:link-in-body is idempotent.

findings.title: Workflow 22: settling a closed change still unassigns the author from an issue a newer change closes
findings.claim: The CLOSED arm of issue:settle looks at the closed change alone, comments 'this is backlog again', and unassigns the author with no look at the open changes.
findings.evidence: By reading issue.sh:301-341; no call to forge:open-prs or any open-change read in the arm.
findings.fix: Skip an issue that an open change of the same author closes.

findings.title: Workflow 16 (partly fixed): kit rebase still calls every failed rebase a conflict
findings.claim: The failed push is now said and exits 1, but any failure of git rebase, a missing origin/<default> or a failed signer, still prints 'conflicts with <target>'. The page rules the signer case left as it is.
findings.evidence: git.sh:497-503: one branch for every non-zero git rebase, with the error '${branch} conflicts with ${target}; the rebase was aborted'.
findings.fix: Tell a conflict by unmerged paths after the failed rebase, and pass git's own words on otherwise.

findings.title: Workflow 24 (partly fixed): kit work still names origin where the primary is meant
findings.claim: facts:document now counts from refs/remotes/<primary>/<default>, but issue.sh still fetches origin, makes the branch from origin/<default>, counts the start commit from it, and fast-forwards the desk to it. This is #68, which no plan covers.
findings.evidence: Literal origin at the four lines, while default_branch comes from git:default-branch, which reads the primary.
findings.fix: Use forge:primary for the default branch's ref in these places.

findings.title: Workflow 27: the gate's justfile is still read with a bare just, outside the toolchain
findings.claim: detect-gate runs just --summary before the toolchain is chosen (line 74) or used (line 89), so a desk with just only in the project toolchain cannot find its gate.
findings.evidence: By reading; the failure would read 'the root justfile could not be read: … command not found'.
findings.fix: Run the probe through toolchain:run, or grep the justfile for a ci recipe.

findings.title: Workflow 25 and Flow 29 (ruled): the default branch is still the literal main when <primary>/HEAD is unset
findings.claim: Unchanged, and ruled: the page records the fallback to main as a decision of the Fail closed plan. On a master repository with no origin/HEAD the default-branch refusals of kit commit and kit rebase do not apply.
findings.evidence: git.sh:40 '[[ -n "${branch}" ]] || branch=main'; policy:base now names the unset HEAD in its remedy.
findings.fix: None asked; reported so the ruling is seen before the release. If reopened: git ls-remote --symref <primary> HEAD, and fail rather than guess.

findings.title: Workflow 4 (partly fixed): an empty change body still gets a leading blank line
findings.claim: The destructive half is fixed (the body read is checked before any edit). The second half stands: an empty body, which every change kit work opens has, is written as a newline then Closes.
findings.evidence: issue.sh:554 body="${body}"$'\n'"Closes ${ref}" with no test for an empty body.
findings.fix: Join with a newline only when the body is not empty.

findings.title: Delivery 18: an unclosed [ in a kind's glob still hangs every verb that classifies
findings.claim: context:glob-ere loops forever on a [ that never closes, and keeps [!x] as written, which means 'not x' to the glob and '! or x' to the ERE.
findings.evidence: context:glob-ere 'notes[1.md' ran until a 5-second alarm (exit 142); glob-ere 'a[!b]c' prints ^a[!b]c$, glob-matches adc 'a[!b]c' is true, [[ adc =~ ^a[!b]c$ ]] is false.
findings.fix: Treat an unclosed [ as a literal, and translate a leading ! to ^.

findings.title: Delivery 17: kit template fix still exits 1 in silence on a file with no hole
findings.claim: Under pipefail grep's status 1 on a file with no ASCII hole ends the verb before the files after it are rewritten.
findings.evidence: kit template fix a.tpl b.tpl, a.tpl with no hole: no output, exit 1, b.tpl still holds <<name>>.
findings.fix: Use { grep … || true; } | wc -l.

findings.title: Delivery 20: lint:pinned still reads uses: by regex, so valid YAML spellings pass unpinned
findings.claim: A flow-style step, a quoted key, and a value on the next line are not seen, so an unpinned action passes the pinned check.
findings.evidence: Of five unpinned steps lint:pinned reports lines 4 and 9 only; '- {uses: actions/checkout@v4}', '- "uses": actions/setup-node@main', and a uses: with its value on the next line pass.
findings.fix: Read .jobs[].steps[].uses and jobs.*.uses through yaml:yq; keep the regex for the line number and comment.

findings.title: Delivery 21 and 22: removing an overriding package leaves its file, and a rendered template loses its mode
findings.claim: package:remove takes out only paths no remaining package delivers, so an overrider's content stays; render writes with printf >, so an executable template arrives 644.
findings.evidence: kit packages remove p2 prints '✅ packages: kit p1', a.txt still says 'from p2', kit check reports a finding; templates/repo/t.sh at 755 arrives -rw-r--r-- beside files/repo/f.sh at -rwxr-xr-x.
findings.fix: After a removal place again every path whose winning source changed; chmod +x a rendered file whose template is executable.

findings.title: Delivery 23: a cached YAML read is still keyed by the read's name and the path alone
findings.claim: The expression, the options, and the release are not in the entry's key, so with the loader running a release per clone, the first release that changes a reader's expression replays the old answer for an unchanged kit.yml for up to seven days.
findings.evidence: yaml:yq c.yml "value a" ".a" prints 1, and yaml:yq c.yml "value a" ".b" prints 1 again.
findings.fix: Add release:version and a digest of the expression and options to the entry's name.

findings.title: Delivery 24 and 27: kit uninstall leaves a one-byte kit.yml, and rewrites blank lines outside the region
findings.claim: grep --invert-match over an empty here-string sees one empty line, so a kit.yml that held only the declaration is not removed; region:strip's held flag survives leading blank lines and drops the trailing one.
findings.evidence: kit.yml of version and packages alone is 1 byte after kit uninstall; region:strip on a file opening with two blank lines drops both, adds a blank line after the first text line, and drops the trailing blank line.
findings.fix: Test [[ -z "${kept}" ]] first; in region:strip hold only the blank line directly before the directive.

findings.title: Delivery 19: bind_parts still drops the newline of a bound hole that stands alone on a line
findings.claim: check (through bind_parts) and unapply (through bind) disagree on a bound lines hole, so kit new file can make a file kit lint refuses. Latent: no shipped template has such a line.
findings.evidence:
For '# head
«name»
rest
', render({name:"foo.sh"}) then parts | bind_parts | match gives {"ok":false,"line":2}, and unapply gives {}, on jq 1.7.1 and 1.8.2.
findings.fix: In bind_parts a bound hole of kind lines becomes $bound[$h] + "\n".

findings.title: Delivery 28 and 29 (29 partly checked): headers and one message still disagree with the code
findings.claim: kit-hydrate says it writes .kit/manifest 'when it is missing' while every full run rewrites it, and the release-mismatch warning is on the full run only; the refusal for --kinds=a"b names --kind=, which does not exist; file.sh says every write goes through it and new:kind writes with >.
findings.evidence: kit new kind q --kinds='a"b' prints '❌ --kind=a"b: a kind's value cannot hold a double quote'. The other items of Delivery 29 were not re-checked.
findings.fix: Correct the two headers and the message (name the flag as typed).

findings.title: Flow 19: widths are still ${#text}, and a clip can still cut inside a character
findings.claim: flow:cell measures and slices by ${#text}: bytes under LC_ALL=C, code points under UTF-8, never display columns.
findings.evidence: Under LC_ALL=C, flow:cell of a Japanese title at width 11 prints bytes iconv -f UTF-8 rejects; under UTF-8 a cell of 10 holds ten CJK characters, 20 columns.
findings.fix: Measure display width, and never slice bytes.

findings.title: Flow 20: kit flow <stage> --text is still refused, and the usage lists two stages that are none
findings.claim: The page says a stage prints as text with --text, and the grammar refuses it; the usage still lists kit flow backlog and kit flow underway, which the verb answers are no stage.
findings.evidence: kit flow issues --text prints '❌ --text cannot be combined with issues'; kit flow backlog prints '❌ backlog is no stage of kit flow'.
findings.fix: Accept --text on a stage, and take the two lines out of the usage.

findings.title: Flow 21 and 22: the GitLab project path is still wrong for three remote spellings, and a branch is not encoded
findings.claim: The sed that makes the project path mishandles an scp-style remote with no user, a trailing slash, and a GitLab under a sub-path; source_branch=$1 goes into the query unencoded (Flow 22, plausible).
findings.evidence: The sed gives 'gitlab.com:group/proj' for gitlab.com:group/proj.git, 'group/proj/' for a trailing slash, and 'gitlab/group/proj' for https://example.com/gitlab/group/proj.git.
findings.fix: Take the path from forge:url-host's own parse, and encode the branch with jq's @uri.

findings.title: Flow 24 and 26: a read in flight still outlives forge:forget, and every GitLab failure names one remedy
findings.claim: forge:forget only removes the snapshots, so a read begun before a change writes its stale answer afterwards (read only). All 11 errors in gitlab.sh say 'run: glab auth status', and four calls of tracker/ado.sh fail with 2>/dev/null and no line (confirmed).
findings.evidence: forge.sh:902-906 is rm -f "${dir}"/*.json alone; grep -c 'glab auth status' gitlab.sh gives 11; ado.sh lines 26, 43, 49, 93 end in 2>/dev/null.
findings.fix: Stamp a generation the snapshot writer checks; tell a rate limit from a login in the GitLab provider as forge/github:limited does, and say why an ado write failed.

findings.title: Flow 25, 27, and 28 (28 partly fixed): a test, the catalog, and the conformance suite still miss the shape
findings.claim: A unit test pins a checks.failing the forge never gives; the builds event enum lists pull_request, which is never emitted; the conformance suite gained failed-read, paging, and fork-pipeline tests but has none for same-named checks, a close in another repository, or a first fetch, and never calls require or pr-set-body.
findings.evidence: tests/flow.bats:821 feeds "failing":2 and expects '❌ 2 failing 3 / 5'; grep -c of 'forge:require' and 'pr-set-body' in tests/forge-conformance.bats gives 0 each. The rest of Flow 27 was not re-checked.
findings.fix: Feed the test a check's name, drop pull_request from the enum, and add the three missing cases with the fixes of R1-1, R1-12, and R1-13.

areas.title: the earlier review: Serve, Command line, Components, Apps
areas.coverage: Read lines 726-1530 of the 11-10 findings and the page; opened the code each finding names. Ran kit serve, 20-odd kit scenarios with fake brew, mise, nix, uv, and nine throwaway Go tests in a copy under out/R2/work. macOS only; no network. Six plausible findings read, not reproduced.
areas.summary: Of the 113 earlier findings in Serve, Command line, Components, and Apps: 36 fixed, 56 open, 15 partly, 6 not rechecked (fixed/open/partly/not checked: Serve 20/5/2/0; Command line 4/19/2/3; Components 4/19/5/2; Apps 8/13/6/1). Serve, which had a plan, holds. Still open and high: the form's choice by ordinal panics (Components 1), a form runs in the wrong repository (Apps 3), welcome panics on page keys and runs a hidden fix (Apps 4, 5), `kit tools run` refuses dash-words (Command line 1), uv locks (Command line 3, 4), paste (Components 4). findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write as a report file, so this result is the only copy.
strengths: kit serve was rebuilt on the earlier findings and holds: an operand that is a word of the verb's syntax is refused offered or not (serve.jq:148-155), check, lint, toolchains, and tools say readOnlyHint false, nothing a client sent rides on a command line or in the environment, a NUL is refused at three depths, and a path is judged as the kernel and as a shell read it. Nineteen hostile request lines each got an answer, exit 0.
The workspace file's lock held 13 of 13 members under 12 parallel writers; `none` is reserved; a scalar file is refused; --workspace checks the file before it reads it; members are spelled one way.
kit tools install finds the dependency providers again after the toolchain installs, and fails, naming each, when a locked provider is still unusable (kit-tools:308-321).
No `... | grep --quiet` under pipefail is left in kit/ (Command line 5), and brew's reads fail loudly (Command line 8).

kittui decodes every load into fresh values (decoding[T], stage.decode), refuses a document of another shape, and keeps the document of a call that exits 1 (kit.partial): Apps 1, 2, and 22 are gone at the root, not patched.
The catalog now drives each tab's command, record, and key; every app's tab has a kit verb behind it; Schema.check refuses a catalog a table cannot index by.
grid.columnWidths measures a slice of rows once, and cost_test.go holds drawing, paging, and the wheel to a frame at 300, 700, and 10,000 rows.
kit flow's words now reach every app (screens.Taking), and ParseWords keeps only the words it knows, so --jq or a second stage name is no longer a filter.
The palette is a table now: its rows take clicks and the wheel, and a verb's long page scrolls with the rows (Components 10 for the palette, Components 16).

findings.title: Components 1, still open: a form's one-of choice is kept by the row's ordinal and lands on another row
findings.claim: Collect and walker.group still key a one-of row's choice by a running count, so a choice outlives its row. The earlier review rated it critical; it is a crash of the form or a command line nobody chose.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test over the shipped tools and packages grammars: second line, its last word, then the first line gives `answers map[0:0 1:3]` then `PANIC: index out of range [3] with length 2` (tools) and `[2] with length 2` (packages). Model.changed calls rebuild(Collect(m.fields)), the same path.
findings.fix: Key a choice by the group's path in the grammar, and drop the choices of rows that left.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced by keys on the shipped grammars: second line, inner row's last word, back to the first line panics in walker.group (fields.go:265), index out of range [3] with length 2 (tools), [2] (packages). Choosing `add` instead survives and puts `--inactive` on the packages line, which nobody chose. choose (fields.go:289-293) has no bounds check.

findings.title: Apps 3, still open: a form's command runs where kittui started, not in the repository the screens show
findings.claim: main keeps the runner it made at start and execs with it (Exec does os.Chdir(r.Dir)), while the root moves its own copy to the picked workspace's checkout; Help is never remade on a pick. After a workspace pick, commit, tidy, or work reads its choices in one repository and runs in another.
findings.evidence: `r := kit.New()` then `execKit(r, verb, args)`; `m.runner.Dir = msg.ws.Checkout` in screens.answered; `readsKitAlone` holds Help. Confirmed from the code, not driven end to end.
findings.fix: Carry the runner in the form's result, or let the root expose its runner, and exec with that.
findings.verdict_note: Driven end to end through run() with the fake kit: after a pick of repository b the title reads `kit help · - o/b · commit`, and execKit receives the runner with Dir = a, where kittui started. Same with Help made after the pick. main.go:55,75 never read the root's runner; screens exposes no accessor.

findings.title: Apps 4, still open: PgUp, PgDn, Home, and End panic on a welcome step whose search hides every check
findings.claim: page still indexes rows[min(max(at+n,0), len(rows)-1)] with no guard for no rows, and leaving the search sets inPane true unconditionally.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test: toolchains step, `/zzzz`, Enter gives `rows=0 inPane=true`; each of pgdown, pgup, home, end then prints `PANIC: runtime error: index out of range [-1]`.
findings.fix: Return from page when len(rows)==0, as down does, and give the pane the keyboard from the search only when it has rows.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: toolchains step, `/zzzz`, Enter gives rows=0, inPane=true, not gridded; pgdown, pgup, home, and end each panic `index out of range [-1]` at welcome.go:969. Down and up survive: down (welcome.go:948) guards the empty rows, page does not.

findings.title: Apps 5, still open: the run key runs the fix of a check the step does not show
findings.claim: find returns index 0 when the step has no rows, and fixUnder judges m.checks[m.cursor] without asking whether it is among the step's rows.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test with the first check made a failed one with a fix (set on the loaded model), every row hidden by a search, then `r`: `rows shown=0 fixUnder="bash" runsHere=true` and `kit ran: [[welcome --fix bash]]`.
findings.fix: Have fixUnder, keeping, and keep require slices.Contains(m.rows(m.step), m.cursor).
findings.verdict_note: Code path is real, but reproduced only with the model doctored. Every unshown-cursor fallback is index 0 (welcome.go:571), and kit's first check is always tool-bash (welcome.sh:517), which always holds with no fix (welcome.sh:372-375). With the shipped kit, `r` and `c` then do nothing. Latent, not high.

findings.title: Command line 1, still open: `kit tools run <command>` refuses a command that holds one of kit tools' own flags
findings.claim: opens still reads an alternative's first node only, and the run line still opens with the optional [--toolchain <name>], so run is never seen as the line's literal. The header says the command is taken as typed, dash-words included.
findings.evidence: `kit tools run echo --check .` prints `kit tools needs --outdated`; `kit tools run echo x --json` prints `unknown argument 'run'`; `kit tools run echo -h` prints kit's page; `kit syntax tools --match -- run prettier --check .` gives status 1, missing --outdated.
findings.fix: Let opens look past leading optional groups, and add a test with --check after run.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: `kit tools run echo --check .` gives `kit tools needs --outdated`, exit 2; --json, --jq, --outdated give `unknown argument 'run'`; -h/--help print kit's page. Unknown dash-words pass. Workaround: `kit tools run -- echo --check . --json -h` runs as typed; the header (kit-tools:38) promises it without `--`.

findings.title: Command line 3, still open: a uv.lock over the argument limit makes every kit tools call fail
findings.claim: The whole lock, as JSON, is still passed to jq as one --argjson argument.
findings.evidence: Fake uv and a generated lock of 1,411,808 bytes: `kit tools` prints `uv.sh: line 36: .../jq: Argument list too long` and `uv: the pinned tools could not be read`. Linux's 128 KiB cap per argument was not run.
findings.fix: Feed the lock on stdin or with --slurpfile.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced on macOS with a 1,411,808-byte lock: `kit tools`, `--outdated` and `--json` print `uv.sh: line 36: jq: Argument list too long`, exit 1, and welcome's uv check fails. But `kit tools install`, `update`, `path` and `run` succeed, so not "every call". A 137 KB lock lists fine on macOS; Linux's 128 KiB cap not run.

findings.title: Command line 4, still open: a package a platform marker excludes is expected in .venv
findings.claim: dependencies/uv:pins lists every package in the lock, and dependencies:installed fails on any that is not installed, so welcome's uv check never holds for a project that locks colorama or the like.
findings.evidence: Lock with click and colorama (marker sys_platform == 'win32'), fake uv listing click alone: `kit tools` draws `colorama 0.4.6` as missing, and `kit welcome --checks` says `uv has not installed every package uv.lock pins`, fix `kit tools install`.
findings.fix: Judge with `uv sync --frozen --check`, or compare only what uv resolves for this platform.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. A lock in uv's real shape (colorama its own [[package]], marker on click's dependency edge), only click installed: `kit tools` draws colorama 0.4.6 missing; `kit welcome --checks --json` gives dependencies-uv ok:false, fix `kit tools install`. uv.sh:39 filters only virtual and editable sources; dependencies.sh:134 fails on any difference.

findings.title: Components 4, still open: a paste types nothing in a form's field, the search, or a preset's name
findings.claim: Nothing handles tea.PasteMsg, and Bubble Tea v2.1.1 turns bracketed paste on unless the view disables it.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'PasteMsg\|DisableBracketedPaste' --include=*.go projects/tui` finds nothing outside tests; cursed_renderer.go:140 enables it; form.Model.Update has no paste case.
findings.fix: Take a paste as typed text in shell.Search and the form's text fields, and route it from every screen.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. A program fed ESC[200~hello ESC[201~ writes ESC[?2004h and delivers tea.PasteMsg, not key presses; form.Model.Update (model.go:131-150) has no case for it, and a focused text field's input stayed "q". Nothing in projects/tui names PasteMsg or DisableBracketedPasteMode; shell/view.go:16-18 leaves paste mode on; search takes KeyPressMsg only.

findings.title: Serve 6, still open: a tool's verb has no deadline, and notifications/cancelled is dropped
findings.claim: tools-call runs the verb in a synchronous subshell with no limit, and every notification returns at once, so one stalled verb blocks every later request, ping included.
findings.evidence: `run kit "${name}" "${words[@]}"` inside `( ... ) </dev/null`; grep for timeout, cancel, deadline over serve.sh, kit-serve, docs/serve.md finds nothing.
findings.fix: Run the verb under a deadline, answer isError when it passes, and end the verb on notifications/cancelled.

findings.title: Serve 15, still open: a credential in an argument is written to the log in full and kept 14 days
findings.claim: kit-call logs every argument as typed, so URL userinfo and --token= words rest in .kit/logs on the desk. The log is git-ignored, so it is a secret at rest, not one published.
findings.evidence: `kit workspaces --show=https://user:ghp_URLTOKEN@github.com/acme/a.git`, then `grep -c ghp_URLTOKEN .kit/logs/kit-*.log` prints 1 and the line holds the URL whole.
findings.fix: Redact URL userinfo and words shaped like --token=, and do not log what follows `kit tools run`.

findings.title: Command line 6, still open: `kit toolchains use brew` is refused where brew is the only project toolchain
findings.claim: The guard refuses whenever usable is non-empty and brew is usable, which holds when usable is brew alone; after `use ambient` there is no way back. The line still says `choose`, and the join still joins nothing.
findings.evidence: Scratch repository with a Brewfile and a fake brew: `kit toolchains use brew` prints `brew fills in for the tools brew does not pin; choose brew`, exit 1, before and after `kit toolchains use ambient`.
findings.fix: Refuse only when usable does not hold brew, and fix the words.

findings.title: Command line 7, still open: `kit toolchains use` reports success while an active toolchain overrides the choice
findings.claim: toolchain:choose never looks at the active toolchain, so the recorded choice is not the one kit uses.
findings.evidence: Fake mise and nix, mise.toml and flake.nix, MISE_SHELL=zsh: `kit toolchains use nix` prints `kit uses nix for the project`, exit 0, and `kit toolchains` then shows mise active and pinned.
findings.fix: Say that the active one wins until its shell is left, or refuse.

findings.title: Command line 9, still open: colour is decided by stderr and written to stdout
findings.claim: flow:paint follows out:sgr, which tests stderr, so piped stdout carries escapes when stderr is a terminal.
findings.evidence: Under `script`, `kit toolchains | cat -v` begins `^[[90mprovider ... chosen^[[0m` and `kit tools | cat -v` begins `^[[90m   name ... found^[[0m`; `kit welcome --checks | cat` was clean.
findings.fix: Writers to stdout test -t 1, as help:styled does.

findings.title: Command line 11, still open: a tool that does not answer --version is called not installed
findings.claim: welcome:version fails when `<tool> --version` exits non-zero, and welcome:tool calls that not installed; go and gofmt exit 2 for --version.
findings.evidence: Calling welcome:tool for go, with go on PATH, prints `"ok":false,"line":"go is not installed; kit lint runs it for go","fix":"brew install go"`.
findings.fix: Tell absent (command -v fails) from does not answer --version.

findings.title: Command line 12, still open: the kittui build's cache key leaves out the embedded files, and nothing prunes the cache
findings.claim: tui:cached digests *.go, go.mod, and go.sum only, while seven JSON files are now embedded with go:embed; an edit to one leaves kit running the stale kittui. It holds in a source checkout only.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn go:embed` lists fields.json, verbs.json, terms.json, customize.json, clones.json, workspaces.json, tutorials.json; the find in tui:cached names none of them.
findings.fix: Digest every file the build reads, and drop old builds.

findings.title: Command line 13, still open: --probe says yes whenever go is on PATH, and a failed build ends the verb
findings.claim: Each hand-off probes without building, then exits 1 when the build fails, where the headers promise text without a kittui. It holds in a source checkout only.
findings.evidence: `tui:binary --probe ... && binary=$(tui:binary) || exit 1` in four verbs and the guard. Read from the code; not run on a pty.
findings.fix: Fall back to text, or to the refusal, when the build fails.

findings.title: Command line 14, still open: `kit <verb> --help` on a terminal opens the palette, not the page
findings.claim: The guard execs kit-help with no --text, and kit-help with one name on a terminal opens kittui, while its header says --help prints the same page as kit help --text <verb>.
findings.evidence: `exec "${kit_root}/bin/kit-help" "${verb}"`. Read from the code; tests/help.bats runs without a terminal.
findings.fix: Exec kit-help --text "${verb}".

findings.title: Command line 15, still open: `kit new` dispatches on $1 though the guard takes options anywhere
findings.claim: An option before the literal sends the call to the file branch, and the shift drops it.
findings.evidence: `kit new --package=x kind foo` prints `no template governs foo`; `kit new --rule=bash file x.sh` prints the same for x.sh, the rule lost.
findings.fix: Dispatch on syntax_literals[0], and read the options from syntax_options.

findings.title: Command line 16, still open: a `--` the guard accepts reaches five verbs as a word
findings.claim: kinds, usage, help, linked, and completion read "$@" or $1 after the guard and treat -- as an argument.
findings.evidence: `kit kinds -- README.md` prints a row for `--`; `kit usage -- version` and `kit help --text -- x` print `unknown verb '--'`; `kit linked -- 5` prints `'--' is not a number`; `kit completion -- zsh` prints nothing, exit 0.
findings.fix: Read syntax_operands, or drop -- in the verb.

findings.title: Components 3, partly fixed: the tab menu is no longer quadratic and still costs 0.15 s a frame at 500 rows
findings.claim: columnWidths is now cached per slice of rows, but enabled still asks Folding and Changes for each fold line on every frame, so an open tab menu costs time linear in the rows.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, View with the menu open: 154-195 ms at 500 rows, 666-790 ms at 2,000, 1.24-1.29 s at 4,000 (was 0.9 s, 13.6 s, 54 s); one `<` takes 0.89 s at 2,000.
findings.fix: Cache the menu's enabled lines per outline and rows.

findings.title: Components 6, still open: groups sort without regard to case and headings are cut by exact value
findings.claim: ranked ends in natural, which calls Bug and bug equal, and same compares exactly, so the values interleave under repeated headings with one key.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, rows labelled Bug, bug, Bug, bug: headings `Bug 1`, `bug 1`, `Bug 1`, `bug 1`, each key twice.
findings.fix: Break the ties of natural by the exact text in the compare of group.

findings.title: Components 7, still open: with one column left, rows stay drawn under a closed heading
findings.claim: FoldAway, Parent, order, and group still tell a data row by len(r.Cells) > 1, and the card's Show line hides any column down to one.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test: grouped by one field, another hidden, one column left, a heading closed: FoldAway returns every row with folded=0, rows #2 and #4 under the closed heading.
findings.fix: Tell rows from asides by Row.Aside in these four places, as Filter already does.

findings.title: Components 8, still open: a level's fold is kept by depth, and nothing clears it when the groups change
findings.claim: LevelKey is still the depth, and neither flow.setPanel nor Sheet.SetPanel touches the outline, so a fold made on one grouping hides a level of the next.
findings.evidence: `func LevelKey(depth int) string { return "group\x01" + strconv.Itoa(depth) }`; setPanel sets View, rebuilds, clamps, fits, remembers. Confirmed by reading, not driven.
findings.fix: Key a level by its field's id, and the rows' level by a name of its own.

findings.title: Components 9, still open: a click right of the last tab selects it, or drops its menu
findings.claim: hit refuses only columns past the screen, not past the tabs, so any column after the last tab is the last tab.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, two tabs on 120 cells (tabs end at cell 31): `hit(100)=1 OnSelected(100,2)=true`.
findings.fix: Return -1 where at >= l.width.

findings.title: Components 10, partly fixed: the palette takes clicks and the wheel now; the form still takes neither
findings.claim: The form's click handles the app menu, the workspace menu, and the search only, and its Update has no wheel case, against the plain-clicks rule.
findings.evidence: The comment on click: `Anywhere else it does nothing`; grep finds MouseWheelMsg in palette, welcome, tutorials, flow, workspaces, and not in form.
findings.fix: Have Layout give each field's lines, so a click focuses and acts as space or enter.

findings.title: Components 11, still open: a column moves by shift and an arrow only, named on a menu's keys bar
findings.claim: Moving a column has no menu line and no click target, and its keys stand on the card's keys bar, against the rules for plain clicks and for a menu's keys bar.
findings.evidence: ShiftKeys binds `shell.Bind("⇧←→", "move", ...)`; the fields dialog moves on shift+up and shift+down only. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Add Move Left and Move Right lines with their keys at the right, and a click target in the dialog.

findings.title: Components 12, still open: the form's opens reads an alternative's first node only
findings.claim: A literal after leading optional groups selects nothing, so `kit tui tools run` opens the form on the first usage line with the word dropped.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, Answers{Literals: [run]} over the tools spec: `first row chosen=0 line=kit tools []`.
findings.fix: Skip optional nodes before the first required one, here and in syntax.jq.

findings.title: Components 13, still open: refreshExtension runs kit on the update loop
findings.claim: refreshExtension calls runner.Extend, a synchronous kit call with a 30 s limit, inside New and Update, so the screen stands still for a kit run.
findings.evidence: `order, args, err := m.runner.Extend(m.spec.Verb, answers)` at line 808, called from lines 98 and 359. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Make it a command and a message, as fetch and tryRun are.

findings.title: Components 18, still open: a long search loses its caret, and the menu bar is one cell too wide
findings.claim: Line cuts the search at its end with pane.Clip, and with SearchAt at 0 the line is two cells plus width-1.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, 50 characters typed on 40 cells: `cells=41 has caret=false ends="ghijabcde…"`.
findings.fix: Use pane.Tail, and count the two cells.

findings.title: Apps 7, partly fixed: Add to Pull Request… works in Flow and can never be enabled in Issues
findings.claim: mine() reads the changes stage of this screen; Flow now has one, and the Issues app's stages are issues, milestones, and iterations, so there the line is dim for good.
findings.evidence: `if s.name != "changes" { continue }` in mine(); apps lists `{shell.Issues, "issues", []string{issuesStage, "issues/milestones", "issues/iterations"}}`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Read the caller's pull requests from kit, or omit the line where the app has no changes stage.

findings.title: Apps 8, still open: an issue's and a change's link is guessed from origin
findings.claim: kit prints no url for an issue or an open change, so kittui builds it from the remote named origin, its last two path segments, in GitLab's shape only where the host's name holds gitlab.
findings.evidence: `page := m.originOf(p.Member).pull(p.Number, "")`; forge.jq's issue and document have no url; ReadOrigin runs `git remote get-url origin`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Have kit print each row's page, as builds and kit workspace's links do, and stop building URLs in Go.

findings.title: Apps 10, still open: a jump to a row that a closed group or a filter hides lands nowhere, without a word
findings.claim: land searches the rows after FoldAway and the panel, and clears the landing once the stage has loaded, so the cursor stays where it was and nothing is said.
findings.evidence: `slices.IndexFunc(m.rows(i), func(r row) bool { return r.Key == key })`, then `m.landing = ""`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Search grid.Every, open the headings over the row, and say so in the notice where the panel hides it.

findings.title: Apps 11, still open: a reload keeps the cursor's index, not its row
findings.claim: take decodes, rebuilds, and clamps; nothing remembers the cursor's key, so after a reload space or an action acts on another row, and watched stages reload by themselves.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test: `cursor on "#3" before the reload, on "#2" after it (index 3)` once one more issue sorts in above.
findings.fix: Remember the cursor's key before the decode and find it after, as welcome's take does.

findings.title: Apps 12, still open: a refresh does not end a stage's first load
findings.claim: The first read runs in the screen's context with no cancel of its own, and Again ends a read only where stop is set, so R during incoming's first fetch starts a second fetch beside it.
findings.evidence: The struct's comment: `ctx ... nil for the first, which has the screen's`; `if l.stop != nil { l.stop() }`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Give NewLoad's first read a cancellable context too.

findings.title: Apps 13, still open: opening an app runs kit on the update loop, and one verb's refusal closes the app
findings.claim: screens.show calls flow.OpenApp, which runs `<verb> --stages` synchronously (30 s each) and returns an error on the first refusal, so Repositories does not open where kit flow --stages refuses.
findings.evidence: `names, err := r.StagesOf(verb); if err != nil { return Model{}, err }` inside OpenApp, called from Update. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Open at once with the stages loading as a source; a verb that refuses costs its own tabs.

findings.title: Apps 17, partly fixed: the catalog now drives the read, and no test holds kittui's fixtures to what kit prints
findings.claim: stage.decode now reads by the catalog's record and key, but the 42 JSON fixtures under flow/testdata are checked against nothing kit prints, so a renamed field keeps the tests green and blanks a column.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'projects/tui/internal' tests bin` names the syntax fixtures only.
findings.fix: Add a bats test that prints each stage in a fixture repository and compares its keys with the fixture's and the catalog's paths.

findings.title: Apps 18, still open: three actions in flow have one way in
findings.claim: A kittui: link is followed by a click only, the legend opens by ? or F1 only, and one row is selected by space only. The tutorials part was not rechecked.
findings.evidence: jump is called from click and JumpMsg alone; `case "?", "f1"`; SelectItems gives Select All and Clear Selection. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Give each a key, a menu line, and a click.

findings.title: Serve 14, still open: a long log line is appended in several writes, so parallel calls interleave
findings.claim: log:write appends the whole line with one printf, which the system splits for a long line.
findings.evidence: Thirty parallel `kit version <40,000 characters>` calls left 30 lines, 3 of them malformed.
findings.fix: Cut the logged command line below one write's size.

findings.title: Serve 16, partly fixed: some invalid requests are still not refused with -32600
findings.claim: Arrays, scalars, and a non-object params are refused now; a non-string method, a wrong jsonrpc, a second object on a line, the id 1e3, an object with no method, and batches are not handled as the protocol says.
findings.evidence: One run: `"method":123` gets `-32601 Method not found: `; `{"a":1}` gets silence; `"jsonrpc":"1.0"` is served; id 9 on a shared line is unanswered; `1e3` returns as `1E+3`; a batch gets -32600.
findings.fix: Refuse a non-string method and a wrong jsonrpc with -32600, and answer each value on a line.

findings.title: Serve 17, still open: no resources/templates/list, and a missing resource is -32602
findings.claim: The server declares resources whose URIs are templates and answers no template list, and names a missing resource with another code than the revisions through 2025-11-25.
findings.evidence: `resources/templates/list` answers `-32601 Method not found`; `kit://nope` answers `-32602 Resource not found`.
findings.fix: Answer an empty template list, and pick the code by the revision.

findings.title: Serve 24, partly fixed: the reload still misses a deleted file and a line that holds "initialize"
findings.claim: The scratch directory is now removed before the exec; a deletion is still never seen, and list_changed is still withheld from any pending line containing the text "initialize".
findings.evidence: `find "${dirs[@]}" -type f -newer "${serve_marker}"`; `[[ "${pending}" != *'"initialize"'* ]]`.
findings.fix: Compare a listing as well as the times, and read the method with jq.

findings.title: Serve 25, still open: the tool list is hand-kept, and no test snapshots the tools' schemas
findings.claim: serve_tools is an array in the module and tests assert single properties of five tools; the syntax snapshots cover 40 of 52 verbs.
findings.evidence: No snapshot for assign, close, facts, gather, ready, settle, trust, tutorials, unassign, uninstall, workspace, workspaces (comm of kit/bin against syntax/testdata).
findings.fix: Snapshot tools/list and every verb's kit syntax, as the Contracts plan (#74) says.

findings.title: Command line 10, partly fixed: the remedy for a missing jq no longer assumes mise; welcome's jq check cannot fail
findings.claim: guard:remedy now names the system toolchain's command, but kit welcome still requires jq in the guard before any check runs, so welcome:jq's not-installed branch is unreachable.
findings.evidence: `guard:require tool:jq || return 2` in guard:arguments, which kit-welcome calls first. Read from the code; running kit without jq would settle it.
findings.fix: Let welcome run its jq check before the guard's requirement.

findings.title: Command line 18, still open: `kit new issue --jq` is refused
findings.claim: The issue line takes --json and not --jq, unlike every other verb with --json.
findings.evidence: `kit new issue --jq` prints `--jq cannot be combined with issue`.
findings.fix: Add --jq to the line.

findings.title: Command line 19, still open: a refusal names the same flag twice
findings.claim: The refusal takes the first key each alternative holds, which may be the same key.
findings.evidence: `kit workspaces --current --add=x --json` prints `--json cannot be combined with --json`.
findings.fix: Name a key the other alternative lacks.

findings.title: Command line 20, still open: `kit syntax <verb> --match` skips the closed choices the guard applies
findings.claim: syntax:judge does not call syntax:closed, so a form can be told a command line is complete that kit then refuses.
findings.evidence: `kit syntax tutorials --match -- --tag=nosuch` gives status 0; `kit tutorials --tag=nosuch` exits 2 with `--tag 'nosuch' is not one of the choices`.
findings.fix: Have syntax:judge call syntax:closed.

findings.title: Command line 21, still open: completion ignores the usage line the words chose
findings.claim: Flags and literals are offered from every usage line, and enumerated values are not offered.
findings.evidence: `kit completion candidates -- flow issues -` offers --marks, --me, --quota, --stages, --capabilities, each refused with issues; `tools --json ''` offers install; `toolchains use ''` offers nothing.

findings.title: Command line 22, partly fixed: an option's value is written two ways across the verbs
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-assign:5, kit/bin/kit-commit:5, kit/bin/kit-gather:5, kit/bin/kit-close:5, kit/bin/kit-work:6-7, kit/bin/kit-tools:5-6, kit/bin/kit-welcome:7, kit/bin/kit-syntax:6
findings.claim: workspaces, flow, new, and tutorials take --option=value; eight headers still write --option <value>, which the page leaves to #160, and the refusal does not name the form.
findings.evidence: `kit flow --owner alice` prints `--owner needs a value`, while `kit tools --toolchain mise` and `--toolchain=mise` both work.
findings.fix: Finish #160, or have the refusal say write --owner=alice.

findings.title: Command line 24, still open: bare `kit` without a terminal exits 2
findings.claim: kit with no verb does not fall back to text, where kit help, kit flow, and kit welcome do.
findings.evidence: `kit </dev/null` prints `kit tui needs an interactive terminal; run: ... kit help tui`, exit 2.
findings.fix: Print kit welcome --text, as bare kit opens the welcome guide on a terminal.

findings.title: Command line 25, still open: `kit toolchains use ambient` outside a repository fails in git's words
findings.claim: toolchain:kept lets git's own error through, and a recorded ambient shows on no row.
findings.evidence: Outside a repository: `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git`, exit 1; after `use ambient` no row of kit toolchains has the pin.
findings.fix: Refuse in kit's words, and draw an ambient row.

findings.title: Command line 26, still open: `kit tools update` says mise rewrote the pins
findings.claim: mise upgrade without --bump never rewrites mise.toml, and toolchain/mise:file names mise.toml where only mise.local.toml is there.
findings.evidence: `mise upgrade --quiet`; `ok "${name} moved every tool to its latest; commit the pins and the lock it rewrote"`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Say what mise does, or pass --bump.

findings.title: Components 15, partly fixed: ReadCatalog checks renderings and presets, not that a rendering is registered
findings.claim: Schema.check refuses a field with no rendering and fields with no preset; Draw still calls a nil func for a rendering no one registered.
findings.evidence: `out := renderers[rendering](f, vs)`; Registered has no caller outside tests. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Call Registered in check.

findings.title: Components 17, still open: the form's emitter writes a literal inside [ ] with no answer beside it
findings.claim: A literal is written wherever the walk goes; no shipped grammar has the shape. The dash-value half is settled: kit reads `--title --force` as the title.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test over `a [file <path>]` with no path: `kit x [a file]`; `kit syntax work --match -- --title --force` gives status 0, title --force.
findings.fix: Write a literal inside [ ] only with an answer beside it.

findings.title: Components 19 and Apps 21, still open: circled glyphs are on the screen
findings.claim: The radio, the filter mark, and the tabs' numbers are still circled glyphs, against the no-circled-glyphs rule, and a golden pins three of them.
findings.evidence: `Unpicked = "⦾"`, `Picked = "⦿"`, `const Filtered = "⊘"`, Marker gives ➀ and ➊; flow/testdata/popover.golden holds ⦾ ⦿ ⊘.
findings.fix: The owner's call per glyph; ⊘ and ⦾ ⦿ are the likely misses.

findings.title: Components 20, still open: a click on a menu's border closes it, and on a dialog's does nothing
findings.claim: The two overlays read a click on their own border differently.
findings.evidence: ClickIn closes unless `x > left && x < left+width-1` on a body line; Placed.Hit answers -1, true on an edge. Confirmed by reading.

findings.title: Components 22, still open: a label over 16 cells is not clipped in the fields dialog
findings.claim: pane.Pad leaves a wider text as it is, so the cells after a long label stand right of where a click is read; no shipped label is that long.
findings.evidence: `pane.Pad(label, LabelCells, false)`; Pad: `A text as wide or wider is left as it is`. Confirmed by reading.
findings.fix: Clip the label.

findings.title: Components 23, still open: the form writes key hints under its fields
findings.claim: ctrl-n is named in a hint under the field and nowhere on the keys bar, against shell's rule that a screen never writes its hints.
findings.evidence: `m.hint(b, indent, glyphs+"⏎ takes it · ctrl-n takes what is typed · type to filter")`. Confirmed by reading.

findings.title: Components 25, still open: the keys bar says 1-9 and never names 0 for the tenth tab
findings.claim: number takes 0 for the tenth tab and the keys bar stops at 9. The StaleAt half was not rechecked.
findings.evidence: `fmt.Sprintf("1-%d", min(len(b.Tabs), 9))`; `case key == "0": return 9, true`.
findings.fix: Name 0 where there are ten tabs.

findings.title: Components 26, still open: natural misorders negative and fractional numbers
findings.claim: A sign is a rune like any other and each run of digits is a whole number, so -5 sorts before -10 and 1.5 before 1.25; no shipped number field is either.
findings.evidence: The code is unchanged from the earlier finding. Confirmed by reading.

areas.title: the earlier review: Infrastructure, Documents, Gaps
areas.coverage: Read whole: findings lines 1531-2099, the review page, bin/release, bin/ci, bin/tutorials, workflows, CI template, tutorials site sources. Read in part: documents and modules each finding names. Ran in throwaway copies: release pack, kit check (jq 1.7.1 and 1.8.2), many verbs, the whole bats suite (1,261 tests). Not checked: forge, network, npm, go test, most Gaps spec rows.
areas.summary: Of the 61 numbered findings in Infrastructure and Documents, 8 are fixed, 9 partly fixed, and 44 open. The release still cannot ship: `bin/release pack` writes a `.sha256` with no digest and exits 0 (reproduced); jq 1.7.1 still fails `kit check`; `kit tools run … --check` is still refused; the uv defects stand. The bats suite is still red, on a new test: the forge seam's header lists six bot calls the provider template lacks. None of the nine tasks of the release-readiness plan is built. Fixed: the tutorials site's build checks, the runner's base for `kit policy`, `kit lint` on a missing path, `kit tools install` ordering, and kittui's placeholder tabs. Full report: out/R3/findings.md
strengths: Fail closed holds where run: `kit lint nosuch.sh` exits 2 (Documents 7), and on a runner the base of a change is the commit the event names (policy:runner-base), which fixes Infrastructure 5.

The tutorials site's build now verifies itself: src/build.ts walks every route and resolves every href and src, siteBase normalises the base, an empty page throws, a pre-release meets its own version, and there is a not-found route and 404.html (Infrastructure 16-19, 32).
Nine tutorials ship in the kit as markdown and open with no network; keep that split.
`kit tools install` finds the dependency providers again after the toolchain installs and fails on an unusable locked provider (kit/bin/kit-tools:308-321, Command line 2).
Every kittui app has a kit verb behind it with --stages (issues, changes, delivery, people, audit, platform, packages, workspace); no tab is a placeholder.
kit serve's three groups of tools are stated the same way in 1st.md, the README, the Claude page, and the verb's header (Documents 1).
`#!/bin/sh` is its own kind with its own rule and is no longer linted as bash.
bin/ci's header lists every step, and coverage is every statement per function, not a rounded 98% floor.
helper:isolate pins TZ, the locale, trust, and git's global configuration; the delivered workflow checks the tarball's digest before unpacking. Of 1,261 bats tests, one fails for a real reason.

findings.title: Infrastructure 1: bin/release pack still writes a .sha256 with no digest, and exits 0
findings.claim: pack calls release:digest, which no module defines (the function is file:digest), so the published .sha256 holds no digest and every consumer's checksum step and kit update would refuse the release. Known since 11-10, still open; task 1 of the release-readiness plan, of which no task is built.
findings.evidence: In a copy, `bin/release pack release/9.9.9-rc.1` printed `release:digest: command not found`, then `✅ packed`, exit 0; the .sha256 is 24 bytes of spaces and file name, and `shasum -a 256 --check` says no properly formatted checksum lines, exit 1.
findings.fix: Call file:digest, fail on an empty digest, and assert 64 hex digits in tests/release.bats.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with the suite's fake go: `release:digest: command not found`, then `packed`, exit 0. The .sha256 is 24 bytes, two spaces and the name; `shasum -a 256 --check` exits 1. Only bin/release:116 names release:digest. tests/release.bats:59 greps only the file name. release.sh:125 and kit-ci.yml:94 would refuse it.

findings.title: Infrastructure 2 (changed): the suite still fails at this commit, on another test
findings.claim: tests/underway.bats is gone, but the gate is still red: the forge seam's header lists bot-app, bot-installation, bot-installations, bot-token, bot-repositories, and bot-revoke among the calls every provider implements, and the forge-provider template has none of them.
findings.evidence: Whole suite: 1,248 ok, 13 not ok of 1,261. Ten passed after `kit hydrate`, two need markdownlint-cli2 which I lacked, and tests/template.bats:281 fails alone too, printing the header's and the template's lists.
findings.fix: Add the six calls to kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/templates/bash/forge-provider, or mark them in the header as calls a provider may implement.
findings.verdict_note: tests/template.bats "each seam's header lists the calls" fails alone, at line 291: forge.sh:175-185 lists six bot-* calls, the forge-provider template has none; only forge/github.sh:1423-1473 defines them. bin/ci:75 runs all of tests/. Snapshot matches commit 0e76266c. The whole-suite count (1,248/13) was not run again.

findings.title: Delivery 6: on jq 1.7.1, kit check still fails a file that passes on jq 1.8
findings.claim: template.jq still mixes `indices` (bytes before jq 1.8) with code-point slices, and the three places that state the minimum still say jq 1.7, which is what macOS ships. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Fresh repository after `kit install agents/generic`: `kit check` passes with jq 1.8.2; with /usr/bin/jq (jq-1.7.1-apple) first on PATH it prints `❌ AGENTS.md does not have the shape of the agents/generic package's host template; it leaves AGENTS.md at line 4`.
findings.fix: Find the literal on code points, or require jq 1.8 in syntax.sh, welcome.sh, and docs/install.md.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: fresh repository after `kit install agents/generic`, `kit check` passes with jq 1.8.2, and with /usr/bin/jq (jq-1.7.1-apple) first on PATH prints the claimed AGENTS.md line 4 refusal. syntax.sh:335, docs/install.md:76, and welcome.sh:386-388 still say 1.7.

findings.title: Command line 1: kit tools run still refuses a command that holds one of kit tools' own flags
findings.claim: The second usage line still opens with the optional [--toolchain <name>], so the literal `run` does not select it and the command's own flags are read as kit tools'. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: `kit tools run echo --check .` prints `❌ kit tools needs --outdated`, exit 2; `kit tools run echo hi --outdated` prints `❌ unknown argument 'run'`; `kit syntax tools --match -- run prettier --check .` gives status 1, missing --outdated.
findings.fix: Let the matcher look past leading optional groups for the literal that opens an alternative, and add a test.
findings.verdict_note: All three outputs reproduced as quoted; --json after the command fails the same way. Moving [--toolchain <name>] after the group in a copy's usage line made both commands run, so the stated cause holds. Not said by the reviewer: `kit tools run -- echo --check .` works at this commit.

findings.title: Command line 3 and 4: the uv provider still passes the whole lock as one argument, and expects every package
findings.claim: dependencies/uv:pins still gives uv.lock as JSON to jq with --argjson, which fails over ARG_MAX, and still lists every locked package, so one a platform marker excludes is never satisfied. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: Code read, unchanged from what the earlier review reproduced: `jq --null-input --raw-output --argjson lock "${lock}"` at uv.sh:36 and the select at line 39 that drops only virtual and editable sources. Not run again.
findings.fix: Feed the lock on stdin or with --slurpfile, and judge against what uv resolves for this platform.
findings.verdict_note: Both halves reproduced with a stand-in uv. A 1.37 MB lock: `uv.sh: line 36: jq: Argument list too long`, pins status 126. A lock with colorama behind a win32 marker, only click installed: pins shows colorama uninstalled, dependencies:installed returns 1. Its one caller is welcome.sh:319. The argument is at line 36, not 33.

findings.title: Infrastructure 4, Documents 6: the README's brew install line, and nothing writes a formula
findings.claim: `brew install empowerite/tap/kit` is still the first install line, and nothing in bin/release or the release workflow writes a formula. Known since 11-10, still open in the tree.
findings.evidence: README.md:78 holds the line; a search of bin/ and .github/ for tap, formula, or brew finds nothing. I could not ask GitHub whether the tap is still empty: `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents` settles it.
findings.fix: Publish the formula from the release, or drop the line until it exists.
findings.verdict_note: README.md:78 and docs/install.md:20 hold the line; bin/ and .github/ carry no tap, formula, or brew step. But the plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-release-readiness.md:29, :341) puts the formula in the tap's own repository, so its absence here is by design. Whether the tap is empty today needs `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents`; not asked.

findings.title: Documents 2 and 9: kit lint is still not one of kit ci's four checks, and the documents imply it
findings.claim: kit ci runs linked, policy, gate, and check only, so a consumer whose gate does not call kit lint has no CI check of pinned actions or file shape, and the documents still list the linters under the four checks. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: kit/bin/kit-ci:33 `for verb in linked policy gate check`; docs/features.md:44 "The four checks are fixed. What each one runs…" followed by rows for the linters, `pinned`, and the templates; "What no check covers" names one gap.
findings.fix: Say where kit lint runs in both tables and in "What no check covers", or make lint a fifth check of kit ci.
findings.verdict_note: kit/bin/kit-ci:33 runs four verbs; the delivered github/ci package never names lint; docs/features.md:44-51 lists linters, `pinned`, templates under "what each one runs". Narrower than high: features.md:41 says lint runs "before a commit", README.md:27 lists it apart from kit ci, and kit commit refuses on it (kit/modules/bash/commit.sh:278). No document says CI skips it.

findings.title: Infrastructure 3, Documents 5 (partly fixed): the tutorials site is still published nowhere
findings.claim: Nine of ten tutorials now ship in the kit and need no network, but the tenth still links to a GitHub Pages site that no workflow builds or deploys, and two documents describe the site as published.
findings.evidence: `kit tutorials --json` gives {"kit":9,"online":1}; `kit tutorials --text` prints https://empowerite.github.io/kit/tutorials/main/kit-tutorials/?kit=unreleased; .github/workflows/ holds kit-ci, release, and retire-pre-releases only. The address was not fetched.
findings.fix: Build the Tutorials 2 plan, or ship the tenth page in the kit and have the documents say the site is not published yet.

findings.title: Infrastructure 7: pack still copies the working tree, and publish still checks no tag
findings.claim: pack copies kit/ with cp -R, so uncommitted edits and stray files ship, and gh release create has no --verify-tag, so an unpushed tag is made at the default branch's head. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: bin/release:107 `cp -R "${kit_root}/bin" "${kit_root}/libexec" …`; bin/release:138 `gh release create "${tag}" …` with --title, --notes, and --prerelease only. Read, not run again.
findings.fix: Pack from `git archive <tag>`, and pass --verify-tag.

findings.title: Infrastructure 8: retiring still deletes the pre-releases that consumers pin
findings.claim: retire deletes every pre-release whose commit no remote branch reaches, so merging this branch without a merge commit and deleting it retires each pre-release tagged on it, and a consumer pinned to one gets a 404. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: The loop at bin/release:151-168 and the README's rule at line 333 are unchanged.
findings.fix: Keep a pre-release until a later release exists, or keep its assets.

findings.title: Infrastructure 9: a release still has no signature and no attestation
findings.claim: The release workflow verifies with the tagged commit's own script and publishes a .sha256 from the same release, which proves transport only. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: release.yml's steps are checkout, trust, cache, tools, verify, publish; no attest step. Whether a ruleset now guards release/* tags was not checked (needs the forge).
findings.fix: Add actions/attest-build-provenance, run verify from the default branch's script, and guard release/* tags with a ruleset.

findings.title: Infrastructure 6: a Dependabot bump of kit-ci.yml still fails kit check
findings.claim: Dependabot bumps the installed .github/workflows/kit-ci.yml and never the template, so its pull request always fails kit check, here and in every consumer that runs Dependabot on actions. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: In a hydrated copy `kit check` passed; after changing the SHA of jdx/mise-action in kit-ci.yml it printed `❌ .github/workflows/kit-ci.yml differs from the pinned release; run: kit update`.
findings.fix: Ignore kit-ci.yml in Dependabot and move the template's pins by release, or have kit check accept a newer pin of the same action.

findings.title: Infrastructure 11: the Claude deny list still misses forms of the commands 1st.md forbids
findings.claim: The deny list is the same 13 `Bash(git <words> *)` entries, which by Claude Code's documented matching do not match `git -C x commit`, `bash -c 'git push'`, `git checkout -B`, `git switch --create`, and others. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: settings.json lines 4-16 unchanged; docs/architecture.md:248 says the deny list prevents the commands. Matching is from the documentation, not executed.
findings.fix: Widen the list and call it best effort, or refuse in a PreToolUse hook that parses the command.

findings.title: Infrastructure 13: a test still runs the gh on PATH, and passes whatever it answers
findings.claim: Three tests reach whatever gh is on PATH; on a runner GH_TOKEN is set, so they reach github.com, and they pass when gh fails. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: With a logging gh that exits 1 first on PATH, tests/across.bats:495 made 24 calls (api rate_limit, api user, issue list, repo view, api --include …) and passed; two tests of tests/platform.bats called `gh api user --jq .login` once each.
findings.fix: Give those tests a fake gh, and fail the suite when a test reaches a forge tool no test put there.

findings.title: Infrastructure 12: helper:isolate still leaves git's and the forge's variables set
findings.claim: helper:isolate-in still unsets none of GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_AUTHOR_*, GH_TOKEN, KIT_BASE, IN_NIX_SHELL, CODESPACES, or DOCKER_HOST, so a caller's environment reaches the tests. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: A search of tests/helper.bash for each name finds nothing. Read, not run again.
findings.fix: Unset what `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` lists, and the rest.

findings.title: Infrastructure 14 and 31: assertions that cannot fail are still in the suite
findings.claim: Eleven `[ a ] && [ b ]` lines stand mid-test where a false left side fails nothing, 39 `run ! grep` lines pass on a missing file, and several `run pty` calls are followed by a negative match only. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: A scratch bats file with `[ 1 -eq 2 ] && [ 1 -eq 1 ]; true` and `run ! grep -q x /nonexistent/file` reports both ok. The eleven lines are listed in findings.md.
findings.fix: One assertion a line, and assert the status after each run pty.

findings.title: Infrastructure 15: the owner and the name still go to gh api graphql with --field
findings.claim: Eleven calls now pass `--field owner=… --field name=…`, which gh types as Int when the value is all digits, so a repository named 2048 fails every GraphQL read. Known since 11-10, still open, and in three more places.
findings.evidence: Lines 106, 188, 305, 458, 557, 648, 893, 1081, 1089, 1143, 1187 of forge/github.sh. From the code and gh's documented typing; the fake gh answers any arguments.
findings.fix: Use --raw-field for owner and name.

findings.title: Infrastructure 10: Settle still runs on pull_request: closed
findings.claim: A fork's or Dependabot's pull request gets a read-only token and no secrets on pull_request, so kit settle cannot comment or unassign. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: The trigger (line 27) and the Settle job (line 128) are unchanged. From GitHub's documented behaviour, not run.
findings.fix: Run Settle on pull_request_target with the base's checkout.

findings.title: Documents 3: "kit flow <stage> prints one stage" is still wrong on a terminal, and --text is refused
findings.claim: Three documents say the stage form prints and that --text prints; with a stage, --text is refused, and on a terminal the stage form opens kittui. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: `kit flow desk --text` prints `❌ --text cannot be combined with desk`; docs/features.md:252 says the stage form opens Flow on that stage.

findings.title: Documents 8: "the gate ran with the pinned tools … in CI" against the delivered default, ambient
findings.claim: The row of "What verifies what" is unchanged, while the package's default is still ci_toolchain: ambient, where nothing is pinned or installed. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: docs/architecture.md:242 and package.yml:11 `ci_toolchain: ambient`.

findings.title: Documents 10 and 25: three diagrams still say what the code does not do

findings.title: Documents 11: the header of kit linked still says an issue counts only when it is this repository's

findings.title: Documents 12 (partly fixed): projects/tui/README.md still opens on six screens, with an example that fails

findings.title: Components 10, 11, 19, and Apps 18: kittui still breaks three of the owner's rules
