findings.title: Infrastructure 20: retire still pipes git branch into grep --quiet under pipefail
findings.claim: When grep exits at its first match while git still writes, git dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline is false, and a pre-release that branches reach is deleted. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: bin/release:160 `git branch --remotes --contains "${commit}" | grep --quiet --invert-match 'origin/HEAD'` is unchanged; the earlier review saw it at 2,500 branches.
findings.fix: Capture the list first, then match it.

findings.title: Infrastructure 21 (partly fixed): two templates still make files the linters refuse
findings.claim: kit new file on a provider's path makes a file with a blank first line and no purpose that kit lint refuses at once, and the workflow template makes empty on:, permissions:, and jobs: that actionlint refuses. kit new provider's remedy is now clean.
findings.evidence: In a consumer: `kit new file modules/bash/forge/x.sh --purpose=…` then `kit lint` gives "does not have the shape of the bash template (script, module)"; the new workflow fails actionlint on the empty jobs section.
findings.fix: Give the provider templates the module's banner, and have the workflow template take its trigger and first job as holes.

findings.title: Infrastructure 22 (partly fixed): the kinds still misclassify common files
findings.claim: #!/bin/sh is now its own kind, but Justfile, .justfile, .bats files, .envrc, and `#!/usr/bin/env -S bash` scripts still have no kind, a nested workflows path is a workflow, and action.yml is not.
findings.evidence: `kit kinds` gives `any` alone for Justfile, .justfile, tests/kit.bats, .envrc, and the env -S script; `.github/workflows/sub/y.yml` is `workflows`; `action.yml` is `any text yaml`.
findings.fix: Add the names and the shebang form, hold the workflows glob to one level, and give action.yml the pinned check.

findings.title: Infrastructure 23: the Claude hook still says a file outside the repository is governed by its rules
findings.claim: context:claude keeps an outside path absolute and matches the kinds' globs against it, and the hook's matcher is still unanchored. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: `echo '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"/tmp/elsewhere/x.sh"}}' | kit context --claude` answers that /private/tmp/elsewhere/x.sh is governed by .kit/rules/bash.md and three styles.
findings.fix: Answer nothing for a path not under the root, and anchor the matcher.

findings.title: Infrastructure 24: the Cursor and Copilot rule files are still hand copies of the kinds' globs
findings.claim: Each per-rule file carries its kind's globs by hand and names the rule only; a test now holds kit's own copies to its kinds, but a kind a repository changes or adds still leaves them stale.
findings.evidence: kit-just.mdc `globs: justfile,**/justfile,**/*.just`; tests/agents.bats:43-59 compares the shipped files with the shipped kinds.
findings.fix: Generate the files from the kinds at install.

findings.title: Infrastructure 28: the six gaps in the infrastructure are still there
findings.claim: Dependabot watches actions only (not projects/tui/go.mod or the site's npm), kit-ci.yml has no concurrency or merge_group, the release jobs have no timeout, the gate never cross-compiles kittui, a pre-release publishes without the gate, and zsh completion is skipped without zsh.
findings.evidence: Read from the three workflows, dependabot.yml, bin/ci, and tests/completion.bats:61.
findings.fix: Add the two ecosystems or say why not, add concurrency, merge_group, and timeouts, and build the four platforms in the gate.

findings.title: Infrastructure 29, Documents 22: ajv still never validates the house package
findings.claim: The gate's globs cover kit/packages/ only, so .kit/packages/house/package.yml and its style's frontmatter are unchecked while bin/ci and docs/packages.md say every. Known since 11-10, still open.
findings.evidence: bin/ci:28-29 and 34 globs; .kit/packages/house/package.yml and styles/house.md exist in the snapshot.
findings.fix: Add the two globs.

findings.title: Infrastructure 30: bin/tutorials catalogue still takes pages it should refuse
findings.claim: A page with top: "true" counts, an id may hold a space, and a page with no front matter is skipped with exit 0 after a jq error. Known since 11-10, still open; the gate's ajv check catches the first for kit's own pages.
findings.evidence: With fixtures, the catalogue lists `id: My Page`, `path: My Page/`, and prints `jq: error … Cannot index string with string ("top")`, exit 0.
findings.fix: Compare `.top == true` in jq, hold the id to a slug, and refuse a page with no front matter.

findings.title: Documents 15: the jq module table lists 11 of 17 modules
findings.claim: apps.jq, glyphs.jq, serve.jq, terminal.jq, version.jq, and workspace.jq are missing from the table; the earlier review counted four missing of 14.
findings.evidence: `ls kit/modules/jq/*.jq` gives 17; the table at docs/modules.md:253-263 has 11 rows.
findings.fix: Generate the table from the modules' first lines.

findings.title: Documents 16: 1st.md still names 11 workflow commands, and kit help lists 20
findings.claim: 1st.md tells agents to run eleven named commands "and in no other way", while 20 verbs are in the workflow group and five of the eleven are in other groups.
findings.evidence: 1st.md:129-132 against `grep '(kit verb: workflow)' kit/bin/*`, 20 hits including assign, close, gather, settle, release.
findings.fix: State the rule for which commands an agent may run instead of a list that drifts.

findings.title: Documents 17 and 29: two samples in the documents are still not the text of any shipped file
findings.claim: The sample AGENTS.md region is one sentence where the real region is a heading and two sentences with the hydrate fallback, and the sample frontmatter pairs the bash rule's lint with the bash style's templates.
findings.evidence: docs/generate.md:30-33 against kit/packages/agents/generic/regions/repo/AGENTS.md; docs/context.md:78-86 against rules/bash.md and styles/bash.md.
findings.fix: Show one real file in each place.

findings.title: Documents 18, 19, 20, and 28: four headers still say less, or other, than the code does
findings.claim: kit help's header equates --help with `kit help --text` though the guard passes no --text; kit new's --group list omits plumbing; kit install and kit packages omit sources:; the CI workflow's header omits that a kit already on PATH is used.
findings.evidence: 1st.sh:711 `exec "${kit_root}/bin/kit-help" "${verb}"`; kit-new:43; kit-install:14 and kit-packages:12; kit-ci.yml template lines 8 and 88. The --help case was not run on a terminal.
findings.fix: Pass --text in the guard, and correct the three headers.

findings.title: Documents 21, 23, 24, and 26: four lists in the documents are still short or out of order
findings.claim: docs/testing.md omits the tutorials site's gate steps; the lists of what the kit package delivers omit the provider templates (and the README, welcome/); "bin/ holds only commands a person runs" stands against the plumbing verbs; features.md lists incoming second of seven stages.
findings.evidence: bin/ci:62-71 against docs/testing.md:8-9; kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/templates/bash/ exists; `kit flow --stages` prints incoming sixth.
findings.fix: Correct the four lists.

findings.title: Documents 1 (partly fixed): the notice at the one prompt still says only "say yes"
findings.claim: The four documents now state the three groups of kit serve's tools, but the notice shown when Claude Code asks whether to use the server still does not say six tools assign, close, and settle issues.
findings.evidence: package.yml:15 "say yes, and the agent can call the kit's verbs as tools".
findings.fix: Add a clause that some tools write to issues and pull requests.

findings.title: Infrastructure 16 (fixed) left a comment that names a script which is gone
findings.claim: A comment says scripts/verify-dist.mjs fails a build, and that directory no longer exists; the check is verify in src/build.ts. Not in the earlier review.
findings.evidence: reader.tsx:24; `ls projects/tutorials/scripts` fails.
findings.fix: Name src/build.ts in the comment.

areas.title: kittui architecture and reuse
areas.coverage: Read whole: README, main.go, 16 of 28 table files, 18 of 29 flow files, palette. Sampled: grid, shell, tabs, welcome, tutorials, workspaces, screens, seven catalogs. Not read: form, opener, most tests. Ran build, vet, gofmt, tests, two reproductions. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refuses report files from subagents; the long form is in `answers` here.
areas.summary: kittui's packages are layered and acyclic, and the table is reused by five screens and dialogs through table.Sheet. Flow, where the table came from, is not on Sheet: it keeps a second host of about 1,050 lines, and the two have drifted (last-left panel, team presets, wording). The catalog drives 27 of 32 stages, but 20 stages have no glyph, color, or legend, a third of fields.json is four fields repeated, and the other screens' catalogs are not read. Chrome is wired by hand in six screens and the tab menu in two. Issue and pull request links are still guessed in Go. Suggested order: links from kit, the small layering moves, the catalog, the chrome, then Flow onto Sheet.
strengths: The package graph is acyclic and layered (style, syntax, source; pane, kit; shell; grid; table; screens; root; main); no screen imports another, only internal/screens knows them all.
internal/source is generic and depends on nothing: Load with supersede, kept copies and marks, Poll, and a Clock tests drive. Keep it as it is.

shell.Layers gives one order for keys, clicks, the keys bar, and drawing, and table.Overlays plugs the table's four layers into any model; the keys bar is derived from where the keyboard is, never written per screen.

The catalog is real data with a strict reader (unknown keys refused, check names every fault at once, renderers registered by name); 27 of Flow's 32 stages need no Go, and the newer row contract (key, links by field id) is the right one to converge on.
table.Sheet works: the palette is 647 lines in all and gets presets, sort, group, filter, the fields dialog, selection, and the wheel; five screens and dialogs stand on it.
One writer for the presets file, written whole beside it and renamed, reading again first so another screen's save stays.
Glyph constants come from one table, kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json, shared with kit help flow.
go vet and gofmt are clean, statement coverage is 100% in 20 packages, tests run a fake kit and a test clock, and main.go's test seams are few and plain.

findings.title: Issue and pull request links are built in Go from a guess at origin, outside the forge seam
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Flow finding 8), still open: kit prints no url for an issue or a change, so kittui builds every such link as https://<host>/<last two path segments>/…, GitLab-shaped only where the hostname contains "gitlab". kit has three forge providers and kittui knows two URL shapes.
findings.evidence: A throwaway test printed: gitlab.com/acme/platform/app gives https://gitlab.com/platform/app/-/merge_requests/7; git@git.acme.example:acme/app gives …/acme/app/pull/7; https://dev.azure.com/acme/Platform/_git/app gives https://dev.azure.com/_git/app/pull/7. rows.go:591 calls pull(p.Number, ""), while the newer stages follow kit's `links` (kit/modules/jq/apps.jq:39-122, flow/workspace.go:24-51).
findings.fix: Have kit flow issues|changes --json print `links` (title, change, state) from the forge seam and let the two builders read them as catalog stages do; delete Origin.issue, pull, gitlab, infix. Size M.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with a throwaway test: all three URLs match the reviewer's exactly, and member rows (rows.go:434-439) go through the same parseRemote. kit's issue and change documents carry no url (forge.jq:119-131, 285-289; underway.jq:19-21), so `given` is always empty. Severity is arguable: links only, GitHub is right; the 11-10 review rated it Medium. (findings.md was absent; judged from the task text.)

findings.title: The table has two hosts: Flow does not use the reusable Sheet the other screens use
findings.claim: Known in part since 11-10 (Flow finding 17). The palette, tutorials, welcome, workspaces, and the opener stand on table.Sheet, but flow.Model still implements table.Host itself, so the table's host is written twice (about 900 lines in sheet.go, about 1,050 in flow) and has drifted.
findings.evidence: saveAs, rename, keep, keepStarred, favor, star, managed, choose, apply, rowKey, click, controlClick, Lines, Header, control, autoGroup each have a twin; KeepLast/ReadLast are called from flow.go:293,655 only, team presets and @me exist only in Flow (sheet.go:251 returns ""), and the empty line reads "no row matches the panel" (view.go:363) against "no row matches the search" (sheet.go:340). About 4,000 lines of flow tests re-test table behavior through the second host; flow's suite took 209 s here.
findings.fix: Three moves: give Sheet what only Flow has (login, team presets, last-left panel, loading/refusal/empty line, modifier clicks; S-M); make flow.stage hold a table.Sheet and hand it keys, clicks, wheel as the palette does (L); delete flow's seven forwarding files and the twins and move the mirrored tests to table.

findings.title: Twenty of 32 stages have no tab glyph, color, or legend; the tables are Go maps by stage name
findings.claim: Known in part since 11-10 (finding 17, "planned tabs have neither"); the tabs now exist and still have neither. stageGlyphs, stageColors, legends, and marks are generated from glyphs.json, which names 14 stages, while fields.json names 32, and nothing checks one against the other.
findings.evidence: A throwaway test counted 20 of 32 catalog stages with no glyph, 20 with no color, 20 with no legend: all of People, Trust, Platform, three of Delivery's five, and the newer Issues and Changes tabs. F1 explains none of the glyphs those rows draw (changes/checks draws ✅ ❌ 🏃).
findings.fix: Put `glyph` and `color` on the catalog entry (table.Schema) and derive a stage's legend from its fields' enum glyphs, field glyphs, and links; glyphs.json keeps the constants. Touches table/catalog.go, flow/fields.json, legend.go, legend.jq, glyph.go, view.go; size M.

findings.title: Every screen wires the shared chrome by hand, and one has already lost a part of it
findings.claim: shell gives the parts (Menu, BooksMenu, Search, Recent, MenuBar, Layers) and no whole, so six screens each declare appMenu, books, search, recent and repeat the same ladder in key and click. Only Flow uses shell.Layers for it.
findings.evidence: The workspaces screen has no shell.Recent: a search there is never remembered and ⌃R is swallowed (workspaces.go:540-548 takes every did != shell.NotSearch), against README.md:27-29 "Search works the same on every screen … ⌃R recalls a past search". The palette's and tutorials' key functions repeat the same eight branches.
findings.fix: Add a shell.Chrome holding the four parts with Key, Click, Layers, MenuBar, and quit, which each screen embeds and gives two callbacks (typed, left). New shell/chrome.go plus the key/click/menuBar of six screens; about 60 lines less a screen; size M.

findings.title: The tab menu and Maximize are copied between Flow and the welcome
findings.claim: internal/tabs holds the bar and the shared menu items and stops there; the menu's placement, keys, clicks, and maximize are written once in flow and again in welcome.
findings.evidence: shortcut, openMenu, menuKey, menuClick, menuBoxIn, menuTop, tabMenuAt, onMenu, barTakes, maximize, banner exist in both packages, differing only in m.width against m.paneWidth(); barTakes and onMenu are the same line for line.
findings.fix: A tabs.Frame (bar, dropdown, maximized, banner, pane top) with Key, Click, Lines, PaneTop, given the screen's items and a pick callback. Touches tabs, flow/menu.go, flow/view.go, welcome/menu.go, welcome/view.go; about 150 lines less in each; size S-M.

findings.title: The path-driven reader lives inside Flow, so no other screen's catalog is read
findings.claim: Known in part since 11-10 (finding 17). Flow now reads record and path for 27 of 32 stages (five keep Go builders), but decode, catalogRows, linkValue, and otherValues are methods of flow's model, so a Sheet cannot use them and Field.Path means a path in one catalog of seven.
findings.evidence: verbs.json has "record": "kit syntax --list, then kit help <verb>" and "path": "the verb's group, other for none"; tutorials.json and workspaces.json have real paths (.title, .members) that nothing evaluates, beside hand-written table.Record builders (tutorials.go:375, workspaces.go:238).
findings.fix: Lift the reader into table as (*Schema).Read(data) ([]Record, error) with a hook for Flow's member and jump links, and have tutorials and workspaces call it; rename or drop record/path in the four catalogs whose rows are not JSON. Size M.

findings.title: A third of fields.json is four fields written out 120 times
findings.claim: fields.json is one 1,219-line, 94 KB file for 32 stages of nine apps, and about 120 of its 361 fields are verbatim copies of four definitions that nothing holds together.
findings.evidence: By jq: member is the same object 31 times, organization 30, repository 29, source 30 (two shapes); {"name":"Default"} 31 times; the enum github, gitlab with glyphs 23 times, with no value for Azure DevOps in any.
findings.fix: ReadCatalog reads an optional `shared` map of fields that a stage names with {"use": id} plus overrides, a stage with no presets gets Default as Sheet.Views already does, and the file splits by app via embed.FS. Size S for the reader, M with the split.

findings.title: Host asks a screen for 30 methods, a dozen of which the table can compute itself
findings.claim: Host has 30 methods, Keyboard adds five, Selecting and Picking are sniffed at run time, and about 130 table functions take a Host; the interface is this wide because it had to describe Flow from outside.
findings.evidence: HeaderName, HeaderTop, and HeadingName are implemented in both hosts as table.ColumnName(h), table.HeaderTop(h), table.FieldName(h) (sheet.go:269-275, flow/host.go:52-58); ShownColumns, Names, GridWidth, Lines, Header, Selector, Settle, Values are derived in both from the schema, records, Table state, settings, and pane placement.
findings.fix: Remove the three forwarding methods now (popover.go:102-107 can call the functions; S); after S1-2 let the controls take *Sheet and shrink Host to what a sheet's owner supplies (login, team presets, opener, empty line); M.

findings.title: An app is declared in four places, and a tab's actions are tied to stage names in Go
findings.claim: Adding an app means editing shell's Screen constants and menu sections, flow's apps table, and the README table, with no check across them; stage-specific behavior is switched on names throughout flow.
findings.evidence: Actions exist for issues and packages/packages only (act.go:47, packages.go:43), the tab count special-cases "incoming" (view.go:210), auto-group special-cases "member" (flow.go:1091), the tab menu dispatches on display names such as "Refresh" and "Open Selected" in two switches (menu.go:127-140,160-177), and refOf parses member and reference back out of the key keyOf built (act.go:96-105, known since 11-10).
findings.fix: One apps.json (screen, name, glyph, verb, tabs) read by shell and flow with a test against the README; menu items carry an id; a catalog entry may list `actions` (name, glyph, key, kit words, asks, one-member) for Packages and the simple Issues actions. S for apps.json and ids, M for actions as data.

findings.title: kittui reads git and the repository's files itself in five places, with two URL parsers
findings.claim: The README says kittui runs kit for everything it knows and reads what it shows from kit as JSON, but several of kit's rules are kept a second time in Go with no test across the two.
findings.evidence: `git remote get-url origin` runs in flow/origin.go:17 and welcome/source.go:94, parsed by parseRemote and by repoOf; `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in flow/team.go:38 and welcome/source.go:31; source.go:29-56 finds welcome pages "as kit welcome --text finds them"; kit/installed.go parses kit.yml and .kit/manifest "as the loader reads them".
findings.fix: Take host and path from the kit.Workspace the root already has (removes ReadOrigin, readRepo, repoOf), and have kit welcome --json name its pages and kit workspace --json say whether the kit is installed and where team presets are. Size M.

findings.title: The table knows Flow's command line, and Flow holds renderers every table could use
findings.claim: table.Schema carries Command, Takes, Staged, Marked, Forge, Slurp and validates kit flow's flags, while generic renderers and table features (last-left panel, team presets) sit in flow.
findings.evidence: table.Takes = owner, no-fetch, fresh, cached, workspace (catalog.go:45); `staged` is true for all 32 stages; the palette's catalog must say {"stages":[{"stage":"help/verbs"}]}; date, day, bytes, path, track are registered from flow's init (fields.go:66-87, workspace.go:124), so another screen's catalog can name them only because the binary links flow.
findings.fix: Split Schema into the table's part and a Source struct flow reads from the same entry, drop `staged`, and move the five generic renderers to table/render.go; leave the word "stages" alone. Size S.

findings.title: The lowest layout package depends on the kit runner, through one glyph
findings.claim: The graph is acyclic, with four edges pointing the wrong way: grid → shell, tabs → table, shell → kit, transcript → form.
findings.evidence: grid imports shell for `Search = shell.Find`, so `go list -deps ./internal/grid` prints style pane syntax kit shell grid; tabs imports table for table.Sweep; shell imports kit for kit.Workspace; transcript (14 lines) imports form for form.Quote.
findings.fix: Move Find and Sweep to style, give shell.BooksMenu its own small Workspace struct filled by screens, and move Quote to transcript or kit. Size S.

findings.title: Five source files and one catalog exceed 1,000 lines, and seven of flow's files only forward
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/flow.go, projects/tui/internal/grid/panel.go, projects/tui/internal/welcome/welcome.go, projects/tui/internal/kit/kit.go, projects/tui/internal/flow/fields.json, projects/tui/internal/flow/pane.go, projects/tui/internal/flow/columns.go
findings.claim: flow.go (1,395), grid/panel.go (1,361), form/model.go (1,070), grid/grid.go (1,037), welcome/welcome.go (1,030), and fields.json (1,219) each hold several separable concerns; flow's pane.go, column.go, heading.go, outline.go, columns.go, labels.go are residue of the extraction.
findings.evidence: flow.go:962-1262 is the stage read, 772-932 the keys, and the clicks and jump are separate blocks; panel.go's `group` alone is lines 543-762; flow has 14 one-line forwards to table and 20 re-exported constants and aliases "by the names flow has always used".
findings.fix: Moves within a package, no signature changes: flow.go into load.go, keys.go, click.go, jump.go; panel.go into group.go, arrange.go, filter.go; welcome.go's search, cursor, fixes; kit.go by caller; fields.json by app; drop the aliases now and the forwarding files with S1-2. S each.

findings.title: grid.Panel is five things in one struct, and a field's setting has two types
findings.claim: Panel mixes the person's view, the schema's facts, kittui's settings, values derived from the rows, and Flow's search state; the person's part also exists as both grid.Field and table.Setting with a 95-line translation each way.
findings.evidence: Schema.Ready copies Sortable, Groupable, Labels, Ones, Owner into the panel on every call; Focused and Recall are set by grid's Find and never read by grid; flow.go:664 stores the whole derived panel back as the stage's view.
findings.fix: Keep Fields and Query in Panel, pass the schema's facts and settings to the row pipeline as a second argument, and move Focused/Recall to the screen (or shell.Chrome). Size M, after S1-2.

findings.title: The welcome's checks are a third table, laid out by hand, with kit's check ids in Go
findings.claim: Two of the welcome's five steps are Sheets; the two with checks draw their own rows with their own cursor, paging, and wheel, and the setup step has its own column model. Whether a Sheet can carry a check's fix buttons under its row I did not establish, which would settle the size.
findings.evidence: setup.go defines column, columns, widths, cell, headings with kit's check ids written in (repo-git, kit-installed, kit-hydrated, hooks-installed, toolchain-project, kit-check); the steps' ids, glyphs, and files are a Go table `known` (welcome.go:60-66).
findings.fix: A checks.json catalog and the checks as records on a Sheet with the fix as the row's detail, kit welcome --checks --json naming each check's column. Size M, after S1-2.

findings.title: Code for file formats that no release has shipped
findings.claim: Ahead of the first release, kittui still migrates views.json into presets.json version 2 and falls back to a .kit/manifest "as a release before the declaration wrote it". What would settle it is whether anyone outside the project holds such files.
findings.evidence: views.go carries named, sortKey, migrate, preset (150 lines); grid.Show, Mine, Others, Panel.Shown, Panel.Showing have no non-test caller but views.go:189,191.
findings.fix: Delete the migration, the Show API, and the manifest fallback (about 200 lines plus tests) before 0.1.0, or name in the code the pre-release they serve. Size S.

findings.title: The table's wall-clock test fails on a busy machine
findings.claim: TestATurnOfTheWheelOverTenThousandRowsIsWellUnderAFramesTime allows 8 ms of wall-clock time, so the gate depends on the runner being idle; the same test exists once per host.
findings.evidence: At a load average near 50 it failed eight runs of eight, alone and in the suite: 12.4, 13.4, 15.4, 17.0, and 28.0 ms against 8 ms. I could not measure it on an idle machine.
findings.fix: Assert the stated property instead, that a turn costs what the screen shows: compare 1,000 rows with 10,000 (ratio under 2) or count cells drawn, and keep the time as a benchmark. Size S.

findings.title: The README describes an earlier kittui
findings.claim: Known in part since 11-10 (Docs finding 12). Four statements are false and seven packages have no Layout entry.
findings.evidence: "It holds no verb by name" though the code names syntax, help, flow, welcome, tutorials, trust, work, gather, close and eight app verbs; "six screens" over a table of nine apps; tutorials "tabbed by audience" and sharing internal/tabs, which tutorials does not import; grid, pane, markdown, fix, opener, workspaces, screens are missing from Layout, and the flow entry is one 170-line bullet.
findings.fix: Correct the four statements, add the seven packages, and move the flow entry's behavior into the package comments it repeats. Size S.

areas.title: the bash CLI architecture
areas.coverage: Read whole: bin/kit, kit-call, 1st.sh, forge.sh, three forge providers, tracker seam and providers, toolchain.sh, dependencies.sh, apps.sh, 20 verbs' code. Part: flow.sh, welcome.sh, forge.jq, workspaces.sh, policy.sh, terminal.sh. Unread: commit, serve, git, delivery modules' insides. Ran: use-graph script, cycle pass, diffs, timings, fake-az reproduction. No bats.
areas.summary: findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write ("subagents return findings as text") and I did not route around it, so everything is in this result. No critical or high finding. The design is sound: the loader, `use`, uniform verb preamble, the forge contract, and jq normalization are strengths. The cost is repetition and misplaced knowledge: Azure Boards is implemented twice and reads its closing states wrongly (reproduced); the forge seam re-resolves its provider on every call; facts about each forge, the forge contract, app stages, and system package managers are typed into bash many times where a table would do; flow.sh sits in a five-module cycle; the kittui hand-off is written ten times.
strengths: The loader: bin/kit is POSIX sh that starts one sed on the common path, refuses an untrusted clone before anything of the clone's runs, and hands on through the environment; its sh copies of clone_root, trust_name, and trusted are deliberate and say so.
`use` is small and strict (once a process, names that cannot leave the path, a path a repository can extend, `super` for overrides), and list:read keeps a status that `< <(…)` loses.
The verb preamble is uniform across all 52 verbs (set -o, source 1st.sh, kit:enter, use, guard:arguments); do not fold it into one call.
A verb's header is data: kit syntax, help, completion, and kittui's forms read the usage lines, which is why 45% of kit/bin is comment and is the right trade.

The forge contract is the best-designed part: answers, none, fails, or unsupported; whole lists or failure; {"limited": N}; versions and lacks; stand-ins; a cross-process snapshot with a lock that names its holder.
Normalizing in jq: every provider folds into shared document, issue, release, build, artifact, environment, and deployment shapes, with jq tests of their own.

terminals.json with terminal.jq and one-call readers, and glyphs.json with the generated region in flow.sh, are the data-driven pattern the proposals copy; the terminal seam is the cleanest of the six.
dependencies.sh with npm.sh and uv.sh: eight calls, two providers that truly differ, 245 lines.
apps.sh as a runner: {rows, errors, limited}, marks, the workspace fan-out, and apps:forge answering no forge, lacked, and off-here in one place.
yaml.sh caches by the file's text, so a changed file is never read stale and a repeated read forks nothing.

findings.title: Azure Boards' closing states are typed in three places, and none reads the setting kit closes with
findings.claim: kit closes a work item to closed_state or removed_state, but reads one as closed only in Closed, Done, or Removed, a list written in jq, in the WIQL, and in tracker/ado:state. A repository that sets closed_state: Resolved closes an issue and then reads it open.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with a fake az answering System.State Resolved under closed_state: Resolved: `tracker:of AB#7 state` printed OPEN and `forge:issue-state 7` printed OPEN, after close sent `--state Resolved`.
findings.fix: One function gives the three defaults plus the two settings, and is passed to ado_closed($states), the WIQL, and tracker/ado:state; it falls out of S2-2. Size S.

findings.title: Azure Boards is implemented twice, and the two have drifted
findings.claim: tracker/ado.sh and the issue-* calls of forge/ado.sh do the same eight things through the same az boards commands, differing only in where the organization and project come from. tracker/ado:create drops the body the contract gives it (kit gather sends its task list there, issue.sh:216), runs az without --detect false, encodes a project by hand, and fails silently.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: tracker create ran `boards work-item create --title … --type Task --project Proj --org … --output json`, while forge issue-create added `--description … --detect false --only-show-errors`. The silent failures are known since 11-10 (Flow item 26), still open.
findings.fix: Move the work-item calls to one module, modules/bash/boards.sh, with the single az wrapper; tracker/ado.sh and forge/ado.sh keep only how each finds the organization and project. About 100 lines go; size S.

findings.title: The forge seam finds its provider, and each provider its repository, again on every call
findings.claim: forge:call runs forge:provider each time (forge:primary twice, settings reads, three git runs, about ten forks), and gitlab's ask and api, like ado's ask and az, each resolve the remote again, twice per read. Only the declaration (forge_lacking) is kept once a process.
findings.evidence: Timed in a throwaway repository, 30 calls each, under load average 74: git remote 20.7 ms, forge:provider 117-124 ms (5.7x), forge/gitlab:project 59-72 ms (3x), forge/ado:place 201 ms. gitlab open-prs makes five reads a merge request, so ten project resolutions each; an idle-machine timing would settle the real cost.
findings.fix: Keep the primary, the provider, and the provider's place in variables once a process, keyed by settings:file so policy:from-base reads afresh. Touches forge.sh, gitlab.sh, ado.sh; size S.

findings.title: Facts about each forge are typed into seven files outside the providers, so Azure DevOps is missing from four
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:404-434, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:468-476, kit/modules/bash/welcome.sh:444-466, kit/modules/bash/welcome.sh:738-748, kit/modules/jq/workspace.jq:24-29, kit/modules/bash/tracker/forge.sh:33-58, kit/modules/bash/issues.sh:117, kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json:5-8
findings.claim: The host table, runner variables, and login files are case arms in forge.sh; welcome.sh maps github to gh and anything else to glab and skips other forges; workspace.jq, tracker/forge.sh, issues.sh, and glyphs.json each branch on forge names. So kit welcome plans no forge check for an ado repository, ado branches and commits get no page link, and ado has no glyph.
findings.evidence: welcome.sh:457-458 `(github:* | gitlab:*) ;; (*) continue`; workspace.jq:27-29 gives a page for github and gitlab, `else null`; issues.sh:117 `IN("gitlab", "ado")` though every provider answers noun; tracker/forge.sh calls undeclared forge/<name>:issue-url by declare -F.
findings.fix: One table, kit/modules/jq/forges.json, read as terminals.json is: per forge its hosts, runner, login file, tool, auth commands, sigil, noun, glyph, and page templates; forge.sh, welcome.sh, workspace.jq, tracker/forge.sh, issues.sh, and the glyphs read it. Size M.

findings.title: The forge contract is stated five times in forge.sh, and again as stubs in the providers
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:60-235, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:288-309, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:697-873, kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh:74-95, kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh:254-286, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:37-55
findings.claim: A call is declared in two header tables, forge_features (31), forge_feature_of (40), forge_call_since (4), and one of 60 wrapper functions whose body also says whether it changes the forge; nothing checks one against another. ado.sh has 11 and gitlab.sh 2 `{ return 3; }` stubs the seam never calls.
findings.evidence: pr-create's fourth argument is 'since 3' in the header but in neither table; ado.sh:253 says 'the seam answers unsupported and never calls this' above a stub. A set comparison shows github defines all 60 calls, gitlab and ado 54, and no test asserts it.
findings.fix: One table of call, feature, since, and kind (read, change, snapshot), as a bash array or a JSON file kittui can also read; a loop defines the plain wrappers and a bats test checks each provider against it. Delete the 13 stubs; about 110 lines go; size S.

findings.title: The three forge providers repeat five patterns a shared layer would hold once
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:555-580, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:646-659, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:891-910, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:1141-1150, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:1185-1204, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:319-328, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:720-731, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:761-778, kit/modules/bash/forge/github.sh:345-362, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:211-229

findings.fix: Add forge:pages (cursor loop), forge:marks-of (providers give only mark-of), forge:here (pr-here), forge:off (status test), and one forge_mark_kinds array to forge.sh. No new seam; about 150 lines leave the providers; size M.

findings.title: flow.sh holds three stages, the shared cells, and two other stages' tables, so five modules use each other in a ring
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:65, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:198-262, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:912-1066, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1194-1206, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1391-1440, kit/modules/bash/changes.sh:14

The seven-stage roster is a case statement in eight places because only four stages follow the unstated <stage>:documents/draw/render shape.

The stage list recurs at flow.sh:153, 1198, 1257, 1270, 1331, 1394, 1459, across.sh:131, marks.sh:37. The other 5-cycle (render, region, place, materialize, manifest) is one component and should stay.

findings.title: An app's stages are a table written as one-line bash functions, and a new stage is edited into five places
findings.claim: Of 12 forge-backed stages in people, delivery, changes, and issues, 11 are exactly `apps:forge <feature> <call> <def>` and every mark is `apps:forge-mark <kind>…`. The six app verbs are the same seven lines under 58 to 86 header lines that restate the forge's details per forge.
findings.evidence: people.sh:23-29 is three such one-liners; kit-audit, kit-changes, kit-delivery, kit-issues, kit-people, kit-platform differ only in the verb's name. A new stage touches the verb's header, <verb>_stages, apps/<verb>.sh, apps.jq, and kittui's fields.json.
findings.fix: modules/jq/apps.json: per app its stages in order, each {stage, feature, call, def, marks} or {stage, elsewhere}; apps:main reads it, kittui can too, and apps/<verb>.sh stays only for stages with code. Removes four modules and most of six headers; size M.

findings.title: The hand-off to kittui is written out at ten sites
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-flow:304-312, kit/bin/kit-flow:320-328, kit/bin/kit-flow:391-399, kit/bin/kit-workspace:183-184, kit/bin/kit-help:77-78, kit/bin/kit-tutorials:64-65, kit/bin/kit-welcome:172, kit/bin/kit-tui:51-52, kit/modules/bash/apps.sh:52-59, kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:737-740
findings.claim: Each site repeats: three terminals, tui:binary --probe, tui:binary, terminal:export-probes, export KIT, exec with the app and workspace. tui.sh only finds the binary, so what kittui needs from its parent lives in nine callers.
findings.evidence: grep finds `export KIT="${kit_root}/bin/kit"` 9 times and terminal:export-probes 9 times; kit-welcome:106 already differs by skipping the probes under --fix.
findings.fix: Add tui:offered and tui:exec <app> [<argument>…] to tui.sh; each site becomes `tui:offered && tui:exec flow "$@"`. Size S.

findings.title: Four verbs hold their logic in bin, so modules reach it across a process
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-tools:62-440, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:160, kit/bin/kit-workspace:206-259, kit/bin/kit-update:107-120, kit/modules/bash/apps/platform.sh:160, kit/modules/bash/apps/audit.sh:181
findings.claim: 1st.sh says work within the modules is a function call, yet kit-tools has 339 code lines and 11 unprefixed functions (needed, draw, split, join, call…), kit-workspaces 260, kit-update 169, kit-policy 121. With no tools.sh, Platform and Audit get their rows by starting kit again.

findings.title: apt.sh, dnf.sh, and pacman.sh are one file three times, and tool facts sit in four tables
findings.claim: With the manager's name replaced, the three providers differ only in header prose, the install words, and the tool-to-package case; 11 functions are identical. welcome:site is a fourth table over the same tools.
findings.evidence: diff of the name-normalized files shows only `install` vs `-S` and the package arms (ShellCheck on Fedora, go-yq and github-cli on Arch).

The toolchain seam ranks mise, nix, brew, docker by name and special-cases brew in three functions.

findings.title: forge.jq and github.sh are each several components in one file
findings.claim: forge.jq interleaves 30 shared definitions with 34 github_, 27 gitlab_, and 23 ado_ ones and is imported at 71 places. github.sh carries, beside its 60 calls, the GitHub App calls (curl and a JWT, 210 lines), the marks, and the alerts, each with a transport of its own.

findings.title: jq that shapes a stage's rows sits inline in bash, where tests/jq cannot reach it
findings.claim: The forge splits well: bash reads, a named def shapes, tests/jq pins the def. Elsewhere the programs are inline: flow.sh has 39 jq call sites against a 38-line flow.jq, across.sh 29 and welcome.sh 24 with no import, workspaces.sh 32.
findings.evidence: flow:incoming-rows builds every incoming row in a 17-line inline program; forge:stand-ins validates stand-ins in a 22-line one that repeats kit.schema.json. About 450 jq call sites, 116 imports, 71 of forge.
findings.fix: As each file is next touched, move any program over five lines, or used twice, to a def with a case in tests/jq. Size M, piecemeal.

findings.title: Modules call functions of modules they do not use
findings.claim: workspaces.sh says `use git yaml file` and calls forge:primary and forge:of, working only because git.sh uses forge; forge.sh calls yaml:* through settings; github's runs relies on the wrapper's `use git`. workspaces:place and placed are stage-document code in the workspace-file module.

findings.fix: Name every module a file calls on its use line, checked by a lint over <module>: prefixes, and move place and placed beside apps:forge. Size S.

findings.title: Nine headers still describe two forges
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:2, kit/modules/bash/git.sh:6, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:7, kit/modules/bash/tracker.sh:10, kit/modules/bash/workspaces.sh:472, kit/bin/kit-issues:31, kit/bin/kit-work:25, kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:284, kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:26
findings.claim: 'The forge (GitHub, GitLab)' and 'github or gitlab, for now' predate the Azure DevOps provider, and tracker.sh:10 says Azure DevOps work items are not on the forge, which is false where the forge is ado. flow.sh:11-13 says the changes' rows live in changes.sh; they are in flow.sh.

findings.fix: Reword to 'the forge' and let forge:providers, or S2-4's table, name them. Size S.

findings.title: Contract 6 (bot-accounts) and secrets.sh ship with no caller
findings.claim: At this commit nothing under kit/bin or kit/modules calls the six forge:bot-* calls or any secrets: function; it is the first half of #258. If v0.1.0 is cut before the verb lands, about 310 lines that mint and revoke tokens ship untried by any command.

areas.title: the contract between kit and kittui, and things defined twice
areas.coverage: Read whole: apps.sh, marks.sh, tutorials.sh, apps.jq, glyphs.json/jq, syntax.jq, fields.json, kit.go, rows.go, glyph.go, legend.go, table's catalog and reader. Sampled: flow.sh, welcome.sh, forge.jq, flow.go, welcome and tutorials Go. Not read: workspaces.sh, serve.jq, flow menus/views. Ran real kit for 9 verbs, 11 stages, 52 syntaxes; three Go probes.
areas.summary: The kit-to-kittui contract agrees today wherever both sides list something: every catalog command, flag, stage, mark, and link key matched the real kit. But 22 definitions live on both sides and only 4 are held (glyphs, flow's stages, syntax, verb groups). The one wrong result is kittui guessing issue and pull request links (GitLab subgroups, Azure DevOps). Structurally: no version on stage documents though a workspace mixes releases; an app's tabs listed in six places with drift; glyphs.json covering 14 of 32 stages; three bash copies of the stage protocol. The smallest contract test is a 40-line bats file. Full write-up: out/S3/findings.md
strengths: glyphs.json is one table that kit generate writes into flow.sh, both help legends, and glyph.go, held by kit generate --check and legend_test.go:307; the other tables should follow this pattern.
internal/table is a real catalog reader (unknown keys refused, check(), renderers registered by name); 28 of 32 stages need no Go of their own.
kit prints links by field id and row:<stage>/<key> for the newer stages, so kittui follows a link without knowing a forge.
kit.Runner is the one door to kit, with partial documents, process groups, and limits; source.Load is generic and small.
Flow's tabs and order come from kit flow --stages at run time, and verb groups from kit syntax --list: neither is defined twice.
tests/syntax.bats:284 holds the Go syntax fixtures to kit, and all 40 are exact today.
apps.sh is a clean convention: a verb declares its stages and three kinds of function and gets JSON, text, marks, the workspace run, and the hand-off.
Every catalog command, flag, stage name, mark, and link key checked against the real kit agrees today; the drift is in fixtures and in what was never listed.

findings.title: kittui builds every issue and pull request link itself, and gets GitLab subgroups and Azure DevOps wrong
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/origin.go:27, projects/tui/internal/flow/origin.go:60, projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:481, projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:591, kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:120, kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:285, kit/modules/jq/workspace.jq:23
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 8), still open; Azure DevOps is new. kit's open issue and change documents carry no url, so kittui guesses each page from origin's last two path segments and whether the host's name contains "gitlab".
findings.evidence: A probe over parseRemote(...).pull(7, "") printed https://gitlab.com/sub/project/-/merge_requests/7 for gitlab.com/group/sub/project and https://dev.azure.com/_git/repo/pull/7 for dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo. Page shapes live in three places: the providers, workspace.jq:23-28, and origin.go.
findings.fix: The issue and change documents carry their page and kit flow issues and changes print links by field, as every newer stage does; then delete issue, pull, gitlab, and infix from origin.go. Size M.
findings.verdict_note: Every fact reproduced by a probe test: parseRemote (origin.go:43) keeps two segments, so a GitLab subgroup gives /sub/project/-/merge_requests/7 and Azure DevOps /_git/repo/pull/7; no issue or change document carries url, and rows.go:591 passes "". origin_test.go:14 pins the truncation. Only severity is overstated: dead links, GitHub unaffected; the 11-10 review rated it Medium.

findings.title: The stage documents carry no version, yet a workspace reads each member with its own release
findings.claim: Over a workspace each member answers with the release its own kit.yml pins, and kittui reads them all with the one fields.json embedded in its binary; {rows, errors} has no version, so a renamed key in a later release is a silently blank column. Not run with two releases: a group whose member pins another release would settle it.
findings.evidence: across:run runs kit in each member's checkout, and bin/kit:437 keeps KIT_VERSION only where KIT_VERSION_ROOT is that clone. ReadFrom gives no value for a path a record lacks, and the forge seam has forge_contract=6 where the stage documents have nothing.
findings.fix: S: a contract number in every stage document and in fields.json, a member that differs named under errors. L: kit serves the data half of the catalog (kit <verb> --stages --json) and kittui keeps only presentation.

findings.title: No test holds fields.json, the Go fixtures, or the app table to what kit prints
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 17), still open. Every Go test of the 32 stages runs on fake-kit and hand-kept fixtures; only kit syntax has a cross-language test.
findings.evidence: Run by hand, the missing check passes for --stages, takes against kit syntax --match, and marked, and fails for fixtures: on 10 of 11 forge-less stages the real rows hold source and organization the fixtures lack, and issues.json's pr has no source. The syntax fixtures are exact, 40 of 40.
findings.fix: One bats file of about 40 lines beside syntax.bats:284 with four checks per catalog stage: in --stages, flags match kit syntax, marked matches the mark functions, row keys match paths and fixtures. Size S; the 19 forge stages need the fakes, M.

findings.title: An app's tabs are listed in six places, and two already disagree
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/apps.go:25, kit/modules/bash/apps.sh:9, kit/modules/bash/workspace.sh:15, kit/modules/bash/apps/delivery.sh:25, kit/bin/kit-workspace:4, projects/tui/internal/shell/shell.go:83
findings.claim: The tabs of an app are in apps.go, in <verb>_stages and <verb>_elsewhere, in each verb's usage lines, in fields.json, in fake-kit, and in apps_test.go, with nothing tying them.
findings.evidence: Repositories has an incoming tab, yet kit workspace incoming answers unknown argument 'incoming', exit 2, where kit delivery releases names kit flow releases. apps.sh:9 says _stages is the tab order, and Repositories' tabs stand in another order than workspace_stages.
findings.fix: One manifest beside glyphs.json (apps.json: screen, name, glyph, verb, tabs in order); apps.go and shell.go's menu become a kit:generate region, _elsewhere and usage lines are checked from it. Size M.

findings.title: glyphs.json covers 14 of 32 stages, so 20 tabs have no glyph, no colour, and no legend
findings.claim: glyphs.json lists stages for flow, workspace, and packages only, so the tabs of the six entity apps' own stages have no tab glyph, no group colour, and a legend that explains none of their rows' glyphs.
findings.evidence: A probe printed 20 of 24 tabs with glyph "", colour "", and 0 legend entries; changes/checks draws ✅ ❌ 🏃 and delivery/deployments ✅ ❌ 🔘 with no legend line. The legend test loops over Flow's five stages alone.
findings.fix: Derive a stage's legend from the glyphs its catalog entry declares, with glyphs.json's meanings; add the 18 stages' tab glyph and group; loop the test over the catalog. Size S for data, M with the derived legend.

findings.title: The stage protocol is written three times in bash, with two envelopes that kittui reconciles
findings.claim: --stages, --marks, <stage> --json, the hand-off, and the workspace run are in apps:main, again in kit-workspace's own functions, and again in kit-flow; flow's stages print an array or an object where every other stage prints {rows, errors}.
findings.evidence: apps.sh:6 says an app verb draws its tabs "as kit workspace draws its own"; kit-workspace:155-260 has its own marks, document, repos, shown. stage.decode switches record on over and calls membersRecords (flow.go:1120-1134).
findings.fix: Move kit workspace onto apps:main through apps/workspace.sh, size M. Before v0.1.0 freezes it, decide whether kit flow <stage> --json prints {rows, errors} everywhere, size M.

findings.title: fields.json repeats what it could name once, and three of its keys copy what kit already says
findings.claim: The catalog holds the same four where-from fields in every stage and glyphs as literals, and its takes, marked, and forge keys copy the verb's usage line, the mark functions, and the apps:forge calls.
findings.evidence: jq counts: 32 stages, 361 fields, 127 of them member, source, organization, repository, 120 byte-identical copies of five definitions; 146 glyph literals for 44 glyphs, the github and gitlab pair 23 times. takes, marked, and forge agree with kit today and nothing checks them.
findings.fix: table.ReadCatalog takes shared field sets ("shared" and "use"), removing about 300 lines, and glyphs are named and resolved at generate time; size S. takes, marked, and forge move to kit with S3-2.

findings.title: Four stages are still built in Go, and the words they derive are derived in bash too
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:325, projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:556, projects/tui/internal/flow/rows.go:656, kit/modules/bash/issues.sh:117, kit/modules/bash/builds.sh:51, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:912
findings.claim: issues, changes, builds, and workspace/repos have a Go struct and builder each, the catalog path of a field a builder sets is never read, and what the builders add is mostly a word kit's text also derives.
findings.evidence: The change sigil is in forge.jq:159,268,515, issues.sh:117, and rows.go:556; the build's event word in builds.sh:51-58 and rows.go:656-664; the checks cell in flow.sh:912-925 and rows.go:216-235. unbuilt (rows.go:248) reads a path only where the builder left the field unset.
findings.fix: kit prints pr.ref, where, and event as its text shows them, each S, and the builders shrink to the catalog as releases did; detail rows need a detail notion in the catalog, M.

findings.title: kittui finds and orders the welcome pages itself, from the release's own layout
findings.claim: readPages repeats welcome:pages, including the path packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/welcome, the ordering, and the id rule; the step list and which steps hold checks are in Go's known and in bash's welcome:step. No divergence found today.
findings.evidence: source.go:30-56,116-121 against welcome.sh:1046-1061; welcome.go:60-66 against welcome.sh:107-112. A release that moves the package's files changes bash and silently not kittui.
findings.fix: kit welcome --pages --json prints [{id, file, path, checked}] in order and kittui reads each path; known keeps the glyphs alone. Size S.

findings.title: A change with no check draws "NONE"
findings.claim: kit gives checks.state "NONE" for a change no check reported on, and the catalog's enum lists only SUCCESS, FAILURE, PENDING with no other, so grouping or filtering by checks shows the raw word.
findings.evidence: A probe printed Glyphed(["NONE"]) = ["NONE"] and a cell with Head:NONE; no fixture holds a NONE. Builds' event still lists pull_request (fields.json:185), which no build emits (11-10, Flow 27).
findings.fix: Add {"value": "NONE"} drawn as none, or have kit print checks: null; an enum check in the test of S3-3 would catch both.

findings.title: Azure DevOps is a provider with no glyph anywhere
findings.claim: source is github, gitlab, or ado, and the glyph table, the 23 enum pairs in fields.json, and forgeGlyphs know only two, so an ado row draws the bare word.
findings.evidence: forge.jq:515 prints source: "ado"; glyphs.json names GitHub and GitLab; quota.go:21 is map{"github": GitHub, "gitlab": GitLab}.
findings.fix: A third glyph and a forges map in glyphs.json, provider id to glyph name, from which forgeGlyphs and the enum pairs are generated. Size S.

findings.title: Three statements about the contract are not true
findings.claim: kit flow --capabilities is said to be for kittui, which never reads it; kit.go says the binary knows no verb by name, and it names more than a dozen; kit-flow omits stand_ins and kit-welcome omits findings from the shapes they print.
findings.evidence: A grep for "capabilit" under projects/tui finds only help fixtures; apps.go:25-38 names eight verbs; kit flow --capabilities printed contract, forge, provider, features, stand_ins.
findings.fix: Say who reads --capabilities, add stand_ins and findings to the two headers, and reword kit.go:3 to: every call to kit goes through this package.

findings.title: Twelve verbs have no syntax fixture, and the test does not notice
findings.claim: key and render exist in jq and in Go, held to kit only through fixtures, and the bats test loops over the fixtures that exist: 40 of 52 verbs.
findings.evidence: Comparing kit syntax with testdata: no fixture for assign, close, facts, gather, ready, settle, trust, tutorials, unassign, uninstall, workspace, workspaces.
findings.fix: Loop the test over kit syntax --list and fail on a verb with no fixture. Size S.

findings.title: table.Schema carries how flow reads kit, and small helpers are copied
findings.claim: The generic table package holds Command, Takes, Staged, Marked, Forge, Slurp and names kit flow's flags; welcome's and tutorials' catalogs fill record and path with prose nothing reads.
findings.evidence: readCatalog, the same panic wrapper, is in flow, palette, welcome, and tutorials; the accent "12" is in style.go:29 and three constants.
findings.fix: A Source struct inside Schema for the six read keys, table.MustReadCatalog, style.Accent. Size S.

findings.title: kit flow's stage sets are spelled out in case patterns beside the list that names them
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1270, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1331, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1459, kit/modules/bash/across.sh:131, kit/modules/bash/marks.sh:37, kit/modules/bash/settings.sh:313
findings.claim: settings_stages is the list, yet the forge subset is written three times and the full set twice more as case patterns.
findings.evidence: (issues | changes | builds | releases) at flow.sh:1270, flow.sh:1331, marks.sh:37; the seven at flow.sh:1459 and across.sh:131.
findings.fix: glyphs.json's stage entries carry forge: true and the purpose, and the patterns read them, so an eighth stage is one entry. Size S.

areas.title: the tests
areas.coverage: Read whole: helper.bash, five fakes, bin/ci, docs/testing.md, six bats files, testkit, golden and cost tests. Read in part: forge-conformance, forge-ado, tracker, four fake-kits. Scripted counts over all 81 bats and 126 Go test files. Ran gofmt, vet, go test with coverage, eight bats files, at load 45-74. Tutorials tests not run.
areas.summary: The suites are large and careful (1,261 bats tests; 1,022 Go tests; all 23 kittui packages at 100.0%), but each side of each seam is tested against a hand-kept copy of the other. kittui's stage fixtures have drifted from what kit prints, and the forge fixtures ignore the 79 research schemas: 12 of 42 reached reject a fixture. Four wall-clock tests failed twice under load. Set-up is copied across files, skips are invisible to the gate, and twelve verbs have no form fixture. Not delivered: findings.md. The harness refused the Write as a subagent report file, and I did not work around it; this result carries the content, and my logs and scripts are in out/S4/.
strengths: kittui: gofmt and go vet clean; every one of the 23 packages at 100.0% of statements (cmd/kittui, app, fix, flow, form, grid, kit, markdown, opener, palette, pane, screens, shell, source, style, syntax, table, tabs, testkit, transcript, tutorials, welcome, workspaces), enforced per function at bin/ci:79, not by the rounded total. 126 test files, 1,022 Test functions.

helper:isolate is thorough and explained line by line (HOME, XDG, TMPDIR, git's global config, time zone, locale, CI variables), and the default teardown fails a test that ends inside the checkout. Keep both.
world-make, world-copy, and world-repo are the right shape, and tests/world.bats and tests/in-order.bats test the helpers themselves. The findings ask for more use of them, not a change.

fake-tool fails an unrouted call, records every call, applies gh's --jq with the provider's own filter, and colours its answer when a desk forces colour. The providers keep --jq filters to plain paths, so jq against gh's gojq is no risk.

tests/jq.bats requires a test file for every jq module, and tests/syntax.bats:283 holds the Go syntax fixtures to the real kit: the data-driven pattern S4-1 and S4-7 extend. legend_test.go reads the real kit/bin/kit-flow and glyph.go is generated from glyphs.json.
tests/contract.bats checks the real mise, offline, against the shapes the fakes assume, and skips honestly.
The conformance suite tests the failure contract as hard as the answers: a forge that cannot answer fails every read with one line, and a list that is not a list fails rather than reading as none.

testkit.Clock and testkit.Drive let the Go tests drive Bubble Tea with no real wait, and the cost tests pair each time bound with a structural one (the same slice is reused); the structural half is the one to keep.
Test titles are sentences that state the behaviour, so a failing title reads as the broken promise. bin/ci sets a per-test timeout, runs one job per CPU, and validates every schema's examples.

findings.title: Nothing holds kittui's fixtures of kit's stage JSON to what kit prints, and they have drifted
findings.claim: Go tests run kittui against hand-kept copies of each stage's JSON and bats runs kit against a fake kittui; only `kit syntax` output is checked across the two (tests/syntax.bats:283). Known since 11-10 (its line 1438), still open, now with confirmed drift, and no test runs the real kittui against the real kit.
findings.evidence: I dumped `kit <verb> <stage> --json` from the bats worlds for 16 app stages (out/S4/real, out/S4/keycmp.sh): audit-controls.json still has `"source": "ruleset"` and no `kind`, while kit prints `"kind":"ruleset","source":"github"` and fields.json:1014 reads `.kind`. 15 of the 16 fixtures lack `organization`, `repository`, and `source`, which kit prints on every row and the default view groups by.
findings.fix: Do for the stages what tests/syntax.bats:283 does for the grammar: one bats test per app verb compares the keys and JSON types of `.rows[]` with flow/testdata/<verb>-<stage>.json and prints the refresh command, then bats' expected rows and Go's fixtures become one file. Size M; touches audit, delivery, people, changes-app, issues, flow, workspace, packages, platform .bats and flow/testdata.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced. tests/audit.bats:163 passes (kit prints kind, source github); the fixture has source ruleset, no kind. keycmp: 14 fixtures lack all three keys, controls lacks two. Go runs only fake-kit (projects/tui/README.md:334), bats only fake-go/fake-kittui. The planned same-keys test (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-contracts.md:193) is absent. Fixture-only drift: kit and fields.json agree.

findings.title: The forge fixtures are a second, unchecked copy of the research schemas
findings.claim: The conformance tests do not use docs/integrations: 351 inline `fixture` heredocs and 451 routes in 23 bats files stand beside 79 schemas with 88 examples of the same tool answers, and bin/ci:53 checks each schema against its own examples only. Nothing says whether a fixture or a schema is right when they disagree.
findings.evidence: I captured every answer the fake gave in forge-conformance and forge-ado (344 distinct pairs) and validated them (out/S4/validate.mjs): of 42 schemas reached by a unique title, 12 reject a fixture. Not all are deliberate: `gh run list` rows have no required `attempt` (hidden by the fold's `.attempt // 1`), `gh run view` a job without `steps`, `az repos pr show` no `lastMergeCommit` or `forkSource`, `az pipelines runs list` no `definition`.
findings.fix: Add `fixture-from <tool>/<schema> [<jq edit>]` to tests/helper.bash, writing the schema's `.examples[0]` edited for the case, and have bin/ci validate the fixtures that stay inline by keeping the fake's answers as I did. Size M for helper and gate check, L to move all 351; touches tests/helper.bash, tests/fakes/fake-tool, bin/ci, the forge worlds.

findings.title: Four tests bound wall-clock time at 8 ms and fail under load
findings.claim: The unit gate holds four timed tests to 8 ms of wall time while `go test ./...` runs packages side by side and flow's 296 tests each start the bash fake several times, so a busy desk or small runner fails the gate with no defect. `loaded()` (flow_test.go:152) also does not check that the stages loaded, so a failed fake start surfaces as an unrelated assertion.
findings.evidence: `go test ./...` failed here at load about 70: `cost_test.go:61: ... take 19.665604ms, over 8ms` (table), `cost_test.go:231: ... take 15.885512ms, over 8ms` (flow), and `menu_test.go:465: with a row selected, hidden: show false, hide false` after 33 s. A second run of flow alone failed again at 11.45 ms; all three passed 3 of 3 when run by name.
findings.fix: Keep the structural halves (`&again[0] != &first[0]`) and state cost as work, with testing.AllocsPerRun or a count of rows visited per turn, leaving times to the existing benchmarks; make `loaded()` call t.Fatalf when a first load errs unasked. Size S; also one `best()` instead of two, and drop `raceEnabled` or add a `-race` run to bin/ci:76.

findings.title: Each bats file rebuilds the same worlds and helpers
findings.where: tests/forge-conformance.bats:21, tests/forge-ado.bats:22, tests/flow.bats:116, tests/tui.bats:20, tests/helper.bash:269, tests/audit.bats:19, tests/delivery.bats:18, tests/across.bats:57
findings.claim: The bats files hold 183 helper functions besides setup, and many are copies, so a change to what a forge tool is asked means editing up to ten worlds. A world is already nearly pure data (fixture and route lines) written as bash.
findings.evidence: `call()` is word for word in five forge files; `pty()` in flow.bats:116 and tui.bats:20 repeats helper.bash:269; `kit()` is in eight files while 68 files spell `"${kit_checkout}/bin/kit"` or `kit_root` out 1,557 times; `fake-tui` is in three files and inlined in five. `github-world` (o/r) is written five times and the ada, empowerite/example, issue 7 world ten times.
findings.fix: Move, do not rewrite: helper.bash gains `kit`, `seam` (today's `call`), `in_tracker`, `fake-tui`, `workspaces-file`, and files drop their copies. A world becomes a directory tests/fixtures/forge/<tool>/<world>/ of `routes` plus answers, the format fake-tool already reads, copied by `forge-world <tool> <world>`. Size M, about 25 bats files.

findings.title: "Every provider" is two providers in a loop and a third in its own file; the seam's calls are no table
findings.where: tests/forge-conformance.bats:244, tests/forge-conformance.bats:331, tests/forge-ado.bats:238, kit/modules/bash/forge.sh:309, kit/modules/bash/forge/gitlab.sh:494, kit/modules/bash/forge/ado.sh:418
findings.claim: 22 tests are titled "every provider" and 20 loop `for forge in github gitlab`; Azure DevOps is tested apart against its own copy of the expected documents. The seam's 60 calls exist only as prose in forge.sh's header (forge_call_since holds four), so no test can ask whether every call is tested for every provider.
findings.evidence: forge-ado.bats:238-252 repeats the expected literal and jq normalising of forge-conformance.bats:331-351. Counting `call <name>` over the six forge files (out/S4/matrix.sh): `pr-set-body` is tested for GitHub alone, never GitLab (gitlab.sh:494) or Azure DevOps (ado.sh:418), and `require` for no real provider; the 11-10 review's finding 28 named both, still open.
findings.fix: Write the contract once as data, kit/modules/forge.calls.json (call, since, feature, kind), read by forge.sh and by one bats test that fails when a provider implements a call no test names; put each expected seam document in tests/fixtures/seam/<call>.json for all three provider files. Table and matrix test S; shared expectations and worlds L.

findings.title: The gate neither fails on nor counts skipped tests
findings.claim: 23 places skip a test when a tool is missing, and bin/ci:75 reads only bats' status, which is 0 with any number of skips. A skip for a tool kit.yml pins means the toolchain is broken and should fail; other skips mean CI silently never runs the test.
findings.evidence: Skips by reason: opa 14, shellcheck 2, mise 2, just, actionlint, markdownlint-cli2, zsh, and `/bin/bash here is bash 4 or later` (loader.bats:235), which skips on every Linux runner. Which of mise and zsh skip on the runner under `ci_toolchain: kit` is plausible, not checked: the skip lines of one CI log would settle it.
findings.fix: Add `needs <tool>` to tests/helper.bash in place of the 22 hand-written `command -v … || skip` lines in nine files; under a variable bin/ci sets it fails for a pinned tool and skips otherwise, and bin/ci prints what skipped. Size S.

findings.title: Syntax fixtures cover 40 of 52 verbs, and the test walks the fixtures, not the verbs
findings.claim: tests/syntax.bats:283 loops over the fixture files, so a verb with no fixture passes, and form/fields_test.go:16 builds its specs from the same directory, so that verb has no form golden either. Known since 11-10 (issue #74, then 10 of 44), still open, now 12 of 52.
findings.evidence: `comm` of kit/bin/kit-* against projects/tui/internal/syntax/testdata gives twelve verbs with none: assign, close, facts, gather, ready, settle, trust, tutorials, unassign, uninstall, workspace, workspaces. Four of them (assign, unassign, close, gather) are verbs kittui's menus run.
findings.fix: Loop over `kit syntax --list` and fail for a verb with no fixture, printing the same refresh command. Size S; touches tests/syntax.bats and adds twelve fixtures and goldens.

findings.title: Verbs that change the forge are tested on the good path, and bash has no measure of what tests reach
findings.claim: `kit settle`, which closes issues and unassigns people, has one test, in a file about Azure Boards, and none of its failure branches is asserted; `kit ready` runs only in forge-stand-ins.bats. Go is held to every statement while the bash, most of the product, has no coverage figure, and test files follow verbs, modules, and features at once.
findings.evidence: grep of `could not be closed`, `could not be put back`, and `no pull request is named` over tests/ finds nothing, though issue.sh:164-184 and 286-338 and kit-settle:39 print them. By text search (out/S4/errcov.py, a lower bound), 198 of 448 `error` lines in kit/bin and kit/modules/bash have a fragment in any test.
findings.fix: Add tests/settle.bats with the failures as a table (which route fails, the line, the status), and likewise for close. Then add a weekly report, not a gate, that runs the suite under BASH_XTRACEFD and lists functions no test entered. Size S for settle, M for the report.

findings.title: Four fake kits re-implement kit's protocol, and the stage list is written five times
findings.claim: Four `testdata/fake-kit` scripts (312, 270, 104, and 28 lines) each stand in for kit, and two repeat the `--workspace` refusal word for word. The apps' stages are listed in both of those, in fields.json, and in kit/modules/bash/apps/<verb>.sh, with no test comparing them.
findings.evidence: flow/testdata/fake-kit:140 holds `app_stages` as a table and kit/testdata/fake-kit:189 the same lists as a `case`; kit's own are `audit_stages=(evidence findings controls waivers policy)` and its siblings. The flow fake is steered by 18 `FAKE_*` variables described in a 30-line header.
findings.fix: One internal/testkit/testdata/fake-kit answering from the directory the package names (`testkit.Runner(t, "flow")` already takes the name), with stages read from fields.json, and one line in S4-1's bats test comparing `kit <verb> --stages` with fields.json. Size M.

findings.title: Screen goldens repeat the chrome, and a mismatch prints the new screen, not the difference
findings.claim: Of 85 golden files, 45 are whole screens, so a change to the menu line or keys bar rewrites about 40 files and buries the change that matters. `Golden` reports the whole new text with no diff, and the 40 form goldens pin a function nothing but tests calls.
findings.evidence: 42 goldens hold the menu line and 41 the keys bar; testkit.go:193 is `t.Errorf("%s differs:\n%s", path, got)`. `RenderStatic` (render.go:56, "for golden tests") has no caller outside *_test.go (known since 11-10, finding 29), and README.md:326 leaves internal/tutorials, which has seven goldens, out of the `-update` command.
findings.fix: Print the first differing line with its number before the text; golden the pane alone for per-stage files with a `body(m)` beside `raw(m)`, keeping bar-120.golden as the one picture of the chrome; draw form goldens from the live `View()`. Size S for message and README, M for the split.

findings.title: A catch-all route answers any GraphQL query the world did not expect
findings.claim: fake-tool fails an unrouted call, but both conformance worlds end with a catch-all for `api graphql*`, so a query a provider adds or rewords is answered with the open pull requests or the milestones instead of being refused. Routes also tell queries apart by fragments of query text, in an order that matters.
findings.evidence: `route gh 'api graphql*' open-prs.json` (line 151) and `route glab 'api graphql*' "${GITLAB_MILESTONES:-gl-milestones.json}"` (line 212); more particular routes read `'api graphql*deployments(first: 50*'`.
findings.fix: Route each query by a name the provider gives it, such as the GraphQL operation name (`query OpenPrs(`), and drop the two catch-alls. Size S in the tests, one word per query in the providers.

findings.title: About 64 tests install the kit as set-up, and some tests are one slow loop
findings.where: tests/kit.bats:15, tests/materialize.bats:1, tests/welcome.bats:1, tests/packages.bats:1, tests/exits.bats:7, tests/helper.bash:11
findings.claim: helper.bash:11-13 advises building an installed repository once per file and copying it, and 13 files do, but five files still run a plain `kit install` inside tests where install is not the subject. Separately, a test that loops over every verb is one unit `--jobs` cannot split.
findings.evidence: Plain `kit install` runs: kit.bats 29, materialize.bats 13, welcome.bats 10, packages.bats 8, uninstall.bats 4; here an install took 2.0 to 2.7 s and `cp -Rp` of the result 0.05 s. exits.bats, one test running `kit help` for 52 verbs, took 85 s at load about 70; forge-conformance plus forge-ado took 121 s for 90 tests at 8 jobs.
findings.fix: Use `world-repo installed` in setup_file where install is only the first line; shard per-verb loops as template.bats:185 does, or register a test per verb with bats_test_function (plausible, not tried). Size S.

findings.title: docs/testing.md is a page about time, and leaves out part of the gate
findings.claim: The page's list of what `kit gate` runs omits the tutorials site's check and the every-statement rule for Go, its timing table has no row for the Go suite, and it says nothing of how the tests are built. That guidance lives in tests/helper.bash's header and projects/tui/README.md, which the page does not link.
findings.evidence: docs/testing.md:8-9 names lint, syntax, schemas, links, bats, Go tests, and kit check; bin/ci:71 also runs `npm ci && npm run check` in projects/tutorials and bin/ci:79 fails any function under 100.0%. The Go suite took 7 min 43 s here under load, flow alone 457 s and then 211 s, against go's 10-minute package limit.
findings.fix: Add the two missing steps, a Go row measured on a quiet machine, and a short section on worlds, fake-tools and routes, tests/jq, the fake kits, and goldens with `-update`, linking both sources. Size S.

areas.title: security
areas.coverage: Read whole: loader, kit-call, 1st.sh, log, trust, secrets, sources, resolve, materialize, file, serve (sh and jq), toolchain/kit, kit-trust/serve/tools, bin/release, workflows, agents packages, opener, browse.go, fix.go. In part: github.sh App code, forge.sh, release:fetch, yaml cache. Not read: GitLab/ADO providers, trackers, across.sh. Ran seven reproductions and shellcheck; no network.
areas.summary: Nineteen findings: 1 critical, 2 high, 5 medium, 11 low; seven reproduced by a run. The trust check fails open twice: a clone not trusted runs its own bash through git's core.worktree answer, and a folder with kit.yml and no .git (a downloaded zip) is trusted unasked. bin/release still writes a .sha256 with no digest, so no loader takes v0.1.0, and the digest check passes when both sides are empty. Before trust, kit appends its log through a clone's symlink, and kit trust can name another release than the loader runs. findings.md was not written: the Write tool refuses report files to subagents, so everything is in this result.
strengths: The loader is POSIX sh, checks trust before it reads what release a clone names, always runs kit trust on the installed release, and runs no git (kit/bin/kit:402-430).
A worktree gets its desk's trust only where the desk's own .git/worktrees entry names it back; a crafted .git file keeps its own name (kit/bin/kit:120-158, 1st.sh:87-108). I found no way round it.

kit serve refuses a NUL before the shell sees it, passes a client's words to jq on stdin or from files, builds the verb's words from a typed schema, refuses a word that acts, judges a path as both the kernel and a shell read it, and runs the verb with stdin at end of file.
Secrets never enter argv: the keychain secret goes in on stdin and is read back to prove it was kept, and the App's JWT and token reach curl through --header @-, the key only as a path openssl reads.
Every download is hashed before it is unpacked, unpacked apart, and moved into place only then; a runner refuses a tools.lock behind kit.yml.
The workflows pin each action to a commit, ask for read permissions and raise them per job, and use pull_request, not pull_request_target.
The yaml cache is mode 700 and used only while it and each entry are no link and owned by this user (yaml.sh:103-157).
kittui never hands a command to a shell: fix.Words refuses anything but plain words (fix.go:238-279).
forge:primary holds a remote's name to what git allows before it reaches git, and forge:host passes --end-of-options.
The documents say plainly what the deny list does not stop (docs/features.md:158-160, docs/architecture.md:248).

findings.title: A clone you have not trusted runs its own bash, through what git answers for its top level
findings.claim: kit help, kit version, and kit trust, the three verbs allowed before trust, ask `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (kit:enter and use:load-path), which answers from the clone's own .git/config. With core.worktree pointing at a folder beside the clone, that folder's kit.yml bash_path is sourced, so "kit runs nothing in a clone until you trust it" does not hold.
findings.evidence: In out/S5/work/bundle/repo (git config core.worktree ../../payload; payload/kit.yml names bash_path mods), with an empty trust file, `kit trust --check` printed "PWNED: code from the bundle ran as the user, before any trust" and exited 1 as not trusted; kit help --text and kit version ran the payload too. kittui runs kit trust --check by itself on opening; a git clone cannot deliver .git/config, an unpacked archive or synced folder can.
findings.fix: Run no git before the trust check passes: with --any-clone, kit:enter and use:load-path take the root from kit:clone-root, and ignore a root that is not at or above the working directory.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in verify-1/bundle with an empty trust file: kit trust --check, kit help --text and kit version each sourced the payload's modules; kit root was refused. No git hardening in the snapshot. It needs a delivered .git/config, and rides on S5-2's rule (kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:140): the payload is trusted because it is in no clone.

findings.title: A folder with a kit.yml and no .git is trusted without a question
findings.claim: kit:trusted-at succeeds outside a clone and the loader checks trust only where it finds a .git, so every kit verb, kit help included, sources the bash_path of a folder that is no clone. A forge's Download ZIP or a source tarball is such a folder.
findings.evidence: In out/S5/work/zipball (kit.yml with bash_path [kit:modules/bash/, mods], no .git, in no clone), `kit help --text` printed "PWNED: help.sh from an unzipped folder ran", and kit version and kit trust --check ran mods/yaml.sh and mods/help.sh. kit trust then refused the folder as "in no clone", so it cannot be asked about.
findings.fix: Honour bash_path, the gate, sources, and generate commands only where the folder holding kit.yml is recorded in the trust file, clone or not, and let kit trust record such a folder. Elsewhere load the release's own modules alone.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: in a kit.yml folder with no .git, kit help --text, kit version and kit trust --check sourced mods/*.sh; kit trust exits 2.
