But it is the designed rule (kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:137, tests/trust.bats:78), the promise names clones only, and it fires only in the folder holding kit.yml, not below it.

findings.title: The release publishes a .sha256 with no digest, so no loader will take v0.1.0
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open: pack calls release:digest, which nothing defines (the function is file:digest), so the .sha256 holds a file name and no digest and pack exits 0. Every loader, kit update, and every consumer's kit-ci.yml then refuse the release.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn release:digest kit bin tests` finds the call at bin/release:116 alone. The loader run against a .sha256 of that shape printed "kit 9.9.9's tarball has digest 68549c4d…, not the  its release publishes; it is not unpacked".
findings.fix: Call file:digest, fail pack when the digest is not 64 hex digits, and assert that in tests/release.bats.
findings.verdict_note: bin/release:116 calls release:digest; nothing defines it, no handler rescues it, errexit does not fire inside printf's argument, so the .sha256 holds no digest. kit/bin/kit:257-262, release.sh:125-131 and kit-ci.yml:94 then refuse. Narrower: kit update goes on without the base (kit/bin/kit-update:94, || true).

findings.title: The digest check passes when both sides are empty
findings.claim: The loader and release:fetch refuse a tarball only when the computed and published digests differ, and check neither for being a digest. With no sha256sum or shasum on PATH and a .sha256 whose first field is empty, as bin/release writes today, the tarball is unpacked and run unverified.
findings.evidence: With the S5-3 files, a fake curl, and a PATH without a sha tool, `kit --version=9.9.9 version` printed "shasum: command not found" then "UNVERIFIED tarball code ran: version", exit 0. With shasum on PATH the same run was refused.
findings.fix: Refuse unless both values match ^[0-9a-f]{64}$, in both places, and name the missing tool.

findings.title: Before any trust, kit appends its log through a link the clone controls
findings.claim: kit-call logs kit help, kit version, and kit trust in a clone not trusted, and log:write decides from the clone's own .kit/.gitignore and follows a symbolic link at .kit/logs/kit-YYYY-MMDD.log. A clone can commit both, so kit appends a line to, or creates, a file outside the clone.
findings.evidence: In out/S5/work/evil (not trusted, .kit/logs/kit-2026-1112.log -> ../../../victim/target.txt), after `kit trust --check` and `kit version` the victim file held "precious" plus two log lines such as "2026-11-12T04:40:23-0800 seconds=0.191 pid=67511 depth=0 status=0 in=. kit version". The yaml cache already refuses links and files this user does not own (yaml.sh:103-157).
findings.fix: Write no log in a clone not trusted, and in any clone refuse a .kit, .kit/logs, or log file that is a link.

findings.title: kit trust shows one release, and the loader runs another
findings.claim: trust:asks reads version from kit.yml with yq; the loader reads it with sed from a line starting version:, and falls back to .kit/manifest. Where they disagree, kit trust's list misstates what runs after a yes.
findings.evidence: In out/S5/work/quiet, with no version line and .kit/manifest "version unreleased", kit trust said the clone "asks kit to run nothing beyond the kit itself", and after trust `kit flow` printed "PWNED: the clone's own kit/bin/kit ran: flow". With kit.yml `"version": 0.1.0` it said "run kit 0.1.0, downloaded from its release and checked against its digest", and the clone's own kit ran again.
findings.fix: One reader for both: trust:asks takes the release as the loader's pinned gives it, manifest included, and says so when yq reads another value.

findings.title: A source whose digest is not a digest is read from wherever the digest points
findings.claim: sources:fetch refuses a malformed digest, but resolve:roots goes on after the failure and sources:roots builds the cache path from the digest as written, as bash_path's <source>:<dir> does. A digest with .. in it makes kit read packages from a folder no digest was checked against.
findings.evidence: In a trusted clone with `digest: "sha256:../../../../elsewhere"`, `kit packages --text` printed "the source team has no digest…" and then listed "planted  team  planted outside any cache, never digested". settings:validate does not apply the schema's digest pattern.
findings.fix: Have sources:rows drop, or the verb refuse, any record whose digest does not match ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, in the one place every reader goes through.

findings.title: A release is verified by the tagged commit's own script, and pinned by version alone
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open in the code: a pushed release/* tag runs the workflow and bin/release from the tagged commit, so the on-main check is the pusher's own code, and the .sha256 comes from the same release as the tarball. kit.yml pins the kit by version while it pins a source by digest.
findings.evidence: release.yml checks out the tag and runs bin/release verify then publish with contents: write; the loader fetches both files from the same release URL. Whether a tag ruleset exists could not be read offline (`gh api repos/empowerite/kit/rulesets` would settle it).
findings.fix: Add a tag ruleset for release/*, verify from the default branch's script, attest the tarball, and let kit.yml carry the kit's own digest.

findings.title: A tool counts as installed by its folder, not its digest, and every checkout shares the folder
findings.claim: Tools live at ~/.kit/tools/<name>/<version>/<platform>/; only place compares .kit-sha256 with the lock, while pins marks a tool installed where the file exists and path prints the folder unasked. Two checkouts locking the same name and version to different downloads share one folder, and the second shows and uses the first's binary.
findings.evidence: kit.sh:123 tests `-f …/.kit-sha256` alone; kit.sh:103-105 builds the path from name, version, and platform with no digest read. Confirmed by reading, not run.
findings.fix: Put the digest in the install path, or have pins and path compare .kit-sha256 with the lock as place does.

findings.title: The deny lists stop one spelling of each command
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open, and docs/features.md says an unlisted form passes. A one-letter change walks past: git checkout -B, git switch -C or --create, git branch -d -f, git -C <dir> commit; git merge, cherry-pick, revert, pull, am, restore, and clean are on neither list, and main is literal.
findings.evidence: The lists hold only "git checkout -b *", "git switch -c *", "git branch -D *" and the like. Not run against either harness.
findings.fix: Add the capital and long forms, render the default branch's name into the two desk entries, and say in .kit/1st.md what features.md says about unlisted forms.

findings.title: A link is handed to open or xdg-open whatever it is
findings.claim: shell.Browse and new:browse run open or xdg-open on any string, and a row's link reaches Browse as it is. A link from a forge's answer or a repository's provider that is file:, a custom scheme, or starts with - starts a file, an app, or is read as an option.
findings.evidence: browse.go:47 is `exec.Command(opener, url)` with no scheme check; forge.jq:810 takes a deployment's logUrl or environmentUrl, which a workflow or App sets; markdown.go:239 already tells http(s) from the rest. Not run; a row whose url is a file:// path to an .app would settle it.
findings.fix: Take http and https alone in Browse and new:browse, and show any other link to copy.

findings.title: Text from a forge reaches the terminal with its control characters
findings.claim: The text path prints cells with printf '%s', and no jq or bash module strips C0 controls from a title, login, or commit subject. A pull request title from a fork holding an escape sequence could set the clipboard or redraw lines for whoever runs kit flow --text.
findings.evidence: A search of kit/modules/jq and kit/modules/bash for any control-character filter finds only policy.sh:103, which holds the repository's own change titles to no control characters. Not run against a forge, and kittui's renderer was not tested; a fixture title with \u001b]0;x\u0007 would settle it.
findings.fix: Replace C0 and C1 controls in every forge string once, where forge.jq folds an answer.

findings.title: secrets:foreign turns any secret made of hex digits into bytes
findings.claim: A value of hex digits alone is taken for the keychain's hex encoding and run through xxd -r -p, so a foreign secret that is itself hex, as a 40- or 64-digit key, comes back as raw bytes. xxd is not checked for.
findings.evidence: `[[ "${value}" =~ ^([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})+$ ]]` then `xxd -r -p`. Confirmed by reading; the function has no caller at this commit.
findings.fix: Tell an encoded value by what the keychain says (security find-generic-password -g marks hex with 0x), or do not guess.

findings.title: secrets:put writes the service and the account unquoted into the line security -i reads
findings.claim: Only the base64 is safe for the one line security -i reads; the service and account go in with %s, so a space, quote, or newline in either becomes more words or a second command. The read-back catches a mis-stored item, not a second command.
findings.evidence: `printf 'add-generic-password -U -s %s -a %s -w %s\n' "$1" "$2" "${encoded}" | security -i`. No caller exists at this commit and security was not run.
findings.fix: Refuse a service or account that is not ^[A-Za-z0-9._:@/-]+$ at the top of secrets:put, secrets:raw, and secrets:delete.

findings.title: Two fetches of one source or release at once leave a stray tree/ in the cache
findings.claim: Both end with mv "${fresh}/tree" "${cache}"; when another process placed the cache meanwhile, mv moves tree into it. The loader's own fetch guards this.
findings.evidence: kit/bin/kit:275 has `[ -e "$2" ] || mv …`; sources.sh:117 and release.sh:141 have the bare mv. Not run.
findings.fix: Use the loader's guard in both.

findings.title: The log keeps every command line whole
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open: every argument of a kit call, and every word of a served tool call, is written to .kit/logs and kept 14 days. A URL with a token in its userinfo, or the words after kit tools run --, are there in full.
findings.evidence: kit-call:48 is `printf -v line ' %q' "$@"`, logged at line 68; serve.sh:604-605 does the same for a tool's words.
findings.fix: Drop a URL's userinfo and do not log what follows kit tools run.

findings.title: A remote on ssh.github.com sends the App's calls to https://ssh.github.com/api/v3
findings.claim: forge:of takes github.com and *.github.com for GitHub, while api-base takes github.com alone for api.github.com and treats every other host as an Enterprise Server. A remote on ssh.github.com, GitHub's SSH-over-443 host, gets a base that serves no API.
findings.evidence: forge.sh:470 `(github.com | *.github.com) forge=github`; github.sh:1274-1278 prints https://<host>/api/v3 unless the host is exactly github.com. Confirmed by reading; the bot calls have no caller at this commit.
findings.fix: Have api-base use the same host pattern as forge:of.

findings.title: bin/release retire reports 0 retired when gh could not list the releases
findings.claim: The loop reads from a process substitution of gh release list, which loses gh's status. A refused token gives no lines and the step ends with a green "retired 0 pre-release(s)", exit 0.
findings.evidence: `done < <(gh release list --limit 1000 …)` at bin/release:168, with no status check. Not run.
findings.fix: Read the list with list:read and fail when it fails.

findings.title: The loader points to a document that is not there
findings.claim: The loader's header says see docs/releases.md, and docs/ holds no such file.
findings.evidence: `ls docs` lists no releases.md; grep for it in docs/ finds nothing.
findings.fix: Write the page, saying what a release's digest does and does not prove, or drop the pointer.

areas.title: performance
areas.coverage: Read whole: bin/kit, kit-flow, 1st, forge, flow, across, render, materialize, generate, yaml, settings, marks; tui flow, kit, source, table/build. Ran shims, xtrace, tmux, benchmarks in copies; load average 37 to 75 inflates times. findings.md not written: the harness refused it. My first shim fork-bombed two minutes (04:36 local); real gh started once, offline.
areas.summary: Time goes to process creation, not to the seams' design. Text tables fork about 25 shells a row: 300 issues take 7,473 bash processes and 19 s of CPU, against 1.6 s for JSON. Every call parses its verb's grammar again (110 of 296 ms for kit flow), use forks per module, and the forge's provider is resolved on every call (47% of a picture's processes). kittui starts 11 to 17 kit processes to open an app, two or three in sequence before it draws, and a typed character lays out every record again. The yaml cache, loader, snapshot, source.Load, and cost tests are well shaped. Scripts and benchmark: out/S6/work/.
strengths: yaml.sh: one yq run per file's text answers every read, replayed with no process and never stale; yaml:get costs 0.4 ms where $(settings:value …) costs 3.8. Keep it and reuse its entry mechanism.
bin/kit runs one sed on the common path, and log.sh writes a line with no process.
materialize:hydrated lets a reading verb skip the full run: kit context is 39 bash processes and 224 ms of CPU. materialize:judge batches digests and readlinks; render:package memoizes.

The forge snapshot holds: issues and changes loading as two processes shared one pull-request GraphQL. The symlink lock names its process, and the marks' ETags are .etag files that forge:forget leaves.
flow:picture starts the forge stages in the background while it fetches, and across:start runs the members at once.
source.Load and source.Poll are small and right: a generation per read, the kept copy standing in, a poll that never asks twice at once; kittui loads every tab at once.

Rows and lines are cached between keys, cost_test.go holds View, a page, and a wheel turn to half a frame, and the renderers are a registry named by fields.json. S6-5 widens this cache; it does not undo it.
kit's calls from kittui run in a process group that ends with the screen.

findings.title: The text tables fork about 25 shells a row, so kit flow issues off a terminal takes 19 s of CPU at 300 issues
findings.claim: Every cell of a text row is drawn by a helper that prints and is taken as $(…), nested: flow:paint forks twice for out:sgr, and one painted, padded age is five forks; issues:draw has 26 command substitutions in its row loop. Text is what an agent, a pipe, and CI get.
findings.evidence: kit flow issues --fresh as text: 988 bash processes at 30 issues, 7,473 at 300 (19.3 s CPU, 23.0 s wall); the same 300 with --json: 254 processes, 1.6 s CPU. kit flow changes as text: 362 processes at 5 changes, 1,437 at 30 (5.0 s CPU).
findings.fix: S: give flow:paint, flow:cell, flow:age, flow:state-sgr, and issues:cell a form that sets a variable (printf -v), as yaml:get and materialize:bring do. M: one jq table function in kit/modules/jq/flow.jq over the rows and a column list (glyph, color, alignment, clip), used by issues:draw, flow:pr-table, flow:issue-row, builds:draw, releases:draw, and flow:checkout-block.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with a fake gh. kit flow issues --fresh as text: 967 bash processes at 30 issues, 6,992 at 300 (20.2 s CPU); --json at 300: 254 processes, 1.9 s CPU. kit flow changes: 362 at 5, 1,437 at 30 (4.4 s CPU). About 22 to 24 forks a row. Absolute times are macOS at load 80; Linux forks are cheaper.

findings.title: Every call parses its verb's grammar again from the comment header: about 110 ms of each kit flow call
findings.claim: guard:arguments runs help:values (awk and a jq that matches the 250-line header against the verb template), syntax:parse (a recursive-descent parser in bash), and a jq for the match, on every call, for a grammar that changes only with the release. kittui starts 11 to 17 such processes to open an app.
findings.evidence: Of the 6,416 bash commands kit flow --stages executes, 4,875 are in syntax:* (76%). In-process phases, least of 8 runs: guard:arguments 109 to 118 ms (help:values 56 to 67, use syntax 19, syntax:parse 17, the jq 12) of about 215 ms; the whole call is 296 ms of CPU.
findings.fix: Keep the compiled grammar per verb: bin/release writes libexec/syntax/<verb>.json and kit lint checks it against the header, or a cache entry keyed by the verb file's text, with yaml:entry and yaml:keep moved out of yaml.sh so both use one mechanism. guard:arguments is then one jq; size S to M.

findings.title: The forge seam works out the primary and the provider again on every call: 47% of a picture's bash processes
findings.claim: forge:call, forge:lacks, forge:snapshots, forge:stand-ins, and forge:none each call forge:provider, which calls forge:primary, forge:of, forge:named (forge:primary again), and use:modules piped to sort. forge_lacking and forge_stand_ins are memoized in a variable, but the callers ask inside $(…), where it dies.
findings.evidence: One call costs 15 bash processes for forge:provider, 25 for forge:snapshots, 55 for forge:stand-ins; one kit flow --json runs forge:primary 56 times and forge:provider 17. Memoized in the main shell (work/kit2, identical JSON): the picture 589 to 313 bash processes and 3,117 to 2,101 ms of CPU, issues 254 to 143, changes 156 to 102; one stage's CPU moved within the noise.
findings.fix: One forge:context, called by the verb in its main shell, that sets the primary, the provider, the URL, the snapshot directory, the lacking features, and the stand-ins as globals keyed by settings_file, which kit policy changes. The other functions read them; size S.

findings.title: kittui pays kit's start-up 11 to 17 times to open an app, two or three of them in sequence before it draws (in part known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: OpenApp asks each verb for its stages and open asks kit trust --check, one after another, before any load starts; the same runs inside Update on a switch to an app not made yet, which freezes the screen (11-10 component finding 13, still open). Each --cached read is a whole kit call that ends in cat, and the marks poll reads each verb's marks in a for loop.
findings.evidence: Flow on five tabs: 17 kit calls in 3.4 s, kit flow --stages 358 to 497 ms then kit trust --check 195 to 263 ms, the first load starting at 716 to 895 ms. Delivery: 14 calls, three in sequence (871 ms), then kit flow --marks 1,246 ms followed by kit delivery --marks 1,448 ms; a --cached read is 56 bash processes and 274 ms of CPU.
findings.fix: S: run OpenApp's and open's calls at once, and the marks of each verb at once. M: one bootstrap call (stages by verb, trusted, origin, workspace, each stage's kept JSON) read by a Runner.Open that is a source.Load, so an app opens at once on tabs that load.

findings.title: One cache generation for every stage: a typed character lays out every record again, and ↓ redraws every row (↓ known since 11-10, still open)
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/flow.go:235, projects/tui/internal/flow/flow.go:636, projects/tui/internal/flow/flow.go:1034, projects/tui/internal/flow/view.go:344, projects/tui/internal/table/build.go:65, projects/tui/internal/grid/panel.go:888
findings.claim: rebuild() drops the rows and lines of all stages on a typed character, a sort, a filter, any load, and a resize, and table.Build then draws every cell of every record though the query only filters; the line cache's key holds the cursor, so ↓ draws every row (11-10's row for #92). A load that lands lays the records out about five times, and grid.Every copies every row in each View at this commit.
findings.evidence: My benchmarks at 160×50 under load: a typed character and its View 66.8 ms and 44,921 allocations at 300 rows, 193 to 422 ms and 116 MB at 2,000, 1,559 ms and 628 MB at 10,000; ↓ 19.9, 51.4, and 427 ms; a load landing 52.7, 353, and 1,492 ms; View 17.5 MB a frame at 10,000. The profile at 2,000 rows puts 70% in table.Build (Lay 45%); cost_test.go has no test of ↓ or of typing.
findings.fix: Three tiers per stage, each with its own key: the cells laid out (data, login, renderings), the rows shown (panel, width), and the window's lines, with the cursor's band and the picked marks applied as the window is drawn. rebuild takes a stage, issues depending on changes; M for the first two tiers, M for the window.

findings.title: use forks once per module
findings.claim: readarray -t files < <(use:find "${module}") starts a process for each module a verb loads, 18 for kit flow, to run a three-line loop.
findings.evidence: With the loop inline (work/kit3) the 18 modules load in 57 to 63 ms, from 131 to 154 ms, and kit flow --stages takes 234 to 256 ms of CPU, from 297 to 313 (19% less); kit version 136 to 147, from 159 to 161.
findings.fix: Fill files in use itself, or give use:find a form that fills a named array, as list:read does. Size S, an hour.

findings.title: The sub-reads of one answer run one after another
findings.claim: forge/github:runs reads the jobs of the five newest runs with one gh run view each in sequence, flow:linked measures each linked worktree in sequence, marks:incoming runs git ls-remote per remote in sequence, and the marks poll reads each verb in sequence. None depends on the one before.
findings.evidence: kit flow worktrees --json started 66 git processes for eight worktrees, about seven each, in order; the trace shows run view after run list. The time is not measured, since my forge and remotes answer at once: a timed run against a real repository would settle it.
findings.fix: Start each in the background into the scratch directory and wait, as flow:picture and across:start already do; in Go, a goroutine per verb. Size S each.

findings.title: builds and releases each spend a forge request to ask who the caller is before they read
findings.claim: builds:documents and releases:documents call forge:require, on GitHub a real gh api user, only to see it succeed; issues and changes do not, and their reads say the same remedy. forge/github:repo is likewise one gh repo view per process, which the snapshot does not share.
findings.evidence: A fresh open of Flow made 10 requests at the fake: api user 2, run list, run view, releases, repo view, issue list, GraphQL 2, rate_limit, then 3 conditional requests for the marks. Two of ten are the pre-flight, on every load and refresh.
findings.fix: Drop forge:require from the two stages, and keep the repository's name beside the snapshots, in the directory named for the URL. Size S.

findings.title: kit flow --marks reads marks no app draws: a git status per linked worktree, every minute
findings.claim: marks:stages computes a mark for every stage of the flow setting, but kittui's Flow draws neither desk nor worktrees and Repositories reads kit workspace --marks. The poll runs once a minute and after every stage that loads.
findings.evidence: kit flow --marks started 11 git processes with no linked worktree and 19 with eight, one git status --porcelain=v2 each; the screen showed five tabs, without desk and worktrees.
findings.fix: kit flow --marks [<stage>…], the stages kittui names, as forge:marks already takes its kinds. Size S.

findings.title: Nothing removes a stage's kept JSON
findings.claim: flow:stage-json keeps a file under kit/flow/ in the common git directory for each stage, checkout, and set of arguments, and a grep of kit/modules/bash and kit/bin for kit/flow finds the writer alone. A removed worktree's files and those of every filter ever typed stay.
findings.evidence: Two runs of mine, with and without --no-fetch, left incoming-2154062707.json and incoming-373129187.json. I did not read kit tidy whole, which would settle it.
findings.fix: kit tidy removes the files of checkouts that are gone, or the writer drops files older than a week, as yaml:cache does. Size S.

areas.title: release, CI, and the toolchain
areas.coverage: Read whole: .github/, bin/{ci,release,refresh,tutorials}, root configs, tools.lock, toolchain.sh and all nine providers, loader, kit-call, kit-tools/ci/gate, release.sh, releases.sh, tui.sh, toolchain and install docs. Sampled 1st.sh, file.sh, terminal.sh. Ran 12 reproductions in a throwaway copy. No network: SHAs, tap, mise, rulesets unchecked. findings.md not written (Write refused report files).
areas.summary: v0.1.0 can be tagged and published today, but not installed: bin/release pack calls an undefined release:digest, exits 0, and publishes a .sha256 with no digest, which the loader, kit update, and every consumer's kit-ci.yml refuse (reproduced; known since 11-10, still open). The Homebrew install has nothing behind it in the tree. New here: a cached tool download is installed without re-checking its digest; bash 4.4, the stated minimum, breaks the terminal probe; retire exits 0 when gh fails; the loader refuses a version shape kit release accepts; tools are staged across file systems. Every action is SHA-pinned, and the digest checks fail closed. findings.md was not written: the Write tool refused it.
strengths: Every `uses:` in the three workflows and the template is a 40-hex SHA with its version beside it (four actions, eight uses, none by tag); permissions are read-only at the top of kit-ci.yml and Settle alone asks for issues: write.
The digest check fails closed in all three readers: the empty digest of S7-1 was refused by the loader and by shasum --check, never unpacked.
tools.lock pins every download for four platforms by sha256, a runner refuses to lock (kit.sh:299-304), and the lock agrees with tools: in kit.yml line for line (52 of 52, checked).

The loader is POSIX sh, runs before bash 4.4, jq, or yq exist, stages a fetch beside its destination, counts its hops, and refuses an older bash with the command that installs a newer one (seen under /bin/bash 3.2).
bin/refresh builds the result in a copy of the index and reads it into the real one once, so a failed render leaves the index as it was.
bin/release verify fails safe (a default branch it cannot read refuses a release), and publish refuses a release at a desk.
kit ci runs the two judgements before any of the branch's own commands, and runs every check even after one fails.
bin/ci fails on any function below 100% coverage rather than on the total, and gives each bats test a time limit.
file.sh keeps one EXIT trap per process and file:replace writes whole or not at all; bin/release's own traps are set first and kept by file:trap.
The toolchain pages match the providers: the detection table in docs/toolchains.md agrees row by row with usable and active in each provider.

findings.title: bin/release pack publishes a .sha256 with no digest, so no machine can fetch the release
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. pack calls release:digest, which nothing defines; as a printf argument its failure is not seen, so pack exits 0 with a digest file holding only the file name, and publish uploads it.
findings.evidence: Run: `bin/release pack release/0.1.0` printed `release:digest: command not found`, then `packed`, exit 0, file content `"  kit-0.1.0.tar.gz"`. The loader then said `tarball has digest af240440…, not the  its release publishes; it is not unpacked`, and `shasum --check` (kit-ci.yml:94) exited 1; the test greps the file name only.
findings.fix: Call file:digest, refuse a digest that is not 64 hex in pack, and assert the digest in tests/release.bats. Have the release workflow fetch its own release through the loader before it reports success.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with the fake go: `release:digest: command not found`, then `packed`, exit 0; the .sha256 is `"  kit-0.1.0.tar.gz"` and `shasum --check` exits 1. Nothing defines release:digest. kit/bin/kit:252, kit/modules/bash/release.sh:125, and kit-ci.yml:94 all refuse it. Narrowing: mise and the by-hand gh install never read the .sha256.

findings.title: The install the README leads with has nothing behind it in this tree
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open in this tree. `brew install empowerite/tap/kit` is the README's only install, and nothing here writes, bumps, or tests a formula; the release notes name mise alone.
findings.evidence: bin/release and release.yml hold no word of a tap or formula. 11-10 found the tap repository empty with gh api; I had no network to ask again, which is what would settle it.
findings.fix: Have the release workflow open the tap's bump and install from the tap in a job before v0.1.0 is announced. Until then lead with the download by hand.
findings.verdict_note: Tree facts hold: README.md:78 and docs/install.md:22 name the tap; bin/release, release.yml, and tests hold no formula; notes name mise only. But docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-release-readiness.md:29,341 put the formula in the tap's own repository by decision (step unchecked). Whether brew install fails needs `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents`.

findings.title: A cached download is installed without its digest being checked again
findings.claim: toolchain/kit:fetch returns at once when a cache file named by the pinned digest exists, so the stated guarantee (other bytes are refused, nothing installed) holds for fresh downloads only.
findings.evidence: Run: tools.lock pinned `hello` at 1111…1111, other bytes planted at ~/.cache/kit/downloads/1111…1111; `kit tools install --toolchain kit` printed `hello: 1.0.0 installed`, exit 0. The installed file hashes to 59ba60a6…, its .kit-sha256 says 1111…, and `kit tools` shows it installed.
findings.fix: Hash the cached file before using it; on a mismatch remove it and download again.

findings.title: On bash 4.4, the stated minimum, the terminal probe dies and leaves the terminal's answers unread
findings.claim: terminal:collect expands EPOCHREALTIME, which bash has only from 5.0, under nounset; log.sh:78 guards it and this does not. terminal:ask has already written its queries to the tty, so on 4.4 (RHEL 8) kit tui, help, flow, welcome, tutorials, and workspace print an error and leave the replies for kittui or the shell to read as keys.
findings.evidence: Run with the variable unset, as on 4.4: `terminal.sh: line 278: EPOCHREALTIME: unbound variable`, status=1, out=''. With it set: status=0, out=$'\E[?62;c'.
findings.fix: Take the time through log:now, and run the terminal suite once under a real bash 4.4.

findings.title: Dependabot's pull request can never pass, here or in any consumer
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. Dependabot bumps the installed kit-ci.yml, never the template under kit/packages/github/ci/, so kit check fails; the group puts every bump in one pull request, so one such bump fails the week's update.
findings.evidence: Run: after changing the checkout SHA in the copy's kit-ci.yml, `kit check` gained the finding `.github/workflows/kit-ci.yml differs from the pinned release; run: … kit update`.
findings.fix: Ignore kit-ci.yml's actions in Dependabot and bump the template by hand or by a job. Say in docs/packages/github/ci.md what a consumer does with Dependabot.

findings.title: bin/release pack packs the working tree, never the tag, and publish does not ask that the tag exists
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. pack reads its tag for the version alone and copies kit/ from disk, so a desk pre-release ships uncommitted and untracked files; without --verify-tag, gh makes a missing tag at the default branch's head.
findings.evidence: Run: `bin/release pack release/0.1.0` succeeded in a repository with no such tag. The gh part is from gh's documented behaviour, not run.
findings.fix: Pack from `git archive "${tag}"` and pass --verify-tag. Drop the desk path for pre-releases, or have the workflow skip a tag whose release exists.

findings.title: retire reports success when it could not list the releases
findings.claim: The loop reads `gh release list` through a process substitution, whose failure errexit never sees, so a bad token, a rate limit, or an outage reads as nothing to retire, with a green run. `--limit 1000` is also a silent ceiling.
findings.evidence: Run with a gh that prints `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` and exits 1: `bin/release retire some-branch` printed `retired 0 pre-release(s)` and exited 0.
findings.fix: Read the list into a variable first and fail when gh fails. Say when the list is at its limit.

findings.title: Under pipefail, retire reads SIGPIPE as 'no branch reaches it' and deletes a pre-release branches reach
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (rated low there), still open. `git branch --remotes --contains | grep --quiet` ends grep at the first line; when git has more to write than the pipe holds it dies of SIGPIPE, pipefail fails the pipeline, and the code falls through to `gh release delete --cleanup-tag`.
findings.evidence: Run, 20 times each: 100 branches kept 20; 400 branches (14 KB) kept 20; 3000 branches (107 KB) would delete 20 of 20.
findings.fix: Capture git's output and test it afterwards, or use `git for-each-ref --contains --count=1`.

findings.title: Tools and fetched releases are staged under TMPDIR and moved across file systems; the loader stages beside the destination
findings.claim: The loader unpacks beside its cache so the move is a rename and skips an existing destination; toolchain/kit:place, toolchain/kit:fetch, and release:fetch stage in /tmp and mv, a copy where /tmp is tmpfs (Fedora, Arch, Debian 13). An interrupted copy can leave a half tool that already holds .kit-sha256 and counts as installed, or a partial download named by its digest.
findings.evidence: By reading: place writes .kit-sha256 into the staged tree (line 390) before the move (391), and line 368 takes its presence as installed; release.sh:141 moves into an existing directory when another process fetched first. Settling it needs a Linux machine with /tmp apart from home and a kill during install.
findings.fix: Stage beside the destination in all three, as the loader does, and write .kit-sha256 after the move.

findings.title: kit release and bin/release verify accept a pre-release version the loader and kit update refuse
findings.claim: releases:valid allows a hyphen inside the suffix, and the suite asserts release/1.2.3-rc-2 verifies; the loader's is_version and release:fetch allow letters, digits, and dots only. Such a pre-release is tagged and published, and no kit.yml can pin it.
findings.evidence: Run: `kit --version=0.1.0-rc-1 version` answers `--version names '0.1.0-rc-1', which is not a kit version`, exit 1.
findings.fix: One definition of the shape, the stricter one, for all four places, and a test that the loader fetches every shape kit release takes.

findings.title: A release carries no proof of where it came from, and verify is the tagged commit's own script
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open in this tree. The .sha256 is an asset of the same release, so it proves the transfer only; release.yml has no attestation step, and verify runs from the tag's checkout, so an edited commit brings its own verify.
findings.evidence: By reading release.yml: checkout, trust, cache, tools, verify, publish, and nothing else. Whether a tag ruleset for release/* exists I could not ask.
findings.fix: A tag ruleset, actions/attest-build-provenance on the tarball, and verify run from the default branch's bin/release.

findings.title: A pre-release pushed by its tag alone is retired by the next deletion of any branch
findings.claim: kit release supports and announces a tag whose commits no remote branch has; retire runs on every branch deletion and deletes every pre-release no remote branch reaches, where the README says 'when the branch it was tagged on is deleted'. kit-ci.yml downloads the pinned release on every run, so a consumer pinned to it fails at once (that part known since 11-10).
findings.evidence: By reading: releases.sh:87 prints 'reachable from <tag> alone'; bin/release:160-165 tests only `git branch --remotes --contains`, for every pre-release, whatever branch was deleted.
findings.fix: Retire only pre-releases the deleted branch reached, or keep a pre-release until a later release of the same version exists.

findings.title: The Settle job cannot write for a fork's or Dependabot's pull request
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. Settle runs on pull_request closed and asks for issues: write, but such runs get a read-only token and no secrets, so kit settle can close or reopen nothing there.
findings.evidence: From GitHub's documented behaviour for pull_request events from forks and Dependabot; not run.
findings.fix: Run Settle on pull_request_target with the base branch's checkout, which runs none of the pull request's code.

findings.title: The kit toolchain checks for curl and tar, and its own lock needs xz, bzip2, and unzip
findings.claim: require and usable ask for curl and tar only, while the lock unpacks .tar.xz, .tar.bz2, and .zip. GNU tar runs the xz and bzip2 programs, which slim images lack, and the failure is 'could not be unpacked' with no remedy.
findings.evidence: By reading: tools.lock pins shellcheck as .tar.xz, parallel as .tar.bz2, gh on macOS as .zip; kit.sh:399-400 hands them to tar and unzip unchecked. Not run on Linux.
findings.fix: Before unpacking, check the program the URL's ending needs and name it through guard:missing.

findings.title: A lock that fails part-way leaves the other platforms' downloads in the cache
findings.claim: toolchain/kit:lock removes other platforms' downloads after its loop, and a failed fetch returns before that, so a moved Go pin whose last platform fails leaves three archives of about 70 MB each that nothing removes.
findings.evidence: By reading: line 316 `digest=$(toolchain/kit:fetch …) || return 1`; the removal loop is at 322-325.
findings.fix: Run the removal on the failure path too.

findings.title: bin/tutorials writes an empty catalogue, exit 0, when the content directory is not there
findings.claim: Both page loops read find through a process substitution, so a find that fails is an empty list, and kit generate would write it into kit/modules/tutorials.yml.
findings.evidence: Run with a project that has audiences.yml and no src/content: `find: …/src/content: No such file or directory`, then the audiences and `tutorials: []`, exit 0.
findings.fix: Refuse a project without src/content, as the header says every unlistable file is refused.

findings.title: The gate fails without a word when gofmt finds a file
findings.claim: `test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"` discards the list it tested, so an unformatted Go file ends the gate with only 'the gate failed: bin/ci' and no file name.
findings.evidence: By reading line 76; lines 79-85 show the pattern the coverage check uses to name what failed.
findings.fix: Print the list and the remedy before exiting.

findings.title: The release fetch is written four times and the copies have drifted
findings.claim: The loader, release:fetch, and the CI and Settle jobs (30 identical lines each) each fetch, compare, and unpack a release. The workflow uses shasum alone where the others take sha256sum or shasum, reads version: with its own sed, and the staging differs.
findings.evidence: By reading: kit-ci.yml:94,162 `shasum --algorithm 256 --check`; kit/bin/kit:202-207 and file.sh:197-201 try sha256sum first. A runner without perl's shasum is told the tarball lacks its published digest.
findings.fix: Have the workflow fetch only the loader and let it fetch the pinned release, or share the step with a YAML anchor. Have release:fetch use the loader's logic.

findings.title: apt, dnf, and pacman are one provider written three times
findings.claim: The three files differ only in the name, the command, and the tool-to-package table; the other eleven functions are the same.
findings.evidence: `diff apt.sh dnf.sh` shows only the name, `apt-get`/`dnf`, and the case table in the package function.
findings.fix: One system-package provider over a table of manager, command, install command, and package names, so a fourth manager is a row.

findings.title: The README's setup runs direnv before the clone is trusted, and never says to trust it
findings.claim: The once-per-clone block runs `direnv allow`, then kit commands, and has no `kit trust`; both kit calls in .envrc are refused in an untrusted clone.
findings.evidence: Run in an untrusted copy without a terminal: `kit tools path --toolchain kit` and `kit hydrate --quick` each print `kit runs nothing in … until you trust it`, exit 1. What direnv then shows, and whether it reloads unasked, I did not run.
findings.fix: Put `kit/bin/kit trust` before `direnv allow` in the block.

findings.title: The release and retire workflows have no time limit and no concurrency group
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open. A hung step runs to GitHub's six hours, and two branches deleted together start two retire runs over one list, where the second `gh release delete` of a tag fails its run.
findings.evidence: By reading: neither job has timeout-minutes or concurrency; kit-ci.yml sets a timeout on both of its jobs.
findings.fix: Add timeout-minutes to both, and a concurrency group on retire with cancel-in-progress false.

findings.title: Small disagreements between the documents and the scripts
findings.where: kit/bin/kit:66, README.md:253, kit/bin/kit-tools:31, docs/toolchains.md:124-125, bin/release:133-135, bin/release:88, bin/ci:28-38
findings.claim: kit/bin/kit names docs/releases.md, which is not in the tree; README says the tarball adds `libexec/kittui` from `tui/` (known since 11-10); kit-tools and the kit tools table leave out the kit toolchain; the release notes say to pin in mise.toml where install.md says the person's own config.
findings.evidence: `ls docs` has no releases.md; kit-tools:31 reads 'mise, nix, brew, docker, devcontainer, or ambient'. Also bin/release:88,149,160 name `origin` where git:default-branch reads the primary remote, and bin/ci's globs leave .kit/packages/house unvalidated.
findings.fix: Correct each line as named.

areas.title: consistency across the whole product
areas.coverage: Read whole: loader, 1st.sh, help.sh, apps.sh, glyphs.json, 5-terms.md, docs/apps.md, apps.go, style.go; 30 of 52 help pages in full, every Exits paragraph. Ran all verbs with --help and a bad flag, 57 probes, 261 documented commands through kit syntax --match. Not read: tests, tutorials site, forge providers, most Go logic.
areas.summary: The product is consistent where one source drives it: all 52 verbs answer --help with 0 and an unknown flag with 2, and help lines share one tense. It drifts where a fact is typed twice. Nine options still take their value as the next word, against 31 written --name=<value>. The app catalogue, the glyphs outside glyphs.json, and the provider lists are each declared by hand in several places and already disagree. kit workspace and kit flow re-implement apps.sh. "change" and "pull request" name one thing. Not delivered: findings.md. The harness refused the write as a report file and I did not route around it, so the full terms table exists only in short form in S8-13.
strengths: The verb header is the single source for help, usage, the argument guard, kittui's form, and completion: all 52 verbs answer --help with exit 0 and an unknown flag with exit 2 in one wording, with no per-verb parsing. Do not move help out of the headers.
Exit codes hold to one scheme, 0 done, 1 could not, 2 usage: 47 of 52 Exits paragraphs state it and all 52 verbs follow it for a usage error by test.
glyphs.json with kit:generate regions into flow.sh and glyph.go is the right pattern; S8-2, S8-6, and S8-14 ask for more of it, not less.
forge:noun gives the forge's own word and sigil where a message names one change. Keep it.
apps.sh with a module per verb is a clean seam: six verbs are three lines each, and a stage is two functions.
Every help line is lower case, third person singular present: 52 of 52.
Every remedy carries cd <folder> &&, so it runs from wherever it is pasted; S8-10 is about where that lives, not whether.
258 of the 261 distinct kit commands the documents show are accepted by the verb's own grammar, placeholders and abbreviations aside.
The provider seams under modules/bash/{forge,tracker,toolchain,policy,dependencies}, listed by use:modules, and the loader in POSIX sh apart from the bash it runs, are well shaped.

findings.title: An option's value is written two ways, and the two are not accepted alike
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-assign:5, kit/bin/kit-close:5, kit/bin/kit-commit:5, kit/bin/kit-gather:5, kit/bin/kit-syntax:6, kit/bin/kit-tools:5, kit/bin/kit-welcome:7, kit/bin/kit-work:6, kit/bin/kit-submit:34, kit/modules/bash/help.sh:343
findings.claim: Ten usage lines write nine options with the value as the next word (--to, --duplicate-of, --message, --file, --title, --choices, --toolchain, --fix, --pr) while 31 distinct options are written --name=<value>. An option written with a space accepts both forms, and one written with = refuses the next word.
findings.evidence: `kit syntax assign --match -- --to=bob 7` and `-- --to bob 7` both give status 0, while `kit syntax facts --match -- --moment commit` gives "--moment needs a value"; `kit welcome` has `--fix <check>` beside `--keep=<check>`. `kit help` shows `kit commit --message '#42 area: subject'` and `kit submit x` answers `kit commit --message=<text>`; the documents write --message with a space 64 times and with = once.
findings.fix: Rewrite the ten usage lines to =, which the guard, the form, and completion follow, then the mentions in documents; have `kit syntax --check` refuse `--name <value>` in a usage line. Size S; known since 11-10 (Command line, finding 22), still open for these nine.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: ten usage lines, nine space-form options, each taking both forms; `kit facts --moment commit` and `kit welcome --keep bash` exit 2. Narrower: kit workspaces joins the next word for its ten = options (kit/bin/kit-workspaces:91-113); the asymmetry is documented grammar (kit/modules/bash/syntax.sh:14). I count 30 = options and 38 spaced --message in *.md, not 31 and 64.

findings.title: The app catalogue is declared in at least six places, and two already disagree
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/apps.go:25, projects/tui/internal/shell/shell.go:38, kit/modules/bash/workspace.sh:15, kit/modules/bash/apps/issues.sh:20, kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json:70, docs/apps.md:9, projects/tui/README.md:44
findings.claim: Which apps exist, with their names, glyphs, verbs, and tabs in order, is typed by hand in seven bash modules, twice in Go, in glyphs.json, in each verb's header, in two documents, and in two tutorials.
findings.evidence: `kit workspace --stages` prints `repos remotes branches worktrees commits tags`, kittui's Repositories draws repos, worktrees, branches, commits, tags, remotes, incoming (apps.go:28), and docs/apps.md:9 says --stages prints "in the app's tab order". glyphs.json:74 names a group `delivery` holding incoming and releases, while the Delivery app holds releases, builds, artifacts, environments, deployments.
findings.fix: One kit/modules/jq/apps.json, [{app, glyph, verb, tabs:[{stage, verb}]}], read by apps.sh in place of <verb>_stages and <verb>_elsewhere and embedded by kittui through the kit:generate mechanism that already carries the glyphs. The document tables and the tutorial's list become generated regions; size M.

findings.title: An app verb is implemented three times
findings.claim: Six verbs are three lines over apps:main, but kit workspace carries its own copy of that body in about 170 lines and kit flow a third, with the kittui hand-off block repeated four times.
findings.evidence: `kit delivery releases --json` answers "releases is printed by another command; run: kit flow releases --json", and the same case `kit workspace incoming --json` answers "unknown argument 'incoming'". workspace:text (workspace.sh:203) and apps:text (apps.sh:203) are the same jq with one name changed.
findings.fix: Add kit/modules/bash/apps/workspace.sh with workspace_stages, apps/workspace:<stage>, mark functions, and workspace_elsewhere=([incoming]='kit flow incoming'), so kit-workspace shrinks to the three lines the others have. For kit flow take out only the hand-off, as apps:handoff; size M.

findings.title: A relative <path> is read from the root by two verbs and from the working directory by four
findings.claim: `kit new file <path>` and `kit region <path>` read a path relative to the repository root, while kit lint, context, kinds, and generate read it relative to the current directory.
findings.evidence: In a subdirectory of a hydrated copy, `kit new file probe.md --title=Probe` printed "made probe.md" and wrote <root>/probe.md. The next command there, `kit lint probe.md`, printed "'probe.md' is not a file or a directory here", exit 2.
findings.fix: kit new file and kit region resolve a relative path from kit_invoked_in, which kit:enter exports for this, and print the path from the root. Size S.

findings.title: The request to merge has two names, and the glossary defines the one the product types least
findings.where: kit/packages/kit/files/repo/.kit/welcome/5-terms.md:103, kit/bin/kit-ready:37, kit/bin/kit-settle:39, kit/modules/bash/across.sh:140, kit/modules/bash/flow.sh:1384, kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json:19, projects/tui/internal/flow/act.go:54
findings.claim: "change" names the verb, the app, the stage, the glyph, and the forge-neutral messages, while the help pages, the glossary, and kittui's menu say "pull request". The JSON carries both, and `change` has a second meaning in kit flow incoming.
findings.evidence: Help pages say "pull request" 73 times in 12 pages and use change as that noun about 28 times; `kit help ready` says pull request and its refusal says "name the change: kit ready <number>". forge:noun exists with six callers, yet kit-settle:39, across.sh:140, and flow.sh:1384 hard-code "pull request"; an issue's row has `pr` and a review's row has `change`.
findings.fix: "change" wins: add it to 5-terms.md as a pull request on GitHub and Azure DevOps and a merge request on GitLab, write it in the help pages, and keep forge:noun where a message names one change. Rename the issue row's `pr` to `change` and incoming's `change` before the JSON is released; size M.

findings.title: Some glyphs carry two meanings and some meanings two glyphs, all outside the one glyph table
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-packages:11, kit/bin/kit-packages:43, projects/tui/internal/style/style.go:22, projects/tui/internal/shell/books.go:43, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:172, kit/bin/kit-toolchains:15, kit/modules/bash/apps.sh:207, projects/tui/internal/opener/open.go:38, kit/modules/jq/glyphs.json:35
findings.claim: glyphs.json holds 41 glyphs and 8 states and generates the bash and Go tables, but about 45 more glyphs are literals, and every clash is among those or between those and the table.
findings.evidence: `kit help packages` says "✅ marks an active package" at header line 11 and "🟢 active" at line 43, and `kit packages --text` prints ✅ and ❌ where the table has 🟢 and ⛔. ⭐ is latest release in the table and favorite in books.go:43 beside ★ in kit-workspaces:172; 📌 is tag and the chosen toolchain; 📚 heads a single member though 📘 is a repository; folder is 📂 and 📁, search 🔎 and 🔍; 🏃 and 🚦 have crossed labels.
findings.fix: Give glyphs.json sections for the app menu, forms, welcome, and text verbs, generate the constants as now, and add a test that no glyph has two meanings unless an entry says alias. Then use 🟢 and ⛔ everywhere, one favorite glyph, and 📘 for a member; size M.

findings.title: A list printed as JSON has four shapes, and one verb changes shape with its arguments
findings.claim: A list is one object a line, a bare array, {rows, errors}, or an object with a named list, depending on the verb. Time fields and outcome words differ between stages too.
findings.evidence: Measured with jq -s: `kit packages --json` is 20 lines of objects and `kit packages packages --json` is {rows, errors}; toolchains, tools, kinds, and policy --rules print lines; `kit flow issues --json` is an array and {rows, errors} under --workspace=. Times are `age` in flow and delivery and epoch `at`, `merged`, `last`, `due` in changes, people, issues; outcomes are passed/failed/pending, running/passed/failed/cancelled, and success/failure; `goneBranches` is the one camel-case key.
findings.fix: {rows, errors} wins, since kittui and the workspace merge already need it: the five line-printing verbs print that document under --json. Name one outcome vocabulary in modules/jq/forge.jq; size M for the five verbs, L with kit flow.

findings.title: The kit options are documented where no command prints them
findings.claim: --workspace=<workspace>, --version=<release>, -v=<release>, and -- are described only in the loader's header, which no help page shows.
findings.evidence: `kit help` prints "USAGE  kit <verb> [<argument>…]" and names no option. Eleven help pages lean on "kit --workspace=<workspace> <verb>, the kit option before the verb", and `kit help update` on `kit --version=0.2.0 update`.
findings.fix: help:overview prints a KIT OPTIONS block read from the loader's header, `kit help kit` prints it as a page, and the usage line reads `kit [<kit-option>…] <verb> [<argument>…]`. Size S.

findings.title: One condition gives different messages and exit codes in sibling verbs
findings.claim: The bash style says the same condition gives the same message everywhere, but settle, ready, and linked answer a missing or malformed change number three ways, and an unknown name or missing path exits 1 or 2 by verb.
findings.evidence: With no change named, settle says "no pull request is named…; run: kit settle <number>" and exits 2, while ready and linked say "name the change: …" and exit 1; `kit ready abc` refuses "'abc' is not a number" with 2 and `kit settle abc` asks the forge first. `kit toolchains use nonexist` exits 1 where an unknown verb, package, tutorial, or workspace exits 2, in five wordings; a missing path is 2 in lint and generate and 1 in template fix.
findings.fix: Two guards in 1st.sh, guard:number and guard:unknown <kind> <name> <choice>…, both exit 2, and one function in forge.sh that names this checkout's change or refuses in one wording. Size S.

findings.title: Error lines come in five shapes, and kittui reads the command back out of the prose
findings.claim: The order of remedy and reason is not fixed, and the line is also a machine contract: out:remedy rewrites every `run: ` and kittui's fix.Command cuts the command out again by punctuation.
findings.evidence: Of 461 error call sites, 69 are `run: <command> (<why>)`, 64 are `<why>; run: <command>` (14 with no separator), 34 end in a see of four spellings, 122 give a remedy in words, and 168 none. kit-linked:131, "run: kit linked again once the tracker answers (…)", parses as a command with prose in it, and projects/tui/README.md:66 says kittui never parses kit's text while fix.Command and progressOf (internal/kit/kit.go:515) do.
findings.fix: One function in 1st.sh, refuse <why> [--run=<command>] [--see=<page>], that writes the line remedy first as guard:missing already does and hands the command to a JSON caller as {error, run}. Move the 133 call sites with run: first; size M.

findings.title: Two apps are not named for their verbs, and two verbs differ by one letter
findings.where: projects/tui/internal/flow/apps.go:28, projects/tui/internal/flow/apps.go:33, projects/tui/internal/shell/shell.go:51, docs/apps.md:215, kit/bin/kit-people:1, kit/bin/kit-issues:1
findings.claim: docs/apps.md:3 says each app's verb is named for it, but Trust's verb is kit audit while kit trust is another verb, and Repositories' verb is kit workspace, one letter from kit workspaces, which does something else.
findings.evidence: apps.go maps shell.Trust to "audit" and shell.Repositories to the workspace verb, and docs/apps.md:218 has to add "Its verb is not kit trust, which trusts a clone". `kit people agents` lists bots though the glossary's agent is a coding agent, and `kit issues` lists milestones and iterations and refuses `kit issues issues --json`.
findings.fix: Before the names are released, rename kit workspace to kit repositories, make the Trust app and its verb one word (Audit, or a renamed verb), and name the People stage bots. Each is a verb file, its app module, one catalogue row, and the documents; size S each.

findings.title: A verb's actions are spelled three ways
findings.claim: An action is a word in some verbs, a flag in others, and in kit workspaces an option whose value is the thing acted on, so like things read unlike.
findings.evidence: `kit packages add style/bash` against `kit workspaces --add=team repo`, `kit toolchains use mise` against `kit workspaces --use=team`, and `kit trust --list` against `kit packages`. `kit workspaces --rename=<name> <new-name>` puts the subject in the option and the new name in the operand.
findings.fix: An action is a word and an option only modifies: `kit workspaces (new | add | remove | rename | delete | use | show | favorite | unfavorite) <name> …` and `kit trust (list | check | revoke)`. kittui builds these words in internal/workspaces/workspaces.go:366-405; size M.

findings.title: The glossary and the product use different words for five things
findings.claim: The glossary says application, defines a toolchain as the tools a tool manager installs, and has no entry for change, provider, or member, while the product says app, calls the manager a toolchain and a provider, and uses all three undefined words.
findings.evidence: Counts as help/docs/kittui: app 1/54/213 against application 1/6/0; stage 181/74/1002 against tab 31/48/609; desk 54/88/79 against root checkout 7/4/0 and main checkout 1/3/0; toolchain 61/247/15 against tool manager 1/3/0 and provider 26/86/14; kittui 43/65/168 against kit tui 9/7/9. projects/tui/README.md:47-53 writes `kit issues <tab>` where every usage line writes <stage>, and `kit toolchains` "lists each manager" under a column headed provider.
findings.fix: Winners: change, app, stage (tab only for the widget kittui draws), desk, forge, toolchain, workspace with group and member, kittui, bot for an automation account, preset, refuse. Add one line each to 5-terms.md for app, change, provider, and member; size S.

findings.title: Lists of providers are typed into headers, and one has lost the kit toolchain
findings.claim: The help of kit toolchains and kit tools lists the toolchains by hand and omits kit, the toolchain this repository's own CI uses. Five app verbs say the source is github or gitlab where it may be ado.
findings.evidence: The header says "They are mise, nix, brew, docker, devcontainer, or, for the system, apt, dnf, or pacman", and `kit toolchains` in the copy prints `kit  project  ✅  📌`. modules/bash/toolchain/kit.sh exists and kit.yml sets ci_toolchain: kit.
findings.fix: A kit:generate region in each header, filled from use:modules 'toolchain/*' and forge:providers, as kit-flow's legend is filled from glyphs.json. Size S.

findings.title: Small errors of fact in headers and documents
findings.where: kit/bin/kit:66, kit/modules/jq/backlog.jq:5, kit/modules/jq/underway.jq:5, docs/integrations/git.md:60, kit/bin/kit-check:10, kit/bin/kit-check:26, kit/bin/kit-flow:1
findings.claim: Three see: lines name files that do not exist, one document names a flag that does not exist, and five Exits lines leave out an exit code the verb gives.
findings.evidence: A check of every see: path found docs/releases.md, modules/bash/backlog.sh, and modules/bash/underway.sh missing; docs/integrations/git.md:60 writes `kit lint --all` and the flag is --all-files. check, gate, hydrate, update, and install each exit 2 on an unknown flag and document no 2; kit-check:10 says "a kit version other than the pinned release" where the code compares with the release that runs; kit help flow orders the stages two ways.
findings.fix: Each is a one-line edit. Add the see: path check to the bash rule kit lint runs, so a dangling one cannot return; size S.

findings.title: Help pages differ in small matters of form
findings.claim: Section headings, argument descriptions, and two menu items do not follow the form the rest of their kind has.
findings.evidence: `kit help` heads sections in capitals (USAGE, WORKFLOW) and a verb's page in title case (Usage, Description, Group); of 151 flag descriptions 84 start with a verb and 67 with a noun, and --json is described in 13 wordings. kittui's menus are in title case but for "Share with team" and "Copy to mine", and `kit help commit` prints --all one column left of the lines under it.
findings.fix: One case in help:page, a line in the verb template that an argument's description starts with a verb, and the two menu items. Size S.

findings.title: The preset operations exist twice in kittui, word for word
findings.claim: flow.Model and table.Sheet each implement keep, keepStarred, star, favor, save, rename, and delete with the same messages; Flow is the one screen not drawn through table.Sheet. The code still says view for what every string calls a preset.
findings.evidence: " saved the preset ", " renamed the preset ", " deleted the preset ", and "%s the preset could not be %s: %v" appear in both flow/views.go (274-381) and table/sheet.go (848-943). I did not trace what else Flow's model needs from the sheet, so the size is a guess.
findings.fix: Flow's stages hold a table.Sheet each and views.go goes, with view renamed to preset in the table package as part of it. Size M to L.

areas.title: the tutorials site
areas.coverage: Read whole: projects/tutorials (all but the lock file), bin/tutorials, tutorials.sh, tutorials.yml, the nine shipped pages, kit-tutorials, docs/tutorials.md, both bats files. Ran in a copy: catalogue (current), bats 27/28 (one needs projects/tui), own probes, node on build.ts/version.ts/entry.ts. Not run: npm ci, tsc, vitest, vite build (no node_modules, no network). No dist in the snapshot.
areas.summary: 13 findings: 1 high, 3 medium, 9 low. The site itself is sound; the four site bugs of 11-10 are fixed. Still open from 11-10: nothing publishes the site (T1-1), and the catalogue region's "is this kit's source" test (T1-4). New: `<Since>` tells readers to run a plain `kit update`, which moves nothing (T1-2), and the catalogue accepts a duplicate id (T1-3). No wrong exit code found in the verb. NOT DONE: findings.md was not written. The Write tool refused it ("Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files"), and I did not work around that with a shell redirect; everything is in this result. My probes are under out/T1/ (work/tests/t1-probe*.bats, node/probe.mjs).
strengths: One source for a tutorial's description: its page's front matter, read into kit/modules/tutorials.yml by a generated region, with generate --check in the gate and a test that the shipped catalogue is current (it is).
bin/tutorials refuses each bad input by file and reason, and every refusal has a fixture and a test, including eight shapes of a bad color.
The build checks what it built: verify fails on a missing or empty route, a dead href or src, and a link outside the base, each named once; build.test.ts breaks a whole dist one way at a time.
sinceState throws on a version that is not X.Y.Z, so a typo fails the build under its route; a pre-release of the passage's own version meets it (11-10 finding fixed and tested).
entry() settles hydrate, render, or leave in one tested function, and useReaderKit uses useSyncExternalStore so the first client render equals the pre-rendered page.
filled uses function replacements so `$&` in a page survives, and siteBase normalises a base and refuses a URL; both tested.

The verb's grammar and exit codes hold in every case run: --json with a tutorial, --text with --json, a second tutorial, an empty or unknown --tag, and an unknown tutorial exit 2; a missing catalogue or shipped page exits 1; a failed or missing opener warns, prints the link, and exits 0.
package.json pins exact versions, package-lock.json agrees with it, and fsevents is denied its install script.

findings.title: Nothing publishes the site, so the online tutorial's link points nowhere
findings.claim: Known since 11-10, still open: `kit tutorials kit-tutorials` opens https://empowerite.github.io/kit/tutorials/<line>/kit-tutorials/, and nothing in the tree builds or deploys a page there. Nothing sets TUTORIALS_LINE either, so no build of a release line exists.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows holds only kit-ci.yml, release.yml, retire-pre-releases.yml, none naming Pages or tutorials; bin/tutorials takes `catalogue` only, where docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-tutorials-2-published.md calls for `bin/tutorials publish` and a workflow. Whether the address answers could not be checked offline.
findings.fix: Carry out the publishing plan before the release, or ship 0.1.0 with kit-tutorials as a markdown page in the kit and no online tutorial. Derive TUTORIALS_BASE and TUTORIALS_LINE from one value in that workflow.
findings.verdict_note: The tree leaves no doubt. .github/workflows has three files, none naming tutorials or Pages; no deploy-pages or gh-pages outside the plan. bin/tutorials publish|site|retire each print the usage and exit 2 (bin/tutorials:95-100). TUTORIALS_LINE is set only in a test. Not checked: whether the address answers. One tutorial, kit-tutorials, is online.

findings.title: <Since> tells a reader on an older kit to run `kit update`, which moves nothing
findings.claim: The page says "To upgrade, install kit X or later, then run `kit update`", but a plain kit update runs the release kit.yml declares and leaves the repository on it. The line was added after 11-10.
findings.evidence: kit/bin/kit-update:7-9: "the release to move to is named with the kit option: kit --version=0.2.0 update. A plain kit update runs the declared release, and brings every delivered file back to it"; README.md:185 gives the same command.
findings.fix: Print `kit --version=<version> update`, change the README sentence, and have the test assert the command.

findings.title: The catalogue takes two tutorials with one id; `kit tutorials <id>` prints both and opens a broken URL
findings.claim: An online page <id>/index.mdx and a shipped page <id>.md share an id space, and catalogue() never compares them. The verb then holds two entries for one id.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with the `shipped` fixture plus shipped/beta.md: catalogue exits 0 listing beta twice; `kit tutorials beta` exits 0, prints "🧭 The screens", a blank line, "🅱 Beta" and the link, and hands the opener a URL starting with a newline. `--choices '<tutorial>'` lists beta twice.
findings.fix: Refuse a second page whose id is already listed, naming both files, and add the fixture.

findings.title: In a repository with its own projects/tutorials, the catalogue region fails or runs that repository's bin/tutorials
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (item 25), still open in a new shape: the region decides it is in kit's source by `[[ -d projects/tutorials ]]`, while its header promises "a bin/tutorials of the repository's own is never run".
findings.evidence: Reproduced in a fresh repository carrying the release at kit/: with an empty projects/tutorials, `kit generate --check kit/modules/tutorials.yml` exits 1 ("bin/tutorials: No such file or directory"); with its own bin/tutorials, `kit generate` runs it and rewrites the region to `audiences: []`, `tutorials: []`, exit 0.
findings.fix: Test for something only kit's source has (projects/tutorials/audiences.yml beside bin/tutorials and kit/bin/kit), or leave the directive out of the release's copy.

findings.title: The build's link check reads `src=` and `href=` in a page's words as attributes and fails the build
findings.claim: verify matches /\s(href|src)=…/ over the whole file, text included, so a tutorial that shows HTML, JSX, or MDX cannot be built, and the message names an attribute the page does not have.
findings.evidence:
node on verify: an article holding `
<img src="logo.png">
` gives `src=""logo.png">" has no file`; the sentence "set src=./in and dest=./out" gives `src="./in" has no file`.
findings.fix: Match attributes inside tags only, or parse the HTML; add both cases to build.test.ts.

findings.title: Two failures in `bin/tutorials catalogue` end in exit 0
findings.claim: find runs in a process substitution, so its failure is lost; and a page whose front matter yq reads as a scalar makes jq fail inside `[[ … ]]`, which skips the page with no file named.
findings.evidence: With src/content missing: find's error, then a catalogue with `tutorials: []`, exit 0 (kit generate would write it over the region). With an MDX file of plain words: "jq: error … Cannot index string with string", exit 0.
findings.fix: Read find into an array and stop when it fails; refuse front matter that is not a mapping, naming the file.

findings.title: Front matter is parsed four ways, and they disagree on a closing fence with a trailing space and on CRLF
findings.claim: bin/tutorials uses yq, bin/ci one awk, tutorials:page another awk, and the site remark-frontmatter; the catalogue lists pages the page printer cannot split.
findings.evidence: A shipped page closed by `--- ` is listed by yq with all fields, and `kit tutorials <id>` prints the title line and nothing else, exit 0. A CRLF page is listed too, and its front matter prints as text.
findings.fix: One function for the front matter and the body, used by the catalogue, the gate, and the printer; or have the catalogue refuse a page the printer cannot split.

findings.title: The site's home page and the catalogue order tutorials differently when one id is a prefix of another
findings.claim: byOrder says it sorts "as the catalogue does … by path, which is its id", but the path is the id plus `/`, which sorts after `-` and `.`. Its test compares nothing with the catalogue.
findings.evidence: With equal order, node gives `kit-tutorials/ kit.next/ kit/`; jq's sort_by([.order, .id]) gives `kit kit-tutorials kit.next`.
findings.fix: Compare ids (the path less its slash) and test with `kit` and `kit-tutorials`.

findings.title: The catalogue lets through what the schema and the site refuse
findings.claim: The gate holds only the site's .mdx pages to frontmatter.schema.json; the nine shipped pages are held to four fields. An online page may also take the id `changelog` or `whats-new`, which the site's fixed routes use.
findings.evidence: `order: first` in a shipped page is listed as `order: "first"`, exit 0. A page at src/content/changelog/index.mdx is listed with `path: changelog/`, giving the site two routes at that path.
findings.fix: Validate kit/modules/tutorials/*.md against the schema in bin/ci, and have bin/tutorials refuse the two reserved ids.

findings.title: An empty catalogue file makes `kit tutorials --json` print an empty line and exit 0
findings.claim: An empty read is taken for an answer: where the header promises one JSON object, nothing prints. It needs a hand-made or truncated catalogue, since the shipped one is generated.
findings.evidence: With KIT_TUTORIALS_CATALOGUE naming a zero-byte file: `--json` status 0, output empty; `--text` says "no tutorials here". Broken YAML is refused with status 1.
findings.fix: Fail when yaml:json prints nothing, or default to `{}` so the object always has its four keys.

findings.title: `filled` keeps the generic title when the shell's <title> is not the one it expects
findings.claim: Both replace calls are silent when their marker is absent. verify catches a missing page later, but not a title, so an edit to index.html:6 leaves every pre-rendered page titled alike.
findings.evidence:
node: filled('Kit Tutorials
', …, '
p
') returns the shell unchanged.
findings.fix: Throw when either marker is missing.

findings.title: Prose that no longer matches: what a tutorial is, a script that is gone, a typed list of audiences
findings.claim: The one online tutorial and the site's README say tutorials are web pages whose buttons open in the browser, while nine of ten catalogue entries are markdown pages in the kit that open in kittui. reader.tsx cites scripts/verify-dist.mjs, which no longer exists, and kit-tutorials types the audience ids by hand.
findings.evidence: index.mdx:10 "kit's tutorials are web pages, one for each feature"; reader.tsx:24 "scripts/verify-dist.mjs fails a build…"; kit-tutorials:30 "newcomer, ui, maintainer".
findings.fix: Rewrite the two passages, point the comment at verify in src/build.ts, and drop or generate the ids in the header.

findings.title: The ordering rule and its default live in four places
findings.claim: "By order, 1000 when none, then id" is written twice in bin/tutorials, in byOrder, and in the schema's default; tutorials.sh sorts again by order alone, twice, relying on jq's stable sort. T1-8 is what this costs.
findings.evidence: bin/tutorials:75 and :85 `order: (.order // 1000)`; routes.tsx:71 `(a.order ?? 1000)`; tutorials.sh:76 and :111 `sort_by(.order)`.
findings.fix: Let the catalogue be the one place that sorts: tutorials.sh reads it in order, and the site compares ids.

areas.title: the Flow screen and the nine apps
areas.coverage: Read whole: README.md, docs/apps.md, docs/workspaces.md, 19 flow files (flow, act, menu, view, rows, legend, glyph, layers, apps, fix, watch), table/keys.go, auto.go, shell keybar/dropdown/search, all 25 goldens. Sampled table, grid, tabs. Not read: most of table, grid/panel.go, pane, tests. Built kittui, drove six tasks in tmux at 80/120/200 against fake-kit.
areas.summary: Candid verdict: the table engine (grouping, filters, saved views, frozen headings) is better than lazygit, k9s, or gh dash; the shell around it is slow and partly hidden by keyboard. A newcomer cannot find quit (q and esc do nothing), gets nothing from ⏎ on a row, needs 12 keys to start work on one issue, 6 to 8 to reach Fields or a preset, and cannot read why a pull request is blocked at 80 or 120 columns. One real bug: a kept @me filter opens an empty table. With a mouse it is good. findings.md was NOT written: the harness refused the Write of a report file, so everything is in this result.
strengths: The keys bar is derived from where the keyboard is (shell/keybar.go), not written per screen; in every state reached, what it named worked and it changed with the cursor (→ show, ← hide, ← group). Keep it.
Search: / then type then ⏎ narrows as you type, is kept per tab, survives an app switch, and recalls with ⌃R.

Error recovery on a stage: ! on the tab, kit's own line in red, and c copy / r run for the remedy it names (fix.go); a slow stage shows … and 'loading' while the others draw, and what kit kept draws first, stale, with a dot.

Selection and batch acts on Issues: ␣, ⇧↑↓, ⌃A, a heading selects its group, ▣ and ◩ say all or some, a row drawn under two groups counts once, a closing action lists its issues first, and every action is a kit verb.
Presets: the panel is remembered per stage across sessions and apps, the pill strikes its name through once the view differs, Save As… is one line, and the file is plain JSON.
The cross-app link with its crumb and ⌫ back returns the cursor to where it was.
The legend shows only the glyphs on the screen, in reading order, and moves out of the way; ? is one key.
At 120 and 200 columns the tables are dense and readable; the automatic step from words to glyphs is a good idea whose order needs tuning (U1-2), not removing.
A menu line's key is drawn on the line and works with the menu closed; a line that cannot act now stays, dim.
Spreadsheet habits carry over: frozen header, click a header for its card, click the rule to sort, filter chips, grouping.

findings.title: A view that filters by @me opens empty: nobody asks kit who the caller is
findings.claim: The caller's login is asked only when a card, a chip, or the issues tab menu opens (askMe), never in Init, so a remembered panel or saved preset holding author: @me matches no row.
findings.evidence: Run: tick @me on changes (row #3 shows), quit, start kittui flow, press 2: tab counts 3, chip reads 'author: @me', pane reads 'no row matches the panel' until the author's card is opened. Same on switching Flow to the Changes app in one session.
findings.fix: Ask kit flow --me once in Init (or when any opening panel holds @me), draw 'loading' until it answers, and say so on the keys bar when it fails. Adjacent to 11-10 finding 25, which is still open; this one is new.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a scratch test: tick @me, reopen over the same presets file: me="", asked=false, zero rows, "no row matches the panel", chip "assignees: @me"; opening the card restores rows. Init (flow.go:328) never calls askMe; OpenApp builds a new Model per app (apps.go:90,107). The reviewer's findings.md was missing; judged from the task text.

findings.title: Changes does not say why a pull request cannot merge at 80 or 120 columns, and opening the row adds nothing
findings.claim: State and checks step down to lone glyphs because threads has one 16-cell rendering that never steps; the open row lists only the issues closed, and the state words are kit tokens (failing:gate, no-check, blocked:approval).
findings.evidence: changes.golden (80) and a 120-column run show state as 🏁 🔨 🔥 and checks as ❌, while Issues at 120 shows '🔥 failing:gate'; the failing check's name appears only at 200 columns, clipped to '❌ lint failing 1 / …' beside about 48 blank title cells. Task count: '2 / login ⏎' = 3 keys + login for the state word, '= c ⏎ 3' more to reach the failing check in the Changes app.
findings.fix: Add one plain-words line per blocker to the open row's detail (failing check and counts, unresolved threads, waiting approval), give threads a short rendering '💬 2' that steps first, and make state the last column to step. Cap the title's share so no other column is clipped while it holds blanks.

findings.title: Nothing acts on the row under the cursor; starting work on one issue takes 12 keys
findings.claim: key() has no case for enter, every action but New… is dim until a row is selected, and the tab menu is one list of 23 lines mixing refresh, folds, selection, and eleven issue actions.
findings.evidence: Run from the start of kit flow: ↓×4 (control line, two group headings, first issue), ␣, :, s×5 or ↓×9, ⏎ = 12 keys, 20 with the switch to the Backlog preset. lazygit, k9s, and gh dash do the same with one key on the highlighted row.
findings.fix: With nothing selected, an action acts on the cursor's row, and ⏎ on a row opens a short menu of that row's actions with the likeliest first. Give Start Local Work a key as Assign to Me has 'a', and let ↓ from the control line land on the first row, not a heading.

findings.title: No key hint says how to leave; q and esc do not quit
findings.claim: Quit is ⌃Q, named only on the last line of the = menu; the keys bar never names it.
findings.evidence: Run: the bar reads '= menu - workspace / search ? legend │ …' on every screen; q did nothing and three esc left me on the tab bar. Only ⌃C got out, with 130.
findings.fix: Add Bind("⌃Q", "quit") to ScreenKeys, and take q as quit while the tab bar has the keyboard and nothing is typed.

findings.title: Fields and the presets have no key of their own; both sit behind a walk along the control line
findings.claim: f opens Fields only while the keyboard is on the preset pill; HeadingKey does not take it, the rows do not, and no key drops the presets.
