findings.evidence: Run on issues: '↓ ⇥⇥⇥⇥ f' = 6 keys from the bar and 7 from a row; switching to Backlog is '↓ ⇥⇥⇥⇥ ⏎ ↓ ⏎' = 8. Columns, sort, group, and Save As… took about 24 keys with a 4-letter name, against 7 clicks.
findings.fix: f opens Fields and p drops the presets from the bar, the control line, and the rows, both named on the keys bar (neither letter is a menu shortcut today). Let ⇧⇥ from the first stop wrap to the pill.

findings.title: A link is followed by a click alone, and a link to another tab's row is not marked
findings.claim: jump and openPage are reached only from click (and Open Selected for pages), and dotted() leaves a kittui: link as plain text, so nothing on the row says it leads anywhere.
findings.evidence: Run: a click on '7' in Trust's waivers jumped to controls, and a click on 🔀 in the Issues app opened Changes with '↩ issues' and '⌫ back'; no key did either. Known since 11-10 (finding 18), still open.
findings.fix: A key on the row (g, or ⏎ where the row menu is not taken) follows the row's first link and cycles where there are several. Underline a row link in the accent as a page link is underlined.

findings.title: esc does not clear a search, and a narrowed table does not say it is narrowed
findings.claim: A query stays through any number of esc, the tab still counts every row, and the empty message uses the code's word 'panel'.
findings.evidence: Run: '2 / jeff ⏎' left one row; 'esc esc esc' kept '🔎 jeff' and the one row with the tab reading 3; clearing took '/ ⌃U ⏎', and ⌃U is named only while the search has the keyboard.
findings.fix: esc on the bar or in the rows clears a query first; the control line's count reads '1 of 3' while a search or filter holds rows back. The empty line names what holds them, as 'no row matches "jeff"; esc clears'.

findings.title: At 80x24 the first row is on line 13 and an issue's title gets 8 to 11 letters
findings.claim: Twelve of 24 lines are chrome, four of them to say 'github · empowerite' to a person in one repository, and the default issues view spends its width on nine columns with the title last.
findings.evidence: issues.golden: menu bar, 3 tab lines, summary, blank, control line, rule, frozen heading, blank, header, rule; the row reads '▸ #1  🛫  jeffr…  8d  🔀 #2  🏁  🌿 here  p… +1  🎫 The firs…'.
findings.fix: Where every heading level has one value, draw the values on the control line and drop the frozen heading and its blank; drop the summary line under 30 lines. Under 100 columns open issues and changes on Compact, or hide labels and where before the title falls under 30 cells.

findings.title: The legend leaves out glyphs the screen draws, uses footnote marks it never explains, and takes four keys from the rows
findings.claim: Issues' legend has no line for the state glyphs it draws, 🔗 and † are never explained, the 18 stages of six apps have no row legend and an internal id in the title, and Home/End/PgUp/PgDn move the legend instead of the rows.
findings.evidence: legend.golden draws 🏁 🔥 🔨 💬 alone in the state column with no legend line for them; the run titled the box 'audit/findings legend'; README.md:168 says 'It takes no other key or click' while legendKey takes four. The glyph and title parts are known since 11-10 (finding 20), still open.
findings.fix: Add the states to issues' legend, end the box with '🔗 opens its page · † goes to its row', and title it with label(name). Move the legend by its arrows alone and give the four keys back to the rows.

findings.title: The title bar reads 'kit trust' and 'kit repositories', which are not the apps' commands
findings.claim: appLabel is "kit " + app, which is the opening command for seven apps and wrong for two.
findings.evidence: Run: Trust's title is '= kit trust', but kit-trust trusts a clone and the app's verb is kit audit (docs/apps.md:218 warns of this); Repositories' title is '= kit repositories' and kit/bin has no such verb (it is kit workspace).
findings.fix: Draw the verb (kit audit, kit workspace), or drop 'kit ' from the title and show the app's name alone.

findings.title: Seven of the nine apps only look; Changes has no action on a pull request
findings.claim: actions() returns lines on the issues stage and on packages and nothing elsewhere, so batch acts exist in two apps of nine.
findings.evidence: Run: the tab menu on changes ends at Open Selected. Acting on three issues works well ('↓↓↓↓ ⇧↓ ⇧↓ a' = 7 keys, 'kit assign #7 #46' ran), and a close lists the issues before it runs.
findings.fix: For 0.1.0 add Copy Links and Start Local Work on the branch to changes; Mark Ready (kit ready) and Rebase (kit rebase) are plausible, not checked against the verbs. Say in the README which apps act and which only show.

findings.title: The controls fixture and docs/apps.md still call a control's kind 'source'
findings.claim: kit prints kind and keeps source for the forge, but the fixture's rows hold source: protection/ruleset and no kind, so the tests draw a screen real kit cannot produce; docs/apps.md:247 repeats the old name and line 73 omits the Compact preset.
findings.evidence: kit/modules/jq/apps.jq:115 is 'del(.url, .source) + {kind: .source, …}'; the run grouped Trust's controls under '▾ source' with headings 'protection' and 'ruleset'. docs/apps.md:225 lists kind and line 26 defines source as the forge.
findings.fix: Regenerate the fixture from kit audit controls --json and correct both doc lines. Hold the app fixtures to kit's output with a bats test, as tests/syntax.bats holds the syntax ones.

findings.title: Tab means five things, and the arrows do not move along the tabs
findings.claim: ⇥ is next tab on the bar, next stop on the control line, a column scroll in the rows, leave in the search, and widen on a card; ← and → on the bar do nothing, and from the rows only a number changes tab.
findings.evidence: tabs.go's header says left and right 'have nothing to fold on it'; flow.go:856 scrolls columns on tab only while some are hidden. The keys bar names each meaning where it applies, which saves it.
findings.fix: ← and → move along the tabs while the bar has the keyboard; ⇧← and ⇧→ (or h and l) change tab from the rows.

findings.title: Small surprises in the Fields dialog and the menus
findings.claim: A field moves to another section of the list the moment it is grouped or hidden, with no undo; the rendering radio offers 'auto age' beside 'age'; a close confirms on ⏎; Save is dim on a built-in with no reason given; ⊘ is a circled glyph.
findings.evidence: Run: twice I hid the wrong field after the list reordered under the cursor, and the way back was choosing the preset again. 'esc no ⏎ yes' stood under 'Close these issues as not planned?'; ⊘ is known since 11-10 (finding 21).
findings.fix: Keep the cursor's line or flash the line's new place, drop the auto line where a field has one rendering, and make y the yes of a dialog that closes or deletes. Save on a built-in opens Save As…; rename the pair to 'Start Work on Each' and 'Start Work on All as One…'.

findings.title: The tab bar hides a fifth tab at 80 columns with no ▹ while the first tab is selected
findings.claim: The mark for more tabs is drawn with the second tab selected and not with the first, the screen kit flow opens on.
findings.evidence: changes.golden ends the bar's middle line with '│ ▹'; issues.golden ends it with '│' and the top line with a dangling '➄╶'. Repositories at 80 and 120 columns cut its last tab the same way in the run.
findings.fix: Draw ▹ in the bar's last cell whenever a tab is hidden or cut on the right, whichever tab is selected.

findings.title: README.md describes the Flow screen as 150 lines of nested prose with no table of keys
findings.claim: Lines 87 to 253 are one bullet of sub-bullets 10 to 30 lines long; accurate where I checked, but a person cannot find a key in it, and it counts 'six screens' then 'nine apps'.
findings.evidence: As line 100: 'The tab's view starts with the control line: the heading over the groups at its left, which, where the rows group by nothing, is the rows' ▾ and their count alone, and the preset line at its right end.'
findings.fix: Add a table of keys by where the keyboard is (bar, control line, rows, menu, dialog), a table of clicks, and the six tasks as worked examples. Move the mechanics under a 'How it is built' heading.

areas.title: an inventory of every action in kittui
areas.coverage: Read whole: README, shell, flow's key/menu/act/view/views/fix files, table's keys/heading/popover/columns/presets/manage/layers, screens, palette, app, form/model. Sampled welcome, tutorials, workspaces, opener, tabs. Not read: grid, pane, style, tests. Built kittui and drove Flow, palette, commit form, welcome, tutorials in tmux on fake kits. One ⏎ on a tutorial card ran macOS `open` on a fixture URL.
areas.summary: kittui is a careful, consistent table UI with a steep first ten minutes. The keys bar, menus, and shared table controls are good. A newcomer hits walls: ⏎ on a row and → on the tab bar do nothing, quit is not on screen, and a paste is dropped. Mouse users cannot select a row or answer an action's dialog; keyboard users need about nineteen presses to sort. Assign to Me (`a`) and Start Local Work for Each write to the forge with no question. Fix order: U2-1, U2-2, U2-4, U2-3, U2-5, U2-6, U2-12, U2-7. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refused report files; its full text is in findings_md.
strengths: The keys bar is computed from where the keyboard is, never written per screen; every key it named in the run did what it said, and it changed as the cursor moved. Do not replace it with static help.
One table everywhere: the nine apps, the palette, the welcome's tables, the tutorials, and the workspaces screen share one control line, Fields dialog, column card, presets menu, and search.

Menus keep the house rules: a line that cannot act is dim and stays, a line's key is at its right, the line for where you are is bold, a letter jumps to the next line that starts with it, and the bar under a menu names three keys.
esc never quits and always backs out one step; ⌃C always quits; consistent on every screen driven.
Plain clicks reach a lot: a tab, the selected tab's menu, a column's name, the dot under it (sort), a fold, a filter chip, the preset pill, the stale dot, a linked glyph, the legend's corner arrows.
The actions that do ask (Unassign, Close as Not Planned, Remove…, Make Only These Active…) list exactly what will change; the workspaces prompt adds a line to click.

What kit ran is echoed, what it did replaces the keys for five seconds, and a refusal stays until a key; a refused stage offers kit's remedy with copy and run by key and click, never through a shell (fix.Words).
The welcome guide is a good first screen: plain prose, each failed check with the command that fixes it, nothing runs until r or ▶️.
The legend lists only the glyphs on the screen under it and marks the ones a click leads from.
Tab numbers are dingbat digits chosen for a fixed one-cell width, and 1-9 jump from anywhere.
Nine tutorial pages on the screen's own parts ship with the kit.

findings.title: Two actions that write to the forge run at once, with no confirmation and no undo
findings.claim: Assign to Me (bare key `a`) and Start Local Work for Each run kit the moment they are chosen, though act.go:3-4 says an action that changes what others see asks first. With the real kit each `kit work` makes a branch, a worktree, a start commit, and a draft pull request, and assigns the issue (kit/bin/kit-work:8-18).
findings.evidence: Reproduced on the fake kit: `↓ ↓ ⌃A a` from launch ran `assign #7 #1 #8 #46 #31 #45`; `⌃A`, `:`, a click on Start Local Work for Each ran six `work #n` commands. The notice showed only `✅ kit work #45`.
findings.fix: Give both the confirm dialog Unassign already has, listing the issues and what will be made; keep `a` instant for one issue only or drop the bare key. Say how many commands ran in the notice.

findings.title: A paste is dropped in every field that types (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: Nothing handles tea.PasteMsg while Bubble Tea v2 turns bracketed paste on, so a commit message, a login, an issue number, a folder, or a preset's name cannot be pasted. This is Components finding 4 of the 11-10 review.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `/` then `tmux paste-buffer -p` of "lint" left the search as `🔎 ▏`, while typing `l i` gave `🔎 li▏`. `grep -rn PasteMsg projects/tui --include=*.go` finds none outside tests.
findings.fix: shell.Type takes a paste as typed text, and each screen routes PasteMsg to the control that types.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced on a build of the snapshot: in flow, `/` then `tmux paste-buffer -p` of "lint" left `🔎 ▏`; typing gave `🔎 li▏`; an unbracketed paste typed. A tea.PasteMsg sent to the commit form's text field left input empty. No PasteMsg or DisableBracketedPasteMode anywhere in projects/tui. It is Components finding 4 of the 11-10 review (line 1120).

findings.title: In the nine apps a row cannot be selected with the mouse, so no action on rows has a mouse path
findings.claim: Every tab-menu action acts on the selected rows, and Flow's click handler only moves the cursor, folds, or follows a link; the selecting click, BoxAt, is called from Sheet.click alone. A mouse user finds every action dim with nothing saying why, against the rule that every action has a plain click.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: clicks at columns 2 to 5 of the `#46` row left the control line without "1 selected" and the row without ▣. Select All is the only mouse route.
findings.fix: Call table.BoxAt in flow.Model.click as the sheet does, and draw a dim ☐ in the gutter of the row under the cursor.

findings.title: ⏎ on a row does nothing, and the actions ignore the row under the cursor
findings.claim: Model.key has no case for enter, so the most natural press on a table row is dead in all nine apps, and with nothing selected `o` and `a` do nothing and say nothing. Opening one issue's page from the keyboard is `␣` then `o`, and `o` is named only at the end of a 26-line tab menu that scrolls.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: cursor on `#7`, ⏎, `o`, and `a` each changed nothing and put up no notice. pages() and acting() read the selection alone.
findings.fix: ⏎ on a row opens its page, named `⏎ open` on the keys bar; with no row selected every action acts on the row under the cursor. A key that cannot act says why on the last line.

findings.title: The dialogs an issues or packages action opens take no click, and say nothing with key hints off
findings.claim: The ask layer has no Click, and a nil Click takes every click and does nothing, so a confirm, a picker, or a typed question opened with the mouse cannot be answered or dismissed with it. Its only cue, `esc no ⏎ yes`, is on the keys bar, which the Key hints setting hides.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with the mouse alone: the dialog "Close these issues as not planned?" ignored clicks inside and outside it; with Key hints off the last three screen lines were blank while it stood open. workspaces/prompt.go:125-133 already has a clickable `✅` line and click-off-closes.
findings.fix: Draw the ask with the workspaces prompt's pattern, and draw a dialog's keys on its bottom edge whenever the keys bar is hidden.

findings.title: Sorting, filtering, or opening Fields from the keyboard takes about twenty presses
findings.claim: `f` opens Fields only while the keyboard stands on the preset pill, and no key sorts or filters from the rows. A sort that is one click is 17 presses from the tab bar and 19 from the rows.
findings.evidence: Counted in the run on Issues: `↓ ⇥ ⇥ ⇥ ⇥ f`, `↓` nine times to age, `s`, `esc`; `f` on the bar and on a heading stop did nothing. Filtering to my issues is about 21.
findings.fix: `f` opens Fields from the bar, the control line, and the rows of every table; add `s` in the rows for a Sort By menu. Put Fields… and Presets… in the tab's menu.

findings.title: A menu draws its shortcuts in capitals, and the capital does nothing
findings.claim: Press lowers the menu's letter but Shortcut compares it with the press as typed, so the key as drawn (`R`, `M`, `N`, `A`, `O`, `W`) is dead, and Caps Lock silently kills every letter shortcut. The keys bar writes its letters in lower case, so the two places disagree.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with FAKE_FLOW_CALLS: `R` ran nothing (15 calls before and after), `r` ran `flow issues --json --fresh`; `M` did not maximize, `m` did.
findings.fix: Shortcut lowers a single-letter press before comparing, or the menu draws the letters in lower case.

findings.title: A verb's form takes no click, and no click opens a form from the palette (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: form.click answers on the menu bar alone and the palette opens a form on ⏎ alone, against the plain-click rule. Since 11-10 the palette's rows gained a click for the cursor and fold and the wheel; the rest of Components finding 10 stands.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on the commit form: a click on `--all` and one on the drawn `‹ verbs` did nothing.
findings.fix: Layout gives each field's lines so a click focuses a field and acts as ␣; `‹ verbs` and the command line take a click. In the palette a second click on the cursor's row, or a button on it, opens the form.

findings.title: In a form, ↓ skips the options drawn right under the cursor
findings.claim: A one-of or any-of group draws its options one under another, but ↑ and ↓ leave the group and only ⇥ and ⇧⇥ move inside it; ← and → do nothing.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on `kit commit`: cursor on `--message`, with `--file` on the next line, `↓` went to `<path>…`.
findings.fix: ↑ and ↓ move through a stacked group's options and leave it past its ends, as they already do in a pick list (model.go:537-548).

findings.title: The same letter does different things from screen to screen, and `r` within one tab
findings.claim: `r` is Refresh on a Flow tab, runs a refused stage's remedy once that line is selected, runs a check's fix in welcome (where Refresh has no key), and renames a workspace or a preset; `a`, `o`, `n`, `c`, `d`, `s`, `f` also change meaning by screen. `d` deletes a preset at once but asks first for a workspace.
findings.evidence: welcome/menu.go:22: "It has no key: r runs a check's fix here"; fix.go:75 takes `r` before the tab menu's shortcut. The full table is in findings_md under Answers.
findings.fix: Keep `r` for Refresh everywhere and run a command with ⏎ on its line; keep one letter per verb across screens and move the rest onto menu lines without a bare key.

findings.title: ← and → do nothing on the tab bar and on the tutorials' grid of cards
findings.claim: Tabs and cards lie left to right but move only by ⇥ and ⇧⇥, because left and right are kept for folding; a newcomer's first press on a row of tabs is →. The bar's hint `⇥·⇧⇥ tab` reads as "tab tab".
findings.evidence: Reproduced: → on Flow's bar left issues selected, and ⏎ on the bar did nothing. tutorials.go:553-571 has no left or right case.
findings.fix: Where nothing folds, ← and → move as ⇥ and ⇧⇥ do; name the bar's binding `⇥ next tab`.

findings.title: How to quit and where the keys are explained are not on the screen
findings.claim: The keys bar never names quit; `⌃Q` stands only on the `=` menu's last line and in a tutorial. `?` shows a legend of glyphs, not keys, and only in the nine apps, and the menu's ❓ Help opens the palette of verbs, so nothing points to the nine tutorial pages that explain the screen.
findings.evidence: In the run `q`, esc, and ⏎ on the bar did nothing; the welcome, tutorials, and palette keys bars showed no `?`.
findings.fix: End the screen's segment with `⌃Q quit`, make `?` work on every screen, and end the legend with a dim line pointing to = → Tutorials.

findings.title: At 80 columns the keys bar keeps the keys the title already shows and clips the ones that act
findings.claim: Path.Line keeps the screen's segment and clips the last segment's end, so about half the bar goes to `=`, `-`, and `/`, which the title line already draws as glyphs, while the keys of the control with the keyboard are cut.
findings.evidence: flow/testdata/issues-open.golden: `= menu - workspace / search ? legend │ … │ esc tabs ↑↓ move [] group ␣·⇧↑↓ sel…`; `→ show`, `← hide`, and `⌃A all` are lost.
findings.fix: When the path does not fit, drop the screen's segment first, then the middle ones, and clip the last segment only after that.

findings.title: A preset is deleted by one key, overwritten by Save As…, and an unsaved arrangement is dropped silently
findings.claim: In the presets dialog `d` or a click on Delete removes the person's preset at once with no way back; Save As… onto an existing name of theirs replaces it; choosing another preset drops a panel with unsaved changes. Deleting a workspace asks first.
findings.evidence: Read from the code, not run: views.go:395-400 calls deletePreset directly; table/views.go:216-217 does `saved[k] = now`.
findings.fix: Keep a deleted preset for the notice's five seconds with `u undo`; Save As… onto an existing name asks "replace X?". Keep unsaved changes as an "unsaved" line in the presets menu.

findings.title: esc in the rows throws the cursor and the scroll back to the top
findings.claim: esc, which a person presses to dismiss anything, also resets the place in a long table, so ↓ ↓ then starts from the first row.
findings.evidence: Read from the code: `s.Cursor, s.Offset, m.inRows = 0, 0, false`.
findings.fix: esc gives the bar the keyboard and leaves the cursor and the window where they are, as a tab's number already does.

findings.title: The palette does not filter as you type
findings.claim: `kit help` opens with the rows focused, and a letter does nothing until `/`, though no letter is bound in its rows and a command palette is expected to narrow on the first letter.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: `c o` left all five verbs and the cursor on commit.
findings.fix: A printable key in the palette's rows gives the search focus with that character typed.

findings.title: Moving a column has no click (known since 11-10, still open)
findings.claim: A column moves by ⇧↑↓ in the Fields dialog and ⇧←→ on a column's card, and by nothing else. This is Components finding 11 of the 11-10 review.
findings.evidence: Columns.Click (columns.go:285-318) and Popover.Click (popover.go:491-505) have no move target.
findings.fix: Move Left and Move Right lines on the card, and ▲ ▼ targets on the dialog's line under the keyboard.

findings.title: Small disagreements in what the screen says
findings.claim: The bar says `↓ groups` on a tab whose rows group by nothing; the Settings dialog ticks with ◼ ◻ where Fields and the cards tick with ☑ ☐; `⇞⇟ page` names keys by glyphs few people know, and kit ships for Linux too.
findings.evidence: Seen in the run on Changes (`▾ 3` on the control line, `↓ groups` on the bar) and in the Settings dialog.
findings.fix: Say `↓ rows` where the heading names no group, use one pair of box glyphs, and write `PgUp·PgDn page`.

findings.title: The README says the tutorials are tabbed by audience; the screen has no tab bar
findings.claim: README lines 25 and 274 say the tutorials are tabbed by audience, and line 275 lists `kit tutorials` among the screens that share the tab bar.
findings.evidence: The screen in the run and tutorials/testdata/tutorials.golden show a rule, a control line, and cards; audiences are a preset, By audience.
findings.fix: Say the cards are a table's rows, grouped by audience by a preset.

areas.title: first run: welcome, tutorials, the palette, and verb forms
areas.coverage: Read whole: README, docs/install.md, the five welcome pages, welcome/tutorials/help/syntax.sh, all non-test Go of the six packages. Sampled goldens and tests. Ran a first hour in tmux (120x40, 80x24) on a built kittui, a stand-in release, a throwaway repository, and a fake gh; go test -cover gives 100%. Not checked: the brew tap, Terminal.app.
areas.summary: The frame is good and consistent: one menu bar, one keys bar, esc never quits, nothing runs unasked. The first hour inside it is rough. One key sequence panics kittui. The forms of kit work and kit commit ignore space until Tab is pressed. The checks sit under 400 words of prose. The palette's search for "work" keeps 20 verbs. The guide never says what to do next. From the guide to a running kit work 7 took 34 key presses, against 11 in a shell. findings.md was not written: the Write tool refuses report files from a subagent, and I did not go around it, so the findings and strengths are all here; the Answers tables are not.
strengths: Nothing runs without consent: the trust question comes first and says what the clone asks kit to run; a check's fix is shown whole, c copies it, r runs it, and its output stays in the scrollback.
A failed check is one sentence, the exact command, and where to read more; an offer is kept apart from a failure, and kit install is an offer, not an error.
One frame on every screen: = menu, - workspace, / search, and a last line naming the keys that work now. esc never quits and ctrl-Q always does.
kit <verb> short of an argument opens that verb's form, which shows the command line it builds and leaves it in the scrollback, so the form teaches the command.
Help, the palette, the form, completion, and the argument check all read one source, the verb's header, through help.sh and syntax.sh. Keep it; do not replace it with per-verb form code.
The palette unfolds a verb's whole help in place, and /commit, Enter, Enter opens a form in nine keys when the match is near the top.
The shipped tutorials are short, concrete, and readable offline; screen.md is a good map of the frame, and each card says who it is for and whether it is in the kit or online.
A house package can replace or add a welcome page by its file name.
Every screen has a text form and a JSON form, so an agent and a pipe get the same facts.
All six Go packages are at 100% statement coverage, with goldens of the rendered screens.
The README is candid about what kit does not hold: the deny list's literal patterns, and CI alone binding every agent.

findings.title: PgDn, PgUp, Home, or End kills kittui on a welcome step whose search finds no check
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Apps 4), still open. page indexes rows[min(max(at+n,0), len(rows)-1)] with no guard for an empty step, and leaving the search sets inPane = true whether or not a row is left.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: kit, 2, /zzzz, Enter, PgDn prints 'Caught panic: runtime error: index out of range [-1]' at welcome.go:969 and kittui exits 1. The package is at 100% coverage, so coverage does not see it.
findings.fix: Return from page when len(rows) == 0, and give the pane the keyboard from the search only when it has rows. Add the test.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in a Go test on a copy: toolchains step, /zzzz, Enter leaves inPane=true with 0 rows and no sheet; PgDn, PgUp, Home, and End each panic "index out of range [-1]" in page (welcome.go:961-969). Up, Down, and Enter survive: down guards len(rows)==0, page does not.

findings.title: On a form's one-of row, space and Enter do nothing until Tab, and the forms of kit work and kit commit open on that row
findings.claim: enter sets a one-of row's cursor to f.Chosen, -1 while nothing is chosen, and pickOption returns when no option is under the cursor; the row still draws its focus mark on the first option and the keys bar says 'space choose'. After a choice no input line shows until another Enter, and that field has no mark and no label.
findings.evidence: In the form of kit work, 7 and space change nothing, Enter moves to the command line, and Enter again answers 'kit work needs <reference> or --title or --pr'; only Tab then space chooses. The tests assert it (model_test.go:109, model_test.go:162).
findings.fix: Put the cursor on the first option when the row gets the keyboard with nothing chosen, let Enter choose it, and draw the chosen option's input line at once. Where an alternative opens with an operand, let a typed character choose it and start its value.

findings.title: The checks of toolchains and setup stand under 464 and 260 words of reference prose, so a step opens with no result on screen
findings.claim: stepHead draws the whole page before the first check, and the pages are reference material a person needs only when a check fails. PgDn and space do nothing until the down arrow gives the pane the keyboard (welcome.go:963).
findings.evidence: At 120x40 toolchains opens with none of its five checks in sight (17 lines below a full pane); at 80x24 it is 42 lines below, and setup 25. All five toolchain checks passed on my run and the page still had to be scrolled to learn it.
findings.fix: Draw the checks first under a lead of two lines at most, the rest of the page after them, and move the precedence rules to docs/toolchains.md. Let PgDn and space scroll from the bar.

findings.title: The Homebrew install the README leads with may install nothing
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Documents 6: the tap repository was empty). Nothing in this tree holds a formula or a release step that writes one, so nothing here shows it was fixed, and it is the first command of the first hour.
findings.evidence: A search for homebrew-tap and formula over bin/, .github/, and kit/ finds only the brew toolchain provider. No network here; gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents settles it.
findings.fix: Publish a formula that depends on bash, jq, and yq before the release, or lead the README with the gh release download lines.
findings.verdict_note: The tree's part holds: no formula, no tap step in bin/release or release.yml. But docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-release-readiness.md:341 puts the formula in empowerite/homebrew-tap, after the 0.1.0 tag, still unchecked, so its absence here is expected. `gh api repos/empowerite/homebrew-tap/contents` settles it.

findings.title: No field of a form takes a click, '‹ verbs' takes none, and no click in the palette opens a form
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Components 10), still open for the form; the palette's rows now take clicks, but only to move and unfold. The shipped tutorial says 'Every action also works with a plain click.'
findings.evidence: With SGR clicks sent in tmux, a click on = drops the menu, a click on '‹ verbs' or on --title changes nothing, and two clicks on a verb's name open no form. The form's click handles the menu bar alone.
findings.fix: A click on an option, a toggle, a list's row, the command line, or '‹ verbs' focuses it and acts as space or Enter does. In the palette a click on the command's name opens its form.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced in Go tests: form.click (model.go:174) handles the menu bar only; a click on '‹ verbs' produces no BackMsg, a click on --all in commit's form moves no focus and toggles nothing. Three clicks on a palette verb produce no OpenMsg; palette_test.go:214 says a click only moves the cursor. screen.md:41 says otherwise.

findings.title: Searching the palette for 'work' keeps all 20 verbs of the workflow group, and kit work is the 18th
findings.claim: The search matches every column, the group's name among them, and leaving the search puts the cursor on the first row, not the best match.
findings.evidence: /work leaves 'workflow 20' whole with work under assign to unassign, so reaching it is /work, Enter, and 17 down arrows. From the guide to a running kit work 7 I counted 34 key presses, against 11 for typing it in a shell.
findings.fix: Search the command and the description, not the group. Rank a command that equals or starts with the query first and put the cursor on it.

findings.title: The guide never says what to do next, and has no page on how work flows, which its banner, the README, and .kit/README.md promise
findings.claim: The five pages are introduction, toolchains, setup, customize, and terms; none says start with kit work, commit with kit commit, push with kit submit, and none names kit tutorials. When every check holds the screen says nothing; 'Nothing is left' exists in --text alone (welcome.sh:1036).
findings.evidence: A grep for kit work, kit commit, kit submit, and tutorial over the pages finds kit work only inside three glossary entries and one settings note. The banner says 'and the workflow' and the README 'Then it explains how work flows'.
findings.fix: Add a page for the first change: the six steps of README 'Getting started', each with its command, ending with kit tutorials applications. End each step's pane with one line that names the next, and show it on the introduction once the checks answer.

findings.title: Outside a repository the guide does not say so
findings.claim: A person who has just installed kit is likely to type kit in their home folder, and nothing on any step says kit found no repository or what to do about it.
findings.evidence: In a folder that is no repository the title is '= kit welcome · -' and setup shows the terminal's checks alone. The one sentence that covers it is in the middle of the setup page's prose.
findings.fix: Where welcome_folders is empty, emit one offer: kit is not in a repository here; cd into one and run kit, or name one with kit --workspace=<host/path> welcome. Draw it first on setup.

findings.title: A folder with no kit.yml shows its kit as 'no…', the case every first run is
findings.claim: widths measures f.head.Kit, empty where no version is declared, so the column is three cells wide and cell cuts the stand-in 'none' to fit.
findings.evidence: Before kit install the row read '💻 consumer  main    no…  ✅   💡   ·'. setup-folders.golden hides it because another folder there has 0.3.0.
findings.fix: Measure 'none' where the version is empty.

findings.title: Welcome reports a missing linter as a failure in a repository that has no file it lints
findings.claim: welcome:linters names every linter the active rules name, whether or not the repository has a file of that kind, so kit install earns a newcomer a new red mark. Its fix is a machine-wide brew install behind a cd to the folder.
findings.evidence: After kit install in a repository holding one README.md, setup went from 2 failures to 3 with 'actionlint is not installed; kit lint runs it for .kit/rules/workflows.md'. kit lint there prints 'nothing to lint' and exits 0.
findings.fix: Plan a linter's check only where a tracked file is governed by its rule, or make it an offer until one is. Leave the cd off a fix the system toolchain runs.

findings.title: A check's own sentence is cut at the pane's edge and cannot be read in full
findings.claim: checkLines clips the check's line and makes only the lines under it a block that scrolls across, so the sentence that says what is wrong is the one that cannot be read.
findings.evidence: At 80 columns: 'This terminal does not speak the kitty keyboard protocol, so ⇧⌫ arrives …' and 'actionlint is not installed; kit lint runs it for .kit/rul…'. At 120 the first is still cut.
findings.fix: Wrap the check's line under its glyph, as stepHead wraps a refusal.

findings.title: The line under a form's command line goes stale, is cut at the screen's edge, and tells a person in the form to run kit help in a shell
findings.claim: m.refusal is cleared only when a run succeeds, Layout writes it on one unwrapped line, and its remedy is 'cd <folder> && kit help <verb>', a shell line shown inside the form that came from that help.
findings.evidence: After choosing <reference> and typing 7 the form showed 'kit work 7' with 'kit work needs <reference> or --title or --pr; run: cd /private/tmp/…' still under it, cut mid-path.
findings.fix: Clear the refusal in changed and typedText, and wrap it with pane.Wrap. In the form say what is missing and leave the remedy out.

findings.title: Terms and customize are full data tables, so a definition is cut at '…' and takes five keys to read
findings.claim: The two reading steps are drawn with the apps' table: a control line, presets, a rule of ×· marks, and rows folded shut. Enter on a row does nothing, and the command each entry gives can be neither run nor copied, though a check's fix can.
findings.evidence: At 120 columns most meanings ended in '…', and customize's about column gets 28 cells ('packages: in kit.yml lists …'). Reading one definition took 5, three down arrows, and the right arrow.
findings.fix: Draw the wrapped column whole by default in these two tables (44 and 6 rows) and send the first down arrow from the bar to the first row. Let Enter on a row open the form of its first command and c copy it.

findings.title: The welcome's goldens are drawn from fixture pages that no longer match the shipped ones, so no test shows the real screen
findings.claim: Every golden shows the checks at the top of the pane, which is not what a person gets (U3-3), and U3-9 passes because a fixture folder has a version.
findings.evidence: The fixture's toolchains page is 3 lines and the shipped one 46. The fixture's setup page still says 'choose now to run it or later to move on', buttons the screen no longer has.
findings.fix: Add goldens over the shipped pages at 80x24 and 120x40, with one fixture of a repository that has no kit.yml. Delete the stale sentences from the fixtures.

findings.title: kit welcome's help describes a screen that no longer exists
findings.claim: The header says step 1 holds 'what it solves, and what the checks found', that the screen opens 'on the first step with a failed check', and that 'now runs it, later moves on'. kit help welcome and the form print this text.
findings.evidence: The screen opened on the introduction with setup at 2 and again at 3 failures (welcome.go:21 says it stays there), the introduction shows no result, and the keys are c copy and r run.
findings.fix: Rewrite lines 11 to 25 from the screen as it is. Or make the header true by opening on the first step with a failed check from the second run on.

findings.title: Two columns of the setup table are headed 'kit'
findings.claim: The first kit is the version kit.yml declares and the second the kit-installed check, and nothing explains 💡 or · in the cells.
findings.evidence: The header reads 'folder  branch  kit  git  kit  .kit  hooks  toolchain  tools  check', in the run and in setup-folders.golden.
findings.fix: Head the first 'version' and the second 'installed'. Add one dim line under the table that names the four marks.

findings.title: The README sends a person to gh pr ready, though kit ready exists and the workflow page names it
findings.claim: README step 5 names the forge's own commands, and the list of workflow verbs at line 155 omits kit ready.
findings.evidence: README.md:245 says 'gh pr ready on GitHub, glab mr update --ready on GitLab'. kit/packages/workflow/files/repo/.kit/workflow.md:23 says 'kit ready, on any forge'.
findings.fix: Name kit ready in both places.

findings.title: A link on a tutorial's page has no key, and 'Read next' is not a link
findings.claim: paging takes esc, /, and the scrolling keys, so only a click follows a kittui: link. Reading the series is esc, move, Enter for each tutorial.
findings.evidence: The seven tutorials screen.md lists under 'Read next' are code spans such as kit tutorials menu-bar. No case in paging follows a link.
findings.fix: Tab and shift-Tab step through a page's links and Enter follows. Accept kittui:tutorials/<id> and write 'Read next' with it.

findings.title: kit help lists the workflow group by alphabet, with the apps' listings among it, and never points at welcome or the tutorials
findings.claim: The eight verbs a person runs in order are scattered among five that list things (audit, changes, delivery, issues, people), and the palette inherits the order. LEARN MORE names .kit/1st.md and no guide.
findings.evidence: kit help --text prints WORKFLOW as 20 verbs from assign to workspaces, with work 18th. Six purpose lines pass 80 columns under a preamble wrapped at 80.
findings.fix: Give the listings a group of their own and list the workflow group in the workflow's order. Add kit welcome and kit tutorials to LEARN MORE.

findings.title: Without a terminal, kit welcome prints 479 lines and puts what is left last
findings.claim: An agent that runs kit welcome to see whether a repository is ready pays for the whole guide to reach two lines.
findings.evidence: kit welcome --text in the throwaway repository printed 479 lines and 2,611 words, 1,143 of them the glossary. '# What is left' is the last eight lines.
findings.fix: Print 'What is left' first, then the pages. Or, without a terminal, print the checks and what is left, and one line that says kit welcome --text prints the guide.

findings.title: kit introduces itself with three different sentences in the first hour
findings.claim: The README and kit help say kit is rules and the checks that hold work to them; the introduction says it is one set of commands for the whole development cycle. A newcomer reads all three within minutes.
findings.evidence: README: 'writes down the rules an agent must follow'. Introduction: 'kit is one set of commands for the whole development cycle'. kit help: 'kit keeps the rules a repository asks its agents to follow'.
findings.fix: Choose one sentence that holds both, the rules and checks and the commands that follow them, and use it in all three.

areas.title: the command line
areas.coverage: Read whole: bin/kit, kit-call, help.sh, syntax.sh, completion.sh, log.sh, features.md, completion.md, 22 verbs; code bodies plus rendered --help of the other 30 (tools, update, welcome, workspace, workspaces: messages only). Ran about 130 calls without a forge, tmux on a built kittui, and two bats walks on the fake gh. Grepped 11-10 afterwards.
areas.summary: The workflow verbs are good: one-line refusals with a remedy, 52 of 52 verbs answer --help, kit work and kit submit are exact. The surface around them fails a newcomer in the first hour: --help on a terminal opens a palette whose page never loads; kit issues and kit changes do not list issues or changes; kit flow --text prints on stderr; kit release tags a stale desk silently. Option values are written two ways, every remedy carries a cd prefix, and help pages run to 345 lines. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the report file, so everything is in this result; run outputs are in out/U4/ (walk.txt, release.txt, help/, usage.txt).
strengths: Every one of the 52 verbs answers --help with exit 0 from the one place its help is written, and kit syntax --check passes: usage, help, the guard, completion, and kittui's forms all read the same header. Keep that single source.

Refusals have one voice: one line, what is wrong, the command to run, exit 2 for usage and 1 for a refusal, and nothing is touched before the arguments are judged. kit comit names commit; kit toolchains use nonesuch names the usable ones; kit commit with nothing staged names git add and --all.
kit work is the best single command: seven lines, a worktree, a branch, a start commit, a draft pull request, and a last line that is the cd to paste; run again, it resumes.
kit submit is quiet and exact ('nothing to submit: 7-fix-the-thing is at origin/7-fix-the-thing'), never forces, and names kit rebase; kit settle on an open pull request says 'nothing to settle'.
kit trust shows what a clone asks kit to run before asking, and the loader refuses all but help, version, and trust until then, in one line with the remedy.
kit tidy --dry-run and kit uninstall --dry-run print what they would do, in sections; kit uninstall took out exactly what kit install had placed.
kit welcome --checks prints each check with its fix under it, and kit flow without an origin still draws the desk and says once what it could not read.
--json and --jq on every listing, NO_COLOR honoured, and prefix help (kit help wor) are right.

findings.title: kit <verb> --help on a terminal opens a full-screen palette whose page never loads
findings.claim: On a terminal, kit commit --help, kit help tidy, and kit tidy --help open kittui's palette with the verb's row open, and the row shows a dim … for ever, so the help text is never seen. The palette opening is known since 11-10 (grammar findings 14 and 18), still open; the stuck page is new.
findings.evidence: Reproduced three times in tmux: after 40 seconds, cursor moves, and closing and reopening the row it still reads …, while a row opened by hand (delivery) loads at once. screens.New drops the command of m.Update(SettingsMsg), whose palette Update already ran fetch() and set the shared asked[verb], so Init's fetch returns nothing.
findings.fix: Have guard:arguments exec kit-help --text <verb> so --help and -h print and return, as in git, gh, jj, and gt. In screens.New keep the first screen's command and add a test that opens the palette at a verb through screens.New.
findings.verdict_note: My Go test (out/U4/verify-1/kitsrc/projects/tui/internal/screens/zz_verify_test.go) drives app.OpenHelp(r,"submit") through screens.New: row stays "…"; without the root it shows Usage. screens.go:76 drops the command of palette.go:378's fetch, which set asked[verb] (palette.go:214). 1st.sh:711 execs kit-help without --text. No test covers it.

findings.title: kit release tags a desk that is behind origin without a word, and has no dry run
findings.claim: The check that a release is on the default branch is merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main, which a stale HEAD passes, and kit never pulls the desk, so merging on the forge and then releasing at the desk tags the commit from before the merge. A version is tagged once, so the number is spent.
findings.evidence: On a bare origin three commits ahead of the desk, kit release 0.2.0 printed '→ tagging 5462ca3 init as release/0.2.0' and '✅ pushed release/0.2.0', exit 0, while origin's main was 'd7035ad merged work 3'. kit release 0.3.0-rc.1 --dry-run answers unknown flag '--dry-run'.
findings.fix: After the fetch the code already does, refuse a release whose HEAD is not the tip of <primary>/<default>, naming how far behind and the remedy, with a flag to confirm as --lower does. Add --dry-run that prints the commit, the tag, and what the push would send.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: desk three behind, kit release 0.2.0 tagged the old commit, exit 0; --dry-run is an unknown flag. But the check is the rule kit-release:14 documents, the step line names the commit and subject, and an older commit on main can be meant. A missing notice and dry run, not a broken check.

findings.title: kit issues does not list issues, and kit changes does not list changes
findings.claim: The most guessable read verbs print something else: kit issues prints milestones and iterations only, kit changes prints reviews, checks, and merged, and kit delivery leaves out releases and builds. In kittui the same verbs open apps whose first tab is the missing one, so the text form is the app without its home tab.
findings.evidence: kit issues --text printed 'milestones:' and 'iterations:' alone; kit issues issues --text was refused with 'issues is printed by another command; run: … kit flow issues --json', naming --json to a person who asked for --text. kit changes changes --text is refused the same way.
findings.fix: Let kit issues [issues|backlog|underway], kit changes changes, and kit delivery releases|builds print what kit flow prints for them, first, as the app shows them. Change the purposes to say so.

findings.title: kit flow --text writes the picture to stderr, and nothing to stdout
findings.claim: The text picture of kit flow, and of kit flow <stage>, goes to stderr, so it cannot be piped, paged, grepped, or saved, while kit issues, kit workspace, kit platform, kit packages, and kit flow --json print on stdout. No header or document says so.
findings.evidence: kit flow --text 2>/dev/null printed nothing and exited 0 (stdout 0 lines, stderr 7); kit flow desk the same. docs/features.md:116 says each stage prints under a heading.
findings.fix: Print the stages on stdout and keep stderr for warnings and errors such as 'no origin: nothing fetched', as the app verbs do.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: kit flow --text --no-fetch gave stdout 0 lines, stderr 11; kit flow desk 0 and 1; kit workspace, platform, issues print on stdout. Only flow.sh function comments (218, 227, 517) say stderr; kit-flow's header and docs/features.md:116 do not, and docs/modules.md:91 says stdout carries data.

findings.title: kit tools run <command> still refuses a command that holds a flag
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (grammar finding 1), still open: the verb that runs a pinned tool cannot run one with an option of kit tools' own name, and bare kit tools run is refused in the wrong words.
findings.evidence: kit tools run echo hi prints hi; kit tools run prettier --check . prints 'kit tools needs --outdated'; kit tools run npm outdated --json and bare kit tools run print "unknown argument 'run'".
findings.fix: As the 11-10 finding says, let the matcher see the literal run past the leading optional group. For bare kit tools run, say 'kit tools run needs <command>'.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced as quoted. Narrower than "cannot": kit tools run -- echo --check . --json prints them (syntax.jq:152), and other dash-words pass (ls -la). The -- escape is absent from kit help tools, whose header promises "as typed, dash-words included"; bare run still says unknown argument 'run'.

findings.title: An option's value is written two ways, and the wrong way is refused as 'needs a value'
findings.claim: kit usage has 32 options written --name=<value>, which take = only, and 9 written --name <value> (--message, --file, --title, --pr, --to, --duplicate-of, --toolchain, --fix, --choices), which take both. Known since 11-10 as low (finding 22), still open; the refusal misleads, so I rate it medium.
findings.evidence: kit flow issues --owner bob, kit facts --moment commit, and kit new verb frob --purpose "does" each print '--owner needs a value' (or --moment, --purpose) to a person who gave one. kit help shows kit commit --message '#42 area: subject' while kit submit's refusal shows kit commit --message=<text>.
findings.fix: Write every usage line --name=<value>, keep accepting the next word for the nine, and refuse the other form with '--owner takes its value after =: --owner=bob', as the loader does for --workspace.

findings.title: Every remedy carries cd <folder> &&, even kit help <verb> typed in that folder
findings.claim: out:remedy puts cd <folder> && before every command after run:, so a usage error typed in a worktree answers with the worktree's whole path before 'kit help commit'. The person is already there, and kit help does not depend on the folder.
findings.evidence: Every refusal I produced read as "unknown verb 'comit'; did you mean commit? run: cd <150-character path> && kit help commit". In the walk, kit flow --text printed the same 190-column 'run: cd <path> && gh auth status (the issues could not be read)' four times, once per stage.
findings.fix: Write the cd only when stderr is no terminal or kittui is the caller, and never before kit help. Say a shared cause such as gh auth status once per run.

findings.title: kit submit refuses in kit commit's words, and names origin whatever the remote is
findings.claim: kit submit shares commit:branch with kit commit, so the verb whose banner says it commits nothing refuses with 'refusing to commit' and 'nothing to commit to'. commit:push-refused says 'origin refused the push' for any remote.
findings.evidence: kit submit on the desk printed 'refusing to commit on main: this is the root checkout, the human's desk; work in a worktree: kit work <N>'; outside a repository it printed 'no branch is checked out here, so there is nothing to commit to'.
findings.fix: Pass the verb's word to commit:branch ('refusing to push main', 'nothing to push') and name ${remote} in the push refusal. Write <reference> for <N>, as every usage line does.

findings.title: kit work and kit submit never print the change's address, and nothing says where the report goes
findings.claim: Neither verb prints the pull request's URL, which gh pr create and gt submit both do, though kit has forge:pr-url. The workflow calls the pull request's body the report, yet no verb writes it, no output says how, and kit ready marks it ready whatever the body holds.
findings.evidence: kit work 7 ended 'Draft pull request #3 on 7-fix-the-thing, primary #7', 'Worktree ready: <absolute path>', and "cd '<absolute path>'" (the path three times); kit submit ended 'pushed 7-fix-the-thing: 1 commit(s)'. The URL appeared only when kit ready failed.
findings.fix: Print the URL in the last line of kit work and kit submit, and the worktree relative to where the command was typed. Have kit ready warn when the body is still the one kit work wrote, or take --body-file=<path>.

findings.title: Several verb names point the wrong way, and the words other tools use get no pointer
findings.where: kit/bin/kit-workspace:2, kit/bin/kit-workspaces:2, kit/bin/kit-audit:2, kit/bin/kit-trust:2, kit/bin/kit-check:2, kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:662-691
findings.claim: workspace (a workspace's git, the app kittui calls Repositories) and workspaces (edit your groups) differ by one letter; audit opens the app called Trust while kit trust trusts a clone; check means drift from the pinned release, not 'check my work'. By my reading of kit help, 17 of 52 verbs are guessable as other tools name them, 13 once seen, 7 mislead (issues, changes, check, workspace, workspaces, audit, delivery), and 15 are kit's own words.
findings.evidence: kit status, kit pr, kit push, kit init, and kit merge each answer "unknown verb '…'; run: kit help" with no suggestion, because guard:unknown-verb matches by spelling alone (kit comit does name commit).
findings.fix: Add a small table to guard:unknown-verb from git, gh, jj, and gt words to kit's (status → flow, push → submit, init → install, sync → rebase, merge → a person merges on the forge). Before 0.1.0, rename workspace to repos and give the Trust app and audit one name.

findings.title: kit help lists twenty workflow verbs by alphabet, so the day's order is not on the page
findings.claim: WORKFLOW holds 20 of the 45 verbs listed, twelve that act shuffled with eight that only show, so work, commit, submit, ready, tidy are lines 18, 5, 15, 11, 16 of the group. completion sits under PLUMBING, 'verbs that scripts, hooks, and the TUI call', so the one verb a person runs to set up a shell is not on the page.
findings.evidence: kit help output as run; ten of its lines pass 80 columns, the width help:reflow holds the verb pages to.
findings.fix: Split the group into workflow, in the order of the day, and views, with flow first. Move completion to installation and shorten the purposes over 66 characters.

findings.title: kit install outside a git repository writes kit.yml and .kit/ there without a word
findings.claim: kit install does not check that it runs in a repository, so a newcomer who reads install as 'install kit on this machine' and types it in the home directory gets kit placed there. Every document says the repository.
findings.evidence: In an empty directory with no .git, kit install printed '── kit install unreleased, packages: kit ──', placed .gitignore, kit.yml, and .kit/, and exited 0. kit uninstall took it all out again.
findings.fix: Refuse outside a git working tree with 'kit install puts kit into a repository, and <dir> is not one; run: git init, or cd to one', or ask on a terminal.

findings.title: The help pages of the app verbs are reference manuals, not help
findings.claim: A page mixes what a person types with the JSON contract kittui and scripts read, so the options are buried. The contract belongs in a document or behind a flag.
findings.evidence: kit flow --help is 345 lines: 15 usage lines, each stage's JSON key by key, a legend of about 70 glyphs, and only then the options (--mine is near line 290). workspace is 193 lines, audit 136, welcome 114, workspaces 111, new 107; the median of the 52 pages is 37.
findings.fix: Keep usage, what it shows, options, and exits in the header, with the options before the legend. Move each stage's row schema to docs/apps.md or behind kit flow --schema.

findings.title: A text table pads every row to its widest cell, 2475 columns for kit platform settings
findings.claim: apps::text sizes each column but the last to its widest cell, so one long value in a middle column makes every row that wide. The text form is unreadable on a terminal where it happens.
findings.evidence: kit platform settings printed 21 rows of 2471 to 2475 columns: the tools setting's whole JSON is in the value column, so 'forge' is followed by about 2450 spaces and then 'default'. kit workspace was 346 columns wide for its two path columns.
findings.fix: In the text form cap a cell at about 60 columns with …, print a map or list as its keys or count, and write paths relative or with ~.

findings.title: git's and bash's own errors leak where there is no remote or no repository
findings.claim: Several verbs do not guard for a missing remote or working tree, so a raw fatal line prints and kit's own line then names the wrong trouble. kit flow and kit issues handle the same cases well.
findings.evidence: kit release 0.1.0 with no origin printed four lines of git ('fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository…') then 'HEAD is not on main at origin'. Outside a repository, kit context foo.sh printed 'context.sh: line 495: cd: null directory', kit check printed '1 finding(s), each named above' with none named, and kit work 5 said 'this repository does not have a remote named origin'.
findings.fix: Add one guard for verbs that need a working tree: 'kit <verb> runs in a repository, and <dir> is in none'. In releases:release, check the primary is a remote before ls-remote, as kit flow does.

findings.title: kit new issue --list prints the forge's refusal as a row, on stdout, and exits 0
findings.claim: The list's third field is url // error, so a tracker that gives no page puts a sentence where an address should be, on stdout, with a zero status.
findings.evidence: With no origin, stdout was '#<tab><tab>this repository does not have a remote named origin, so kit cannot tell its forge; run: cd … && git remote add origin <url>…', stderr was empty, and the exit status was 0.
findings.fix: Print a tracker with no page on stderr and exit 1 when none has one, or keep the row with an empty address.

findings.title: No short flags, no did-you-mean for a flag, and a closed set is not named in its refusal
findings.claim: The flag typed most, -m, is refused though git, gh, jj, and gt all take it; a misspelled flag gets no nearest name though a misspelled verb does; and a value off a closed set is refused without the set.
findings.evidence: kit commit -m x: "unknown flag '-m'"; kit commit --mesage x and kit tidy --dryrun: unknown flag, nothing nearer; kit facts --moment=zzz: "--moment 'zzz' is not one of the choices" where the choices are ci and commit. kit new: 'needs file or kind or rule or style or package or template or module or provider or verb or issue'.
findings.fix: Take -m for --message and -a for --all in kit commit, and run flags through the distance the verbs use. List a closed set of up to about eight in the refusal, and join alternatives as 'one of: …'.

findings.title: A first run and an ordinary commit say more than they need to
findings.claim: Implicit hydration lists every file before the verb's own output, and a passing commit prints a line for each check that had nothing to do plus an unsigned warning on every commit.
findings.evidence: In a fresh clone, kit context README.md printed 59 '→ .kit/…: placed' lines before its 4 lines of answer. A passing kit commit printed five lines, among them '✅ no rule governs the 1 path(s); nothing was linted', '✅ generate: no kit:generate directive to expand', and '⚠️ commits here are not signed…'.
findings.fix: Sum implicit hydration up in one line and keep the list for kit hydrate itself. Print a passing check only when it ran something, and warn of unsigned commits once per worktree.

findings.title: Bare kit always opens the welcome's introduction, and a form opens before a refusal that is already known
findings.claim: kit with no verb opens the welcome guide's Introduction every time, also where every check holds, when a returning person wants Flow. A verb short of an argument hands off to its form before its cheap refusals run.
findings.evidence: In tmux, bare kit opened 'kit welcome' on tab 1, introduction (main.go: case "welcome", ""). kit commit on the desk opened the commit form, though kit commit --message x there answers 'refusing to commit on main: this is the root checkout'.
findings.fix: Open Flow when the welcome's checks hold in a repository, leaving the welcome under = and kit welcome. Run the desk, default-branch, and no-repository refusals before the hand-off to the form.

findings.title: docs/features.md leaves kit ready out of the workflow, and lists the stages in another order
findings.claim: The page's six workflow steps omit kit ready, which its own header calls the last step of the workflow, and kit settle. The stage bullets differ in order from kit flow --stages (known since 11-10, finding 26, still open), and kit-help:9 still says --help prints.
findings.evidence: features.md steps: work, commit, submit, rebase, gate, 'A human merges, and kit tidy'; .kit/workflow.md:23 has kit ready as step 4. Bullets run issues, incoming, desk, worktrees, changes, builds, releases; kit flow --stages prints issues, desk, worktrees, changes, builds, incoming, releases.
findings.fix: Add kit ready as a step and one sentence on kit settle, and reorder the bullets. Correct kit-help:9 with U4-1.

findings.title: Small disagreements in the words kit prints
findings.where: kit/modules/bash/1st.sh:576, kit/bin/kit-install:46, kit/modules/bash/issue.sh:652-653, kit/bin/kit-ready:37, kit/bin/kit-settle:39, kit/modules/bash/apps.sh:109-112
findings.claim: A remedy is written two ways, capitals are uneven, one thing has two nouns, and an empty stage prints a bare heading. None is wrong alone; together they read as several hands.
findings.evidence: Counted over kit/bin and kit/modules/bash: '<wrong>; run: <command>' 63 times and 'run: <command> (<wrong>)' 52 times; error starts lowercase 249 to 2, ok 36 to 9, step 31 to 12. kit ready says 'name the change' where kit settle says 'no pull request is named'; kit issues with no forge prints 'milestones:', a blank line, 'iterations:', exit 0.
findings.fix: Use one shape, reason first, lowercase throughout, and one noun from forge:noun. Print 'none' under an empty stage, with 'no forge here' where that is why.

findings.title: Completion is zsh only, and asking for bash does not say so
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 as a gap, still open: kit runs on bash and completes zsh alone. The refusal for another shell does not say which shell there is.
findings.evidence: kit completion bash and kit completion fish both answer "unknown argument 'bash'" (or 'fish'), with a pointer to kit help completion.
findings.fix: Add a bash script around COMPREPLY over kit completion candidates, about twenty lines. Until then refuse with 'kit completes zsh alone so far: kit completion zsh'.

findings.title: The ordinary day is 11 to 12 kit commands plus 4 to 5 steps outside kit, and five of its steps are not told
findings.claim: Pick (kit flow issues), kit work, cd, git add, kit commit, kit submit, write the report on the forge, kit gate, kit ready, answer review (kit changes reviews, reply on the forge, commit, submit, perhaps kit rebase), a person merges, git pull at the desk, kit release, kit tidy: about what git with gh costs (12 to 14) and more than Graphite (4 to 5). The tool does not tell: that kit issues is not the list, where the report goes, how to reply to review, that the desk must be pulled before a release, and that --help needs --text on a terminal.
findings.evidence: Walk run on the suite's fake gh: kit work 7 printed 7 lines ending in the cd to paste; kit commit with nothing staged named git add and --all; kit submit, kit settle, and kit tidy --dry-run were exact. No output named the pull request's URL, kit gate, or kit ready.
findings.fix: Fix U4-1, U4-2, U4-3, and U4-9. End kit work's and kit submit's output with the next step, as 'next: kit gate, then kit ready', and the URL.

areas.title: how it will be received
areas.coverage: Read whole: README, features, architecture, install, apps, terminals, kit.yml, consumer 1st.md and .kit/README, five welcome pages; 17 of 85 goldens. Ran the real kit (12 verbs) in a throwaway repository and kittui in tmux at four sizes, about 60 keys. Not checked: a forge, the tap, real fonts, mouse. findings.md not written: the Write tool refuses report files.
areas.summary: The command line is good: exact refusals with their remedies, a clear help page, honest limits. kittui is a capable grid with a weak first five minutes: a grammar of its own (␣ before any action, ⌃Q, `?` for glyphs, ⇥ before a form's first field), no view of content, and a dependence on emoji and a Nerd Font. The README sells half the product and never shows it, and the default install points no agent at the rules while saying it does. Verdicts: a senior engineer pilots the rules, not the workflow; a new contributor is productive within a day once told three keys; a platform engineer runs it in two repositories behind a non-required check and asks for a fleet update path and a `checks:` setting.
strengths: Every refusal I provoked names what is wrong and the command that fixes it, with the `cd` in front, as `❌ refusing to commit on master: this is the root checkout, the human's desk; work in a worktree: kit work <N>`. This is better than gh; keep it.
`kit help --text` is one screen, grouped (workflow, files, checks, installation), with three examples, and needs no change.

The README is honest about what is not enforced: the deny list "matches literal patterns, so `git -C <dir> commit` and `git merge` get through", "kit does not ship a ruleset", and "What no check covers". A senior engineer trusts it more for this.
Leaving is cheap and shown: `kit uninstall --dry-run` listed every path it would take out, and a consumer's kit.yml after `kit install` is four lines.
Each tab's subtitle states the question the tab answers, as "Builds — Is the default branch green? CI runs outside any pull request".
The table adapts well: a column shows a glyph when narrow and the word when there is room, search is live, and it is the same on every screen.
The `=` menu names the nine apps in plain words with one glyph each, and menu lines carry their key at the right; the keys bar changes with the focus.
The form refuses a missing argument with kit's own line and puts the cursor back on the field.
The tutorial "The screen at a glance" draws the screen with its parts named and gives five keys; it deserves to be the first thing a newcomer sees.
The welcome checks show the fix under the failure and offer to copy or run it, and `kit trust` says what the clone asks kit to run before it asks.
Toolchains are a seam over mise, Nix, Homebrew, Docker, and dev containers, not a replacement for them.
The requirement is bash 4.4, not 5, and the loader checks it before anything else runs and says what to install.
`kit work <N>`, an issue to a worktree, a linked branch, and a draft pull request in one command, is the best moment kit has and the thing no compared tool does.

findings.title: The default `kit install` points no agent at the rules, and says every agent reads them
findings.claim: `kit install` with no names activates the `kit` package alone, which writes no AGENTS.md, adapter, or hook, so nothing sends any agent to `.kit/1st.md`. Its closing line still says "Every agent reads .kit/1st.md first."
findings.evidence: In a throwaway repository, `git status --short` after `kit install` showed only `?? .gitignore` and `?? kit.yml`. `release:finish` sets `local read=' Every agent reads .kit/1st.md first.'` whatever packages are active.
findings.fix: Make `agents/generic` a default beside `kit`, or have `release:finish` say, when no `agents/*` package is active: "No agent is sent here yet; run: kit packages add agents/claude (or agents/generic for AGENTS.md)".
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: `kit install` in a fresh trusted repo left only `?? .gitignore` and `?? kit.yml`, no AGENTS.md, and ended "Every agent reads .kit/1st.md first." But the bare default is documented and tested (docs/packages/agents/generic.md:19-20, tests/workflow.bats:24; README.md:98-112 lists agent packages). Defect is the misleading closing line and missing hint, not a broken install.

findings.title: The README never introduces kittui, shows no screen, and gives 41 percent of itself to kit's own maintainers
findings.claim: The README's first word on the terminal UI is line 92, "terminal settings that make kittui slower or worse", with no sentence saying what kittui is, and the nine apps, the palette, and the forms are in no section. Lines 198 to 336 are for working on kit itself, under "Setup" and "Getting started", where a consumer reads "Every commit must be signed" though `require_signing` is optional.
findings.evidence: `grep -n kittui README.md` gives lines 92, 253, and 327 only, and `docs/` holds three architecture SVGs and no screenshot or recording. README, features.md, `kit help`, and the welcome guide each give a different one-line account of what kit is.
findings.fix: Open with the pitch in U5-18, one screenshot of Flow, one of a refusal with its remedy, and a "Try it in two minutes" block (`brew install`, `cd` any repository, `kit`, `kit flow`). Move lines 198 to 336 to CONTRIBUTING.md.

findings.title: In the form `kit commit` opens, the required message cannot be typed until ⇥ and then ⏎
findings.claim: The form opens with `▸` on `--message` under "one of required" but with no option under the cursor, so typing is swallowed and ␣, which the keys bar names "␣ choose", does nothing. Only ⇥ and then ⏎ reveal the input, and by the code every one-of row of every verb behaves the same.
findings.evidence: Driven live with `kittui -- commit`: `hello` drew nothing, ␣ changed nothing, ⏎ moved on, and the run came back `❌ kit commit needs --message or --file`; the shortest path is ⇥ ⏎, the text, ⏎ ⏎ ⏎ ⏎. `enter()` sets `m.cursor = f.Chosen`, which is -1, and `pickOption` returns when the cursor is below 0.
findings.fix: On a one-of row with nothing chosen, start the cursor on the first option. When a printable key arrives on a one-of row whose option takes text, choose that option and start its value with the key.

findings.title: Nothing in the tree publishes the Homebrew formula the README's install line needs
findings.claim: Known since 11-10 (Gaps, Release), still open: `brew install empowerite/tap/kit` is the README's only install line for macOS and Linux, and nothing here writes a formula. No workflow deploys the tutorials site that the online tutorial cards link to either.
findings.evidence: A search of `bin/` and `.github/` for `homebrew`, `formula`, and `/tap` finds nothing; the workflows are kit-ci.yml, release.yml, and retire-pre-releases.yml. I could not read the tap or the site (no network), which is what would settle it.
findings.fix: Have `bin/release publish` write the formula with `depends_on` bash, jq, and yq. Until it does, lead the README with the `gh release download` lines.
findings.verdict_note: In-tree facts hold: no formula, tap step, or Pages deploy in .github/workflows/ or bin/. But the formula is planned outside this tree (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-release-readiness.md:29-30; step 6 at :341 still unchecked). Whether the tap or site is live needs network: brew install empowerite/tap/kit, and a fetch of the Pages URL.

findings.title: An action in Flow acts only on rows selected with ␣, and its key does nothing, silently, without one
findings.claim: Partly known since 11-10 (Apps 18), still open: with the cursor on an issue, `A` (Assign to Me) and `O` (Open Selected) change nothing and say nothing until the row is selected with ␣, and ⏎ on a row is unbound. gh dash, k9s, and lazygit all act on the row under the cursor.
findings.evidence: I pressed `A` and `O` on a row and the screen and keys bar stayed as they were; `acting` returns disabled while `m.selected() == 0` and `pages()` reads `selectedRows()` only. Starting work on one issue took ↓×3, ␣, `:`, ↓×8, ⏎, 14 keys against 12 typed for `kit work 46`.
findings.fix: With nothing selected, act on the row under the cursor and word the menu so ("Assign #46 to Me"). When a key's action cannot run, say why in the keys bar, as a refusal already does.

findings.title: The welcome guide's Customize step draws its explanations in a column twelve cells wide
findings.claim: Each part of `4-customize.md` is a paragraph, and the step draws it as the `about` cell of a table, cut to about eleven characters. The page as `kit welcome --text` prints it is easier to read than the screen.
findings.evidence: The 80-column golden pins `▸ Packages  pac…  kit.yml +1  packages: i…  kit packages`. Live at 100 columns, → on Policy wrapped two sentences over 14 lines of one or two words, and Show More left `⬇⁹⁸` lines to scroll.
findings.fix: Draw Customize as the page it is, as Introduction is drawn, each `kit …` line a link that opens its form. Or give `about` the width left after `part` and put settings, where, and commands under the opened row.

findings.title: The checks a newcomer came for sit under 20 to 30 lines of prose, and no golden draws the shipped pages
findings.claim: On the Toolchains and Setup steps the first screen is all prose about roles and precedence, and the ✅ and ❌ lines are below the fold. The goldens look tidy because they render a fixture page of two sentences, so the suite never draws what ships.
findings.evidence: Live at 100x40 with the real kit, Toolchains ended `kit runs on four tools: ⬇²⁴` with no check in view, and Setup showed about 20 lines before its table; one ↓ does jump to the first check. The fixture page reads "A toolchain installs tools. When several are usable, choose one."
findings.fix: Draw the checks first and the prose after, or cut each shipped page to the fixture's length and move the rest to docs/toolchains.md. Add one golden per step that renders the shipped page at 80x24.

findings.title: kittui's pills need a Nerd Font, no page says so, and there is no fallback
findings.claim: Every label on an issue or change, the preset name on every table's control line, and the tutorial cards' audience tags are drawn between U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, private-use code points only a Nerd Font or a terminal with built-in Powerline glyphs draws. README, install.md, and terminals.md name no font, and no probe can see one.
findings.evidence: `PillLeft = ""`, `PillRight = ""`, with no other branch in `Pill`; terminals.md lists six needs and says "a font ... is not a finding". How the code points draw in Terminal, GNOME Terminal, or Alacritty I did not see; a look in each would settle the severity.
findings.fix: Draw a pill's ends as a space on the pill's background, so it is a colored block in any font. Or add the font to "What kittui needs" with a `pills: plain` setting.

findings.title: kittui has no mode without emoji and reads none of the terminal probes
findings.claim: Columns rely on two-cell emoji, about 100 distinct emoji and symbols are drawn, and a terminal that fails the `emoji-width` probe gets a finding in `kit welcome` and the same misaligned screen. terminals.md says kit "passes the answers down in KIT_TERMINAL_PROBES", and nothing under projects/tui reads that variable.
findings.evidence: A search of the tree for `KIT_TERMINAL_PROBES` finds bash, tests, and docs only; a count over kittui's non-test sources, fields.json, and glyphs.json gives 101 distinct code points in the emoji and symbol blocks. The catalog already has a `text` rendering per field, shown in each column's card.
findings.fix: Add a `glyphs: text` mode that uses each field's `text` rendering and ASCII for the chrome, chosen by itself when the probe fails. Have kittui read the probes, or drop the sentence from terminals.md.

findings.title: `?` explains glyphs and not keys, leaves out the state glyphs on Issues, and esc does not close it
findings.claim: The state glyphs are known since 11-10 (Apps 20), still open: at 80 columns the Issues tab's state column is 🏁, 🔥, 🔨, or 💬 alone and the legend names none, though the tutorial says it "names every glyph on the screen". A person from k9s, lazygit, or gh dash presses `?` for the keys and gets 24 glyphs, one of them `·` with two meanings and `†` with none.
findings.evidence: Seen live at 80x24 and in legend.golden; `states` is appended only `if name == "changes"`. Esc left the legend open twice in my run, and only `?` closed it.
findings.fix: Append `states` on issues too and add a line for `†` and `🔗`. Give the legend a footer with the tutorial's five keys (`=`, `/`, `?`, esc, ⌃Q), and let esc close it.

findings.title: Nothing on an app's screen says how to leave it
findings.claim: Quit is ⌃Q, named only on the last line of the `=` menu; `q` does nothing and says nothing, and esc never quits by design. The form opened straight from a verb does print `⌃Q quit` first in its keys bar, so the pattern exists.
findings.evidence: Every app's keys bar reads `= menu - workspace / search ? legend │ ⇥·⇧⇥ tab ↓ groups 1-5 jump : tab menu`. I pressed `q` in Flow and nothing changed.
findings.fix: When `q` is pressed where it types nothing, show `⌃Q quits · esc goes back` in the keys bar for five seconds, as other notes are shown. Put `⌃Q quit` at the bar's right end where the width allows.

findings.title: The welcome guide says kit works with Jira and Linear, and kit can only open their pages
findings.claim: The first page a newcomer reads lists "Azure DevOps work items, and others such as Jira and Linear" under "One set of commands across your tools". For those two kit has only the `web` provider, which opens pages and refuses every read and write.
findings.evidence: The tracker providers are forge.sh, ado.sh, and web.sh, and web.sh says kit "cannot read, assign, close, or comment on an issue, nor say who the caller is, so those calls refuse".
findings.fix: Write: "Trackers: the forge's own issues and Azure DevOps work items; for others, such as Jira and Linear, kit links to the issue's page and cannot read or change it yet."

findings.title: A team cannot take the delivered CI job without one issue per pull request
findings.claim: `kit ci` always runs `kit linked`, and the only setting that bears on it is `linked_exempt`, a list of logins. A team that wants the rules, the drift check, and the gate without an issue for every change must write its own job, and no page describes that smaller adoption.
findings.evidence: `for verb in linked policy gate check` in kit-ci, and features.md: "The four checks are fixed." The schema's keys hold no switch for a check.
findings.fix: Add a `checks:` list in kit.yml, all four by default, that `kit ci` reads. Add a README paragraph "Take only the rules": `kit install agents/claude style/markdown` and a pipeline step `kit check && kit gate`.

findings.title: Half of the file every agent reads first is about packaging
findings.claim: `.kit/1st.md` is 216 lines and 14 KB, read in every session, and lines 116 to 216 describe how files are placed, every package including those the repository did not take, and how to replace a file. The integrity rules, which are the product, are lines 8 to 19.
