findings.evidence: `wc -l` gives 216; "What the kit delivers" starts at line 116 and "Changing what kit adds" at 198. `.kit/README.md`, "for the person at the desk", covers the same ground in 68 lines.
findings.fix: End 1st.md after "Rules by file type" with one line that sends a reader to .kit/README.md for how kit places files and how to change them. Move the two sections there.

findings.title: kittui shows rows and never content: no issue text, diff, check log, or review thread
findings.claim: Against gh dash (preview pane, approve, comment, checkout on one key) and lazygit (hunks, diffs, the graph), kittui is a set of lists: → only unwraps cells that were cut, and every question past the row means the browser. What it has that they lack is one row holding the issue, its pull request, its checks, and the worktree it is in, across three forges.
findings.evidence: → on issue #7 added its second assignee and the rest of its title, nothing else; `RowKeys` binds no ⏎. `ls kit/bin` holds no verb that prints a diff, a log, or a review.
findings.fix: Bind ⏎ on a row to a detail pane read from one `--json` call: the body, each check with its failed step, the unresolved threads. Leave merging to the forge, as the workflow intends.

findings.title: Nothing opens the pull request that moves a repository to the next kit release
findings.claim: "A pull request that bumps the version updates it" is the README's case for a release over a copy, and the only path given is a person running `kit --version=0.2.0 update` in each repository. Renovate does exactly this job for every other pin, and has no manager for `version:` in kit.yml.
findings.evidence: A search of README.md and docs/*.md for `renovate` finds nothing, and `dependabot` appears only as an exempt login and an alert source. I did not read every verb for a fleet form of `update`, which would settle it.
findings.fix: Ship a Renovate `customManagers` snippet for `version:` in kit.yml, and a workflow in `github/ci` that runs `kit --version=<new> update` and opens the pull request. Say in the README which one a platform team should use.

findings.title: No page answers the three objections a team will raise first
findings.claim: The objections will be: 53 bash verbs at 0.1.0 with no other user; an issue, a worktree, and a draft pull request for every change, with no stacks and no word on jj; and rules that by the README's own account are not enforced, so what does this add to AGENTS.md, pre-commit, and one required check. No page places kit beside gh, gh dash, lazygit, mise, pre-commit, Renovate, Graphite, or Backstage.
findings.evidence: A search of README.md and docs/*.md for those names finds only lefthook's "pre-commit hook". kit.yml:56-124 shows what kit's own toolchain costs beside mise: a URL template with an `os` and an `arch` map for each tool.
findings.fix: Add "How kit fits with what you have": keep gh, lazygit, mise, and pre-commit, which kit calls or sits beside. Then the three things kit adds: a rule changed once reaches every repository as a merge, `kit context` gives the right rule at the edit in any harness, and `kit work`.

findings.title: The README makes the first half of the pitch and not the second
findings.claim: The README's opening and "Why a release, and not a copy" sell the rules, the checks, and the pinned release well, and give the workflow one bullet of twelve and the UI nothing. The welcome guide sells the commands across forges and not the rules.
findings.evidence: README.md:11-13 against 1-introduction.md:5-6, "one set of commands for the whole development cycle, the same for people and for coding agents". GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps are named together nowhere in the README's first 100 lines.
findings.fix: Use in both places: "kit gives every repository the same rules for people and coding agents: one file every agent reads first, a rule and a linter for each kind of file, and four checks in CI, delivered as a pinned release that a pull request updates. It also runs the path from an issue to a merged pull request with the same few commands on GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps, and shows where all of it stands in a terminal UI."

findings.title: The README and the architecture page send people to `gh pr ready`, though `kit ready` exists
findings.claim: Both pages say "`gh pr ready` on GitHub, `glab mr update --ready` on GitLab" and give nothing for Azure DevOps, and the README's list of workflow verbs leaves `kit ready` out. It is the one step where the README breaks its own claim of the same commands on each forge.
findings.evidence: `kit/bin/kit-ready` "marks a draft pull request ready for review" on every forge, `.kit/workflow.md:23` uses it, and docs/architecture.md:197 names it sixty lines after line 138.
findings.fix: Write `kit ready` in all three places.

findings.title: The glossary has 44 terms, lacks words the screens use, and draws each meaning cut short
findings.claim: About 20 of the 44 terms carry a meaning of kit's own (desk, gate, stage, kind, region, hydrate, house package, primary, incoming, underway, ambient), and preset, adapter, harness, submit, settle, gather, tidy, swimlane, legend, and watch are used elsewhere and not defined. On the screen every meaning ends in `…` after about 46 characters, so reading the glossary is 44 presses of →.
findings.evidence: `grep -c '^### '` gives 44, and a grep of the page for each of the ten words gives 0. Live at 100 columns: "The project's files and their history, kept b…".
findings.fix: Add the ten words, and draw each meaning wrapped under its term with the command at the right. In the README and the first welcome page give the common word first and kit's once in brackets, as "your main checkout (kit calls it the desk)".

findings.title: Sorting by a column from the keyboard takes thirteen keys
findings.claim: The only keyboard path to a sort is the Fields dialog, and `f` opens it from one stop of the control line only. A click on the `·` before a column's name does it in one, and k9s sorts by age with one key.
findings.evidence: Measured on Issues: ↓, ⇥ three times to the preset pill, `f`, ↓ six times to `age`, `s`, esc. `f` on the control line's first stop opened nothing.
findings.fix: Take `f` anywhere on the control line and in the rows. Add ⇧← and ⇧→ in the rows to walk the header, with `s` to turn the sort of the column reached.

findings.title: Small things a first look meets on the screens
findings.claim: The folders table has two columns headed `kit` (the pinned version, then the installed check); in one repository the Issues tab spends four lines on a `source · organization · repository` heading with one value each; state words reach the screen as tokens (`failing:gate`, `comments:open`). With the search unfocused nothing names the keys that clear it, the workspace menu cut a refusal before its remedy, and no welcome page links to "The screen at a glance", the best first page kit has.
findings.evidence: setup-folders.golden: `folder  branch  kit  git  kit  .kit  hooks`; live with a one-repository fixture: `▾ github · empowerite · kit 7` under the heading and its rule. Esc kept the filter `lint`, and `grep tutorial` over the five welcome pages finds nothing.
findings.fix: Name the first column `version`, draw no group heading when every level has one value, and print states as words ("gate failing"). End the welcome introduction with a link to the tutorial, and wrap a refusal in a menu.

findings.title: The README disagrees with itself and with the screen on two facts
findings.claim: Line 253 says kittui is "built from `tui/`" and line 327, with the tree, says `projects/tui/`. Line 47 gives `kit flow` seven stages, while kittui's Flow has five tabs and no page says the desk and the worktrees are shown in Repositories.
findings.evidence: The two README lines as quoted; features.md's table gives Flow "issues, changes, builds, incoming, releases", and the live tab bar showed those five.
findings.fix: Write `projects/tui/` at line 253. Say at line 47 that the text form prints seven stages and the UI shows five, with the desk and the worktrees under Repositories.

findings.title: The reference pages are written in chained clauses that take two readings
findings.claim: Sentences in docs/apps.md and the UI part of docs/features.md stack three or four dependent clauses, each leaning on "as", "which", or "its own". A platform engineer reading to answer for the tool will skim them and miss the limits they state.
findings.evidence: docs/apps.md:10-12: "A mark is a text that changes when what its stage draws does, and `null` for a stage with none, which kittui reads again only on Refresh, as it offers no Watch for a tab kit never marks."
findings.fix: One fact a sentence in README, install.md, the welcome pages, and each table's lead-in. For apps.md, move the per-forge detail under each table into a second table: forge, how it is read, its cap.

findings.title: The tab markers are one-cell circled digits told apart by their fill
findings.claim: Every screen marks the selected tab ➊ and the others ➁ ➂, dingbat circled digits one cell wide. At small sizes in common terminal fonts the two forms read alike and the digit inside is hard to make out.
findings.evidence: The golden's line 2, `➊╶───────────────╮➁╶────────────────╮➂╶`. I saw them only as text in tmux; a look in iTerm2 and Terminal at 12 points would settle it.
findings.fix: Draw the plain digit, bold on the selected tab, since the open box under it already marks the selection.

areas.title: the experience of an AI agent
areas.coverage: Read whole: every file in scope. Read in part: headers of twelve verbs, issue.sh's start and sweep, test names. Ran in a private copy: kit serve (about 45 calls), kit context and its hook, lint, commit in five spellings, trust, a consumer install. No forge called; kittui not driven; work/close/settle judged from code.
areas.summary: An agent can start, commit, and submit, and kit's refusals are unusually actionable, but the agent surface is built for a session that sits in the worktree, while kit itself starts the agent at the desk. From there the MCP lint says "nothing to lint", the hook names the wrong rules for a workflow file, and kit work takes the human's uncommitted work along. The workflow demands a report no verb writes, and an untrusted clone hands the agent "kit trust --yes". Reading before acting is about 8,500 tokens, 41% of it needed. findings.md was NOT written: the Write tool refuses report files from a subagent, so the full text is only in this result.
strengths: Every refusal I provoked named the next command (run: cd <path> && ...) or the missing flag, and an unknown verb offers the nearest; no kit message recommends a command the deny list refuses.

The MCP server's own refusals let an agent correct itself in one step: unknown argument with the names taken, 'fit no usage' with every usage, path outside the repository, and a listing-only tool's 'run it in a terminal to ...'.

Tools are typed from the verbs' headers by the code kit help uses, so schema, help, and verb cannot drift; 1st.md, docs/serve.md, claude.md, kit help serve, and serve.sh name the same 17 tools in the same three groups.
Annotations are honest: readOnlyHint only on the seven tools where it holds, destructiveHint on close, settle, and unassign, openWorldHint on what asks the forge.

kit commit takes the error-prone decisions from the agent: it supplies #N from the branch, refuses the desk and the default branch, lints and judges policy before the commit exists, and opens no editor.
One rule text, never copied: the hook and the mirrors name a rule and do not quote it.
The AGENTS.md region is 212 bytes and harness-neutral; the Integrity section is 778 bytes of concrete, checkable rules; kit help with no argument is a 3.9 KB map with examples.
The package pages say plainly what each harness cannot enforce, and 1st.md says the deny list works by literal pattern.
The hook answers in about 0.3 s and a context call in about 0.5 s; the server reloads changed code without a reconnect.

Token budget measured (bytes/4): AGENTS region 55, 1st.md 3,550, workflow.md 770, tools/list 4,100, instructions 50: about 8,500 before the first action, about 41% needed; plus 1,600 before a first .sh edit, 2,250 for a justfile, 1,000 for Markdown. A first task is 13 tool calls when nothing goes wrong, about 18 in practice.

findings.title: The MCP tools answer for the desk, so lint tells an agent in a worktree there is nothing to lint
findings.claim: Every tool runs its verb in the directory the server started in, the root checkout, and no tool can name a worktree, while the rules send the agent to work in one. lint, check, settle, and flow desk therefore answer for the desk.
findings.evidence: With a bad.sh staged in worktrees/7-fix-the-thing, tools/call lint {} returned isError=false and "nothing to lint"; cd into the worktree and kit lint printed the shellcheck finding and "2 rule(s) refused".
findings.fix: Give lint, check, context, kinds, and settle an optional worktree property (enum from git worktree list) and run the verb there. Until then have lint name the checkout it read and say in serve_instructions that tools read the root checkout.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced: desk server's `lint {}` answers "nothing to lint", isError=false, with bad.sh staged in the worktree. Narrower than claimed: lint with path worktrees/7-fix-the-thing/bad.sh passes serve:inside and reports both findings; a server started in the worktree answers for it; settle takes a number; flow desk is the desk by definition. check has no handle.

findings.title: A file in a worktree is classified from the desk's root, so the hook and the context tool miss its rule
findings.claim: context:relative makes a path relative to the checkout the command runs in, so from the desk a worktree file starts with worktrees/<N>-<slug>/ and every root-anchored glob stops matching. The CLI, the Claude hook, and the MCP context tool all give the wrong rule set.
findings.evidence: From the desk, kit context worktrees/7-fix-the-thing/.github/workflows/kit-ci.yml printed only styles/house, prose, yaml; from inside the worktree the same file also got rules/workflows.md, styles/workflows.md, and rules/bash.md. The hook's additionalContext and the tool's kinds [any,text,yaml] were wrong the same way.
findings.fix: In context:relative find the root with git -C <the path's nearest existing directory> rev-parse --show-toplevel, classify relative to it, and read that checkout's .kit/kinds. Add a test that passes a worktree path from the desk.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced all three from the desk: CLI, `kit context --claude` with the absolute worktree path, and the MCP tool give styles house, prose, yaml only, kinds [any,text,yaml]; inside the worktree the same file adds rules/workflows.md, styles/workflows.md, rules/bash.md. context.sh:72-86 strips only the current root; context:claude ignores the payload's cwd.

findings.title: kit work moves the human's uncommitted desk work into the agent's worktree, against 1st.md
findings.claim: 1st.md says the desk is the human's and an agent never changes it in place, then sends the agent to kit work, which stashes everything uncommitted on the desk, applies it in the new worktree, and leaves the desk clean. The MCP work tool always runs from the desk, is annotated destructiveHint false, and nothing an agent reads mentions the sweep.
findings.evidence: issue.sh:625 "Sweeping the uncommitted work on ${desk_branch} into the worktree"; tests/work.bats:252 "kit work sweeps the desk's uncommitted work into the worktree, and leaves the desk and the stash clean". Not run against a forge.
findings.fix: Add kit work --no-sweep, make it a serve_implied flag of the work tool, and tell agents in 1st.md to use it. With a dirty desk and no terminal, refuse and name both choices.
findings.verdict_note: Sweep is real: tests/work.bats:252 passes against its stub forge, desk left clean; serve.sh:100 says destructiveHint false; 1st.md and workflow.md are silent. Overstated: kit/bin/kit-work:18-22, the kit://help/work page the tool description names, states the sweep; it runs only when the server started at the desk (issue.sh:623); no work is lost.

findings.title: In a fresh clone the agent is handed the command that trusts the clone without asking anyone
findings.claim: Trust is meant to be a person's judgment, but an agent reaches kit trust --yes in three calls by following kit's own remedies, and no rule or deny list says the decision is not its own. In that state the hook and kit serve both exit 1 silently.
findings.evidence: Reproduced: AGENTS.md says run kit hydrate; it answers "kit runs nothing in ... until you trust it ... kit trust"; kit trust without a terminal answers "to trust it without asking, run: cd ... && kit trust --yes ...". Plausible only in that an agent follows a printed remedy.
findings.fix: Add to the AGENTS.md region: if kit says the clone is not trusted, stop and ask the person to run kit trust. Print the --yes remedy only where CI is set, and add kit trust to the Claude and Gemini deny lists.
findings.verdict_note: Chain reproduced: hydrate names kit trust; kit trust without a terminal prints the `kit trust --yes` command; hook and serve exit 1 with stderr only; no rule or deny entry mentions trust. Severity is lower: it needs an agent to act on a printed remedy, and an agent with a shell can already run the clone's code directly.

findings.title: The workflow requires a report in the pull request body, and no kit command writes one
findings.claim: Every agent task must end with the report in the pull request body, but kit ready takes only a number and no verb sets a body, so the agent must guess the forge and use gh, glab, or az. The body also holds kit's own Closes lines, which a replaced body removes.
findings.evidence: forge:pr-set-body is called only at issue.sh:561; no verb header has a body or report argument. That a replaced body breaks kit linked is plausible, not run.
findings.fix: Give kit ready --report=<text> and --report-file=<path> (or add kit report) that write the report above the kit's Closes lines through forge:pr-set-body, and name it in workflow.md step 4.
findings.verdict_note: forge:pr-set-body has one caller, issue.sh:561; github.sh:667 opens the pull request with an empty body; kit ready takes only a number, and no verb header has a body or report argument. kit-linked:89 and kit settle read Closes lines from the body. Loss on replacement was not run against a forge.

findings.title: kit commit -m is refused without naming --message, and 1st.md never shows the command whole
findings.claim: 1st.md says to run kit commit "exactly as written here" but writes it without a message, and the form every agent carries over from git fails. An unknown verb gets a suggestion; an unknown flag does not.
findings.evidence: kit commit -m "add notes" printed "unknown flag '-m'; run: cd ... && kit help commit"; -a the same; bare kit commit printed "kit commit needs --message or --file".
findings.fix: Accept -m, -a, and -F for kit commit, or have the refusal name the long flag. Write the full line once in 1st.md: git add <path>... && kit commit --message='<subject>'.

findings.title: The deny lists stop git checkout -b and do not stop a merge
findings.claim: "Never merge" is the contract's hardest rule, yet all 13 Claude patterns and 11 Gemini prefixes are git commands: gh pr merge, glab mr merge, az repos pr update, and kit trust are absent. git restore, git clean, and git stash on the desk are absent too, and main is literal.
findings.evidence: Read both lists. The git -C and git branch -d forms are known since 11-10 (packages finding 11), still open.
findings.fix: Add the three merge commands and kit trust to both lists, add git restore, git clean, and git stash, and deliver the main entries from a template filled with the default branch.

findings.title: The tool list costs about 4,100 tokens a session, and syntax with no argument returns 147 KB
findings.claim: tools/list is 16,373 bytes for 17 tools, of which an agent's own work uses four; flow alone is 3,927 bytes with eight kittui-only flags, and nine properties are --jq or --text "for a person". syntax is read-only with nothing required, so it is called unprompted.
findings.evidence: tools/call syntax {} returned 146,737 bytes, about 37,000 tokens. Per-tool sizes measured from the tools/list answer.
findings.fix: Drop syntax and version from serve_tools, and add text, jq, and flow's stages, me, capabilities, quota, marks, and cached to serve_hidden. If syntax stays, require verb.

findings.title: The rules are not in the repository git sees, so a hosted agent is pointed at files that are not there
findings.claim: A consumer commits AGENTS.md and the mirrors, which all point at .kit/1st.md and .kit/rules/*.md, files kit hydrate places and git ignores. The Copilot page says the files apply to the coding agent and code review on GitHub.com, where no kit is installed and .kit/ was never placed.
findings.evidence: git ls-files in a fresh consumer lists 25 files, none under .kit/; no package delivers a setup step. The hosted environments were not run, hence plausible.
findings.fix: Have agents/copilot deliver .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml that installs the pinned kit and runs kit hydrate, and say in the page that code review does not see the rules. Make the AGENTS.md region say what to do when kit itself is missing.

findings.title: The Cursor and Copilot mirrors tell the agent less than 1st.md does, and one never applies
findings.claim: 1st.md says run kit context before any change; each mirror says read the one rule and implies kit context is only for a file with no suffix, so styles that kit lint enforces and embedded rules are never named. kit-sh.instructions.md has applyTo "" and never applies, and both pages say seven files where there are eight.
findings.evidence: Read all 16 mirrors; the sh kind has no paths. My bad.sh was refused at lint for the bash style's template shape, which no mirror mentions. Rule-only mirrors are known since 11-10 (finding 24), still open.
findings.fix: Make every mirror's body one sentence: before you change this file, run kit context <path> and read every file it prints. Drop the Copilot sh file and correct the count.

findings.title: Four workflow rules can be met only by guessing
findings.claim: Step 2 says run kit work and contract item 3 says never run it, with "worker" defined as whoever implements; no text says how to get an issue (kit work --title); 1st.md's command list omits kit ready yet says run them exactly as written; and a repository with no gate leaves items 6 to 8 undecided.
findings.evidence: Read both files. In a fresh consumer kit gate printed "set gate in kit.yml ... there is no gate to run". Item 10's "Nothing more" also excludes the "what was left out" that step 4 requires.
findings.fix: Head the contract "When you are handed a worktree someone else started", add kit work --title=<text> to step 1 and kit ready to the list, and replace "exactly as written" with what it means. Say that no gate is reported as no gate and may be marked ready.

findings.title: More than half of the entry file is reference for whoever configures the kit
findings.claim: 1st.md is 14,214 bytes and 54% of it (What the kit delivers, Changing what kit adds) describes packages, CI, and placement, none of which bears on starting, changing, committing, or submitting. rules/bash.md spends 1,229 of 3,300 bytes on the kit's own modules, providers, and verb headers in every consumer.
findings.evidence: Section byte counts by awk: 6,059 and 1,579 of 14,214; the parts an agent acts on total about 4,400 bytes, 31%.
findings.fix: Keep 1st.md to the five sections an agent acts on and move the two reference sections to a .kit/packages.md linked in one line. Move the modules, providers, and verb paragraphs to a rule of their own kind.

findings.title: The Claude hook fails open and silent, and repeats itself on every edit
findings.claim: The hook needs kit on the harness's PATH; this repository's house package registers the MCP server by path for that reason but leaves the hook, and in an untrusted clone the hook exits 1. Either way the edit goes on and the agent hears nothing; when it works it says "read each before this change" on every edit.
findings.evidence: Hook in an untrusted clone: status 1, no JSON. The exit 127 case rests on Claude Code's documented behaviour (known since 11-10, finding 23, still open).
findings.fix: Have house deliver the hook by path as it does the server, and print one additionalContext line when kit cannot answer. Keep the rule files already named per session_id and say nothing for a set named before.

findings.title: Resource descriptions lose the kind on macOS, and two styles name the wrong kind
findings.claim: All eleven kit://kinds/* descriptions end "a file of kind " with no kind, because awk -F '\x1f' does not split in the system awk. A rule's or style's description uses the file name as its kind, so styles/prose and styles/house say kind prose and house; both govern text.
findings.evidence: resources/list output; printf 'a\x1fbash\x1fname\x1fbash\n' | awk -F '\x1f' '$3 == "name" {print $2}' prints nothing, and with -F $'\x1f' prints bash.
findings.fix: Use awk -F $'\x1f', and build the rule and style descriptions from context_file_kinds.

findings.title: Several tool descriptions and schemas promise what the tool refuses
findings.claim: tools, packages, and toolchains are described as installing, changing, and recording though each is a listing only; package offers a glob its enum refuses; close marks only reference required; and issue and pull request numbers must be strings. A verb's refusal reaches an MCP caller as a shell remedy.
findings.evidence: packages {"package":["style/*"]} gave "is not one of"; close {"reference":["7"]} ran and exited 2; settle {"number":7} gave "number is a string"; assign {"reference":[7]} gave "reference is a list of strings".
findings.fix: Describe a listing-only tool as a listing, drop the glob sentence where an enum is given, and mark a required group with anyOf. Accept a JSON integer for an operand.

findings.title: This repository's own agent files say things the tree does not bear out
findings.claim: AGENTS.md says kittui is built from tui/, which does not exist (it is projects/tui/). The repository takes the workflow package's "never commit a plan as a file" and commits 17 plans and 7 specs under docs/superpowers/ with AGENTS.md silent; docs/context.md says the bash rule lists five templates, and it lists six.
findings.evidence: ls tui fails; find docs/superpowers lists the files. The first two are known since 11-10 (findings 26 and 27), still open.
findings.fix: Write projects/tui/, add one line to AGENTS.md saying where plans and specs go in this repository, and write "six".

areas.title: terminals, width, colour, and access
areas.coverage: Read whole: docs/terminals.md, terminal.sh, log.sh, ten readers, terminals.json, glyphs.json, terminal.jq, style, grid.go, tabs.go, shell.go, flow view/glyph/legend. Sampled the rest of flow, table, shell; not form, welcome, tutorials. Ran kittui in tmux at eleven sizes, under NO_COLOR, dumb, and 16 colours; glyph inventory, fc-list, contrast, go test.
areas.summary: kittui's layout engine, keys bar, and legend are strong, and it survived every size from 200x50 to 2x1. Its surface assumes a dark theme, 256 colours, a Nerd Font, colour emoji, and a Mac keyboard, and says none of it. On a light theme the cursor row is unreadable; under NO_COLOR no menu, dialog, or heading shows focus; stock fonts put boxes round every label. Enter does nothing on a row, sorting takes 15 keys, and A bulk-assigns unasked. Three findings are known since 11-10 and still open. findings.md was not written: the harness refused the Write as a report file, so everything is here, the keystroke counts under U7-6.
strengths: Narrow and tiny screens are handled with care: nothing broke or wrapped from 200x50 down to 2x1 or across a live resize; columns scroll with ◃ ▹, the first column stays, and a wide glyph cut by an edge becomes a space (pane.Cells, shell.Splice).
The keys bar is derived from where the keyboard is, never written per screen, and drops its middle segments first when narrow.
The legend lists only the glyphs now on the screen, in reading order, and marks which are links.

Selection, folding, tabs, and staleness each have a glyph (▣ ◩ ▸ ▾ ➊ •), not a colour alone; an alert count is bold as well as red; a pill's ink is chosen by luma, and all twelve pastels pass 4.5:1 with white.
One table of glyphs (glyphs.json) feeds the Go constants and kit help, and one table of terminals feeds every check.
The terminal checks never write a setting, time out in a second, stop their children, and say plainly when they could not read; terminal:color mirrors colorprofile's rules line for line.
The tab numbers were chosen for fixed cell width, and the reasoning is written at tabs.go:182.

findings.title: The cursor row is a fixed dark grey band, unreadable on a light background and faint on dark themes
findings.claim: The row under the cursor is drawn on 256-colour 236 (#303030) whatever the terminal's background is, with the terminal's default text on it, and kittui never asks for the background. A group heading or one-cell row under the cursor has no other mark, and the tab and menu colours (221, 114, 215, 75, bright cyan) are dark-only too.
findings.evidence: Capture shows ESC[48;5;236m on the cursor line; black text on #303030 is 1.59:1 (Terminal Basic), the band is 1.06:1 from One Dark and Nord and 1.26:1 from VS Code Dark+, and at TERM=xterm it is emitted as ESC[40m, black on black. Tab colour 221 is 1.39:1 on white, 114 is 1.74:1, 75 is 2.32:1.
findings.fix: Ask the background once (tea.RequestBackgroundColor), keep a light and a dark palette, and set the band a fixed step from the real background. Add a mark that is no colour, such as a bar in the gutter's first cell on every line of the cursor's row, headings included.

findings.title: Under NO_COLOR the keyboard focus cannot be seen in any menu, dialog, control, or group heading
findings.claim: style.Selected is a background and a foreground colour and nothing else, and strips the line's own styles, so with NO_COLOR=1 the line under the keyboard is drawn like every other, or as the one name that is not bold. Known since 11-10 as a gap (no NO_COLOR code or test), still open; TERM=dumb also loses dim, the only sign of a disabled menu line.
findings.evidence: Run at 100x30 with NO_COLOR=1: in the = menu after two downs only 'Flow' (where you are) differs; on the control line the focused stop 'source' is the only name not bold; a heading under the cursor has no escape sequence at all. README.md:309 says style honors NO_COLOR and shell.go:338 calls the line 'inverse'.
findings.fix: On tea.ColorProfileMsg at Ascii or below draw Selected in reverse video and the band as reverse or a gutter mark. Add a golden of an open menu and of the rows under NO_COLOR.
findings.verdict_note: Reproduced with a fresh build at 100x30. NO_COLOR=1: the menu line under the keyboard carries no attribute, focused `source` is the one name not bold, and moving between rows changes nothing on screen. TERM=dumb emits no attributes. The row and heading cursor is style.Band (table/draw.go:95, grid/grid.go:330), not presets.go:229, which is the preset pill; README is projects/tui/README.md:309.

findings.title: Every label and the preset selector need a Nerd Font, which nothing documents and nothing replaces
findings.claim: Pill ends are private-use U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, and a key and value are joined by U+E0B4 with the = or : dropped, on Flow's first screen. Stock fonts lack them, so labels are flanked by boxes or gaps, and without colour priority=high reads 'priorityhigh'.
findings.evidence: Capture bytes are 'ee 82 b6 priority ee 82 b4 h'; fc-list here finds U+E0B6 only in Nerd Fonts, not Menlo or Monaco; pill.go is the only file that mentions a Nerd Font and docs/terminals.md:23 says a font is not a finding. 'priorityh…' seen under NO_COLOR=1 and at TERM=xterm, where both segments map to red; what a given terminal draws for the missing glyph is plausible, not seen.
findings.fix: Draw a pill as a padded block on its colour without end caps unless a setting asks for them, and keep the separator where the two segments share a colour or have none. Say in docs/terminals.md what the caps need.

findings.title: A assigns every selected issue at once with no question, and space on a heading selects its whole group
findings.claim: Assign to Me runs kit assign over the whole selection on one unshifted key, though the file's header says an action that changes what others see asks first, and Unassign and Close do ask. With the cursor hard to see on a heading, one space and one a assign a group.
findings.evidence: Run against the fake kit: five downs put the cursor on heading 'kit 6', space selected six rows, and 'a' printed '✅ kit assign #1 #8 #46 #31 #45'. act.go:296 is 'return m.run(each("assign")(""))' while Unassign at 299 calls confirm.
findings.fix: Ask, listing the issues, whenever more than one is selected, as Unassign does.

findings.title: At 80 columns a pull request's state is an emoji alone, and the issues legend does not explain it
findings.claim: At 100 and 80 columns the issues stage narrows the state column to its glyph (🏁 🔥 🔨 💬), and the legend adds the nine states only on the changes stage. Known since 11-10 (Apps 20), still open, and now it bites at the commonest width.
findings.evidence: 80x24 and 100x24 runs show 'state' holding the glyph alone where 120 columns shows '🏁 ready'; flow/testdata/legend.golden lists 24 glyphs for issues and none of the states. legend.go:156 is 'if name == "changes"'.
findings.fix: Give the issues stage "states" in glyphs.json as changes has, and regenerate the Go region.

findings.title: On a row enter does nothing, actions ignore the row under the cursor, and sorting takes 15 keys
findings.claim: Flow's key handler has no case for enter in the rows while Help's rows say '⏎ open', every action needs space first, 'f' works only on the preset line, and ⌃Q is the only quit and no keys bar names it. Opening the thing you are on and sorting are both harder than a newcomer expects.
findings.evidence: Counted by run: sort by age is esc, ↓, ⇥x4, f, ↓x6, s, esc = 15 presses against 2 clicks; tab switch 1; search 1 plus text; quit 1 (⌃Q, named only in the = menu; q and esc do nothing). By code: open the cursor's issue is ␣ then O (O named only in the : menu); Packages app is =, p three times, ⏎ = 5.
findings.fix: Enter on a row opens its page, the tab menu's actions fall back to the cursor's row when nothing is selected, and 'f' opens Fields from the rows. Add '⌃Q quit' to the screen's segment of the keys bar.

findings.title: The keys bar names keys in macOS glyphs, with no legend for them
findings.claim: The bar and menus read ⇥·⇧⇥, ␣, ⌃A, ⌃Q, ⇞⇟, ⏎, ⌥←→, which a person on Windows Terminal or Linux has no keys for, and ? explains none of them. The Windows Terminal lines of terminals.json and docs/terminals.md:223 say ⌥ as well.
findings.evidence: Captured bar: '⇥·⇧⇥ tab ↓ groups', '␣·⇧↑↓ select ⌃A all', '⇞⇟ page'. legend.go:116-143 lists the legend's parts and holds no key glyph.
findings.fix: Off macOS (WSL included) write Ctrl+Q, Alt+←, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, PgUp. Or add the key glyphs to the legend.

findings.title: The width probe measures the safest emoji, and kittui does nothing with any probe's answer
findings.claim: The probe prints 📚 (Unicode 6) while kittui draws 🟢 (12), six Unicode 11 emoji, and one variation-selector sequence ▶️, so old width tables pass it and still shift columns. No Go file reads KIT_TERMINAL_PROBES, so a failed probe changes nothing kittui draws and there is no plain-glyph fallback.
findings.evidence: Glyph inventory: 92 two-cell emoji, newest U+1F7E2; grep finds KIT_TERMINAL_PROBES in bash only. terminal.jq run for a console-like terminal gives 'draws 📚 in 1 cell(s), not two, so kittui's columns shift; no setting kit knows explains it' with fix null, while docs/terminals.md:45 says a failed probe 'says what kittui does instead'.
findings.fix: Print 🟢 and ▶️ too and report the worst. Give glyphs.json a one-cell text form per glyph and have kittui use it when emoji_width is not 2 or a setting asks.

findings.title: Copy says it copied where the terminal threw the request away
findings.claim: Copy Links prints a success notice and sends OSC 52 with no way to know it landed; at tmux's default set-clipboard external it is discarded. The docs' tmux section omits set-clipboard and the 'copy' need has no probe.
findings.evidence: tmux 3.8, default 'set-clipboard external': notice '🔗 copied 1 links', then 'tmux show-buffer' says 'no buffers'. After 'set -g set-clipboard on' the same keys leave a buffer '- #45 kit flow is the one picture…'.
findings.fix: Add set-clipboard to the tmux section and read it (tmux show -gv set-clipboard) in a tmux reader. Say 'sent to the clipboard' where kit cannot know, and write '1 link'.

findings.title: At 24 rows, twelve lines of chrome stand above the first row
findings.claim: At 80x24 the menu bar, three lines of tabs, the tab's title, a blank, the control line, its rule, the outer heading, a blank, the header, and its rule come before any issue. Eleven lines are left for rows and headings, nine once ⬆ and ⬇ take one each.
findings.evidence: 80x24 capture: first data row on line 13. At 80x16 one row shows between '⬆₂' and '⬇⁶'; Maximize (M, inside the : menu) starts the pane on line 3.
findings.fix: Under about 30 rows drop the title line and the two blanks, or maximize by default.

findings.title: With the legend open, page up and page down move the legend while the bar says they page the rows
findings.claim: legendKey takes home, end, pgup, and pgdown before the rows see them, and returns true even when the legend is already in that corner, so the rows cannot be paged while it shows. At 80x16 the legend also covers the whole pane.
findings.evidence: flow.go:791 'if m.legendKey(k.String()) { return m, nil }' precedes the rows' pgup and pgdown cases. The 80x16 capture with the legend open still shows '⇞⇟ page' in the rows' segment; confirmed by reading, the paging itself not timed by run.
findings.fix: Move the legend with its own arrows and a key of its own, and leave paging to the rows.

findings.title: Several marks come from no monospaced font, and the radio's two states differ by a dot
findings.claim: ➊ ➁, ⦿ ⦾, ⤢, ⧉, and ⬇ are drawn from fallback fonts at another size, and ⬆ ⬇ are emoji-capable code points. Known since 11-10 (Components 19, circled glyphs against the project's own rule), still open.
findings.evidence: fc-list on this Mac: U+278A, U+2781, U+29BF, U+29BE, U+2922, U+29C9, U+2B07 are in none of Menlo, Monaco, MesloLGS NF, or FiraCode Nerd Font. How each terminal then draws them is plausible, not seen.
findings.fix: Use ◉ and ○ (both in Menlo) or '(•)' and '( )' for the radio. Use ↑ and ↓ for rows above and below.

findings.title: welcome fails a stock terminal for ⌥, which kittui has plain keys for
findings.claim: The 'option' finding is ok: false on the shipped defaults of Terminal, iTerm2, kitty, Alacritty, Warp, and Tabby, for one shortcut (⌥←→ folds a level) that < and > also do. Terminal's fix line itself says it breaks layouts such as AZERTY.
findings.evidence: terminal.jq run with Terminal's default object gives terminal-apple-option ok:false with the Use Option as Meta fix; the docs' Default columns show the bad value as the default for the other five. grep finds alt+left and alt+right as the only ⌥ bindings beside tab digits, and tabs/menu.go:37 binds > and < to Show More and Show Less.
findings.fix: Report the option findings as advice (💡), not as failures.

findings.title: ▼ is both a descending sort and the presets menu
findings.claim: In this snapshot one glyph has two meanings on adjacent lines, and the legend can list both. The branch's later history names a change for it (#282), which I did not read.
findings.evidence: legend.go:133 'presets menu' and legend.go:136 '▼ descending: click to clear'; the run after sorting shows ▲ on the header's rule beside 'All Issues ▼'.
findings.fix: Nothing if #282 landed after this commit; else give the sort a mark of its own.

findings.title: The mark for hidden tabs is withheld on the first tab
findings.claim: ▹ is blanked when scrolling would cut the selected tab, so on the first tab a hidden last tab leaves no sign. The package comment at line 16 says the triangle is dim there, and the code draws a space.
findings.evidence: kittui welcome at 80x24 opens with four tabs and no ▹; pressing 3 shows ▹ and a fifth tab, 'terms', exists (customize-40.golden).
findings.fix: Draw the triangle dim and inert where it cannot scroll.

findings.title: A wall-clock test fails on a busy machine
findings.claim: TestATurnOfTheWheelOverTenThousandRowsIsWellUnderAFramesTime holds an 8 ms bound on real time, so it fails whenever the machine is loaded.
findings.evidence: Three runs of three failed here ('take 15.67097ms, over 8ms') with a load average of 55 from other sessions; the other five packages passed.
findings.fix: Count work (rows measured, lines drawn) in place of time, or skip under load.

findings.title: Small prose slips and one colour rule broken
findings.claim: Two messages read badly, and the preset pill's text uses colour 0, which style.go:45 says a theme may remap and avoids by using 16.
findings.evidence: 'draws 📚 in 1 cell(s), not two' from the jq run; '🔗 copied 1 links' from the run; presets.go:242 'Foreground(lipgloss.Color("0"))'.
findings.fix: Say 'one cell' and '1 link', and use 16.

areas.title: files no reviewer read whole
areas.coverage: Read whole: `kit/modules/bash/issues.sh`, `changes.sh`, `builds.sh`; `kit/packages/kind.schema.json`, `package.schema.json`, `rule.schema.json`; `kit/packages/hooks/lefthook/` (both files) and the root `lefthook.yml`; every comment of the 17 modules in `kit/modules/jq/` (code read whole for issues, changes, backlog, underway, flow, apps, completion, glyphs, merge; comments only for the rest, with `github_prs` read as code). Read as far as needed: `kit/bin/kit-flow`, `flow.sh` (cells, filters, pr-table, stage, picture, render), `forge.sh` (open-prs, open-issues, runs), `forge/github.sh` (runs), `workspaces.sh` (placed), `resolve.sh`, `context.sh` (load, read-kinds, compile), `lint.sh`, `kit/bin/kit-lint`, `template.sh` (head), `render.sh` (fill, holes), `settings.sh` (answers), `bin/ci`, `docs/packages.md`, `docs/context.md`, `docs/packages/hooks/lefthook.md`, the tests named in the brief. `materialize.sh` and `syntax.sh` read no kind, package, or rule metadata themselves (grep), so they were not read further. Run, in a copy under `out/X1/work`: `tests/changes.bats` and `tests/builds.bats` (14 pass); my own bats cases over the fake `gh` (wide and tabbed titles, C locale, fork branches, a cross-repository closing reference, 300 issues, a failed read, flags, a worktree); a small validator for the keywords the three schemas use (`out/X1/v/validate.js`; `ajv` is not installed and there is no network) over all 19 `package.yml`, 16 frontmatters, 11 kinds, and the house package; kinds, rules, and packages the schemas refuse, against the code; the pinned lefthook 2.2.2 over both `lefthook.yml` files with a stub `kit`. Checked and found sound: a failed forge read exits 1 in issues, changes, and builds, in text and JSON, and is not drawn as an empty stage; the column arithmetic of `issues:draw` and `builds:draw`; `\x1f` rows keep empty cells; `kit flow changes 007` and a 23-digit number; the guard refuses `--today`, `--no-fetch`, and owner flags where the usage does not offer them; every real package, rule, style, and kind validates; lefthook quotes staged names, skips `kit generate --check` with nothing staged, and skips a missing `.kit/lefthook.yml` without a word, as the documents say. Not re-reported: builds reads the 50 newest runs of any kind and says "no build since the last 20 runs" (`docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-11-10-code-review-findings.md`, item 12). Not checked: kittui's drawing of the same rows; GitLab and Azure DevOps providers; `across.sh` over a workspace.
areas.summary: A follow-up reader of issues.sh, changes.sh, builds.sh, the three package schemas, the delivered lefthook.yml, and the jq comments.
strengths:
failed read is never an empty stage: issues, changes, and builds each exit 1 with the provider's line, in text and
  in JSON, and status 3 (a forge without the feature) is the only failure read as "none", in one visible place each.

x1f` between cells, with the reason written once (`flow.sh`, `flow:check-cell`), keeps empty cells in place; no
  row I fed it lost a column.

ssues:draw` leaves out a column no row fills and blanks a glyph with its text, and the arithmetic of the title's
  width matches the cells exactly; `builds:draw` gives way in a stated order with floors, and a test holds it to 76
  columns.

e guard, not the stage, refuses a flag a form does not take, so `changes:documents` can treat every other word
  as a number.

l three schemas close their objects (`additionalProperties: false`) and every real file validates; the answers
  key pattern agrees with `render:holes` and with `kit.schema.json`.

e delivered `lefthook.yml` states the one thing a reader would get wrong (`kit lint` takes no `{staged_files}`,
  and why), and its claim about a missing include is true of the pinned lefthook.
erge.jq`, `version.jq`, `changes.jq`, and `flow.jq` are the comments to copy: short, one fact a sentence.

findings.title: an issue another repository holds, closed by a change here, replaces this repository's issue of that number
findings.claim: The issues stage matches a change's `closes` to the open issues by number alone, though `github_prs` keeps the issues of other repositories under `closes`, each with its own organization and repository (`kit/modules/jq/forge.jq:179-184`). With an open issue #12 here ("Our own twelve", milestone v9) and a change #5 that closes `other/elsewhere#12`, `kit flow issues --json` gives no row for this repository's #12 and one underway row `[12,"Elsewhere twelve","underway","other","elsewhere","v9",5]`: the other repository's issue, carrying this repository's milestone. `kit-flow` says issues "lists every open issue". Fix: in `backlog::unclaimed`, count an issue closed only when the closing reference's organization and repository are this repository's (or null), and in `issues::rows` take milestone, iteration, and swimlane from `$open` under the same test; add the case to `tests/jq/backlog.test` and `tests/jq/issues.test`.

findings.title: a fork's branch is matched to a local branch of the same name
findings.claim: `underway::rows` sets `here`, `local`, and `worktree` from the change's branch name alone, and `changes:documents` in a worktree keeps every change whose `.branch` equals the worktree's. A pull request from a fork whose head branch is `main`, the ordinary case for a fork, is drawn `💻 here  🍴 mallory` at any desk on `main`, with `worktree` the desk's path. In the worktree `7-fix-the-thing`, `kit flow changes` draws two changes: its own #3 and a fork's #5 from a branch of the same name, though the header says "the change its branch holds". Fix: require `.fork == null` in both places (a fork's work is on its author's desk); add a fork case to `tests/issues-underway.bats` and `tests/changes.bats`.

findings.title: a cell is measured in characters, so a wide character, a tab, or a C locale breaks the table
findings.claim: `flow:cell`, the title clips, and every width use `${#text}`. Three results, each reproduced: - A title in CJK is clipped at the right count of characters and drawn twice as wide: with `COLUMNS=100`, the row of a backlog issue is 137 columns, and a change's row and a build's row overflow the same way. - A tab in a title is printed as a tab, so the cells after it leave their columns (builds: the age and took columns). - Under `LC_ALL=C`, which a cron job, a bare ssh command, or a container may have, `${title:0:width-1}` cuts inside a character: `kit flow issues` with a title of 60 `é` ends its row in the byte `\303` before `…`, invalid UTF-8. `tests/helper.bash:7` pins the locale "so a width measured with ${#text} counts characters", so no test sees it. Fix: measure and clip by display width in one place (jq can fold East Asian wide ranges; or a small awk), replace control characters in a cell with a space, and run the measuring under a UTF-8 `LC_CTYPE` when the locale is not one.

findings.title: the text table of issues starts about 25 processes per row
findings.claim: `issues:draw` calls `flow:age`, `flow:cell`, `flow:paint`, `issues:cell`, `flow:state-emoji`, and `flow:state-sgr` in command substitutions, twice over the rows. With 300 open issues, `kit flow issues --json` takes 1 s and `kit flow issues` takes 10 s on this machine; the stage reads up to 10000 issues, and `kit flow --text` and every piped `kit flow` draw through it. `builds:draw` and `flow:pr-table` have the same shape with fewer rows. Fix: have jq, which already makes the rows, give each row's padded cells and widths in one pass, and let bash only paint; or make the helpers set a variable (`printf -v`) rather than print.

findings.title: only this repository's gate applies the three schemas, and the readers take in silence what they refuse
findings.claim: `bin/ci` runs `ajv` over `kit/packages/*/package.yml`, `kit/packages/*/*/package.yml`, the rules of top-level packages, the styles of namespaced packages, and the kinds of top-level packages. Nothing else validates with the schemas: not a repository's own package under `.kit/packages/`, not a source's, and not this repository's own `.kit/packages/house/package.yml` and `styles/house.md`, which `bin/ci`'s globs leave out (both are valid today), as they would a rule in a namespaced package or a style in a top-level one. `docs/packages.md:103` says that without a validator "`kit install` applies the same contract"; `resolve:validate` checks four things. What the schemas refuse and the code accepts, each run in an installed repository: - `depends: style/bash` and `includes: style/json` as scalars: `kit packages add mine` prints `✅ packages: kit mine`; the dependency is dropped (`resolve.sh:188-191` reads anything but a list as `[]`). - `description: 5`, `default: "true"`, `answers: {Key9: 7}`: accepted. - an `expects` entry with no `remedy`: accepted, with a default line (`resolve.sh:445`); a `notices` entry with no `text`: printed as `→ mine.txt:` with nothing after it. - a kind with `paths: "**/*.y"` (a scalar) or `path:` (misspelt): `kit kinds` lists it and no path is of it. `docs/context.md` says "a classification that cannot be made fails, and is never read as a path of no kind". - a kind with only `name` and `embeds`, a `kinds:` or `embeds:` that names no kind, a name such as `My Kind`. - a rule with `kind: bash` (a scalar) or no `kind`: it governs nothing, and `kit lint` passes without running it. The other way, the schemas accept what cannot work: `paths: []` satisfies the `anyOf` of `kind.schema.json`, and any `checks` name passes `rule.schema.json` (X1-6). Fix: make the readers refuse a known key of the wrong type and an unknown key in a kind or a frontmatter, as `resolve:validate` refuses an unknown key in `package.yml`; widen `bin/ci`'s globs to `kit/packages/**` and `.kit/packages/**`; add `minItems: 1` to `paths`, `content`, and `kinds`; and word `docs/packages.md:103` as the four checks it lists.

findings.title: `names` and `choices` are checks a rule can name, and kit lint offers `choices` as one
findings.claim: `kit lint` takes any function `lint:<name>` for a check. `lint.sh` also defines `lint:names` and `lint:choices`, which are not checks. A rule with `checks: [names, choices]` runs both: "the names check over 1 path(s)" prints the check names and passes, and "the choices check" fails with no finding. For an unknown name the refusal says "the checks are: choices jq-compiles pinned". The schema's pattern accepts all three. Fix: name the checks' functions apart (`lint:check:<name>`, or a declared list), and make `checks.items` an `enum` of `jq-compiles` and `pinned`, which a test compares with `lint:names`.

findings.title: the schemas' own words about rules and templates do not match the code
findings.claim: - The title names `.kit/rules/<kind>.md and .kit/styles/<kind>.md`, and `variant` is "the template's name under .kit/templates/<kind>/". The code uses the rule file's name, not a kind (`template.sh:52-66`), and they differ: `styles/prose.md` and the house package's `styles/house.md` govern the kind `text`. - `templates` is "a style's key", but the kit package's bash rule lists six templates; `docs/context.md:75` says "the bash rule lists five". - `package.schema.json:28` calls a dependency "another package in the release"; `resolve:locate` also finds it in a source or in the repository. - `context.sh:196` and `resolve.sh:383` send the reader to `packages/kind.schema.json` and `packages/package.schema.json`, paths under the release's root that a repository with the kit installed does not have; only `.kit/kit.schema.json` is delivered. Fix: say "<name>" for the file and the templates' directory, drop "a style's key", count six, and print the schema's full path (`${kit_root}/packages/…`) in the two errors.

findings.title: this repository's `refresh` runs after the kit's two commands, so what it stages is committed unchecked
findings.claim: Lefthook 2.2.2 runs the merged commands in name order: `kit-generate`, `kit-lint`, `kit-syntax`, `refresh` (run with both files and a stub `kit`). `bin/refresh` renders the installed copies and stages them, after `kit lint` has read the staged list. A template under `kit/packages/github/ci/templates/` is of kind `yaml` only; `actionlint` and the `pinned` check see the rendered `.github/workflows/kit-ci.yml`, which the hook stages too late to lint. The gate still catches it. The root file's comment says the repository "adds a command"; it adds two. The delivered file, `docs/packages/hooks/lefthook.md`, `README.md`, and `.kit/1st.md` agree with each other and with what runs. Fix: give `refresh` `priority: 1` (and the others a higher number), and say "two commands" in `lefthook.yml:4`.

findings.title: in a worktree, `--mine` drops the author column of a change that may be someone else's
findings.claim: `changes:documents` says that in a worktree "the owner flags change nothing", and it skips the filter; but `changes:render` still passes `flow:choice-of "$@"` to `changes:draw`, so `kit flow changes --mine` in a worktree draws the row without `👤 <author>` (run: the column goes), whoever opened the change. Fix: pass `all` as the choice when `flow:in-worktree`.

findings.title: a change with no author draws `👤` beside nothing
findings.claim: GitHub gives `author: null` for a deleted account, and `github_prs` folds it to `""`. The issues row then reads `🔀 #5 📭 no-check  👤` with an empty cell where the desk is named, and the change's row `👤` and spaces. Every other cell of `issues:draw` blanks its glyph with its text. Fix: draw the cell blank, or a word such as `ghost`.

findings.title: backlog.jq and underway.jq point at modules that do not exist and keep code nothing calls
findings.claim: Both `see:` lines name `modules/bash/backlog.sh` and `modules/bash/underway.sh`; neither file is in the tree, and `underway.jq:1` describes "the underway stage", which `kit-flow` says is no stage. `underway::by_owners` is called only by `tests/jq/underway.test` (`issues.sh` calls `issues::by_owners`, a copy), and `backlog::unclaimed`'s `$logins` and `$except` are only ever `[]` and `false` outside `tests/jq/backlog.test`. Fix: point both at `modules/bash/issues.sh` and `modules/jq/issues.jq`, delete `underway::by_owners` and the two parameters with their tests, or fold both modules into `issues.jq`.

findings.title: jq comments that must be read twice, and three that were never wrapped
findings.claim: The modules' comments are complete, and a reader who knows the code can check each clause. One who does not meets the same three habits throughout: a sentence of six to ten clauses behind commas; "as X" standing for "such as X" or for "because"; and a possessive with its noun dropped. The worst of each, by line: - Never wrapped, so the edit that made them was not reread: `syntax.jq:69` (201 columns) and `:70` (176), `template.jq:19` (220). `syntax.jq:68-70` is also the hardest sentence in the directory: "else the one that holds a given flag or option, two holding different ones and neither all being a refusal, as is a word left for an operand that opens another alternative". It documents `choose`, which is defined at line 78, inside `walk_sequence`. - One word in two senses: `forge.jq:146-148`, "A closed issue's assignees are those the answer's open issues with an assignee give it; an issue they do not name has none: one with no assignee, one closed, ...". The first "closed issue" is an issue the pull request closes; "one closed" is an issue whose state is closed. - Many clauses: `forge.jq:149-153` (reviewers: one sentence, seven clauses, two "as … gives them"), `forge.jq:60-62` (`colored`: "that has no color the one $colors gives its name, as a project's label list does on GitLab, as hex gives it"), `forge.jq:231-236` (`gitlab_mark`), `forge.jq:709-714` (`environment`: one sentence for five fields), `forge.jq:890-896` (`github_bots`), `forge.jq:1124-1129` (`github_bypasses`), `forge.jq:1165-1169`, `apps.jq:185-188` (`text`), `apps.jq:117-119` (`waiver`), `glyphs.jq:12-15` (the `stages` key), `workspace.jq:56-62` (`branches`), `terminal.jq:9-15`. - "as" for "such as": `forge.jq:106` "as a deleted account", `forge.jq:257` "as a fork's may not be", `forge.jq:926` "as an invitation not yet taken", `forge.jq:1127`, `toolchain.jq:42` "as a tarball", `apps.jq:103` ("for a stage that reads it twice, as Trust's alerts are read once for the findings and the waivers": twice, then once). "as" for "because": `forge.jq:313`, `:562`, `:674`, `:687`, `:698`, `:939`, `:1018`. `forge.jq:594-596` has both a garden path and a dangling participle: "as a GitLab older than 17.2, which orders none by its merge, lists them, ... more than $limit read meaning GitLab holds more". - Possessive with no noun: `forge.jq:145` and `:264` "pushed is the head commit's", "the head pipeline's"; `forge.jq:464`, `:602`, `:745`, `:962` "under $url, the project's"; `forge.jq:746` "GitLab's approvers are its approval rules'"; `forge.jq:872` "t<i> the i-th team's"; `apps.jq:109` "are the waivers'"; `apps.jq:162` "each place of level $i's"; `glyphs.jq:11` "stages, the group's; and screen, as a stage's"; `workspace.jq:61`; `toolchain.jq:8-9` "only the Brewfile's count", where "count" is the verb. - Opaque though short: `glyphs.jq:17` "A meaning is one glyph's wherever it is drawn, so a stage's legend never words it otherwise"; `glyphs.jq:43` "if its verb is $screen: flow, else its screen"; `glyphs.jq:46-48`; `forge.jq:676` "An artifact of a run GitHub no longer names is its download"; `apps.jq:4` and `workspace.jq:5` "key, the row's own within its stage". Fix: one sentence a field in the long lists (a table as `forge.jq:6-24` and `glyphs.jq:6-15` already use), "such as" and "because" where they are meant, the noun after each possessive, `choose`'s comment at `choose`, and a line check in the jq rule so a comment past 120 columns fails `kit lint`.

findings.title: forge.jq's header describes one of the documents it folds, and its list of `closes` is short
findings.claim: Line 1 says "a forge's answers, folded into the pull request document kit flow renders", and lines 3-24 list that document alone. The 1199 lines also fold issues, releases, builds, marks, quotas, merged changes, milestones, iterations, artifacts, environments, deployments, collaborators, teams, bots, attestations, alerts, rulesets, and bypasses. Line 18 lists `closes` as `{number, title, assignees, labels, age, source}`; each also carries `organization` and `repository` (line 114, and the JSON run in X1-1). Fix: split the module by document, as `issues.jq` and `apps.jq` already are, or list the documents in the header; add the two keys.

findings.title: comments that say what the one line under them says
findings.claim: `glyphs.jq:23` "data gives glyphs.json" over `def data: $glyphs::glyphs[0];`, and the same at `terminal.jq:27`; `glyphs.jq:57`, `:60`, `:84` and `terminal.jq:101` (each an overload that fills one argument); `workspace.jq:11`, `:14`, `:17` (`fields`, `lines`, `some`); `forge.jq:132`, `:246` ("reads … and gives its runs"); `forge.jq:1011`; `toolchain.jq:24` says "one line per name in $names, one per line". Fix: drop them, or say what the code does not: why `data` is `[0]`, which statuses `github_runs` reads as pending.

findings.title: 15 of the 17 jq modules lack the banner lines the house style asks for
findings.claim: `.kit/packages/house/files/repo/.kit/styles/house.md` rule 1: "A file with a banner has a line of dashes to column 120 under it, and another at the end of the file", and rule 2: "The line under the dashes is never a bare #". Only `apps.jq` and `version.jq` have both lines. `backlog.jq`, `changes.jq`, `completion.jq`, `serve.jq`, and `underway.jq` have neither, with a bare `#` on line 2; `syntax.jq` lacks the first; the other nine lack the last. `kit lint` checks the shape only where a rule has templates, and the jq rule has none. Fix: add a `module` template for jq and the lines.
